pages.title: Button
pages.description: A button with four intents and three sizes. It can also lend its styles to a link.
pages.markdown:
# Button

A button with four intents and three sizes. It can also lend its styles to a link.

Use a button for an action: saving a form, opening a dialog, deleting something. If clicking it takes you to another page, it's a link, and [it should stay one](#as-a-link).

```tsx
import { Button } from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return <Button>Save changes</Button>;
}
```

## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

## Import

```tsx
import { Button } from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `intent` | `"danger" \| "ghost" \| "primary" \| "secondary"` | `"primary"` | How much visual weight the button carries. Use `primary` for the main action in a view, and `danger` for actions that destroy something. |
| `size` | `"lg" \| "md" \| "sm"` | `"md"` |  |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead of a `button`, and give it the button's classes and props. This is how you make a link look like a button. |

Everything else is passed to the `<button>` element, including `ref`, `className`, `disabled` and event handlers.

One default differs from HTML. `type` is `"button"`, not `"submit"`, so a button inside a form doesn't submit it by accident. Pass `type="submit"` on the one that should.

## Intents

`intent` says how much weight the action carries. A view should have one `primary` button at most.

```tsx
import { Button } from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <>
      <Button intent="primary">Save</Button>
      <Button intent="secondary">Cancel</Button>
      <Button intent="ghost">Skip for now</Button>
      <Button intent="danger">Delete</Button>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Sizes

```tsx
import { Button } from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <>
      <Button size="sm">Small</Button>
      <Button size="md">Medium</Button>
      <Button size="lg">Large</Button>
    </>
  );
}
```

On a touch screen every size is at least 44 pixels tall and wide, and `lg` is 48. The smaller heights (32, 40 and 48 pixels) only apply when a mouse or trackpad is the main input, and [density](page:theming#density) moves them. Sizes still differ in padding and font size on touch.

## As a link

`asChild` renders the element you pass in and gives it the button's classes. Use it for navigation, so the result is still a real link that people can open in a new tab.

```tsx
import { Button } from "@nuvui/react";
import Link from "next/link";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Button asChild intent="secondary">
      <Link href="/">Read the docs</Link>
    </Button>
  );
}
```

## Disabled

```tsx
import { Button } from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <>
      <Button disabled>Save changes</Button>
      <Button intent="secondary" disabled>
        Cancel
      </Button>
    </>
  );
}
```

A disabled button can't be focused, so a keyboard user can't find out why it's disabled. If the reason isn't obvious from the page, leave the button enabled and explain what's missing when it's pressed.

## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves focus to the button. Disabled buttons are skipped. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Presses the button. |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> | Presses the button. |

### What the component handles

- It renders a native `<button>`, so the role and keyboard behavior come from the browser.
- Keyboard focus shows a 2 pixel ring in `--color-ring`. A mouse click doesn't.
- Every intent meets WCAG AA contrast in light and dark. The test suite checks this with axe.
- With `asChild` and `disabled`, the child gets `aria-disabled="true"` and is taken out of the tab order, because a link has no `disabled` attribute.

### What you need to handle

- An icon-only button needs a name. Add `aria-label`.
- Say what the button does. "Delete project" is better than "OK".

## CSS variables

Set any of these on the button, or on anything around it. They aren't declared by the library, so there's nothing to out-specify.

```css
.toolbar {
  --nuv-button-radius: var(--radius-full);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-button-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 2)` | Space between an icon and the label. |
| `--nuv-button-padding-inline` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 4)`, `calc(var(--spacing) * 3)`, `calc(var(--spacing) * 6)` | Padding left and right. Differs by size. |
| `--nuv-button-border` | `transparent`, `var(--color-border)` | Border color. Only the secondary intent shows one by default. |
| `--nuv-button-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius. |
| `--nuv-button-font-size` | `var(--text-sm)`, `var(--text-base)` | Font size. Larger on the lg size. |
| `--nuv-button-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-sm)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-md)`, `max(var(--nuv-touch-size), var(--nuv-control-height-lg))`, `var(--nuv-control-height-lg)` | Minimum height, and minimum width. Differs by size and by whether the device is touch. |
| `--nuv-button-bg` | `var(--color-primary)`, `var(--color-muted)`, `transparent`, `var(--color-danger)` | Background color. Differs by intent. |
| `--nuv-button-fg` | `var(--color-primary-foreground)`, `var(--color-foreground)`, `var(--color-danger-foreground)` | Text color. Differs by intent. |
| `--nuv-button-bg-hover` | `color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-primary) 88%, var(--color-foreground))`, `color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-primary) 88%, oklch(from var(--color-primary-foreground) calc(1 - l) 0 0))`, `color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-muted) 88%, var(--color-foreground))`, `var(--color-muted)`, `color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-danger) 88%, var(--color-foreground))`, `color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-danger) 88%, oklch(from var(--color-danger-foreground) calc(1 - l) 0 0))` | Background color while hovered. Differs by intent. |

## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-button` | Every button. |
| `.nuv-button--danger` | intent="danger" |
| `.nuv-button--ghost` | intent="ghost" |
| `.nuv-button--lg` | size="lg" |
| `.nuv-button--md` | size="md" |
| `.nuv-button--primary` | intent="primary" |
| `.nuv-button--secondary` | intent="secondary" |
| `.nuv-button--sm` | size="sm" |

A disabled button has the `data-disabled` attribute. Style that, not a modifier class.

## Server components

Button has no `"use client"` directive and uses no state, so it renders in a server component as it is. An `onClick` handler is the usual reason to need a client component around it. That's a React rule about passing functions from the server, not something specific to this library.

## Do and don't

**Do**

- Keep one primary button per view.
- Use `danger` for actions that destroy something, and ask for confirmation first.
- Use `asChild` with a link when the action is navigation.

**Don't**

- Don't put a click handler on a `<div>` and style it as a button. It won't be focusable.
- Don't disable a button without telling people why somewhere on the page.
- Don't shrink the touch size with `--nuv-button-height` on pages people use on phones.

pages.title: ButtonGroup
pages.description: Joins buttons, and the inputs or selects next to them, into one strip with shared edges.
pages.markdown:
# ButtonGroup

Joins buttons, and the inputs or selects next to them, into one strip with shared edges.

Use a button group for actions that belong together, for a main action with a menu of variations beside it, or to attach a button to an input. Each thing in the group keeps working as it did. The group only changes how they're drawn.

```tsx
import { Button, ButtonGroup } from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <ButtonGroup aria-label="Message actions">
      <Button intent="secondary">Reply</Button>
      <Button intent="secondary">Forward</Button>
      <Button intent="secondary">Archive</Button>
    </ButtonGroup>
  );
}
```

## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

## Import

```tsx
import { Button, ButtonGroup } from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Which way the buttons run. |

Everything else is passed to the `<div>` it renders, including `ref`, `className` and `aria-label`.

## What can go in one

The group works on its direct children. It takes the round corners off where two meet and overlaps their edges, so there's one line between them and not two.

These all have an edge of their own and join cleanly: [Button](page:components/button), [Input](page:components/input), `SelectTrigger`, [Toggle](page:components/toggle) and [InputGroup](page:components/input-group). A menu's trigger works too when it's a button, as in the next example.

[NativeSelect](page:components/native-select) and [PasswordInput](page:components/password-input) draw their edge on an element inside a wrapper, so the group can't square their corners. Keep them out of a group.

## A main action with a menu

```tsx
import {
  Button,
  ButtonGroup,
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <ButtonGroup>
      <Button>Publish</Button>
      <DropdownMenu>
        <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>
          <Button aria-label="More ways to publish">
            <svg
              aria-hidden="true"
              viewBox="0 0 16 16"
              width="16"
              height="16"
              fill="none"
              stroke="currentColor"
              strokeWidth="1.5"
              strokeLinecap="round"
              strokeLinejoin="round"
            >
              <path d="M4 6l4 4 4-4" />
            </svg>
          </Button>
        </DropdownMenuTrigger>
        <DropdownMenuContent align="end">
          <DropdownMenuItem>Publish at a set time</DropdownMenuItem>
          <DropdownMenuItem>Save as a draft</DropdownMenuItem>
        </DropdownMenuContent>
      </DropdownMenu>
    </ButtonGroup>
  );
}
```

Two filled buttons side by side would read as one, so the second gets a thin line on the side where they meet. It's mixed from the button's own text color, so it shows on any fill.

## With an input

```tsx
import { Button, ButtonGroup, Input } from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <ButtonGroup style={{ inlineSize: "100%", maxInlineSize: 360 }}>
      <Input type="email" aria-label="Email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
      <Button>Subscribe</Button>
    </ButtonGroup>
  );
}
```

The input takes the room the buttons leave. To put something inside the input's box instead, such as an icon or a unit, that's an [InputGroup](page:components/input-group).

## Vertical

```tsx
import { Button, ButtonGroup } from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <ButtonGroup orientation="vertical" aria-label="Zoom">
      <Button intent="secondary" aria-label="Zoom in">
        +
      </Button>
      <Button intent="secondary" aria-label="Zoom out">
        −
      </Button>
    </ButtonGroup>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

### Keyboard

A group adds no keyboard behavior. <kbd>Tab</kbd> goes to each button in turn, as it would without the group.

If you want a strip that's one tab stop with arrow keys inside it, that's a [toggle group](page:components/toggle-group).

### What the component handles

- It has `role="group"`, so a screen reader can say that the buttons belong together. Give it a name with `aria-label` when that helps, for example "Message actions".
- The button with keyboard focus is drawn above its neighbours, so no part of its ring is covered.
- The joined corners follow the reading direction: in a right-to-left layout the first button is on the right and has the round corners there.

### What you need to handle

- Give an icon-only button its own `aria-label`. The group's name doesn't replace it.
- On a phone, check that the strip fits. A group doesn't wrap, because a strip that breaks onto two lines no longer looks joined.

## CSS variables

The group reads one variable of its own. Everything else about how the buttons look comes from the [button's variables](page:components/button#css-variables), which you can set on the group to change every button in it.

```css
.editor-toolbar {
  --nuv-button-radius: var(--radius-full);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-button-group-divider` | `color-mix(in oklab, currentcolor 35%, transparent)` | Color of the line between two filled buttons, those with the primary or danger intent. |

## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-button-group` | The group. |
| `.nuv-button-group--horizontal` | orientation="horizontal" |
| `.nuv-button-group--vertical` | orientation="vertical" |

## Server components

ButtonGroup has no `"use client"` directive and uses no state, so it renders in a server component as it is.

## Do and don't

**Do**

- Group actions that act on the same thing.
- Keep one intent across a group. A primary button joined to a secondary one looks like a mistake.

**Don't**

- Don't use a group for a choice between options. That's a [toggle group](page:components/toggle-group) or a [radio group](page:components/radio-group).
- Don't join more buttons than fit on a phone.

pages.title: Card
pages.description: A box with an edge that groups a title, some content and the actions that go with them.
pages.markdown:
# Card A box with an edge that groups a title, some content and the actions that go with them. Use a card to set one thing apart from the things around it: a plan, a server, a customer. A page of settings that all belong together doesn't need a card around each one. A heading and some space do that with less on the screen. ```tsx import { Button, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return ( Team plan Billed once a year, on 1 March. Twelve seats, four of them in use. Seats you don't use aren't charged until someone is invited to them. ); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `Card` | The box. | | `CardHeader` | The title and description, with room at the end for an action. | | `CardTitle` | The title. An `h3` unless you say otherwise. | | `CardDescription` | A line under the title, in a paler color. | | `CardAction` | Something to do with the whole card, at the end of the header. | | `CardContent` | The body. | | `CardFooter` | The buttons. | Every part is optional. Leave out what a card doesn't need. ## Props ### CardTitle | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead of an `h3`, and give it the title's class and props. This is how you pick the heading level that fits the page. | The other parts add no props of their own. Each takes what its element takes, including `ref` and `className`. ## The heading level `CardTitle` renders an `h3`, which is right for a card under an `h2`. Where that isn't the level the page needs, pass `asChild` and put the right heading inside. It gets the title's look. ```tsx

Team plan

 ``` The level is about the page's outline, not about size. Screen reader users move through a page by its headings, and a level that skips or repeats sends them to the wrong place. The size is `--nuv-card-title-size`. ## An action in the header `CardAction` goes inside `CardHeader` and sits at the end of it, level with the title. Use it for a status, a menu button or one small action that applies to the whole card. ```tsx import { Badge, Button, Card, CardAction, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle, } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return ( Production eu-west, deployed 12 minutes ago Healthy All 14 checks passed on the last deploy. The next one is scheduled for tonight. ); } ``` ## Content that reaches the edges The card has no padding at its sides. Each part has it instead. So anything you put straight inside `Card`, outside the parts, runs from edge to edge: a picture, a table, a list with dividers. A picture at the top also needs the card's top padding gone and its corners clipped. ```tsx import { AspectRatio, Card, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle, } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return (

Quarterly report

 Updated on 4 July ); } ``` ## On small screens The padding is 16 pixels on a phone and 24 from the `sm` breakpoint up. The footer's buttons stack on a phone, each as wide as the card, with the last one in the code on top. From the `sm` breakpoint they sit in a row at the end. Write the main action last, and it's on top on a phone and at the end of the row on a wider screen. A long word in the title or the description breaks, so a card never grows wider than the room it has. ## Accessibility A card has no keyboard behavior of its own. The buttons and links inside it work as they do anywhere. ### What the component handles - The title is a heading, so the card shows up in the page's outline. - The description is a paragraph. - The edge is a border, which is still drawn where the browser forces its own colors, as Windows high contrast does. - The description's color has at least 4.5:1 against the card in every theme. ### What you need to handle - Pick the heading level that fits the page, with `asChild`. - Don't make the whole card a link or a button with other controls inside it. A control inside a control can't be reached from the keyboard in every browser, and a screen reader reads the whole card as the link's name. Make the title the link. - A card that's a region of the page people will want to jump to can be a `section` with `aria-labelledby` pointing at its title. Most cards don't need it. ## CSS variables Set any of these on `Card`, or on anything around it. ```css .dashboard { --nuv-card-padding: calc(var(--spacing) * 4); --nuv-card-shadow: none; } ``` | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-card-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 4)`, `calc(var(--spacing) * 6)` | Space between the header, the content and the footer. Larger from the sm breakpoint. | | `--nuv-card-padding` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 4)`, `calc(var(--spacing) * 6)` | Padding at the top and bottom of the card, and at the sides of each part. Larger from the sm breakpoint. | | `--nuv-card-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Border color. | | `--nuv-card-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius. | | `--nuv-card-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color. | | `--nuv-card-shadow` | `var(--shadow-xs)` | Shadow. Set it to none for a flat card. | | `--nuv-card-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color. | | `--nuv-card-title-size` | `var(--text-base)` | Font size of the title. | | `--nuv-card-muted-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the description. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-card` | Card. | | `.nuv-card__action` | CardAction. | | `.nuv-card__content` | CardContent. | | `.nuv-card__description` | CardDescription. | | `.nuv-card__footer` | CardFooter. | | `.nuv-card__header` | CardHeader. | | `.nuv-card__title` | CardTitle. | ## Server components The card parts have no `"use client"` directive and use no state, so they render in a server component as they are. ## Do and don't **Do** - Give every card in a set the same parts in the same order. - Keep one main action per card. **Don't** - Don't put a card inside a card. Use a [separator](page:components/separator) or a heading inside the one card. - Don't use a card only to get a border around a whole page section.

## An action in the header

`CardAction` goes inside `CardHeader` and sits at the end of it, level with the title. Use it for a status, a menu button or one small action that applies to the whole card.

```tsx
import {
  Badge,
  Button,
  Card,
  CardAction,
  CardContent,
  CardDescription,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
} from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Card style={{ width: "100%", maxWidth: 380 }}>
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>Production</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>eu-west, deployed 12 minutes ago</CardDescription>
        <CardAction>
          <Badge intent="success">Healthy</Badge>
          <Button intent="ghost" size="sm">
            Logs
          </Button>
        </CardAction>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>
        All 14 checks passed on the last deploy. The next one is scheduled for
        tonight.
      </CardContent>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

The padding is 16 pixels on a phone and 24 from the `sm` breakpoint up.

The footer's buttons stack on a phone, each as wide as the card, with the last one in the code on top. From the `sm` breakpoint they sit in a row at the end. Write the main action last, and it's on top on a phone and at the end of the row on a wider screen.

A long word in the title or the description breaks, so a card never grows wider than the room it has.

## Accessibility

A card has no keyboard behavior of its own. The buttons and links inside it work as they do anywhere.

### What the component handles

- The title is a heading, so the card shows up in the page's outline.
- The description is a paragraph.
- The edge is a border, which is still drawn where the browser forces its own colors, as Windows high contrast does.
- The description's color has at least 4.5:1 against the card in every theme.

### What you need to handle

- Pick the heading level that fits the page, with `asChild`.
- Don't make the whole card a link or a button with other controls inside it. A control inside a control can't be reached from the keyboard in every browser, and a screen reader reads the whole card as the link's name. Make the title the link.
- A card that's a region of the page people will want to jump to can be a `section` with `aria-labelledby` pointing at its title. Most cards don't need it.

| `--nuv-card-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color. |
| `--nuv-card-title-size` | `var(--text-base)` | Font size of the title. |
| `--nuv-card-muted-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the description. |

pages.title: Carousel
pages.description: Slides to move through by dragging or with buttons, with dots or thumbnails to go straight to one.
pages.markdown:
# Carousel Slides to move through by dragging or with buttons, with dots or thumbnails to go straight to one. Use a carousel for a few things of the same kind where one at a time is enough: the photographs of a product, the steps of a tour, cards that don't all fit in a row. It hides most of what it holds, so don't put anything in it that everyone has to see. A list or a grid shows all of it at once. ```tsx import { Carousel, CarouselContent, CarouselDots, CarouselItem, CarouselNext, CarouselPrevious, } from "@nuvui/react"; const slides = ["Plan the quarter", "Invite the team", "Connect billing"]; const slide = { display: "grid", placeItems: "center", blockSize: 160, border: "1px solid var(--color-border)", borderRadius: "var(--radius-lg)", background: "var(--color-muted)", }; export default function Example() { return ( {slides.map((title) => (
{title}
 ))}
); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Carousel, CarouselContent, CarouselItem, CarouselPrevious, CarouselNext, CarouselDots, CarouselThumbnails, CarouselThumbnail, CarouselPlayPause, } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `Carousel` | The carousel. It keeps which slide it's at. | | `CarouselContent` | The window the slides are seen through, and the row of them. | | `CarouselItem` | One slide. | | `CarouselPrevious`, `CarouselNext` | The buttons that go back and on. | | `CarouselDots` | A dot for each stop, to go straight to it. | | `CarouselThumbnails`, `CarouselThumbnail` | The same with a small picture of yours for each. | | `CarouselPlayPause` | The button that stops and starts a carousel that moves by itself. | Only the first three are needed. The parts are set out one under another, in the order you write them. Where the buttons and the dots sit is yours to say, with an element of your own around them. It's built on [Embla Carousel](https://www.embla-carousel.com/), which does the dragging and the moving. ## More than one slide at a time A slide is as wide as the carousel unless you say otherwise. `--nuv-carousel-slide-size` makes it a share of that, and `--nuv-carousel-gap` is the space between two. A size that leaves part of the next slide showing says there is a next slide. ```tsx import { Carousel, CarouselContent, CarouselItem, CarouselNext, CarouselPrevious, } from "@nuvui/react"; import type { CSSProperties } from "react"; const plans = ["Starter", "Team", "Business", "Enterprise", "Education"]; const slide = { display: "grid", placeItems: "center", blockSize: 120, border: "1px solid var(--color-border)", borderRadius: "var(--radius-lg)", background: "var(--color-muted)", }; export default function Example() { return ( {plans.map((plan) => (
{plan}
 ))}
); } ``` `options` goes to the engine. `align: "start"` lines slides up with the start of the carousel, and `slidesToScroll` moves several at once. With several slides in view there are fewer stops than slides: the carousel stops where the last slide reaches the end. `CarouselDots` draws a dot for each stop. ## Up and down `orientation="vertical"` moves the slides up and down. Give `CarouselContent` a height: the slides fill it. ```tsx import { Carousel, CarouselContent, CarouselItem, CarouselNext, CarouselPrevious, } from "@nuvui/react"; const notes = ["Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday"]; const slide = { display: "grid", placeItems: "center", blockSize: "100%", border: "1px solid var(--color-border)", borderRadius: "var(--radius-lg)", background: "var(--color-muted)", }; export default function Example() { return ( {notes.map((day) => (
{day}
 ))}
); } ``` ## Thumbnails A `CarouselThumbnail` is a button that goes to one slide, with whatever you put in it. sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import {
  Carousel,
  CarouselContent,
  CarouselItem,
  CarouselPrevious,
  CarouselNext,
  CarouselDots,
  CarouselThumbnails,
  CarouselThumbnail,
  CarouselPlayPause,
} from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Carousel` | The carousel. It keeps which slide it's at. |
| `CarouselContent` | The window the slides are seen through, and the row of them. |
| `CarouselItem` | One slide. |
| `CarouselPrevious`, `CarouselNext` | The buttons that go back and on. |
| `CarouselDots` | A dot for each stop, to go straight to it. |
| `CarouselThumbnails`, `CarouselThumbnail` | The same with a small picture of yours for each. |
| `CarouselPlayPause` | The button that stops and starts a carousel that moves by itself. |

Only the first three are needed. The parts are set out one under another, in the order you write them. Where the buttons and the dots sit is yours to say, with an element of your own around them.

It's built on [Embla Carousel](https://www.embla-carousel.com/), which does the dragging and the moving.

sections.markdown:
## Keeping the slide yourself

`index` and `onIndexChange` put the slide it's at in your hands, counted from 0. `defaultIndex` says where it starts and leaves the rest to the carousel.

```tsx
const [index, setIndex] = useState(0);

<Carousel aria-label="Tour" index={index} onIndexChange={setIndex}>
```

For anything the props don't reach, `onApi` gives you the engine itself once it's running.

sections.heading: Carousel props
sections.markdown:
## Carousel props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Which way the slides move: sideways, or up and down. Up and down needs a height on `CarouselContent`. |
| `index` | `number` |  | The stop it's at, counted from 0, when you control it. |
| `defaultIndex` | `number` | `0` | The stop it starts at, when you don't. |
| `onIndexChange` | `((index: number) => void)` |  | Called with the stop it has moved to. |
| `loop` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether going on from the last slide comes round to the first. |
| `autoplay` | `number` |  | Moves to the next slide by itself, this many milliseconds after the last. It needs a `CarouselPlayPause` inside, so it can be stopped. It waits while the pointer is over the carousel, stops for good when the keyboard reaches it, and doesn't start for someone who has asked for less motion. |
| `getSlideLabel` | `((index: number, count: number) => string)` | `"1 of 5", and so on` | What a screen reader calls each slide, from its number and how many there are. |
| `options` | `Partial<OptionsType>` |  | More for the engine, Embla Carousel: `align`, `slidesToScroll`, `dragFree` and the rest of its options. |
| `onApi` | `((api: CarouselApi \| undefined) => void)` |  | Called with the engine once it's running, and with `undefined` after. |

It also takes what a `div` takes, including `ref` and `className`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

It follows the [carousel pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/) of the ARIA Authoring Practices, in the form with a button for each slide.

### Keyboard

Every control is a button and a stop for Tab. There are no arrow keys: they belong to whatever has focus inside a slide.

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves through the buttons, and through what's in the slides that can be seen. |
| Enter, Space | Presses the button: back, on, a dot, a thumbnail, or stop and start. |

### What the component handles

- The carousel is a `region` that a screen reader calls a "carousel", and each slide a `group` it calls a "slide", named "1 of 5" and so on.
- A slide that's out of sight is `inert`: Tab doesn't go to what's in it, and a screen reader doesn't read it.
- When a button moves the carousel, a screen reader is told "Slide 2 of 5". While the carousel moves by itself it's told nothing, or it would never stop talking.
- The dot or thumbnail the carousel is at has `aria-current="true"`. The dot is longer as well as darker, and the thumbnail has a ring, so neither is told apart by color alone.
- A dot is 8 pixels across, inside a button that's larger. With a finger the button is 44 pixels tall and 24 wide: dots sit in a row, and wider ones would overlap. With a mouse it's 24 both ways. The buttons to go back and on are 44 both ways.
- The buttons to go back and on are disabled at the ends of a carousel that doesn't loop.
- Someone who has asked for less motion gets slides that change at once, without the slide across.
- In a right-to-left page the slides run the other way, and so do a drag and the arrows.

### What you need to handle

- Name the carousel with `aria-label`, such as "Photographs of the chair". Don't put the word "carousel" in it: a screen reader adds it.
- Name each thumbnail.
- With `autoplay`, include a `CarouselPlayPause`. Without one there's no way to stop it, and WCAG's 2.2.2 asks for one.
- Give a slide a name of its own with `aria-label` where "3 of 5" says too little.
- In another language, give the words: `getSlideLabel` on the carousel, `getDotLabel` and `aria-label` on the dots, `aria-label` on the buttons and the thumbnails' row, and `getLabel` on the stop and start button. The words said when a slide changes are English for now.
- Dragging is one way to move it and not the only one. Keep the buttons, or the dots.

# Checkbox A box that's checked, unchecked or partly checked. It works with a label and submits with a form. Use a checkbox for a choice that's saved along with the rest of a form, or for picking several things from a list. If the change applies the moment it's made, a [switch](page:components/switch) says that better. ```tsx import { Checkbox } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return (

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `checked` | `CheckboxPrimitive.CheckedState` |  | The state, when you control it yourself. Use it with `onCheckedChange`. |
| `defaultChecked` | `CheckboxPrimitive.CheckedState` |  | The state it starts in, when you don't control it. |
| `onCheckedChange` | `((checked: CheckboxPrimitive.CheckedState) => void)` |  | Called with the new state when someone toggles it. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Stops it from being focused or toggled. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks it as required. Inside a form, the browser won't submit until it's checked. |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name it's submitted under in a form. |
| `value` | `string \| number \| readonly string[]` |  | The value submitted when it's checked. It's `"on"` if you don't set one. |

Everything else is passed to the `<button>` that Radix renders, including `ref`, `id`, `className` and `aria-label`. The [Radix Checkbox reference](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/checkbox#api-reference) has the full list.

sections.heading: States
sections.markdown:
## States ```tsx import { Checkbox } from "@nuvui/react"; const row = { display: "flex", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 }; export default function Example() { return (
); } ```

sections.heading: Indeterminate
In a form
sections.markdown:
## In a form

Give the checkbox a `name` and it's submitted like a native one. Inside a `<form>`, Radix renders a hidden `<input type="checkbox">` next to the button, so `FormData`, `required` and form resets all work.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves focus to the checkbox. Disabled ones are skipped. |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> | Checks or unchecks it. |

<kbd>Enter</kbd> does nothing, the same as on a native checkbox.

### What the component handles

- It renders a `<button>` with `role="checkbox"` and `aria-checked`, which is `mixed` while indeterminate. This part is Radix.
- A click on a `<label>` that points at it toggles it.
- The box is 20 pixels, which is too small for a finger. On a touch screen the area that responds to a tap is 44 by 44 pixels, centered on the box. With a mouse it's the box alone.
- The edge of the box uses `--color-border-strong`, which has at least 3:1 contrast with the page in light and dark, so an empty box is still visible as a control.
- Keyboard focus shows a 2 pixel ring in `--color-ring`.
- The color change is only animated when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion.

### What you need to handle

- Give it a name. Use a `<label>` whose `htmlFor` matches the checkbox's `id`, or `aria-label` when there's no visible text.
- Leave room around it on phones. If two checkboxes are less than 44 pixels apart from center to center, their tap areas overlap and the one later in the page wins the overlap.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on the checkbox, or on anything around it.

```css
.settings {
  --nuv-checkbox-radius: var(--radius-full);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-checkbox-size` | `1.25rem` | Width and height of the box. |
| `--nuv-checkbox-border` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Border color while unchecked. |
| `--nuv-checkbox-radius` | `var(--radius-sm)` | Corner radius. |
| `--nuv-checkbox-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color while unchecked. |
| `--nuv-checkbox-fg` | `var(--color-primary-foreground)` | Color of the check mark and the dash. |
| `--nuv-checkbox-checked-bg` | `var(--color-primary)` | Background and border color while checked or indeterminate. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-checkbox` | The box, which is the button itself. |
| `.nuv-checkbox__check` | The check mark. |
| `.nuv-checkbox__dash` | The dash shown while indeterminate. |
| `.nuv-checkbox__icon` | The SVG that holds both marks. |
| `.nuv-checkbox__indicator` | The wrapper around the mark. Radix only renders it while the box is checked or indeterminate. |

Radix sets `data-state` on the box to `checked`, `unchecked` or `indeterminate`, and `data-disabled` when it's disabled. Style those, not a modifier class.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

Checkbox is a client component. It carries `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files.

You can render it from a server component, as the first example on this page does. It needs a client component of your own once you pass `onCheckedChange` or control `checked`.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Make the label clickable by linking it with `htmlFor`. It's a much bigger target than the box.
- Word the label so that checked means yes. "Email me updates", not "Don't email me".
- Use the indeterminate state for a parent whose children are partly selected.

**Don't**

- Don't use a checkbox for something that takes effect right away. That's a switch.
- Don't use checkboxes for a choice where only one option can be picked.
- Don't check a box for someone when it signs them up for something.

pages.description: A checkbox or a radio button drawn as a card, with room for a title and a description, where the whole card can be pressed.
pages.markdown:
# ChoiceCard A checkbox or a radio button drawn as a card, with room for a title and a description, where the whole card can be pressed. Use choice cards where each option needs a few words to explain it: plans, add-ons, ways to pay. `RadioCard` is for one of several and `CheckboxCard` for any number. For options that are a word each, a plain [radio group](page:components/radio-group) or [checkbox](page:components/checkbox) takes less room. ```tsx import { ChoiceCardDescription, ChoiceCardTitle, RadioCard, RadioGroup, } from "@nuvui/react"; const plans = [ { value: "starter", name: "Starter", text: "Up to 5 people. $0 a month." }, { value: "team", name: "Team", text: "Up to 50 people. $12 a seat." }, { value: "enterprise", name: "Enterprise", text: "Any number of people, single sign-on and an audit log.", }, ]; export default function Example() { return (
Plan {plans.map((plan) => ( {plan.name} {plan.text} ))}
); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { CheckboxCard, ChoiceCardDescription, ChoiceCardTitle, RadioCard, RadioGroup, } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `RadioCard` | A card with a radio button in it. It goes in a `RadioGroup`. | | `CheckboxCard` | A card with a checkbox in it. It stands alone. | | `ChoiceCardTitle` | The choice's name, which names the control. | | `ChoiceCardDescription` | More about it, which a screen reader reads after the name. | A card can hold anything else as well: a price, a badge, an icon. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `indicator` | `"end" \| "start"` | `"start"` | Which end of the card the checkbox or the radio button is at. | | `children` | `ReactNode` | | The card's content: a `ChoiceCardTitle`, and anything else. | `RadioCard` also takes everything a [`RadioGroupItem`](page:components/radio-group) does, such as `value` and `disabled`, and `CheckboxCard` everything a [`Checkbox`](page:components/checkbox) does, such as `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `onCheckedChange`, `name` and `disabled`. `ref` is the control's. `className` goes on the card. ## One of several `RadioCard`s go in a [`RadioGroup`](page:components/radio-group), which holds the value, the name for a form and the arrow keys. The group lays its children out in a column. Give it a grid of your own for cards side by side. ## Any number A `CheckboxCard` is a checkbox with a card around it, and each one stands alone. Group related ones in a `fieldset` with a `legend`, which is what names them together. ```tsx import { CheckboxCard, ChoiceCardDescription, ChoiceCardTitle, } from "@nuvui/react"; const addOns = [ { name: "sso", title: "Single sign-on", text: "Sign in through your identity provider.", on: true, }, { name: "audit", title: "Audit log", text: "Who changed what, kept for a year.", on: false, }, { name: "support", title: "Priority support", text: "An answer within four working hours.", on: false, disabled: true, }, ]; export default function Example() { return (
Add-ons {addOns.map((addOn) => ( {addOn.title} {addOn.text} ))}
); } ``` Here `indicator="end"` puts the checkbox at the far end of the card. ## Accessibility The keys are the control's own. A radio card is reached with Tab and changed with the arrow keys. Accessibility

## Accessibility

The keys are the control's own. A radio card is reached with Tab and changed with the arrow keys. A checkbox card is reached with Tab and changed with Space.

### What the component handles

**Do**

- Keep every card in a set to the same parts, in the same order.
- Choose one for people when there's a sensible default, as with a plan.

pages.title: Collapsible
pages.description: A button that shows and hides a piece of content below it.
pages.markdown:
# Collapsible A button that shows and hides a piece of content below it. Use a collapsible for detail most people don't need: the technical part of an error, the rest of a long list, advanced options. For several sections where opening one may close another, use an [accordion](page:components/accordion). For content that floats over the page, use a [popover](page:components/popover). ```tsx import { Button, Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return (

The request to /api/orders timed out after 30 seconds. Request ID 7f3a-22c1.

); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `Collapsible` | The wrapper. It holds the open state. | | `CollapsibleTrigger` | The button. | | `CollapsibleContent` | What's shown and hidden. | ## Props ### Collapsible These come from Radix. | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `open` | `boolean` | | Whether it's open, when you control it yourself. Use it with `onOpenChange`. | | `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | | Whether it starts open, when you don't control it. | | `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean) => void)` | | Called with the new state when the button is pressed. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | | Stops the button from being focused or pressed. | ### CollapsibleTrigger | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `asChild` | `boolean` | | Render the single child element instead of a `button`, and give it the trigger's behavior. | ### CollapsibleContent | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `forceMount` | `true` | | Keep the content in the page while closed. Hiding it is then up to you. Radix sets `data-state` to go by. | Each part also takes what its element takes, including `ref` and `className`. ## The trigger has no look of its own `CollapsibleTrigger` is a plain button with Radix's behavior and no styles. Pass `asChild` and put a [`Button`](page:components/button) inside, as the examples do, or style your own element. What a collapsible's button should look like depends too much on where it is for one look to fit. ## Showing more of a list The trigger doesn't have to come first. Here it sits under the content, and its text says what a press will do. ```tsx "use client"; import { Button, Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; const more = ["Billing address", "Tax number", "Purchase order"]; export default function Example() { const [open, setOpen] = useState(false); return (
  • Company name
  • Contact email
    {more.map((field) => (
  • {field}
    • ))}
); } ``` ## Padding goes on something inside The height of `CollapsibleContent` is animated from zero to the height of what's in it. Padding or a margin on that element isn't part of that measure, and the panel jumps at the end. Put the spacing on an element inside it. ## Content that has to be found while closed While it's closed, the content isn't in the page. The browser's find-in-page can't reach it, and neither can a crawler. `forceMount` keeps it in the page. Hiding it is then yours to do: Radix sets `data-state="closed"` on the element and leaves it showing. Hide it with a rule on that attribute, or use the browser's own [`
`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/details) element, which some browsers open by themselves when a search matches inside it. ## Accessibility ### Keyboard | Key | What it does | | --- | --- | | Tab | Moves focus to the button. Once open, the next stop is the first control inside the content. | | Space or Enter | Shows or hides the content. Focus stays on the button. | ### What the component handles - The button has `aria-expanded`, and `aria-controls` pointing at the content. This part is Radix. - Closed content is taken out of the page, so nothing inside it can be reached by Tab or read by a screen reader. - The slide is only animated when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion. ### What you need to handle - Write a label that says what's hidden: "Show the error details", not "More". - Either keep the label the same in both states, or change it to say what the next press does. `aria-expanded` already tells a screen reader which state it's in. - Don't hide something people need in order to finish a task, such as a required field. - Give the trigger a visible focus ring if you style your own. `Button` has one. ## CSS variables | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-collapsible-duration` | `var(--nuv-duration-slow)`, `var(--nuv-duration-base)` | How long the slide takes, both ways. By default opening takes a little longer than closing. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-collapsible__content` | CollapsibleContent. | `Collapsible` gets `nuv-collapsible` and `CollapsibleTrigger` gets `nuv-collapsible__trigger`. No styles are attached to either. Radix sets `data-state` to `open` or `closed` on all three parts, and `data-disabled` when the collapsible is disabled. ## Server components The collapsible parts are client components. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files. You can render them from a server component, as the first example on this page does. ## Do and don't **Do** - Put the button next to what it shows. - Start open when most people will want the content. **Don't** - Don't nest one collapsible in another. Two levels of hiding are hard to keep track of. - Don't use it to shorten a page that people read from top to bottom. Scrolling is easier than pressing.

sections.markdown:
## Props

### Collapsible

These come from Radix.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Whether it's open, when you control it yourself. Use it with `onOpenChange`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` |  | Whether it starts open, when you don't control it. |
| `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean) => void)` |  | Called with the new state when the button is pressed. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Stops the button from being focused or pressed. |

### CollapsibleTrigger

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `asChild` | `boolean` |  | Render the single child element instead of a `button`, and give it the trigger's behavior. |

### CollapsibleContent

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `forceMount` | `true` |  | Keep the content in the page while closed. Hiding it is then up to you. Radix sets `data-state` to go by. |

Each part also takes what its element takes, including `ref` and `className`.

`CollapsibleTrigger` is a plain button with Radix's behavior and no styles. Pass `asChild` and put a [`Button`](page:components/button) inside, as the examples do, or style your own element. What a collapsible's button should look like depends too much on where it is for one look to fit.

Padding goes on something inside

sections.markdown:
## Content that has to be found while closed

While it's closed, the content isn't in the page. The browser's find-in-page can't reach it, and neither can a crawler.

`forceMount` keeps it in the page. Hiding it is then yours to do: Radix sets `data-state="closed"` on the element and leaves it showing. Hide it with a rule on that attribute, or use the browser's own [`<details>`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/details) element, which some browsers open by themselves when a search matches inside it.

sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves focus to the button. Once open, the next stop is the first control inside the content. |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> or <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Shows or hides the content. Focus stays on the button. |

### What the component handles

- The button has `aria-expanded`, and `aria-controls` pointing at the content. This part is Radix.
- Closed content is taken out of the page, so nothing inside it can be reached by <kbd>Tab</kbd> or read by a screen reader.
- The slide is only animated when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion.

### What you need to handle

- Write a label that says what's hidden: "Show the error details", not "More".
- Either keep the label the same in both states, or change it to say what the next press does. `aria-expanded` already tells a screen reader which state it's in.
- Don't hide something people need in order to finish a task, such as a required field.
- Give the trigger a visible focus ring if you style your own. `Button` has one.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-collapsible-duration` | `var(--nuv-duration-slow)`, `var(--nuv-duration-base)` | How long the slide takes, both ways. By default opening takes a little longer than closing. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-collapsible__content` | CollapsibleContent. |

`Collapsible` gets `nuv-collapsible` and `CollapsibleTrigger` gets `nuv-collapsible__trigger`. No styles are attached to either. Radix sets `data-state` to `open` or `closed` on all three parts, and `data-disabled` when the collapsible is disabled.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

The collapsible parts are client components. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files. You can render them from a server component, as the first example on this page does.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Put the button next to what it shows.
- Start open when most people will want the content.

**Don't**

- Don't nest one collapsible in another. Two levels of hiding are hard to keep track of.
- Don't use it to shorten a page that people read from top to bottom. Scrolling is easier than pressing.

pages.title: ColorPicker
pages.description: Picks a color with an area and a hue slider, a field to type into, and presets.
pages.markdown:
# ColorPicker Picks a color with an area and a hue slider, a field to type into, and presets. Use a color picker where someone chooses a color that isn't on a short list: a brand color, the color of a label or a chart series. It's built from parts, so a picker can be all of them in a popover, or only a row of presets. ```tsx "use client"; import { ColorPicker, ColorPickerArea, ColorPickerContent, ColorPickerHue, ColorPickerInput, ColorPickerSwatch, ColorPickerSwatches, ColorPickerTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; const presets = [ { value: "#dc2626", name: "Red" }, { value: "#ea580c", name: "Orange" }, { value: "#ca8a04", name: "Yellow" }, { value: "#16a34a", name: "Green" }, { value: "#2563eb", name: "Blue" }, { value: "#7c3aed", name: "Violet" }, ]; export default function Example() { return ( {presets.map((preset) => ( ))} ); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { ColorPicker, ColorPickerTrigger, ColorPickerContent, ColorPickerPanel, ColorPickerArea, ColorPickerHue, ColorPickerInput, ColorPickerSwatches, ColorPickerSwatch, } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `ColorPicker` | Keeps the color. It draws nothing itself. | | `ColorPickerTrigger` | The button that opens the popover. It shows the color as a swatch and as text. | | `ColorPickerContent` | The popover, with a panel in it. | | `ColorPickerPanel` | The parts, one under the other. Use it by itself for a picker in the page. | | `ColorPickerArea` | The square to pick from: more color to the right, lighter towards the top. | | `ColorPickerHue` | The slider for the hue. | | `ColorPickerInput` | A field to type the color into. | | `ColorPickerSwatches` | A set of presets. | | `ColorPickerSwatch` | One preset, picked with a press. | Every part but the first is optional. Leave out what you don't want. The color is always a string, `#rrggbb`, in lower case. There's no transparency. ## In the page Without a trigger and a popover, `ColorPickerPanel` puts the picker where you write it. ```tsx "use client"; import { ColorPicker, ColorPickerArea, ColorPickerHue, ColorPickerInput, ColorPickerPanel, } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { const [color, setColor] = useState("#0d9488"); return (

The color is {color}.

); } ``` ## Presets only Where the colors to choose from are a list you've decided, leave out the area, the slider and the field. Give each swatch a name. Here the trigger shows the name in place of the hex. ```tsx "use client"; import { ColorPicker, ColorPickerContent, ColorPickerSwatch, ColorPickerSwatches, ColorPickerTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; // The colors a label can have, and no others. const labels = [ { value: "#b91c1c", name: "Urgent" }, { value: "#c2410c", name: "Waiting" }, { value: "#15803d", name: "Done" }, { value: "#1d4ed8", name: "In review" }, { value: "#6d28d9", name: "Idea" }, { value: "#475569", name: "Archived" }, ]; export default function Example() { const [color, setColor] = useState("#15803d"); const name = labels.find((label) => label.value === color)?.name; return ( {name} {labels.map((label) => ( ))} ); } ``` ## Saving the color `onValueChange` is called all through a drag, many times a second. That's right for a preview. To save, use `onValueCommit`, which is called once the color has settled: when a drag ends, a key is pressed, a preset is chosen, or a typed color is entered. ```tsx "use client"; import { ColorPicker, ColorPickerArea, ColorPickerHue, ColorPickerPanel, } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { const [color, setColor] = useState("#db2777"); const [saved, setSaved] = useState([]); return (
setSaved((before) => [...before, value])} >

Saved {saved.length} {saved.length === 1 ? "time" : "times"} {saved.length > 0 ? `, last as ${saved.at(-1)}` : ""}.

); } ``` ## In a form `name` puts the color in a form under that name. To give the trigger a label and a description, wrap it in a [field](page:components/field)'s `FieldControl`. ```tsx "use client"; import { Button, ColorPicker, ColorPickerArea, ColorPickerContent, ColorPickerHue, ColorPickerInput, ColorPickerTrigger, Field, FieldControl, FieldDescription, FieldLabel, } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { const [sent, setSent] = useState(""); return (
{ event.preventDefault(); const data = new FormData(event.currentTarget); setSent(`Sent accent=${String(data.get("accent"))}`); }} > Accent color Used for links and buttons.

{sent}

); } ``` ## ColorPicker props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` | `string` | | The color, as `#rrggbb`, when you control it. | | `defaultValue` | `string` | `"#000000"` | The color at first, when you don't. | | `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void)` | | Called with the color as it changes, many times during a drag. | | `onValueCommit` | `((value: string) => void)` | | Called with the color once it's settled: when a drag ends, a key is pressed, a preset is chosen, or a typed color is entered. The place to save from. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Stops the color being changed, and the trigger from opening. | | `name` | `string` | | Puts the color in a form under this name. | | `open` | `boolean` | | Whether the popover is open, when you control it. | | `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | | Whether it's open at first, when you don't. | | `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean) => void)` | | Called when the popover opens or closes. | | `children` | `ReactNode` | | The trigger and the content, or the panel alone for a picker in the page. | ## ColorPickerTrigger props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `children` | `ReactNode` | | What the button shows after the swatch. Left out, it's the color as text, `#rrggbb`. | It also takes what a `button` takes, including `ref` and `className`. ## ColorPickerContent props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `aria-label` | `string` | `"Color picker"` | The popover's name for a screen reader. It's a dialog, and a dialog has to have one. | It also takes what a [popover](page:components/popover)'s `PopoverContent` takes: `side`, `align`, `showArrow`, `container` and the rest. It's aligned to the start of the trigger unless you say otherwise. ## ColorPickerArea props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `aria-label` | `string` | `"Saturation and brightness"` | The thumb's name for a screen reader. | | `getValueText` | `((saturation: number, brightness: number) => string)` | `"Saturation 50%, brightness 50%"` | What a screen reader says for where the thumb is. It's given the saturation and the brightness, each from 0 to 100. | It also takes what a `div` takes, including `ref` and `className`. ## ColorPickerHue props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `aria-label` | `string` | `"Hue"` | The slider's name for a screen reader. | ## ColorPickerInput props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `aria-label` | `string` | `"Hex color"` | The field's name for a screen reader. | It also takes what an `input` takes, but for `value` and `type`. ## ColorPickerSwatch props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` (required) | `string` | | The color it picks, as `#rrggbb`. | It also takes what a `button` takes. `ColorPickerSwatches` and `ColorPickerPanel` take what a `div` takes. ## Working with the color yourself The functions the picker uses are exported too, for checking a color someone typed elsewhere or working out a shade. ```tsx import { hexToHsv, hsvToHex, parseHex } from "@nuvui/react"; parseHex("2563EB"); // "#2563eb" parseHex("#fa0"); // "#ffaa00" parseHex("blue"); // null const { h, s, v } = hexToHsv("#2563eb"); hsvToHex({ h, s, v: v / 2 }); // the same blue, half as bright ``` ## Accessibility There's no ARIA pattern for a color picker. Each part follows the pattern for what it is: a [slider](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/slider/) for the area and the hue, a text field, and buttons. ### Keyboard | Where | Key | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | The trigger | Enter, Space | Opens the popover. Escape closes it and focus goes back. | | The area | Right, Left | More and less saturation, by 1. | | The area | Up, Down | Lighter and darker, by 1. | | The area | Shift and an arrow | By 10. | | The area | Page Up, Page Down | Lighter and darker, by 10. | | The area | Home, End | No saturation, and all of it. | | The hue | Arrows | Round the hues, by 1 degree. Shift, Page Up and Page Down go by 10. | | The hue | Home, End | The first hue and the last, which are both red. | | The field | Enter | Takes what's typed as the color, if it is one. | | A preset | Enter, Space | Picks it. | Tab moves between the parts, in the order you wrote them. ### What the component handles - The popover is a dialog with a name, "Color picker", which `aria-label` on `ColorPickerContent` changes. - The area's thumb is a `slider` whose value is said in words: "Saturation 62%, brightness 80%". A slider has one value and this has two, so the words are where both are told. - The trigger's color is its description, so a screen reader says it after the name, whatever the name comes from: `aria-label`, a `label`, or a field. - The preset that's the color now has `aria-pressed="true"`, and a ring inside it that doesn't depend on telling two colors apart. - A thumb has a white ring with a dark line round it, so it shows on any color. - Typing something that isn't a color marks the field invalid. Leaving the field puts back the color it had. - Where the browser forces its own colors, the area, the hue track, the swatches and the thumbs keep theirs. They're what's being shown, and without them there'd be nothing to pick from. - The area and the hue aren't turned round in a right-to-left page, and their arrow keys go with what's drawn: Right is always more saturation. ### What you need to handle - Name the trigger: with `aria-label`, or with a label through a field. - Name each preset with `aria-label`, such as "Red". Without one its name is its hex, which says little to someone who can't see it. - Name the set of presets with `aria-label` on `ColorPickerSwatches`. - In another language, give the parts their words: `aria-label` on the content, the area, the hue and the field, and `getValueText` on the area. - The picker doesn't check that the color can be read against anything. If it's for text or for something text sits on, check the contrast yourself and say when it's too low. - Don't make the area the only way in. Someone who can't tell the colors apart, or can't see them, needs the field or named presets. ## On small screens The popover keeps to the screen, and the panel is as wide as it. A preset is 44 pixels square with a finger and 24 with a mouse. A drag in the area or along the hue moves the thumb and not the page. ## CSS variables Set any of these on a part, or on anything around it. A popover is drawn at the end of the page, so for one, set them on `ColorPickerContent`. ```css .brand-picker { --nuv-color-picker-area-height: 12rem; } ``` | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-color-picker-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 3)` | Space between the parts. | | `--nuv-color-picker-width` | `15rem` | Width of the panel. | | `--nuv-color-picker-trigger-border` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Color of the trigger's edge. | | `--nuv-color-picker-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius of the trigger and the area. | | `--nuv-color-picker-trigger-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background of the trigger. | | `--nuv-color-picker-color` | `transparent` | Set by the component: the color a swatch or a thumb shows. | | `--nuv-color-picker-area-height` | `10rem` | Height of the area. | | `--nuv-color-picker-hue` | `transparent` | Set by the component: the area's hue at full strength. | | `--nuv-color-picker-y` | `0%` | Set by the component: where the area's thumb is, down. | | `--nuv-color-picker-x` | `0%` | Set by the component: where the area's thumb is, across. | | `--nuv-color-picker-thumb-size` | `1.25rem` | Size of the two thumbs. | | `--nuv-color-picker-track-size` | `0.75rem` | Thickness of the hue track. | | `--nuv-color-picker-hues` | `none` | Set by the component: the gradient of the hue track. | | `--nuv-color-picker-swatch-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 2)` | Space between presets. | | `--nuv-color-picker-swatch-size` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `calc(var(--spacing) * 6)` | Size of a preset. Larger by default with a finger than with a mouse. | | `--nuv-color-picker-swatch-radius` | `var(--radius-sm)` | Corner radius of a preset. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-color-picker` | ColorPickerPanel | | `.nuv-color-picker__area` | ColorPickerArea | | `.nuv-color-picker__area-thumb` | The area's thumb. | | `.nuv-color-picker__content` | ColorPickerContent, with the popover's own class. | | `.nuv-color-picker__hue` | ColorPickerHue | | `.nuv-color-picker__hue-thumb` | The thumb of the hue slider. | | `.nuv-color-picker__hue-track` | The track of the hue slider. | | `.nuv-color-picker__input` | ColorPickerInput, with the input's own class. | | `.nuv-color-picker__swatch` | ColorPickerSwatch | | `.nuv-color-picker__swatches` | ColorPickerSwatches | | `.nuv-color-picker__trigger` | ColorPickerTrigger | | `.nuv-color-picker__trigger-swatch` | The swatch in the trigger. | | `.nuv-color-picker__value` | The color as text, in the trigger. | | `.nuv-color-picker__value--hidden` | The same, when the trigger shows something else: read and not drawn. | A disabled panel and area have `data-disabled`. ## Server components ColorPicker starts with `"use client"`: it keeps the color. You can render it from a server component as long as you leave out `onValueChange`, `onValueCommit` and `onOpenChange`, since a function can't be passed from the server. With `name`, a form still gets the color. ## Do and don't **Do** - Offer presets for the colors people most often want. Most never touch the area. - Save from `onValueCommit`, and preview from `onValueChange`. **Don't** - Don't use it to choose between a few named things. That's a [select](page:components/select) or a [radio group](page:components/radio-group), with the color as decoration. - Don't leave out both the field and the presets. The area alone can't be used without seeing it.

## Working with the color yourself

The functions the picker uses are exported too, for checking a color someone typed elsewhere or working out a shade.

```tsx
import { hexToHsv, hsvToHex, parseHex } from "@nuvui/react";
```

sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

There's no ARIA pattern for a color picker. Each part follows the pattern for what it is: a [slider](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/slider/) for the area and the hue, a text field, and buttons.

### Keyboard

| Where | Key | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The trigger | Enter, Space | Opens the popover. Escape closes it and focus goes back. |
| The area | Right, Left | More and less saturation, by 1. |
| The area | Up, Down | Lighter and darker, by 1. |
| The area | Shift and an arrow | By 10. |
| The area | Page Up, Page Down | Lighter and darker, by 10. |
| The area | Home, End | No saturation, and all of it. |
| The hue | Arrows | Round the hues, by 1 degree. Shift, Page Up and Page Down go by 10. |
| The hue | Home, End | The first hue and the last, which are both red. |
| The field | Enter | Takes what's typed as the color, if it is one. |
| A preset | Enter, Space | Picks it. |

Tab moves between the parts, in the order you wrote them.

### What the component handles

- The popover is a dialog with a name, "Color picker", which `aria-label` on `ColorPickerContent` changes.
- The area's thumb is a `slider` whose value is said in words: "Saturation 62%, brightness 80%". A slider has one value and this has two, so the words are where both are told.
- The trigger's color is its description, so a screen reader says it after the name, whatever the name comes from: `aria-label`, a `label`, or a field.
- The preset that's the color now has `aria-pressed="true"`, and a ring inside it that doesn't depend on telling two colors apart.
- A thumb has a white ring with a dark line round it, so it shows on any color.
- Typing something that isn't a color marks the field invalid. Leaving the field puts back the color it had.
- Where the browser forces its own colors, the area, the hue track, the swatches and the thumbs keep theirs. They're what's being shown, and without them there'd be nothing to pick from.
- The area and the hue aren't turned round in a right-to-left page, and their arrow keys go with what's drawn: Right is always more saturation.

### What you need to handle

- Name the trigger: with `aria-label`, or with a label through a field.
- Name each preset with `aria-label`, such as "Red". Without one its name is its hex, which says little to someone who can't see it.
- Name the set of presets with `aria-label` on `ColorPickerSwatches`.
- In another language, give the parts their words: `aria-label` on the content, the area, the hue and the field, and `getValueText` on the area.
- The picker doesn't check that the color can be read against anything. If it's for text or for something text sits on, check the contrast yourself and say when it's too low.
- Don't make the area the only way in. Someone who can't tell the colors apart, or can't see them, needs the field or named presets.

| `--nuv-color-picker-swatch-radius` | `var(--radius-sm)` | Corner radius of a preset. |
