sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

ColorPicker starts with `"use client"`: it keeps the color. You can render it from a server component as long as you leave out `onValueChange`, `onValueCommit` and `onOpenChange`, since a function can't be passed from the server. With `name`, a form still gets the color.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Offer presets for the colors people most often want. Most never touch the area.
- Save from `onValueCommit`, and preview from `onValueChange`.

**Don't**

- Don't use it to choose between a few named things. That's a [select](page:components/select) or a [radio group](page:components/radio-group), with the color as decoration.
- Don't leave out both the field and the presets. The area alone can't be used without seeing it.

pages.title: Combobox
pages.description: A select with a search field. It holds one value or several, filters as you type, and works with a label, the keyboard and forms.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import {
  Combobox,
  ComboboxContent,
  ComboboxEmpty,
  ComboboxItem,
  ComboboxTrigger,
  ComboboxValue,
} from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Combobox` | Holds the value and the open state. Renders nothing itself, apart from a hidden input when it has a `name`. |
| `ComboboxTrigger` | The control on the page. It shows the value and an arrow. |
| `ComboboxValue` | The text inside the trigger: what's picked, or the placeholder. |
| `ComboboxContent` | The popup. It holds the search field, and the list its children go in. |
| `ComboboxItem` | One option. |
| `ComboboxGroup` | Options that belong together, under a heading. |
| `ComboboxSeparator` | A line between groups. |
| `ComboboxEmpty` | What's shown while nothing matches. |
| `ComboboxLoading` | What's shown while the options are being fetched. |

These are separate exports, not properties of `Combobox`. `Combobox.Item` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

### Combobox

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `multiple` | `false` | `false` | Lets more than one option be picked. The value is then a list. |
| `value` | `string` |  | The picked option's value, when you control it. `""` is none. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | The option picked to begin with, when you don't control it. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void)` |  | Called with the new value when an option is picked. |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Whether the list is open, when you control it. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the list starts open, when you don't control it. |
| `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean) => void)` |  | Called when the list opens or closes. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the trigger. |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the value is sent under when a form is submitted. With `multiple`, each value is sent under it. |
| `form` | `string` |  | The `id` of the form the value belongs to, if it isn't inside it. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  |  |

With `multiple`, `value` and `defaultValue` are arrays of strings, and `onValueChange` is called with one.

### ComboboxValue

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placeholder` | `ReactNode` |  | What's shown while nothing is picked. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | What's shown for the picked value. Left out, it's the value itself, or with `multiple` the values with commas between them. |

### ComboboxContent

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `"Search"` | The search field's name, for screen readers. It names the popup as well, unless that has an `aria-label` of its own. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |
| `listLabel` | `string` | `"Options"` | The list's name, for screen readers. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |
| `searchPlaceholder` | `string` |  | The search field's placeholder. |
| `search` | `string` |  | What's typed in the search field, when you control it. |
| `onSearchChange` | `((search: string) => void)` |  | Called with the text when the search field changes. |
| `shouldFilter` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the list is filtered as you type. Turn it off when the options are fetched for each search, and already are the matches. |
| `filter` | `CommandFilter` | `comboboxFilter` | Scores an option against the search. Zero hides it, and options with a higher score come first. It's given the option's text as the first keyword. |
| `loop` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the arrow keys go round from the last option to the first. |
| `align` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start"` | `"start"` | Which edge of the trigger the list lines up with. |
| `sideOffset` | `number` | `6` | The gap between the trigger and the list, in pixels. |
| `collisionPadding` | `number \| Partial<Record<"bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top", number>>` | `8` | How close the list may get to the edge of the screen, in pixels. |
| `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the list is rendered into. Set this when the list should pick up a `data-theme` from a section of the page. |

It also takes what Radix's popover content takes, such as `side` and `onEscapeKeyDown`. The [Radix Popover reference](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/popover#content) lists them.

### ComboboxItem

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | What the option stands for. It's what `value` and `onValueChange` deal in, and it has to differ from every other option's. |
| `textValue` | `string` |  | The text the search looks through. Left out, it's the children when they're a string. Give it when they aren't. |
| `keywords` | `string[]` |  | Other words that should find this option. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the option can be picked. |
| `onSelect` | `((value: string) => void)` |  | Called with the option's value when it's picked. |

### ComboboxGroup

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `heading` | `ReactNode` |  | The text over the group's options. It also names the group. |

### ComboboxSeparator

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `alwaysRender` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the line stays while something is typed in the search field. Left off, it goes, because the groups it was between may have gone. |

### ComboboxLoading

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `"Loading"` | What a screen reader is told while this is shown, and what's drawn if there are no children. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |

`ComboboxTrigger` is a `button` and takes what a button takes. `ComboboxEmpty` is a `div`.

sections.heading: Values and what's shown for them
Several values
Groups
sections.markdown:
## Groups

```tsx
import {
  Combobox,
  ComboboxContent,
  ComboboxEmpty,
  ComboboxGroup,
  ComboboxItem,
  ComboboxSeparator,
  ComboboxTrigger,
  ComboboxValue,
} from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Combobox>
      <ComboboxTrigger aria-label="Assignee">
        <ComboboxValue placeholder="Assign to" />
      </ComboboxTrigger>
      <ComboboxContent label="Search people" searchPlaceholder="Search">
        <ComboboxEmpty>Nobody by that name.</ComboboxEmpty>
        <ComboboxGroup heading="Design">
          <ComboboxItem value="Ada Okafor">Ada Okafor</ComboboxItem>
          <ComboboxItem value="Mei Tanaka">Mei Tanaka</ComboboxItem>
        </ComboboxGroup>
        <ComboboxSeparator />
        <ComboboxGroup heading="Engineering">
          <ComboboxItem value="José Álvarez">José Álvarez</ComboboxItem>
          <ComboboxItem value="Priya Nair">Priya Nair</ComboboxItem>
          <ComboboxItem value="Tom Becker" disabled>
            Tom Becker
          </ComboboxItem>
        </ComboboxGroup>
      </ComboboxContent>
    </Combobox>
  );
}
```

A group whose options have all been filtered out goes with them. The separators go while there's something in the search field, because the groups they were between may have gone.

sections.heading: How the search matches
Options from a server
In a form
Width
sections.markdown:
## Width

The trigger is at least 12rem wide and grows with the text in it, up to the width of its container. Set `--nuv-combobox-width: 100%` to make it fill the container.

A value that's still too long is cut short with an ellipsis. The popup is at least as wide as the trigger.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

The trigger is 44 pixels tall on a touch screen and 40 with a mouse. Options are 44 and 32. The search field's text is 16 pixels on a touch screen, because iOS zooms the page in when a field with smaller text takes focus.

The popup is never taller than the room around the trigger, and the list scrolls inside it under the search field. On a phone the keyboard comes up once the field has focus and covers part of the screen, so less of the list shows there. That's the price of a search field, and a reason to use a [native select](page:components/native-select) for a short list on a form that's mostly filled in on phones.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>, <kbd>Space</kbd>, <kbd>↓</kbd> or <kbd>↑</kbd> | On the trigger, opens the list with focus in the search field. |
| Typing | Filters the list. The first match becomes the active option. |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> and <kbd>↑</kbd> | Move to the next or previous option. Disabled options are skipped. |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> | Move to the first or last option. They don't move the caret in the search field. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Picks the active option. With one value that closes the list. With `multiple` it stays open. |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Closes the list and keeps the value it had. |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Closes the list and puts focus back on the trigger. The next <kbd>Tab</kbd> moves on from there. |

### What the component handles

- The trigger has `role="combobox"`, with `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup="dialog"`. A plain button that's named by a label loses its own text to a screen reader. With this role the label is the name and the text is the value, the way a select is read.
- The popup is a dialog that holds the search field and the list. The field has `role="combobox"` and controls the list, which has `role="listbox"`. Each group is named by its heading.
- Focus stays in the search field. The field's `aria-activedescendant` says which option the arrow keys are on, and that option has `aria-selected`. The library that does the filtering, cmdk, leaves that attribute empty until an arrow key is pressed. This component keeps it right from the moment the list opens.
- The picked option has `aria-checked`. With `multiple`, every option says whether it's checked.
- When nothing matches, the text of `ComboboxEmpty` is put in a status region next to the list, so a screen reader says it. The copy that's drawn inside the list is hidden from screen readers, because a list of options may only hold options. `ComboboxLoading` works the same way.
- The active option is filled with the primary color. That fill has at least 3:1 contrast with the popup, and the text on it keeps 4.5:1. Where the browser forces its own colors, as Windows high contrast does, the option has an outline instead.
- The search field shows that it has focus with a line in the ring color along the bottom of its row.
- <kbd>Tab</kbd> closes the list. The popup is rendered at the end of the page, so without that, the next stop would be the browser's own buttons.
- The popup only animates when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion.

### What you need to handle

- Give the trigger a name. Use a `<label>` whose `htmlFor` matches the trigger's `id`, a [field](page:components/field), or `aria-label`.
- Don't use the placeholder as the label. It goes away once something is picked.
- `label` on `ComboboxContent` names the search field, and the popup too. Give the popup an `aria-label` of its own, such as the field's name, if hearing "Search" twice isn't what you want.
- Translate `label`, `listLabel` and the text of `ComboboxEmpty` and `ComboboxLoading` with the rest of your interface.
- When the value is wrong, set `aria-invalid` on the trigger and say what's wrong in text. A field does both.

### What hasn't been checked

The tests check the roles, names and states that a browser passes on to a screen reader. What each screen reader then says hasn't been checked by a person. `aria-checked` on an option is in the ARIA standard, and screen readers differ in how they read it.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

The trigger sits in the page, so its variables can be set on it or on anything around it. The popup renders at the end of `<body>`, so set the others on `:root` or `body`, or straight on `ComboboxContent`.

```css
.filters {
  --nuv-combobox-width: 100%;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-combobox-width` | `12rem` | The narrowest the trigger gets. Set it to 100% to fill the container. |
| `--nuv-combobox-border` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Border color of the trigger. |
| `--nuv-combobox-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius of the trigger. |
| `--nuv-combobox-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of the trigger. |
| `--nuv-combobox-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Text color of the trigger once something is picked. |
| `--nuv-combobox-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-md)` | Minimum height of the trigger. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. |
| `--nuv-combobox-content-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Border color of the popup, and the color of the lines inside it. |
| `--nuv-combobox-content-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of the popup. |
| `--nuv-combobox-content-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of the popup. |
| `--nuv-combobox-content-shadow` | `var(--shadow-lg)` | Shadow under the popup. |
| `--nuv-combobox-content-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color of the popup. |
| `--nuv-combobox-input-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-md)` | Minimum height of the search field. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. |
| `--nuv-combobox-input-font-size` | `var(--text-base)`, `var(--text-sm)` | Size of the search field's text. Keep it at 16 pixels or more on touch screens. |
| `--nuv-combobox-input-placeholder` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the search field's placeholder. |
| `--nuv-combobox-list-height` | `18rem` | The tallest the list gets before it scrolls. It's shorter when there's less room. |
| `--nuv-combobox-item-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-sm)` | Minimum height of an option. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. |
| `--nuv-combobox-highlight-bg` | `var(--color-primary)` | Background of the active option, from the pointer or the arrow keys. Keep it at 3:1 against the popup. |
| `--nuv-combobox-highlight-fg` | `var(--color-primary-foreground)` | Text color of that option. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-combobox` | ComboboxTrigger. |
| `.nuv-combobox__body` | The element inside the popup that holds the search field and the list. |
| `.nuv-combobox__content` | ComboboxContent, the popup. |
| `.nuv-combobox__empty` | ComboboxEmpty. |
| `.nuv-combobox__icon` | The arrow in the trigger. |
| `.nuv-combobox__indicator` | The check at the end of a picked option. |
| `.nuv-combobox__input` | The search field. |
| `.nuv-combobox__item` | ComboboxItem. |
| `.nuv-combobox__label` | A group's heading. |
| `.nuv-combobox__list` | The part that scrolls, with the options in it. |
| `.nuv-combobox__loading` | ComboboxLoading. |
| `.nuv-combobox__search` | The row the search field is in. |
| `.nuv-combobox__search-icon` | The magnifying glass in that row. |
| `.nuv-combobox__separator` | ComboboxSeparator. |
| `.nuv-combobox__status` | The region a screen reader hears "no results" and "loading" from. It isn't drawn. |
| `.nuv-combobox__value` | ComboboxValue. It's what cuts a long value short. |

The trigger has `data-state`, which is `open` or `closed`, and its value part has `data-placeholder` while nothing is picked. An option has `data-selected="true"` while it's the active one, `data-state`, which is `checked` or `unchecked`, and `data-disabled="true"` when it can't be picked.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

The combobox parts are client components. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files.

You can put a combobox together inside a server component, as the first example on this page does. It only needs a client component of your own when you control `value` or `search`, or pass a function such as `onValueChange` or `filter`.

sections.heading: Themed sections
sections.markdown:
## Themed sections

A popup opened from inside a `data-theme="dark"` section doesn't inherit that theme, because it isn't rendered inside the section. Pass the section's element as `container` to `ComboboxContent` and it will be.

sections.heading: What it's built on
sections.markdown:
## What it's built on

The list and its filtering are [cmdk](https://github.com/pacocoursey/cmdk), and the popup is Radix's popover. Both are installed with the library. Radix has no combobox of its own.

Four things are done differently from cmdk on its own. The active option is always announced. The match is on letters in a row and not on scattered ones. The separator is hidden from screen readers. And a screen reader is told when nothing matches. The [command](page:components/command) page says more about the first.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Put a visible label above or beside it.
- Order the options in a way people can predict: alphabetical, or most used first.
- Write `ComboboxEmpty` so that it says what wasn't found: "No customer found", not "No results".

**Don't**

- Don't use one for a handful of options. A [select](page:components/select) or a [radio group](page:components/radio-group) is quicker.
- Don't use one for actions. That's a [command](page:components/command) palette or a [dropdown menu](page:components/dropdown-menu).
- Don't put thousands of options in it. Fetch the matches as the person types.

pages.title: Command
pages.description: A search field over a list of commands that filters as you type, in the page or in a dialog opened with a shortcut.
pages.markdown:
# Command A search field over a list of commands that filters as you type, in the page or in a dialog opened with a shortcut. Use a command list to let people find something by typing a few letters of its name: a page to go to, an action to run, a record to open. In a dialog that opens with a shortcut it's what's often called a command palette. To pick a value for a form, use a [combobox](page:components/combobox). It's the same list behind a button, with a value it remembers. ```tsx import { Command, CommandEmpty, CommandGroup, CommandInput, CommandItem, CommandList, CommandSeparator, CommandShortcut, } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return ( No commands found. New file Ctrl+N Open file Ctrl+O Save a copy Toggle theme Zoom in Zoom out ); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Command, CommandDialog, CommandEmpty, CommandGroup, CommandInput, CommandItem, CommandList, } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `Command` | The box around the field and the list. It does the filtering and holds which item is active. | | `CommandDialog` | A `Command` in a dialog, with an optional shortcut that opens it. | | `CommandInput` | The search field. | | `CommandList` | The part that scrolls, with the items in it. | | `CommandItem` | One command. | | `CommandGroup` | Items that belong together, under a heading. | | `CommandSeparator` | A line between groups. | | `CommandShortcut` | The keys that do the same thing, shown at the end of an item's row. | | `CommandEmpty` | What's shown while nothing matches. | | `CommandLoading` | What's shown while the items are being fetched. | These are separate exports, not properties of `Command`. `Command.Item` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component. ## Props ### Command | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `label` | `string` | `"Search"` | The search field's name, for screen readers. Translate it with the rest of your interface. | | `shouldFilter` | `boolean` | | Whether the list is filtered as you type. Turn it off when the items are fetched for each search, and already are the matches. | | `filter` | `CommandFilter` | | Scores an item against the search. It's called with the item's value, the search and the item's keywords. Zero hides the item, and items with a higher score come first. | | `loop` | `boolean` | | Whether the arrow keys go round from the last item to the first. | | `vimBindings` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether Ctrl+N, Ctrl+J, Ctrl+P and Ctrl+K move through the list as the arrow keys do. Off by default, because in a text field on a Mac some of those keys already do something else. | | `value` | `string` | | The value of the active item, when you control it yourself. Use it with `onValueChange`. | | `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void)` | | Called with an item's value when it becomes the active one. | ### CommandDialog | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `open` | `boolean` | | Whether the dialog is open, when you control it. | | `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the dialog starts open, when you don't control it. | | `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean) => void)` | | Called when the dialog opens or closes. | | `shortcut` | `string \| null` | | A key that opens and closes the dialog when pressed with Ctrl, or with Command on a Mac. `"k"` is the usual one. Left out, there's no shortcut. | | `title` | `string` | `"Command palette"` | The dialog's name, for screen readers. It isn't drawn. Translate it with the rest of your interface. | | `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the dialog is rendered into. Set this when the dialog should pick up a `data-theme` from a section of the page. | It takes everything `Command` does as well, and passes it on. ### CommandInput | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `placeholder` | `string` | | What the field shows while it's empty. | | `value` | `string` | | The search text, when you control it yourself. Use it with `onValueChange`. | | `onValueChange` | `((search: string) => void)` | | Called with the text when it changes. | ### CommandItem | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `onSelect` | `((value: string) => void)` | | Called with the item's value when it's run, by a click or by Enter. | | `value` | `string` | | What the search matches against, and what `onSelect` is called with. Left out, it's the item's text. It has to differ from every other item's. | | `keywords` | `string[]` | | Other words that should find this item. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | | Stops the item from being run. The arrow keys skip it. | ### CommandList | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `label` | `string` | `"Suggestions"` | The list's name, for screen readers. Translate it with the rest of your interface. | ### CommandGroup | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `heading` | `ReactNode` | | The text over the group's items. It also names the group. | ### CommandSeparator | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `alwaysRender` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the line stays while something is typed in the search field. sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import {
  Command,
  CommandDialog,
  CommandEmpty,
  CommandGroup,
  CommandInput,
  CommandItem,
  CommandList,
} from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Command` | The box around the field and the list. It does the filtering and holds which item is active. |
| `CommandDialog` | A `Command` in a dialog, with an optional shortcut that opens it. |
| `CommandInput` | The search field. |
| `CommandList` | The part that scrolls, with the items in it. |
| `CommandItem` | One command. |
| `CommandGroup` | Items that belong together, under a heading. |
| `CommandSeparator` | A line between groups. |
| `CommandShortcut` | The keys that do the same thing, shown at the end of an item's row. |
| `CommandEmpty` | What's shown while nothing matches. |
| `CommandLoading` | What's shown while the items are being fetched. |

These are separate exports, not properties of `Command`. `Command.Item` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

### Command

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `"Search"` | The search field's name, for screen readers. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |
| `shouldFilter` | `boolean` |  | Whether the list is filtered as you type. Turn it off when the items are fetched for each search, and already are the matches. |
| `filter` | `CommandFilter` |  | Scores an item against the search. It's called with the item's value, the search and the item's keywords. Zero hides the item, and items with a higher score come first. |
| `loop` | `boolean` |  | Whether the arrow keys go round from the last item to the first. |
| `vimBindings` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether Ctrl+N, Ctrl+J, Ctrl+P and Ctrl+K move through the list as the arrow keys do. Off by default, because in a text field on a Mac some of those keys already do something else. |
| `value` | `string` |  | The value of the active item, when you control it yourself. Use it with `onValueChange`. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void)` |  | Called with an item's value when it becomes the active one. |

### CommandDialog

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Whether the dialog is open, when you control it. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the dialog starts open, when you don't control it. |
| `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean) => void)` |  | Called when the dialog opens or closes. |
| `shortcut` | `string \| null` |  | A key that opens and closes the dialog when pressed with Ctrl, or with Command on a Mac. `"k"` is the usual one. Left out, there's no shortcut. |
| `title` | `string` | `"Command palette"` | The dialog's name, for screen readers. It isn't drawn. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |
| `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the dialog is rendered into. Set this when the dialog should pick up a `data-theme` from a section of the page. |

It takes everything `Command` does as well, and passes it on.

### CommandInput

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  | What the field shows while it's empty. |
| `value` | `string` |  | The search text, when you control it yourself. Use it with `onValueChange`. |
| `onValueChange` | `((search: string) => void)` |  | Called with the text when it changes. |

### CommandItem

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onSelect` | `((value: string) => void)` |  | Called with the item's value when it's run, by a click or by Enter. |
| `value` | `string` |  | What the search matches against, and what `onSelect` is called with. Left out, it's the item's text. It has to differ from every other item's. |
| `keywords` | `string[]` |  | Other words that should find this item. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Stops the item from being run. The arrow keys skip it. |

### CommandList

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `"Suggestions"` | The list's name, for screen readers. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |

### CommandGroup

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `heading` | `ReactNode` |  | The text over the group's items. It also names the group. |

### CommandSeparator

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `alwaysRender` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the line stays while something is typed in the search field. Left off, it goes, because the groups it was between may have gone. |

### CommandLoading

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `"Loading"` | What a screen reader is told while this is shown, and what's drawn if there are no children. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |

`CommandEmpty` is a `div` and `CommandShortcut` is a `span`. They take what those elements take.

sections.heading: In a dialog
Shortcuts next to items
sections.markdown:
## Shortcuts next to items

`CommandShortcut` shows the keys at the end of a row. It only shows them. Listening for the keys is up to you.

It's hidden from screen readers, so that "New file" isn't read as "New file Ctrl+N" with no pause. Put the same keys in `aria-keyshortcuts` on the item, and they're announced as a shortcut.

sections.heading: How the search matches
sections.markdown:
## How the search matches

The match is loose: the letters you type have to appear in the item in that order, and don't have to be next to each other. `stg` finds Settings. Items that match better come first, so the order of the list changes as you type.

That suits a list of commands, where people type as little as they can. It's the opposite choice from [Combobox](page:components/combobox#how-the-search-matches), which keeps its options in order and only matches letters in a row.

`keywords` adds other words that should find an item. The first example finds "Toggle theme" when you type `dark`.

sections.heading: Items from a server
On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

Items are 44 pixels tall on a touch screen and 32 with a mouse. The search field is 44 and 40, and its text is 16 pixels on a touch screen, because iOS zooms the page in when a field with smaller text takes focus.

On a phone the dialog sits at the top of the screen, 16 pixels in from each edge, and not at the bottom the way a [dialog](page:components/dialog) does. The field is the first thing in it, and the keyboard comes up from the bottom. From the `sm` breakpoint it's 36rem wide and sits towards the top, so the list can grow and shrink under the field without the field moving.

The list is at most 20rem tall and scrolls inside itself.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Typing | Filters the list. The best match becomes the active item. |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> and <kbd>↑</kbd> | Move to the next or previous item. Disabled items are skipped. |
| <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>↓</kbd> and <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>↑</kbd> | Move to the first item of the next or previous group. |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> | Move to the first or last item. They don't move the caret in the search field. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Runs the active item. |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | In a dialog, closes it. |
| The `shortcut` | Opens and closes a `CommandDialog`. |

### What the component handles

- The search field has `role="combobox"` and controls the list, which has `role="listbox"`. Items have `role="option"`, and each group is named by its heading.
- Focus stays in the field. Its `aria-activedescendant` says which item the arrow keys are on, and that item has `aria-selected`.
- cmdk, the library underneath, works that attribute out a moment too early. On its own it leaves the attribute empty when the list first shows and after each letter typed, and after a letter is erased it names an item that's no longer the active one. A screen reader would then say nothing, or the wrong thing, about what <kbd>Enter</kbd> is about to run. This component watches which item is marked active and keeps the attribute pointing at it. A test goes through each of those steps.
- When nothing matches, the text of `CommandEmpty` is put in a status region next to the list, so a screen reader says it. The copy that's drawn inside the list is hidden from screen readers, because a list of options may only hold options. `CommandLoading` works the same way.
- cmdk's separator has `role="separator"`, which a list of options isn't allowed to hold. This component's separator is decoration and hidden from screen readers. Groups are told apart by their headings.
- The active item is filled with the primary color. That fill has at least 3:1 contrast with the panel, and the text on it keeps 4.5:1. Where the browser forces its own colors, as Windows high contrast does, the item has an outline instead.
- The search field shows that it has focus with a line in the ring color along the bottom of its row.
- The dialog has a name that isn't drawn, set with `title`. Opening it moves focus to the field. Closing it gives focus back to whatever had it before.
- The dialog only animates when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion.

### What you need to handle

- Give people another way in. A shortcut nobody has been told about isn't found, and a phone has no <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> key. A button that opens the palette covers both.
- Don't make the palette the only way to reach something. It's a quicker route to what's also in the menus.
- Translate `label`, `title`, the list's `label` and the text of `CommandEmpty` and `CommandLoading` with the rest of your interface.
- Safari doesn't give a button focus when it's clicked. So after a palette that was opened by a click there closes, focus isn't on the button. Opened from the keyboard, focus goes back where it was.

### What hasn't been checked

The tests check the roles, names and states that a browser passes on to a screen reader. What each screen reader then says hasn't been checked by a person.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

A `Command` in the page takes its variables from itself or anything around it. One in a `CommandDialog` renders at the end of `<body>`, so set them on `:root` or `body`.

```css
:root {
  --nuv-command-width: 40rem;
  --nuv-command-list-height: 24rem;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-command-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of the panel, and of the dialog. |
| `--nuv-command-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of the panel. |
| `--nuv-command-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color of the panel. |
| `--nuv-command-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of the dialog's edge, and of the lines inside the panel. |
| `--nuv-command-input-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-md)` | Minimum height of the search field. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. |
| `--nuv-command-input-font-size` | `var(--text-base)`, `var(--text-sm)` | Size of the search field's text. Keep it at 16 pixels or more on touch screens. |
| `--nuv-command-input-placeholder` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the search field's placeholder. |
| `--nuv-command-list-height` | `20rem` | The tallest the list gets before it scrolls. |
| `--nuv-command-item-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-sm)` | Minimum height of an item. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. |
| `--nuv-command-highlight-bg` | `var(--color-primary)` | Background of the active item, from the pointer or the arrow keys. Keep it at 3:1 against the panel. |
| `--nuv-command-highlight-fg` | `var(--color-primary-foreground)` | Text color of that item. |
| `--nuv-command-overlay-bg` | `var(--color-overlay)` | Color of the layer that dims the page. |
| `--nuv-command-shadow` | `var(--shadow-xl)` | Shadow under the dialog. |
| `--nuv-command-width` | `36rem` | The widest the dialog gets, from the sm breakpoint up. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-command` | Command. |
| `.nuv-command__dialog` | The dialog around the Command. |
| `.nuv-command__empty` | CommandEmpty. |
| `.nuv-command__input` | CommandInput. |
| `.nuv-command__item` | CommandItem. |
| `.nuv-command__label` | A group's heading. |
| `.nuv-command__list` | CommandList. |
| `.nuv-command__loading` | CommandLoading. |
| `.nuv-command__overlay` | The layer that dims the page behind a CommandDialog. |
| `.nuv-command__search` | The row the search field is in. |
| `.nuv-command__search-icon` | The magnifying glass in that row. |
| `.nuv-command__separator` | CommandSeparator. |
| `.nuv-command__shortcut` | CommandShortcut. |
| `.nuv-command__status` | The region a screen reader hears "no results" and "loading" from. It isn't drawn. |
| `.nuv-command__title` | The dialog's name. It isn't drawn. |

An item has `data-selected="true"` while it's the active one, and `data-disabled="true"` when it can't be run. The dialog and its overlay have `data-state`, which is `open` or `closed`.

The panel has no edge of its own, so that it can sit inside a card or a popover without doubling one. The examples on this page that show it in the page give it a border.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

The command parts are client components. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files.

The parts can be put together inside a server component, as the first example is. An `onSelect` is a function, so a list that runs things needs a client component of your own.

sections.heading: Themed sections
sections.markdown:
## Themed sections

A `CommandDialog` opened from inside a `data-theme="dark"` section doesn't inherit that theme, because it isn't rendered inside the section. Pass the section's element as `container` and it will be.

sections.heading: What it's built on
sections.markdown:
## What it's built on

The filtering and the keyboard handling are [cmdk](https://github.com/pacocoursey/cmdk), and the dialog is Radix's. Both are installed with the library.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Name commands by what they do, starting with a verb: "Create an order", not "Orders".
- Group them, and put what people reach for most at the top.
- Show the shortcut that opens the palette somewhere people will see it.

**Don't**

- Don't put a form's fields in one. Use a [combobox](page:components/combobox) for a value.
- Don't keep the palette open after a command that changes the page. People lose track of what happened behind it.
- Don't put thousands of items in it. Fetch the matches as the person types.

pages.title: Compare
pages.description: Two pictures of the same thing, before and after, in one box. A divider dragged by its handle shows part of each, or a switch shows one at a time.
pages.markdown:
# Compare Two pictures of the same thing, before and after, in one box. A divider dragged by its handle shows part of each, or a switch shows one at a time. Use a compare to show what changed: a room before and after it was redone, a photo before and after it was edited, a screen of your app before and after a redesign. Both pictures are drawn in the same box. A divider shows before on one side of it and after on the other, and it's dragged by its handle. ```tsx import { Compare } from "@nuvui/react"; import { kitchenAfter, kitchenBefore } from "./pictures"; export default function Example() { return (
} after={ } />
); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Compare } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `before` (required) | `ReactNode` | | What it looked like before, such as an `img` with its own `alt`. | | `after` (required) | `ReactNode` | | What it looks like after. Both are drawn in the same box. | | `mode` | `"slider" \| "toggle"` | `"slider"` | `"slider"` shows both, split by a divider that's dragged by its handle. `"toggle"` shows one at a time, with a switch under it. | | `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Which way the divider moves. `"horizontal"` puts before at the start of the line and after at the end. `"vertical"` puts before on top. | | `position` | `number` | | How much of before shows, from 0 to 100, when you control it. In `"slider"` mode only. | | `defaultPosition` | `number` | `50` | How much of before shows at first, when you don't control it. | | `onPositionChange` | `((position: number) => void)` | | Called with the new position while the divider moves. | | `step` | `number` | `1` | How far one arrow key moves the divider. Page Up and Page Down move it ten times as far. | | `shown` | `"after" \| "before"` | | Which one shows, when you control it. In `"toggle"` mode only. | | `defaultShown` | `"after" \| "before"` | `"before"` | Which one shows at first, when you don't control it. | | `onShownChange` | `((shown: CompareSide) => void)` | | Called with the one that was chosen. | | `beforeLabel` | `string` | `"Before"` | The name of before, on the picture and on its switch. Translate it with the rest of your interface. | | `afterLabel` | `string` | `"After"` | The name of after, on the picture and on its switch. | | `labels` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows the two names on the picture. The switch in `"toggle"` mode shows them either way. | | `dividerLabel` | `string` | `"Before and after"` | Accessible name of the divider, which a screen reader reads as a slider. | | `valueLabel` | `((position: number, before: string, after: string) => string)` | `(position, before, after) => '${position}% ${before}, ${100 - position}% ${after}'` | What a screen reader says the position is. | | `switchLabel` | `string` | `"Show"` | Accessible name of the switch in `"toggle"` mode. | It's a `div`, and takes what a `div` takes, including `ref` and `className`. ## The pictures `before` and `after` take anything: an `img`, a `picture`, a `video`, or markup of your own. An `img` or a `video` fills the box and is cropped to it, as with `object-fit: cover`. Give each its own `alt`, which says what it shows, since the two are read one after the other. The box is as tall as `after` is. For a shape of your own, set `--nuv-compare-ratio`, and both pictures are cropped to it: ```css .kitchen { --nuv-compare-ratio: 16 / 9; } ``` Use two pictures of the same size, taken from the same place. The divider only reads as a change if what doesn't change lines up. ## The divider The divider moves only when it's dragged: by its handle, or by the line anywhere along its length. A drag anywhere else on the picture is the page's, so on a phone a finger on the picture scrolls the page as it does everywhere else. The line is as wide as a finger to take hold of, though it's drawn thinner. A picture in the box can't be picked up and dragged out of it, as a browser lets an image be, since a press on it was most likely meant for the divider. `position` is how much of before shows, from 0 to 100. Leave it out and the divider starts at `defaultPosition`, which is 50. Set it, with `onPositionChange`, to move the divider from your own controls: ```tsx "use client"; import { Button, ButtonGroup, Compare } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; import { kitchenAfter, kitchenBefore } from "./pictures"; export default function Example() { const [position, setPosition] = useState(50); return (
} after={ } />

{Math.round(position)}% before

); } ``` ## Vertical With `orientation="vertical"`, before is on top and after below, and the divider moves up and down. ```tsx import { Compare } from "@nuvui/react"; import { dashboardAfter, dashboardBefore } from "./pictures"; export default function Example() { return (
} after={ } />
); } ``` ## A switch With `mode="toggle"`, there's no divider. One picture shows at a time, with a switch under it to choose the other, and the change wipes across from one to the other. It's for pictures where a half of each says little, and for anyone who finds dragging hard. `shown`, `defaultShown` and `onShownChange` work as `position` does. ```tsx import { Compare } from "@nuvui/react"; import { kitchenAfter, kitchenBefore } from "./pictures"; export default function Example() { return (
} after={ } />
); } ``` The picture a switch hides is hidden from screen readers too, and nothing in it can take focus. ## Right to left On a right-to-left page, before is on the right and after on the left, the start and end of the line there. The left arrow key moves the divider left, as it points, which shows more of before. ## Names "Before" and "After" are drawn on the picture, and are the names on the switch. Change them with `beforeLabel` and `afterLabel`, to translate them or to say something closer to what's shown, such as "Old" and "New". `labels={false}` takes them off the picture. The switch keeps them. ## Accessibility ### Keyboard | Key | What it does | | --- | --- | | Tab | Moves focus to the divider. | | ← and → | Move a divider that goes across by one step, the way the arrow points. Move a divider that goes up and down by one step, right for more of before. | | ↑ and ↓ | Move a divider that goes up and down by one step, the way the arrow points. Move a divider that goes across by one step, up for more of before. | | Page Up and Page Down | Move it by ten steps, more of before and less. | | Home and End | Show all of after, or all of before. | In `mode="toggle"`, the switch is a group of two radio buttons: Tab reaches the chosen one, and the arrow keys choose the other. ### What the component handles - The divider has `role="slider"`, a name, `aria-valuenow` from 0 to 100, and `aria-orientation`. A screen reader says how much of each shows, such as "40% Before, 60% After". - Both pictures are in the page and in the order a screen reader reads them, with their names on them. - The handle is 44 by 44 pixels, and the line can be taken anywhere along its length at the same width. Only the divider takes a drag, so the rest of the picture scrolls the page. - Keyboard focus shows a 2 pixel ring around the handle. - The names are white on a dark backing that reaches 4.5:1 over any picture. - Where the browser forces its own colors, the line is drawn in the text color, the handle gets an edge, and the names a backing in the page's colors. - For a visitor who asked for less motion, the switch changes the picture at once, without the wipe. ### What you need to handle - Write an `alt` for each picture that says what it shows, so the two can be told apart without seeing them. - Say in words what changed, near the pictures, if the change is the point. A screen reader user can't see a difference that's only in the picture. - Translate the names, `dividerLabel` and `valueLabel` with the rest of your interface. ## CSS variables Set any of these on the `Compare`, or on anything around it. ```css .kitchen { --nuv-compare-radius: 0; --nuv-compare-ratio: 4 / 3; } ``` | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-compare-gap` | `0.75rem` | Space between the picture and the switch. | | `--nuv-compare-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | How round the picture's corners are. | | `--nuv-compare-ratio` | `auto` | The shape of the box, such as 16 / 9. By default it's as tall as after. | | `--nuv-compare-fit` | `cover` | How an img or video fills the box: cover, the default, crops it; contain shows all of it. | | `--nuv-compare-position` | `50%` | Where the divider is, as a percentage. The component writes this. Don't set it. | | `--nuv-compare-label-inset` | `0.75rem` | How far a name is from the edges. | | `--nuv-compare-label-bg` | `color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-black) 65%, transparent)` | The backing behind a name on the picture. | | `--nuv-compare-label-fg` | `var(--color-white)` | The color of a name on the picture. | | `--nuv-compare-line-width` | `2px` | How thick the divider's line is drawn. | | `--nuv-compare-line` | `var(--color-white)` | The color of the divider's line. | | `--nuv-compare-handle-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | How round the handle's corners are. | | `--nuv-compare-handle-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | The handle's background. | | `--nuv-compare-handle-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | The color of the arrows on the handle. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-compare` | Compare. | | `.nuv-compare--toggle` | One picture at a time, with a switch. | | `.nuv-compare--vertical` | A divider that moves up and down. | | `.nuv-compare__divider` | The divider, as wide as a finger. Its line is drawn by `::before`. | | `.nuv-compare__frame` | The box the pictures are drawn in. | | `.nuv-compare__handle` | The handle in the middle of the divider. | | `.nuv-compare__icon` | The arrows on the handle. | | `.nuv-compare__label` | A name on the picture. | | `.nuv-compare__label--after` | After's name. | | `.nuv-compare__label--before` | Before's name. | | `.nuv-compare__layer` | Around one picture. | | `.nuv-compare__layer--before` | Around before, which lies over after and is cut off at the divider. | Three more have no styles of their own, and are there for yours: `nuv-compare--horizontal` on the root, `nuv-compare__layer--after` around after, and `nuv-compare__switch` on the switch, a [ToggleGroup](page:components/toggle-group). The mode and the direction are also in `data-mode` and `data-orientation` attributes on the root. ## Content Security Policy Where the divider is, is a `style` attribute in the page from the server. Under a policy without `style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'`, the divider is in the middle until the page's script runs, whatever `defaultPosition` says, and where it should be from then on. The [Content Security Policy](page:content-security-policy) page has the details. ## Server components Compare starts with `"use client"`: it follows the pointer and the keys. A server component can render it with pictures it wrote, as long as it passes no functions, such as `onPositionChange` or `valueLabel`. ## Do and don't **Do** - Use two pictures taken from the same place, the same size. - Say what changed in words as well. **Don't** - Don't compare two different things. It's for one thing that changed. - Don't put text that has to be read across the divider. Half of it is in each picture.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `before` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | What it looked like before, such as an `img` with its own `alt`. |
| `after` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | What it looks like after. Both are drawn in the same box. |
| `mode` | `"slider" \| "toggle"` | `"slider"` | `"slider"` shows both, split by a divider that's dragged by its handle. `"toggle"` shows one at a time, with a switch under it. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Which way the divider moves. `"horizontal"` puts before at the start of the line and after at the end. `"vertical"` puts before on top. |
| `position` | `number` |  | How much of before shows, from 0 to 100, when you control it. In `"slider"` mode only. |
| `defaultPosition` | `number` | `50` | How much of before shows at first, when you don't control it. |
| `onPositionChange` | `((position: number) => void)` |  | Called with the new position while the divider moves. |
| `step` | `number` | `1` | How far one arrow key moves the divider. Page Up and Page Down move it ten times as far. |
| `shown` | `"after" \| "before"` |  | Which one shows, when you control it. In `"toggle"` mode only. |
| `defaultShown` | `"after" \| "before"` | `"before"` | Which one shows at first, when you don't control it. |
| `onShownChange` | `((shown: CompareSide) => void)` |  | Called with the one that was chosen. |
| `beforeLabel` | `string` | `"Before"` | The name of before, on the picture and on its switch. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |
| `afterLabel` | `string` | `"After"` | The name of after, on the picture and on its switch. |
| `labels` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows the two names on the picture. The switch in `"toggle"` mode shows them either way. |
| `dividerLabel` | `string` | `"Before and after"` | Accessible name of the divider, which a screen reader reads as a slider. |
| `valueLabel` | `((position: number, before: string, after: string) => string)` | `(position, before, after) => '${position}% ${before}, ${100 - position}% ${after}'` | What a screen reader says the position is. |
| `switchLabel` | `string` | `"Show"` | Accessible name of the switch in `"toggle"` mode. |

It's a `div`, and takes what a `div` takes, including `ref` and `className`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves focus to the divider. |
| <kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd> | Move a divider that goes across by one step, the way the arrow points. Move a divider that goes up and down by one step, right for more of before. |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd> | Move a divider that goes up and down by one step, the way the arrow points. Move a divider that goes across by one step, up for more of before. |
| <kbd>Page Up</kbd> and <kbd>Page Down</kbd> | Move it by ten steps, more of before and less. |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> | Show all of after, or all of before. |

In `mode="toggle"`, the switch is a group of two radio buttons: <kbd>Tab</kbd> reaches the chosen one, and the arrow keys choose the other.

### What the component handles

- The divider has `role="slider"`, a name, `aria-valuenow` from 0 to 100, and `aria-orientation`. A screen reader says how much of each shows, such as "40% Before, 60% After".
- Both pictures are in the page and in the order a screen reader reads them, with their names on them.
- The handle is 44 by 44 pixels, and the line can be taken anywhere along its length at the same width. Only the divider takes a drag, so the rest of the picture scrolls the page.
- Keyboard focus shows a 2 pixel ring around the handle.
- The names are white on a dark backing that reaches 4.5:1 over any picture.
- Where the browser forces its own colors, the line is drawn in the text color, the handle gets an edge, and the names a backing in the page's colors.
- For a visitor who asked for less motion, the switch changes the picture at once, without the wipe.

### What you need to handle

- Write an `alt` for each picture that says what it shows, so the two can be told apart without seeing them.
- Say in words what changed, near the pictures, if the change is the point. A screen reader user can't see a difference that's only in the picture.
- Translate the names, `dividerLabel` and `valueLabel` with the rest of your interface.

pages.title: Confetti
pages.description: A burst of confetti from an element, for a moment worth marking, such as a first sale or a finished setup. The pieces fall back and rest on the element. It's decoration, and isn't thrown for anyone who asked for less motion.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { burstConfetti } from "@nuvui/react";
```

It's a function, not a component: call it with the element the confetti comes from, from an event handler or an effect.

```tsx
<Button onClick={(event) => burstConfetti(event.currentTarget)}>
  Publish
</Button>
```

sections.heading: Options
sections.markdown:
## Options

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | `number` | `80` | How many pieces are thrown. At most 150. |
| `colors` | `string[]` |  | The pieces' colors, as any CSS color, or a variable such as `var(--color-primary)`, read where the target is. Without them the pieces take the theme's chart colors. |

`burstConfetti` returns a promise that settles when its last piece is gone, for anything that should wait until then.

sections.heading: Colors
sections.markdown:
## Colors

The pieces take the theme's chart colors, `--color-chart-1` and on, as they are where the element is. So a theme set on a part of the page colors what's thrown from it. `colors` takes your own: any CSS color, or a variable such as `var(--color-primary)`, which is read where the element is.

sections.heading: Say it in words too
Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

Confetti has no role and can't take focus.

### What the component handles

- The pieces are drawn on one canvas over the page, which is hidden from screen readers and lets every press through to what's under it.
- For a visitor who asked for less motion, nothing is thrown.
- Where the browser forces its own colors, nothing is thrown either: the pieces are colors and nothing else.
- A burst is over in about three seconds, and the canvas is taken out of the page when its last piece is gone.
- No more than 150 pieces are thrown at once, and no more than 300 are in the air however many bursts there are. A tab that's hidden stops drawing.

### What you need to handle

- Say what happened in words, as above.
- Keep it for a moment that matters. Thrown every time something is saved, it becomes noise.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-confetti-z-index` | `calc(var(--nuv-z-toast) + 1)` | Where the canvas is in the stack. Over toasts unless you say otherwise. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-confetti` | The canvas the pieces are drawn on. |

The canvas is put at the end of the page's `body` while pieces are in the air. It's fixed over the window, whatever stylesheet is loaded.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

`burstConfetti` runs in the browser, from a client component's event handler or effect. It has no `"use client"` directive of its own, since it isn't a component, and a server component has nothing to call it with.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Throw it from the thing that was done: the button that finished it, or the list that's now complete.
- Say the same thing in words.

**Don't**

- Don't throw it when a page opens.
- Don't throw it for a mistake put right, or anything someone would rather not be congratulated on.

pages.title: Context menu
pages.description: A menu of actions that opens where someone right-clicks, or presses and holds on a touch screen.
pages.markdown:
# Context menu A menu of actions that opens where someone right-clicks, or presses and holds on a touch screen. Use a context menu to offer the actions for one thing where the pointer already is: a file in a list, a row in a table, a block on a canvas. Nothing on the page says the menu is there, so it can only be a shortcut. Every action in it needs another way to be reached. ```tsx import { ContextMenu, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuLabel, ContextMenuSeparator, ContextMenuShortcut, ContextMenuTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return ( Right-click, or press and hold report.pdf Open Enter Rename F2 Share Delete ); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { ContextMenu, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuLabel, ContextMenuSeparator, ContextMenuTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `ContextMenu` | Holds the open state. Renders nothing itself. | | `ContextMenuTrigger` | The area that takes the right click. It renders a `span`. Pass `asChild` to use your own element. | | `ContextMenuContent` | The panel with the items. | | `ContextMenuItem` | One action. | | `ContextMenuCheckboxItem` | An item that's on or off. | | `ContextMenuRadioGroup` | Wraps radio items and holds which one is chosen. | | `ContextMenuRadioItem` | One choice in a radio group. | | `ContextMenuLabel` | A heading for the items under it. It can't be focused. | | `ContextMenuSeparator` | A line between groups of items. | | `ContextMenuShortcut` | The keys that do the same as an item, shown at the end of its row. | | `ContextMenuGroup` | Groups items for screen readers. It has no look of its own. | | `ContextMenuSub` | Holds the open state of a submenu. | | `ContextMenuSubTrigger` | The item that opens the submenu. | | `ContextMenuSubContent` | The submenu's panel. | These are separate exports, not properties of `ContextMenu`. `ContextMenu.Item` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component. The parts and their props match the [dropdown menu](page:components/dropdown-menu), so the items of one can be moved to the other by changing the names. ## Props ### ContextMenuContent | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `collisionPadding` | `number \| Partial>` | `8` | How close the menu may get to the edge of the screen, in pixels. It moves or flips to keep this much room. | | `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the menu is rendered into. sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import {
  ContextMenu,
  ContextMenuContent,
  ContextMenuItem,
  ContextMenuLabel,
  ContextMenuSeparator,
  ContextMenuTrigger,
} from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `ContextMenu` | Holds the open state. Renders nothing itself. |
| `ContextMenuTrigger` | The area that takes the right click. It renders a `span`. Pass `asChild` to use your own element. |
| `ContextMenuContent` | The panel with the items. |
| `ContextMenuItem` | One action. |
| `ContextMenuCheckboxItem` | An item that's on or off. |
| `ContextMenuRadioGroup` | Wraps radio items and holds which one is chosen. |
| `ContextMenuRadioItem` | One choice in a radio group. |
| `ContextMenuLabel` | A heading for the items under it. It can't be focused. |
| `ContextMenuSeparator` | A line between groups of items. |
| `ContextMenuShortcut` | The keys that do the same as an item, shown at the end of its row. |
| `ContextMenuGroup` | Groups items for screen readers. It has no look of its own. |
| `ContextMenuSub` | Holds the open state of a submenu. |
| `ContextMenuSubTrigger` | The item that opens the submenu. |
| `ContextMenuSubContent` | The submenu's panel. |

These are separate exports, not properties of `ContextMenu`. `ContextMenu.Item` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component.

The parts and their props match the [dropdown menu](page:components/dropdown-menu), so the items of one can be moved to the other by changing the names.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

### ContextMenuContent

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `collisionPadding` | `number \| Partial<Record<"bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top", number>>` | `8` | How close the menu may get to the edge of the screen, in pixels. It moves or flips to keep this much room. |
| `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the menu is rendered into. Set this when the menu should pick up a `data-theme` from a section of the page. |

The menu opens at the pointer, so there's no `side` or `align` to set.

### ContextMenuItem

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `intent` | `"danger" \| "neutral"` | `"neutral"` | Use `"danger"` for an action that destroys something. |

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onSelect` | `((event: Event) => void)` |  | Called when the item is chosen, by click or by keyboard. Call `event.preventDefault()` in it to keep the menu open. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Stops the item from being chosen. The arrow keys skip it. |
| `textValue` | `string` |  | The text that typing a letter matches against. Only needed when the item's content isn't plain text. |

### ContextMenuTrigger

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Leaves the area alone, so a right click on it opens the browser's own menu. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` |  | Renders the element you pass in place of the `span`, and gives it the right click. |

### ContextMenu

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean) => void)` |  | Called when it opens or closes. |
| `modal` | `boolean` |  | On unless you pass `false`. While a modal menu is open, the rest of the page can't be clicked or scrolled, and screen readers can't reach it. |
| `dir` | `"ltr" \| "rtl"` |  | The reading direction. With `"rtl"`, submenus open to the left and the left and right arrow keys swap. |

A context menu can't start out open, because it has no place to open at until someone points. There's no `defaultOpen`.

### ContextMenuSubContent

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `collisionPadding` | `number \| Partial<Record<"bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top", number>>` | `8` | How close the submenu may get to the edge of the screen, in pixels. |
| `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the submenu is rendered into. Pass the same one as the menu's. |

`ContextMenuCheckboxItem`, `ContextMenuRadioGroup` and the other parts take the same props as the Radix parts they wrap. The [Radix Context Menu reference](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/context-menu#api-reference) lists them.

sections.heading: Checkable items
Submenus
sections.markdown:
## Submenus

```tsx
import {
  ContextMenu,
  ContextMenuContent,
  ContextMenuItem,
  ContextMenuSub,
  ContextMenuSubContent,
  ContextMenuSubTrigger,
  ContextMenuTrigger,
} from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <ContextMenu>
      <ContextMenuTrigger
        style={{
          display: "grid",
          placeItems: "center",
          inlineSize: "min(100%, 18rem)",
          blockSize: "7rem",
          border: "1px dashed var(--color-border)",
          borderRadius: "var(--radius-lg)",
          fontSize: 14,
        }}
      >
        photo.jpg
      </ContextMenuTrigger>
      <ContextMenuContent aria-label="photo.jpg">
        <ContextMenuItem>Copy link</ContextMenuItem>
        <ContextMenuSub>
          <ContextMenuSubTrigger>Send to</ContextMenuSubTrigger>
          <ContextMenuSubContent>
            <ContextMenuItem>Email</ContextMenuItem>
            <ContextMenuItem>Messages</ContextMenuItem>
          </ContextMenuSubContent>
        </ContextMenuSub>
      </ContextMenuContent>
    </ContextMenu>
  );
}
```

A submenu opens beside its parent, and on a phone there's little room beside anything. It stays on the screen by opening on whichever side has more room and getting narrower to fit. A flat menu is easier to use there.

sections.markdown:
## Shortcuts

`ContextMenuShortcut` shows the keys that do the same thing as an item. It only shows them: listening for the keys is your code's job.

It's hidden from screen readers, because its text would otherwise run into the item's name. To have the keys announced, put them in `aria-keyshortcuts` on the item, written the way that attribute expects: `aria-keyshortcuts="Control+N"`.

sections.heading: On touch screens
sections.markdown:
## On touch screens

There's no right click on a touch screen. The menu opens when a finger stays on the area for 700 milliseconds, at the place it's touching. A finger that moves or lifts before that opens nothing, so the area can still be scrolled and tapped.

Rows are 44 pixels tall on a touch screen and 32 when a mouse or trackpad is the main input.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>F10</kbd>, or the menu key | On Windows and Linux, with focus in the area, opens the menu. The browser turns these keys into the same event as a right click, and decides where the menu appears. |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> and <kbd>↑</kbd> | Move to the next or previous item. Disabled items are skipped. |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> | Move to the first or last item. |
| A letter | Moves to the next item that starts with it. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> | Chooses the focused item. |
| <kbd>→</kbd> | On a submenu's trigger, opens the submenu. |
| <kbd>←</kbd> | Inside a submenu, closes it and goes back to its trigger. |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Closes the menu. |

### What the component handles

Most of this is Radix. The library doesn't change it.

- The panel has `role="menu"`. Items have `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` or `menuitemradio`, and the checkable ones have `aria-checked`.
- Focus moves into the menu when it opens.
- The row that has focus is filled with the primary color. That fill is the focus indicator: it has at least 3:1 contrast with the panel, and the text on it keeps 4.5:1. Radix moves focus to the row under the pointer too, so hovering and arrowing look the same.
- Where the browser forces its own colors, as Windows high contrast does, the fill isn't drawn. The focused row has an outline there instead.
- The menu stays on the screen, wherever it's opened from.
- The open and close animations only run when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion.

### What you need to handle

- Give every action another way in, as in [the example above](#another-way-to-the-same-actions). Nothing on the page shows that the menu is there, and not every keyboard has a key that opens it.
- The area has to hold something that can take focus, or take it itself with `tabIndex={0}`, for the keyboard shortcut to have anywhere to work from.
- Name the menu with `aria-label` on `ContextMenuContent`. Unlike a dropdown menu, it has no button to take a name from.
- Ask before doing something that can't be undone. A `danger` item should open an [alert dialog](page:components/alert-dialog) that confirms it.
- In a right-to-left layout, pass `dir="rtl"`.

### A note on automated checks

While a menu is open, Radix hides the rest of the page from screen readers. If you run axe on a page in that state, it reports whatever in the hidden part can take focus under its `aria-hidden-focus` rule.

Focus can't actually get there. <kbd>Tab</kbd> and clicks outside the menu are blocked until it closes. The library's own tests leave that rule out for open menus for this reason. Passing `modal={false}` avoids the report, and leaves the page reachable behind the menu.

sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Menus render at the end of `<body>`, so set these on `:root` or `body`, or straight on `ContextMenuContent` with `style` or a class. They're separate from the dropdown menu's variables: changing `--nuv-dropdown-menu-width` doesn't change a context menu.

```css
:root {
  --nuv-context-menu-width: 14rem;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-context-menu-width` | `12rem` | The narrowest the menu gets. It grows to fit its longest item. |
| `--nuv-context-menu-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Border color of the panel, and the color of the separators. |
| `--nuv-context-menu-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of the panel. |
| `--nuv-context-menu-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of the panel. |
| `--nuv-context-menu-shadow` | `var(--shadow-lg)` | Shadow under the panel. |
| `--nuv-context-menu-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color. |
| `--nuv-context-menu-item-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-sm)` | Minimum height of a row. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. |
| `--nuv-context-menu-highlight-bg` | `var(--color-primary)` | Background of the row that has focus, from the pointer or the arrow keys. Keep it at 3:1 against the panel. |
| `--nuv-context-menu-highlight-fg` | `var(--color-primary-foreground)` | Text color of that row. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-context-menu` | ContextMenuContent and ContextMenuSubContent. |
| `.nuv-context-menu__check` | The check mark inside it. |
| `.nuv-context-menu__chevron` | The arrow at the end of ContextMenuSubTrigger. |
| `.nuv-context-menu__dash` | The dash shown while a checkbox item is indeterminate. |
| `.nuv-context-menu__indicator` | The mark at the end of a checked item. Radix only renders it while the item is checked or indeterminate. |
| `.nuv-context-menu__item` | Every kind of item, and ContextMenuSubTrigger. |
| `.nuv-context-menu__item--danger` | An item with intent="danger". |
| `.nuv-context-menu__label` | ContextMenuLabel. |
| `.nuv-context-menu__separator` | ContextMenuSeparator. |
| `.nuv-context-menu__shortcut` | ContextMenuShortcut. |

`ContextMenuTrigger` has no class. It's your area, and it looks however you make it look. Radix sets `data-state="open"` on it while its menu is open, which you can style.

Radix sets `data-highlighted` on the row that has focus, `data-disabled` on a disabled one, and `data-state` on the panels, the submenu triggers and the checkable items. The fill and the animation hang off those.

## Server components

The menu parts are client components. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files.

You can put a menu together inside a server component, as the first example on this page does. An `onSelect` handler is the usual reason to need a client component of your own.

## Themed sections

A menu opened from inside a `data-theme="dark"` section doesn't inherit that theme, because it isn't rendered inside the section. Pass the section's element as `container` to `ContextMenuContent`, and to `ContextMenuSubContent` if there is one.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Offer the same actions somewhere that can be seen.
- Keep the menu about the thing that was clicked, not about the page.
- Put the destructive item last, after a separator, with `intent="danger"`.

**Don't**

- Don't take over the right click on a whole page. People use the browser's own menu to copy, inspect and open links.
- Don't put a context menu on text people may want to select or copy.
- Don't go more than one submenu deep.

pages.title: Dialog
pages.description: A modal window that takes over the page until it's closed. A sheet on phones, centered on larger screens.
pages.markdown:
# Dialog A modal window that takes over the page until it's closed. A sheet on phones, centered on larger screens. Use a dialog when someone has to answer or finish something before going on: confirming a delete, filling in a short form. It blocks the rest of the page, so don't use it for information people may want to keep open while they work. ```tsx import { Button, Dialog, DialogClose, DialogContent, DialogDescription, DialogFooter, DialogTitle, DialogTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return ( Delete this project? The project and its 12 files will be removed. This can't be undone. ); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Dialog, DialogBody, DialogClose, DialogContent, DialogDescription, DialogFooter, DialogHeader, DialogTitle, DialogTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that. ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `Dialog` | Holds the open state. Renders nothing itself. | | `DialogTrigger` | The button that opens the dialog. | | `DialogContent` | The panel. It also renders the overlay behind it and the close button in its corner. | | `DialogTitle` | The heading. Required, because it's the dialog's accessible name. | | `DialogDescription` | A sentence or two under the title, announced when the dialog opens. | | `DialogHeader` | Optional. Holds the title and description when the dialog has a `DialogBody`. | | `DialogBody` | Optional. The part that scrolls when the content is taller than the screen. | | `DialogFooter` | A row for the action buttons. | | `DialogClose` | Closes the dialog when pressed. The sizes only differ once there's room to center the dialog. ))} ); } ``` `size` sets the maximum width once the screen is at least 40rem wide: 24rem for `sm`, 32rem for `md` and 48rem for `lg`. Below that, the dialog is a sheet across the bottom of the screen whatever the size. It's never taller than the screen. If the content is longer, it scrolls. [Long content](#long-content) covers which part does. ## Long content Put the title and description in `DialogHeader`, the content in `DialogBody` and the buttons in `DialogFooter`. {changes.map(([area, change]) => (
{area}
{change}
))}
