Differs by size. | ## Classes The overlay and the panel sit next to each other in the page, not one inside the other. That's why the overlay is its own flat class. | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-dialog` | The panel. | | `.nuv-dialog--lg` | The panel with size="lg". | | `.nuv-dialog--sm` | The panel with size="sm". | | `.nuv-dialog__body` | DialogBody. | | `.nuv-dialog__close` | The close button in the corner. | | `.nuv-dialog__description` | DialogDescription. | | `.nuv-dialog__footer` | DialogFooter. | | `.nuv-dialog__header` | DialogHeader. | | `.nuv-dialog__overlay` | The layer behind the panel. | | `.nuv-dialog__title` | DialogTitle. | The panel also gets `nuv-dialog--md` at the default size. sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogBody,
  DialogClose,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
} from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Dialog` | Holds the open state. Renders nothing itself. |
| `DialogTrigger` | The button that opens the dialog. |
| `DialogContent` | The panel. It also renders the overlay behind it and the close button in its corner. |
| `DialogTitle` | The heading. Required, because it's the dialog's accessible name. |
| `DialogDescription` | A sentence or two under the title, announced when the dialog opens. |
| `DialogHeader` | Optional. Holds the title and description when the dialog has a `DialogBody`. |
| `DialogBody` | Optional. The part that scrolls when the content is taller than the screen. |
| `DialogFooter` | A row for the action buttons. |
| `DialogClose` | Closes the dialog when pressed. Wrap your own button with `asChild`. |

These are separate exports, not properties of `Dialog`. `Dialog.Content` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

`DialogContent` adds these to what Radix provides:

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `"lg" \| "md" \| "sm"` | `"md"` | The widest the dialog gets once the screen is big enough to center it. On a phone it's always a full-width sheet. |
| `showCloseButton` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether to render the close button in the corner. If you turn it off, give people another visible way to close the dialog. |
| `closeLabel` | `string` | `"Close"` | Accessible name of the close button. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |
| `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the dialog is rendered into. Set this when the dialog should pick up a `data-theme` from a section of the page. |

`Dialog`, `DialogTrigger`, `DialogClose`, `DialogTitle` and `DialogDescription` take the same props as the Radix parts they wrap, including `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal` and `asChild`. The [Radix Dialog reference](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/dialog#api-reference) lists them.

`DialogHeader`, `DialogBody` and `DialogFooter` are plain `div` elements. They take `ref`, `className` and anything else a `div` does.

sections.markdown:
## Long content Put the title and description in `DialogHeader`, the content in `DialogBody` and the buttons in `DialogFooter`. The header and footer stay where they are, and the body scrolls between them, so the title and the buttons are always in view. ```tsx import { Button, Dialog, DialogBody, DialogClose, DialogContent, DialogDescription, DialogFooter, DialogHeader, DialogTitle, DialogTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; const changes = [ ["Billing", "Invoices are now sent on the first working day of the month."], ["Seats", "A seat is counted from the day an invitation is accepted."], ["Exports", "Exports include archived projects unless you leave them out."], ["Sign-in", "Single sign-on can be required for everyone in a workspace."], ["Storage", "Files in the trash count towards storage until it's emptied."], ["Roles", "A project can have more than one owner."], ["Audit log", "Entries are kept for a year, then removed."], ["Notifications", "Email digests are sent weekly unless you change it."], ["API", "Tokens expire after 90 days and can be renewed before they do."], ["Support", "Replies come within one working day on every plan."], ]; export default function Example() { return ( {/* Kept short here, so that the body scrolls on a large screen too. */} Changes to your plan These apply from your next renewal.
{changes.map(([area, change]) => (
{area}
{change}
))}
); } ``` Without a `DialogBody`, the whole panel scrolls, and the title and buttons scroll away with the rest. That's fine for a dialog that rarely gets that tall. The body's scrollbar sits on the edge of the panel. Its text still lines up with the title, because the body has the same padding at its sides as the panel.

sections.heading: Controlling it yourself
Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> | On the trigger, opens the dialog. |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves to the next control inside the dialog. From the last one it goes back to the first. |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves to the previous control, and from the first to the last. |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Closes the dialog. |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> <kbd>Page Up</kbd> <kbd>Page Down</kbd> | Scroll the body, when it has focus. |

### What the component handles

Most of this is Radix. The library doesn't change it.

- The panel has `role="dialog"`, named by `DialogTitle` and described by `DialogDescription`.
- Opening moves focus to the first control in the content. Closing returns it to the trigger.
- Focus can't leave the dialog while it's open, and the rest of the page is hidden from screen readers.
- The trigger gets `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`.
- The close button is a real button with an accessible name, and is at least 44 pixels on touch screens. This matters on phones, where there's no <kbd>Esc</kbd> key.
- A `DialogBody` that scrolls and has nothing inside that takes focus becomes a tab stop itself, named after the dialog. Without that, someone who doesn't use a mouse would have no way to scroll it. A body that fits, or that holds a field or a button, is left alone.
- The open and close animations only run when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion.

### What you need to handle

- Always include a `DialogTitle`. If the design has no visible heading, hide it visually but keep it.
- If you leave out `DialogDescription`, pass `aria-describedby={undefined}` to `DialogContent`, or Radix logs a warning.
- Translate `closeLabel` along with the rest of your interface.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Dialogs render at the end of `<body>`, so set these on `:root` or `body`, not on the element around the trigger.

```css
:root {
  --nuv-dialog-radius: var(--radius-md);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-dialog-overlay-bg` | `var(--color-overlay)` | Color of the layer that dims the page. |
| `--nuv-dialog-padding` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 6)` | Padding inside the panel. One length, used on every side. |
| `--nuv-dialog-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Border color of the panel. |
| `--nuv-dialog-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of the panel. |
| `--nuv-dialog-shadow` | `var(--shadow-xl)` | Shadow under the panel. |
| `--nuv-dialog-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color. |
| `--nuv-dialog-radius` | `var(--radius-xl)` | Corner radius. As a sheet on phones, only the top corners are rounded. |
| `--nuv-dialog-width` | `32rem`, `24rem`, `48rem` | Maximum width once the dialog is centered. Differs by size. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

The overlay and the panel sit next to each other in the page, not one inside the other. That's why the overlay is its own flat class.

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-dialog` | The panel. |
| `.nuv-dialog--lg` | The panel with size="lg". |
| `.nuv-dialog--sm` | The panel with size="sm". |
| `.nuv-dialog__body` | DialogBody. |
| `.nuv-dialog__close` | The close button in the corner. |
| `.nuv-dialog__description` | DialogDescription. |
| `.nuv-dialog__footer` | DialogFooter. |
| `.nuv-dialog__header` | DialogHeader. |
| `.nuv-dialog__overlay` | The layer behind the panel. |
| `.nuv-dialog__title` | DialogTitle. |

The panel also gets `nuv-dialog--md` at the default size. No styles are attached to it, since medium is the base.

Radix sets `data-state="open"` or `data-state="closed"` on the overlay and the panel. The animations hang off those.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

The dialog parts are client components. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files.

You can still put a dialog together inside a server component, as in the first example on this page. It only needs a client component of its own when you add state or handlers, as in the controlled example.

sections.heading: Themed sections
sections.markdown:
## Themed sections

A dialog opened from inside a `data-theme="dark"` section doesn't inherit that theme, because it isn't rendered inside the section. Pass the section's element as `container` and it will be.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Name the buttons after what they do. "Delete project" and "Cancel", not "Yes" and "No".
- Keep it short. If it needs its own navigation, it should be a page.
- Leave the close button in, unless there's another visible way out.

**Don't**

- Don't open a dialog from inside a dialog.
- Don't open one without the person doing something to ask for it.
- Don't put the only copy of important information in one. It's gone once it's closed.

pages.title: Dropdown menu
pages.description: A menu of actions that opens from a button, with keyboard navigation, checkable items and submenus.
pages.markdown:
# Dropdown menu A menu of actions that opens from a button, with keyboard navigation, checkable items and submenus. Use a dropdown menu for a list of actions on one thing: rename, duplicate, delete. For picking a value in a form, use a [select](page:components/select). ```tsx import { Button, DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuLabel, DropdownMenuSeparator, DropdownMenuTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return ( Project Rename Duplicate Archive Delete ); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuLabel, DropdownMenuSeparator, DropdownMenuTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `DropdownMenu` | Holds the open state. Renders nothing itself. | | `DropdownMenuTrigger` | The button that opens the menu. Wrap your own with `asChild`. | | `DropdownMenuContent` | The panel with the items. | | `DropdownMenuItem` | One action. | | `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem` | An item that's on or off. | | `DropdownMenuRadioGroup` | Wraps radio items and holds which one is chosen. | | `DropdownMenuRadioItem` | One choice in a radio group. | | `DropdownMenuLabel` | A heading for the items under it. It can't be focused. | | `DropdownMenuSeparator` | A line between groups of items. | | `DropdownMenuShortcut` | The keys that do the same as an item, shown at the end of its row. | | `DropdownMenuGroup` | Groups items for screen readers. It has no look of its own. | | `DropdownMenuSub` | Holds the open state of a submenu. | | `DropdownMenuSubTrigger` | The item that opens the submenu. | | `DropdownMenuSubContent` | The submenu's panel. | These are separate exports, not properties of `DropdownMenu`. `DropdownMenu.Item` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component. ## Props ### DropdownMenuContent | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `align` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start"` | `"start"` | Which edge of the trigger the menu lines up with. | | `sideOffset` | `number` | `6` | The gap between the trigger and the menu, in pixels. | | `collisionPadding` | `number \| Partial>` | `8` | How close the menu may get to the edge of the screen, in pixels. It moves or flips to keep this much room. | | `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the menu is rendered into. Set this when the menu should pick up a `data-theme` from a section of the page. | One more from Radix that's often useful: | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `side` | `"bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top"` | | The side of the trigger the menu opens on. It's `"bottom"` unless you say otherwise, and it flips to the opposite side when there isn't room. | ### DropdownMenuItem | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `intent` | `"danger" \| "neutral"` | `"neutral"` | Use `"danger"` for an action that destroys something. | | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `onSelect` | `((event: Event) => void)` | | Called when the item is chosen, by click or by keyboard. Call `event.preventDefault()` in it to keep the menu open. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | | Stops the item from being chosen. The arrow keys skip it. | | `textValue` | `string` | | The text that typing a letter matches against. Only needed when the item's content isn't plain text. | ### DropdownMenuCheckboxItem | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `checked` | `"indeterminate" \| boolean` | | Whether the item is on. `"indeterminate"` shows a dash. | | `onCheckedChange` | `((checked: boolean) => void)` | | Called with the new state when the item is chosen. | ### DropdownMenuRadioGroup | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` | `string` | | The `value` of the radio item that's chosen. | | `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void)` | | Called with an item's `value` when it's chosen. | ### DropdownMenu | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `open` | `boolean` | | Whether it's open, when you control it yourself. Use it with `onOpenChange`. | | `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | | Whether it starts open, when you don't control it. | | `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean) => void)` | | Called when it opens or closes. | | `modal` | `boolean` | | On unless you pass `false`. While a modal menu is open, the rest of the page can't be clicked or scrolled, and screen readers can't reach it. | | `dir` | `"ltr" \| "rtl"` | | The reading direction. With `"rtl"`, submenus open to the left and the left and right arrow keys swap. | ### DropdownMenuSubContent | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `collisionPadding` | `number \| Partial>` | `8` | How close the submenu may get to the edge of the screen, in pixels. | | `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the submenu is rendered into. Pass the same one as the menu's. | The other parts take the same props as the Radix parts they wrap. The [Radix Dropdown Menu reference](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/dropdown-menu#api-reference) lists them. ## Doing something Give each item an `onSelect`. It runs for a click, a tap, Enter and Space alike, and the menu closes afterwards. ```tsx "use client"; import { Button, DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { const [last, setLast] = useState("Nothing yet"); return (
setLast("New file")}> New file setLast("Open")}> Open setLast("Save")}> Save

Last chosen: {last}

); } ``` ## Checkable items A checked item shows a check at the end of its row. Putting it there keeps every label lined up, whether or not the menu has checkable items. ```tsx "use client"; import { Button, DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuCheckboxItem, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuLabel, DropdownMenuRadioGroup, DropdownMenuRadioItem, DropdownMenuSeparator, DropdownMenuTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { const [hidden, setHidden] = useState(false); const [sort, setSort] = useState("name"); return ( Show hidden files Sort by Name Date changed Size ); } ``` ## Shortcuts `DropdownMenuShortcut` shows the keys that do the same thing as an item, at the end of its row. It only shows them: listening for the keys is your code's job. ```tsx import { Button, DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuSeparator, DropdownMenuShortcut, DropdownMenuTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return ( Duplicate Ctrl+D Rename F2 Delete Del ); } ``` It's hidden from screen readers, because its text would otherwise run into the item's name. To have the keys announced, put them in `aria-keyshortcuts` on the item, as the example does. That attribute has its own way of writing keys: `Control+D`, not `Ctrl+D`. ## Submenus ```tsx import { Button, DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuSub, DropdownMenuSubContent, DropdownMenuSubTrigger, DropdownMenuTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return ( Copy link Send to Email Messages ); } ``` A submenu opens beside its parent, and on a phone there's little room beside anything. It stays on the screen by opening on whichever side has more room and getting narrower to fit, which can leave it cramped. A flat menu is easier to use there. Keep submenus for places you know have the width. ## On small screens Rows are 44 pixels tall on a touch screen and 32 when a mouse or trackpad is the main input. A menu is never taller than the room around its trigger. A long one scrolls inside itself. ## Accessibility ### Keyboard | Key | What it does | | --- | --- | | Enter, Space or ↓ | On the trigger, opens the menu and moves focus to its first item. | | ↓ and ↑ | Move to the next or previous item. Disabled items are skipped. | | Home and End | Move to the first or last item. | | A letter | Moves to the next item that starts with it. | | Enter or Space | Chooses the focused item. | | → | On a submenu's trigger, opens the submenu. | | ← | Inside a submenu, closes it and goes back to its trigger. | | Esc | Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger. | ### What the component handles Most of this is Radix. The library doesn't change it. - The panel has `role="menu"` and is named by its trigger. Items have `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` or `menuitemradio`, and the checkable ones have `aria-checked`. - The trigger gets `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`. - Focus moves into the menu when it opens and back to the trigger when it closes. - The row that has focus is filled with the primary color. That fill is the focus indicator: it has at least 3:1 contrast with the panel, and the text on it keeps 4.5:1. Radix moves focus to the row under the pointer too, so hovering and arrowing look the same. - A `danger` item is filled with the danger color instead. - Where the browser forces its own colors, as Windows high contrast does, the fill isn't drawn. The focused row has an outline there instead. - The open and close animations only run when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion. ### What you need to handle - Give the trigger a name. An icon-only button needs `aria-label`. - Ask before doing something that can't be undone. A menu item is easy to hit by mistake, so a `danger` item should open a [dialog](page:components/dialog) that confirms it. - In a right-to-left layout, pass `dir="rtl"`. ### A note on automated checks While a menu is open, Radix hides the rest of the page from screen readers. If you run axe on a page in that state, it reports the trigger under its `aria-hidden-focus` rule, because the trigger is a focusable element inside the hidden part. Focus can't actually get there. Tab and clicks outside the menu are blocked until it closes. The library's own tests leave that rule out for open menus for this reason. Passing `modal={false}` avoids the report, and leaves the page reachable behind the menu. ## CSS variables Menus render at the end of ``, so set these on `:root` or `body`, or straight on `DropdownMenuContent` with `style` or a class. ```css :root { --nuv-dropdown-menu-width: 14rem; } ``` | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-dropdown-menu-width` | `12rem` | The narrowest the menu gets. It grows to fit its longest item. | | `--nuv-dropdown-menu-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Border color of the panel, and the color of the separators. | | `--nuv-dropdown-menu-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of the panel. | | `--nuv-dropdown-menu-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of the panel. | | `--nuv-dropdown-menu-shadow` | `var(--shadow-lg)` | Shadow under the panel. | | `--nuv-dropdown-menu-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color. | | `--nuv-dropdown-menu-item-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-sm)` | Minimum height of a row. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. | | `--nuv-dropdown-menu-highlight-bg` | `var(--color-primary)` | Background of the row that has focus, from the pointer or the arrow keys. Keep it at 3:1 against the panel. | | `--nuv-dropdown-menu-highlight-fg` | `var(--color-primary-foreground)` | Text color of that row. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-dropdown-menu` | DropdownMenuContent and DropdownMenuSubContent. | | `.nuv-dropdown-menu__check` | The check mark inside it. | | `.nuv-dropdown-menu__chevron` | The arrow at the end of DropdownMenuSubTrigger. | | `.nuv-dropdown-menu__dash` | The dash shown while a checkbox item is indeterminate. | | `.nuv-dropdown-menu__indicator` | The mark at the end of a checked item. Radix only renders it while the item is checked or indeterminate. | | `.nuv-dropdown-menu__item` | Every kind of item, and DropdownMenuSubTrigger. | | `.nuv-dropdown-menu__item--danger` | An item with intent="danger". | | `.nuv-dropdown-menu__label` | DropdownMenuLabel. | | `.nuv-dropdown-menu__separator` | DropdownMenuSeparator. | | `.nuv-dropdown-menu__shortcut` | DropdownMenuShortcut. | Radix sets `data-highlighted` on the row that has focus, `data-disabled` on a disabled one, and `data-state` on the panels, the submenu triggers and the checkable items. sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuLabel,
  DropdownMenuSeparator,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `DropdownMenu` | Holds the open state. Renders nothing itself. |
| `DropdownMenuTrigger` | The button that opens the menu. Wrap your own with `asChild`. |
| `DropdownMenuContent` | The panel with the items. |
| `DropdownMenuItem` | One action. |
| `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem` | An item that's on or off. |
| `DropdownMenuRadioGroup` | Wraps radio items and holds which one is chosen. |
| `DropdownMenuRadioItem` | One choice in a radio group. |
| `DropdownMenuLabel` | A heading for the items under it. It can't be focused. |
| `DropdownMenuSeparator` | A line between groups of items. |
| `DropdownMenuShortcut` | The keys that do the same as an item, shown at the end of its row. |
| `DropdownMenuGroup` | Groups items for screen readers. It has no look of its own. |
| `DropdownMenuSub` | Holds the open state of a submenu. |
| `DropdownMenuSubTrigger` | The item that opens the submenu. |
| `DropdownMenuSubContent` | The submenu's panel. |

These are separate exports, not properties of `DropdownMenu`. `DropdownMenu.Item` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

### DropdownMenuContent

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `align` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start"` | `"start"` | Which edge of the trigger the menu lines up with. |
| `sideOffset` | `number` | `6` | The gap between the trigger and the menu, in pixels. |
| `collisionPadding` | `number \| Partial<Record<"bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top", number>>` | `8` | How close the menu may get to the edge of the screen, in pixels. It moves or flips to keep this much room. |
| `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the menu is rendered into. Set this when the menu should pick up a `data-theme` from a section of the page. |

One more from Radix that's often useful:

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `side` | `"bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top"` |  | The side of the trigger the menu opens on. It's `"bottom"` unless you say otherwise, and it flips to the opposite side when there isn't room. |

### DropdownMenuItem

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `intent` | `"danger" \| "neutral"` | `"neutral"` | Use `"danger"` for an action that destroys something. |

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onSelect` | `((event: Event) => void)` |  | Called when the item is chosen, by click or by keyboard. Call `event.preventDefault()` in it to keep the menu open. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Stops the item from being chosen. The arrow keys skip it. |
| `textValue` | `string` |  | The text that typing a letter matches against. Only needed when the item's content isn't plain text. |

### DropdownMenuCheckboxItem

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `checked` | `"indeterminate" \| boolean` |  | Whether the item is on. `"indeterminate"` shows a dash. |
| `onCheckedChange` | `((checked: boolean) => void)` |  | Called with the new state when the item is chosen. |

### DropdownMenuRadioGroup

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` |  | The `value` of the radio item that's chosen. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void)` |  | Called with an item's `value` when it's chosen. |

### DropdownMenu

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Whether it's open, when you control it yourself. Use it with `onOpenChange`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` |  | Whether it starts open, when you don't control it. |
| `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean) => void)` |  | Called when it opens or closes. |
| `modal` | `boolean` |  | On unless you pass `false`. While a modal menu is open, the rest of the page can't be clicked or scrolled, and screen readers can't reach it. |
| `dir` | `"ltr" \| "rtl"` |  | The reading direction. With `"rtl"`, submenus open to the left and the left and right arrow keys swap. |

### DropdownMenuSubContent

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `collisionPadding` | `number \| Partial<Record<"bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top", number>>` | `8` | How close the submenu may get to the edge of the screen, in pixels. |
| `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the submenu is rendered into. Pass the same one as the menu's. |

The other parts take the same props as the Radix parts they wrap. The [Radix Dropdown Menu reference](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/dropdown-menu#api-reference) lists them.

sections.heading: Doing something
sections.markdown:
## Doing something Give each item an `onSelect`. It runs for a click, a tap, Enter and Space alike, and the menu closes afterwards. ```tsx "use client"; import { Button, DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { const [last, setLast] = useState("Nothing yet"); return (
setLast("New file")}> New file setLast("Open")}> Open setLast("Save")}> Save

Last chosen: {last}

); } ```

sections.heading: Checkable items
sections.markdown:
## Checkable items

A checked item shows a check at the end of its row. Putting it there keeps every label lined up, whether or not the menu has checkable items.

```tsx
"use client";

import {
  Button,
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuCheckboxItem,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuLabel,
  DropdownMenuRadioGroup,
  DropdownMenuRadioItem,
  DropdownMenuSeparator,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from "@nuvui/react";
import { useState } from "react";

export default function Example() {
  const [hidden, setHidden] = useState(false);
  const [sort, setSort] = useState("name");

  return (
    <DropdownMenu>
      <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>
        <Button intent="secondary">View</Button>
      </DropdownMenuTrigger>
      <DropdownMenuContent>
        <DropdownMenuCheckboxItem checked={hidden} onCheckedChange={setHidden}>
          Show hidden files
        </DropdownMenuCheckboxItem>
        <DropdownMenuSeparator />
        <DropdownMenuRadioGroup value={sort} onValueChange={setSort}>
          <DropdownMenuLabel>Sort by</DropdownMenuLabel>
          <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="name">Name</DropdownMenuRadioItem>
          <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="date">
            Date changed
          </DropdownMenuRadioItem>
          <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="size">Size</DropdownMenuRadioItem>
        </DropdownMenuRadioGroup>
      </DropdownMenuContent>
    </DropdownMenu>
  );
}
```

sections.heading: Shortcuts
sections.markdown:
## Shortcuts

`DropdownMenuShortcut` shows the keys that do the same thing as an item, at the end of its row. It only shows them: listening for the keys is your code's job.

```tsx
import {
  Button,
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuSeparator,
  DropdownMenuShortcut,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <DropdownMenu>
      <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>
        <Button intent="secondary">Edit</Button>
      </DropdownMenuTrigger>
      <DropdownMenuContent>
        <DropdownMenuItem aria-keyshortcuts="Control+D">
          Duplicate
          <DropdownMenuShortcut>Ctrl+D</DropdownMenuShortcut>
        </DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuItem aria-keyshortcuts="F2">
          Rename
          <DropdownMenuShortcut>F2</DropdownMenuShortcut>
        </DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuSeparator />
        <DropdownMenuItem intent="danger" aria-keyshortcuts="Delete">
          Delete
          <DropdownMenuShortcut>Del</DropdownMenuShortcut>
        </DropdownMenuItem>
      </DropdownMenuContent>
    </DropdownMenu>
  );
}
```

It's hidden from screen readers, because its text would otherwise run into the item's name. To have the keys announced, put them in `aria-keyshortcuts` on the item, as the example does. That attribute has its own way of writing keys: `Control+D`, not `Ctrl+D`.

sections.heading: Submenus
sections.markdown:
## Submenus

```tsx
import {
  Button,
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuSub,
  DropdownMenuSubContent,
  DropdownMenuSubTrigger,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <DropdownMenu>
      <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>
        <Button intent="secondary">Share</Button>
      </DropdownMenuTrigger>
      <DropdownMenuContent>
        <DropdownMenuItem>Copy link</DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuSub>
          <DropdownMenuSubTrigger>Send to</DropdownMenuSubTrigger>
          <DropdownMenuSubContent>
            <DropdownMenuItem>Email</DropdownMenuItem>
            <DropdownMenuItem>Messages</DropdownMenuItem>
          </DropdownMenuSubContent>
        </DropdownMenuSub>
      </DropdownMenuContent>
    </DropdownMenu>
  );
}
```

A submenu opens beside its parent, and on a phone there's little room beside anything. It stays on the screen by opening on whichever side has more room and getting narrower to fit, which can leave it cramped. A flat menu is easier to use there. Keep submenus for places you know have the width.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

Rows are 44 pixels tall on a touch screen and 32 when a mouse or trackpad is the main input.

A menu is never taller than the room around its trigger. A long one scrolls inside itself.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>, <kbd>Space</kbd> or <kbd>↓</kbd> | On the trigger, opens the menu and moves focus to its first item. |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> and <kbd>↑</kbd> | Move to the next or previous item. Disabled items are skipped. |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> | Move to the first or last item. |
| A letter | Moves to the next item that starts with it. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> | Chooses the focused item. |
| <kbd>→</kbd> | On a submenu's trigger, opens the submenu. |
| <kbd>←</kbd> | Inside a submenu, closes it and goes back to its trigger. |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger. |

### What the component handles

Most of this is Radix. The library doesn't change it.

- The panel has `role="menu"` and is named by its trigger. Items have `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` or `menuitemradio`, and the checkable ones have `aria-checked`.
- The trigger gets `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`.
- Focus moves into the menu when it opens and back to the trigger when it closes.
- The row that has focus is filled with the primary color. That fill is the focus indicator: it has at least 3:1 contrast with the panel, and the text on it keeps 4.5:1. Radix moves focus to the row under the pointer too, so hovering and arrowing look the same.
- A `danger` item is filled with the danger color instead.
- Where the browser forces its own colors, as Windows high contrast does, the fill isn't drawn. The focused row has an outline there instead.
- The open and close animations only run when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion.

### What you need to handle

- Give the trigger a name. An icon-only button needs `aria-label`.
- Ask before doing something that can't be undone. A menu item is easy to hit by mistake, so a `danger` item should open a [dialog](page:components/dialog) that confirms it.
- In a right-to-left layout, pass `dir="rtl"`.

### A note on automated checks

While a menu is open, Radix hides the rest of the page from screen readers. If you run axe on a page in that state, it reports the trigger under its `aria-hidden-focus` rule, because the trigger is a focusable element inside the hidden part.

Focus can't actually get there. <kbd>Tab</kbd> and clicks outside the menu are blocked until it closes. The library's own tests leave that rule out for open menus for this reason. Passing `modal={false}` avoids the report, and leaves the page reachable behind the menu.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Menus render at the end of `<body>`, so set these on `:root` or `body`, or straight on `DropdownMenuContent` with `style` or a class.

```css
:root {
  --nuv-dropdown-menu-width: 14rem;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-dropdown-menu-width` | `12rem` | The narrowest the menu gets. It grows to fit its longest item. |
| `--nuv-dropdown-menu-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Border color of the panel, and the color of the separators. |
| `--nuv-dropdown-menu-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of the panel. |
| `--nuv-dropdown-menu-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of the panel. |
| `--nuv-dropdown-menu-shadow` | `var(--shadow-lg)` | Shadow under the panel. |
| `--nuv-dropdown-menu-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color. |
| `--nuv-dropdown-menu-item-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-sm)` | Minimum height of a row. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. |
| `--nuv-dropdown-menu-highlight-bg` | `var(--color-primary)` | Background of the row that has focus, from the pointer or the arrow keys. Keep it at 3:1 against the panel. |
| `--nuv-dropdown-menu-highlight-fg` | `var(--color-primary-foreground)` | Text color of that row. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-dropdown-menu` | DropdownMenuContent and DropdownMenuSubContent. |
| `.nuv-dropdown-menu__check` | The check mark inside it. |
| `.nuv-dropdown-menu__chevron` | The arrow at the end of DropdownMenuSubTrigger. |
| `.nuv-dropdown-menu__dash` | The dash shown while a checkbox item is indeterminate. |
| `.nuv-dropdown-menu__indicator` | The mark at the end of a checked item. Radix only renders it while the item is checked or indeterminate. |
| `.nuv-dropdown-menu__item` | Every kind of item, and DropdownMenuSubTrigger. |
| `.nuv-dropdown-menu__item--danger` | An item with intent="danger". |
| `.nuv-dropdown-menu__label` | DropdownMenuLabel. |
| `.nuv-dropdown-menu__separator` | DropdownMenuSeparator. |
| `.nuv-dropdown-menu__shortcut` | DropdownMenuShortcut. |

Radix sets `data-highlighted` on the row that has focus, `data-disabled` on a disabled one, and `data-state` on the panels, the submenu triggers and the checkable items. The fill and the animation hang off those.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

The menu parts are client components. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files.

You can put a menu together inside a server component, as the first example on this page does. An `onSelect` handler is the usual reason to need a client component of your own. That's a React rule about passing functions from the server, not something specific to this library.

sections.heading: Themed sections
sections.markdown:
## Themed sections

A menu opened from inside a `data-theme="dark"` section doesn't inherit that theme, because it isn't rendered inside the section. Pass the section's element as `container` to `DropdownMenuContent`, and to `DropdownMenuSubContent` if there is one.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Start each item with a verb: "Rename", "Duplicate", "Delete".
- Put the destructive item last, after a separator, with `intent="danger"`.
- Leave an unavailable item in place and disable it, so the menu doesn't change shape.

**Don't**

- Don't use a menu for navigation between pages. Those are links.
- Don't hide the main action of a screen in a menu. Give it a button.
- Don't go more than one submenu deep.

pages.title: Empty
pages.description: What a list, a table or a search shows when it has nothing in it, with a way to get something into it.
pages.markdown:
# Empty What a list, a table or a search shows when it has nothing in it, with a way to get something into it. Use an empty state wherever a screen can have nothing to show: a list before the first item, a search with no matches, a folder that was cleared. Say why it's empty and offer the next step. A blank area leaves people wondering whether the page is still loading. ```tsx import { Button, Empty, EmptyActions, EmptyDescription, EmptyMedia, EmptyTitle, } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return ( No invoices yet Invoices show up here once you send the first one to a customer. ); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Empty, EmptyActions, EmptyDescription, EmptyMedia, EmptyTitle, } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `Empty` | The box, with everything centered in it. | | `EmptyMedia` | An icon or a small picture, on a filled square. | | `EmptyTitle` | What's missing. An `h3` unless you say otherwise. | | `EmptyDescription` | Why, and what to do about it. | | `EmptyActions` | The buttons or links. | Only `Empty` and `EmptyTitle` are needed. ## Props ### EmptyTitle | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead of an `h3`, and give it the title's class and props. This is how you pick the heading level that fits the page. | The other parts add no props of their own. Each takes what its element takes, including `ref` and `className`. ## A search with no matches A search that finds nothing isn't the same as a list that was never filled. Say what was searched for, and offer a way back to results. ```tsx import { Button, Empty, EmptyActions, EmptyDescription, EmptyTitle, } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return (

Nothing matches "nrothwind"

 Check the spelling, or search all customers instead of only the active ones. ); } ``` The title here is an `h4`, set with `asChild`, because this example sits under an `h3` on this page. Pick the level that fits where the empty state is used. ## Three kinds of empty What to write depends on why there's nothing there. | Why it's empty | Say | Offer | | --- | --- | --- | | Nothing has been made yet | What will show up here | The button that makes the first one | | A search or filter matched nothing | What was searched for | Clearing the search, or widening it | | The visitor isn't allowed to see it | That there's something they can't see | Who to ask for access | When something went wrong, that's an error and not an empty state. Use an [alert](page:components/alert) and say what happened. ## On small screens The padding is 24 pixels on a phone and 48 from the `sm` breakpoint up. The description wraps at 28rem however wide the box is, so its lines stay short enough to read. Buttons that don't fit in one row wrap. ## Accessibility An empty state has no keyboard behavior of its own. The buttons and links in `EmptyActions` work as they do anywhere. ### What the component handles - The title is a heading, so the empty state can be found in the page's outline. - `EmptyMedia` is hidden from screen readers. The title says what the picture shows. - The dashed edge is a border, which is still drawn where the browser forces its own colors. The square behind the picture gets an edge there too. - The description's color has at least 4.5:1 against the page in every theme. ### What you need to handle - Pick the heading level that fits the page, with `asChild`. - When a search or a filter empties a list while the page is open, a screen reader user isn't told. Say it in an element with `role="status"`, such as "No customers match". - Keep the page's other controls where they were. A search field that disappears along with its results leaves no way to change the search. ## CSS variables Set any of these on `Empty`, or on anything around it. ```css .table-empty { --nuv-empty-border: transparent; --nuv-empty-padding: calc(var(--spacing) * 8); } ``` | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-empty-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 2)` | Space between the parts. | | `--nuv-empty-padding` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 6)`, `calc(var(--spacing) * 12)` | Padding inside the box. Larger from the sm breakpoint. | | `--nuv-empty-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of the dashed edge. Set it to transparent for no edge. | | `--nuv-empty-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius. | | `--nuv-empty-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Text color of the title. | | `--nuv-empty-media-size` | `3rem` | Width and height of the square behind the picture. | | `--nuv-empty-media-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background color of that square. | | `--nuv-empty-media-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of an icon inside it. | | `--nuv-empty-title-size` | `var(--text-base)` | Font size of the title. | | `--nuv-empty-text-width` | `28rem` | The widest the description gets. | | `--nuv-empty-muted-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Text color of the description. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-empty` | Empty. | | `.nuv-empty__actions` | EmptyActions. | | `.nuv-empty__description` | EmptyDescription. | | `.nuv-empty__media` | EmptyMedia. | | `.nuv-empty__title` | EmptyTitle. | ## Server components The empty parts have no `"use client"` directive and use no state, so they render in a server component as they are. ## Do and don't **Do** - Write the title as a plain statement: "No invoices yet". - Make the main button the same action as the page's own "new" button. **Don't** - Don't show an empty state while the data is still loading. Use a [skeleton](page:components/skeleton) until you know. - Don't blame the visitor. "Nothing matches" is enough.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import {
  Empty,
  EmptyActions,
  EmptyDescription,
  EmptyMedia,
  EmptyTitle,
} from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Empty` | The box, with everything centered in it. |
| `EmptyMedia` | An icon or a small picture, on a filled square. |
| `EmptyTitle` | What's missing. An `h3` unless you say otherwise. |
| `EmptyDescription` | Why, and what to do about it. |
| `EmptyActions` | The buttons or links. |

Only `Empty` and `EmptyTitle` are needed.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

### EmptyTitle

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead of an `h3`, and give it the title's class and props. This is how you pick the heading level that fits the page. |

The other parts add no props of their own. Each takes what its element takes, including `ref` and `className`.

sections.heading: A search with no matches
sections.markdown:
## A search with no matches A search that finds nothing isn't the same as a list that was never filled. Say what was searched for, and offer a way back to results. ```tsx import { Button, Empty, EmptyActions, EmptyDescription, EmptyTitle, } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return (

Nothing matches "nrothwind"

 Check the spelling, or search all customers instead of only the active ones. ); } ``` The title here is an `h4`, set with `asChild`, because this example sits under an `h3` on this page. Pick the level that fits where the empty state is used.

sections.heading: Three kinds of empty
sections.markdown:
## Three kinds of empty

What to write depends on why there's nothing there.

| Why it's empty | Say | Offer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nothing has been made yet | What will show up here | The button that makes the first one |
| A search or filter matched nothing | What was searched for | Clearing the search, or widening it |
| The visitor isn't allowed to see it | That there's something they can't see | Who to ask for access |

When something went wrong, that's an error and not an empty state. Use an [alert](page:components/alert) and say what happened.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

The padding is 24 pixels on a phone and 48 from the `sm` breakpoint up. The description wraps at 28rem however wide the box is, so its lines stay short enough to read. Buttons that don't fit in one row wrap.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

An empty state has no keyboard behavior of its own. The buttons and links in `EmptyActions` work as they do anywhere.

### What the component handles

- The title is a heading, so the empty state can be found in the page's outline.
- `EmptyMedia` is hidden from screen readers. The title says what the picture shows.
- The dashed edge is a border, which is still drawn where the browser forces its own colors. The square behind the picture gets an edge there too.
- The description's color has at least 4.5:1 against the page in every theme.

### What you need to handle

- Pick the heading level that fits the page, with `asChild`.
- When a search or a filter empties a list while the page is open, a screen reader user isn't told. Say it in an element with `role="status"`, such as "No customers match".
- Keep the page's other controls where they were. A search field that disappears along with its results leaves no way to change the search.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on `Empty`, or on anything around it.

```css
.table-empty {
  --nuv-empty-border: transparent;
  --nuv-empty-padding: calc(var(--spacing) * 8);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-empty-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 2)` | Space between the parts. |
| `--nuv-empty-padding` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 6)`, `calc(var(--spacing) * 12)` | Padding inside the box. Larger from the sm breakpoint. |
| `--nuv-empty-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of the dashed edge. Set it to transparent for no edge. |
| `--nuv-empty-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius. |
| `--nuv-empty-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Text color of the title. |
| `--nuv-empty-media-size` | `3rem` | Width and height of the square behind the picture. |
| `--nuv-empty-media-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background color of that square. |
| `--nuv-empty-media-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of an icon inside it. |
| `--nuv-empty-title-size` | `var(--text-base)` | Font size of the title. |
| `--nuv-empty-text-width` | `28rem` | The widest the description gets. |
| `--nuv-empty-muted-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Text color of the description. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-empty` | Empty. |
| `.nuv-empty__actions` | EmptyActions. |
| `.nuv-empty__description` | EmptyDescription. |
| `.nuv-empty__media` | EmptyMedia. |

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

The empty parts have no `"use client"` directive and use no state, so they render in a server component as they are.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Write the title as a plain statement: "No invoices yet".
- Make the main button the same action as the page's own "new" button.

**Don't**

- Don't show an empty state while the data is still loading. Use a [skeleton](page:components/skeleton) until you know.
- Don't blame the visitor. "Nothing matches" is enough.

sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Field` | The wrapper. It holds the ids and the state the other parts read. |
| `FieldLabel` | The label. It's a [Label](page:components/label) that points at the control. |
| `FieldControl` | Wraps the control and passes the field's props to it. It renders nothing itself. |
| `FieldDescription` | A hint under the control. |

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

### Field

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"vertical"` | `"vertical"` stacks the label, the control and the text under it. `"horizontal"` puts the first two side by side, which suits a checkbox or a switch with its label. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  | Marks the control as invalid. Left out, the control is invalid while a `FieldError` has something in it. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Makes the control required and puts a mark after the label. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the control and fades the label. |
| `controlId` | `string` |  | The `id` the control gets. The label, the description and the error take theirs from it. Left out, one is made up. |

Everything else is passed to the `<div>` it renders.

### FieldLabel

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `requiredIndicator` | `ReactNode` | `"*"` | What follows the label's text while the field is required. It's hidden from screen readers, which hear "required" from the control itself. |

It also takes everything [Label](page:components/label) does, `asChild` included.

### FieldControl

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The control: one element, which gets the field's props. |

`FieldDescription` and `FieldError` take the props of a `<div>`.

sections.heading: What the control is given
sections.markdown:
## What the control is given

`FieldControl` holds one element and adds these props to it. Anything you set on the control yourself wins, except `aria-describedby`, where yours is kept and the field's ids are added after it.

| Prop | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | The field's id, which the label's `htmlFor` matches. |
| `aria-labelledby` | The label's id, once there is a `FieldLabel`. |
| `aria-describedby` | The description's id and the error's id, for whichever of the two is on the page. |
| `aria-invalid` | `true` while the field is invalid. |
| `required` | Set when `Field` has `required`. |
| `disabled` | Set when `Field` has `disabled`. |

Set the id on `Field` with `controlId` and not on the control, or the label will point at an id that isn't there.

sections.heading: Errors
Required and disabled
sections.markdown:
## Required and disabled

`required` on `Field` reaches the control and puts an asterisk after the label. The asterisk is hidden from screen readers, which hear "required" from the control. Change it with `requiredIndicator` on `FieldLabel`, or pass `null` to leave it out.

`disabled` reaches the control and fades the label.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

A field has no keyboard behavior of its own.

### What the component handles

- The label is a real `<label>` with `htmlFor`, so a click on it focuses the control.
- The control is named by the label and described by the description and the error, in that order. The ids only appear in `aria-describedby` while the part they belong to is on the page.
- `aria-invalid` follows the error, so the two can't disagree.
- The error is drawn in `--color-danger`, which has at least 4.5:1 contrast with the page in every theme. It's text, so it doesn't depend on the color being seen.
- The ids come from React's `useId`, so they're the same on the server and in the browser.

### What you need to handle

- Write the error so it says what to do: "Enter a date after today", not "Invalid date".
- After a failed submit, move focus to the first invalid control. Form libraries usually do this for you.
- The parts report themselves to the field after they've rendered. On a page rendered on the server, `aria-describedby` is added when the page hydrates.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on the field, or on anything around it.

```css
.form {
  --nuv-field-gap: calc(var(--spacing) * 2);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-field-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 1.5)` | Space between the parts. |
| `--nuv-field-column-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 2)` | Space between the control and the label when they're side by side. |
| `--nuv-field-required` | `var(--color-danger)` | Color of the required mark. |
| `--nuv-field-description` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Text color of the description. |
| `--nuv-field-error` | `var(--color-danger)` | Text color of the error. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-field` | Field. |
| `.nuv-field--horizontal` | orientation="horizontal" |
| `.nuv-field--vertical` | orientation="vertical" |
| `.nuv-field__description` | FieldDescription. |
| `.nuv-field__error` | FieldError. |
| `.nuv-field__required` | The required mark inside the label. |

`Field` has the `data-invalid` attribute while it's invalid and `data-disabled` while it's disabled. `FieldLabel` has the class `nuv-label`.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

The field parts are client components. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files.

You can put a field together inside a server component, as the first example on this page does. Showing an error needs state somewhere, which means a client component of your own or a form library.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Use a field for every labelled control in a form, so they all behave the same.
- Put the hint in `FieldDescription`, where a screen reader reads it with the control.
- Keep the error next to its control.

**Don't**

- Don't set `id` on the control inside `FieldControl`. Use `controlId` on `Field`.
- Don't put two controls in one field. Give each its own, and group them with a [Fieldset](page:components/fieldset).
- Don't rely on the asterisk alone. Say which fields are optional or required somewhere in words.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Put radio buttons and related checkboxes in a fieldset.
- Word the legend as the question or the thing being described.

**Don't**

- Don't use a fieldset only to draw a box around something. Use it where the group needs a name.
- Don't put a single control in one. A [Field](page:components/field) is the right wrapper for that.

Use it to let people pick files from their device or drag them in. It holds the files and nothing more: sending them to a server, and showing how that's going, is your code's job. ```tsx import { FileUpload, Label } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return (

Only applies with `multiple`. | | `onReject` | `((rejections: FileRejection[]) => void)` | | Called with the files that were turned away and the reason for each. Nothing is shown for them, so this is where you tell the person. | | `children` | `ReactNode` | `"Drop files here, or choose them from your device"` | The text in the drop area. | | `showList` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether to list the chosen files under the drop area, each with a button to take it out again. | | `removeLabel` | `((name: string) => string)` | `(name) => 'Remove ${name}'` | Accessible name of the button that takes a file out, from the file's name. New ones are added to the list. Without it, a new file takes the place of the last. | | `accept` | `string` | | Which files are allowed, as on any file input: extensions such as `.pdf`, types such as `image/png`, or a family such as `image/*`. It's checked for dropped files too. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | | Stops files from being chosen, dropped or taken out. | | `required` | `boolean` | | Inside a form, the browser won't submit until a file is chosen. | | `name` | `string` | | The name the files are submitted under in a form. | | `onChange` | `ChangeEventHandler` | | The input's own change event. It also fires after a drop and after a file is taken out. | `className` goes on the element around the drop area and the list. Everything else, `ref` and `id` included, goes to the ``. ## How it's built The drop area holds a real file input, laid over the whole of it and invisible. So a click anywhere in the area opens the browser's file picker, the keyboard reaches a real file input, and a form submits the files without any code from you. sections.heading: How it's built
sections.markdown:
## How it's built

The drop area holds a real file input, laid over the whole of it and invisible. So a click anywhere in the area opens the browser's file picker, the keyboard reaches a real file input, and a form submits the files without any code from you.

A file picker hands over its files and forgets them, so a plain file input can't add to what was chosen before, and can't take one file out. This component can. After every change it writes the full list back into the input, and fires the input's `change` event. A form library that listens to the input sees what it would see from any file input.

sections.heading: Limits
In a form
sections.markdown:
## In a form

Give it a `name` and the files are part of the form's data, under that name. `required` works as on any file input. Resetting the form empties the list.

```tsx
<form action="/upload" method="post" encType="multipart/form-data">
  <label htmlFor="report">Report</label>
  <FileUpload id="report" name="report" accept=".pdf" required />
  <Button type="submit">Send</Button>
</form>
```

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves to the file input, then to the button on each file in the list. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> | On the input, opens the file picker. On a file's button, takes that file out. |

Dragging isn't possible from the keyboard, and doesn't need to be: the picker does the same job.

### What the component handles

- The control is a native `<input type="file">`, so its role and its keyboard behavior come from the browser, and it reports the chosen files as its value.
- The text in the drop area is the input's description, after any `aria-describedby` of your own.
- While the input has keyboard focus, the ring goes around the whole drop area.
- The area's edge uses `--color-border-strong`, at least 3:1 against the page in every theme. While files are dragged over it, the edge turns solid and takes the primary color, so the change doesn't depend on color alone.
- Each file's button is named after the file, "Remove report.pdf". `removeLabel` replaces that, for another language. On a touch screen its tap area is 44 by 44 pixels.
- After a file is taken out, focus moves to the input, since the button that had it is gone.
- A file's size is written in the visitor's own number format. `formatSize` replaces that.

### What you need to handle

- Give it a name. Use a [label](page:components/label) whose `htmlFor` matches its `id`, or put it in a [Field](page:components/field).
- Say what's allowed before people choose: which kinds of file and how big. Put it in the drop area's text or in a description.
- Tell people when a file was turned away, and why. `onReject` gives you what you need.
- Uploading is yours to build, and so is saying how it's going. Announce when an upload finishes or fails, for example with a [toast](page:components/toast).

pages.title: FormattedNumber
pages.description: A number written the way a language and region write it, as plain digits, a currency, a percentage or a short form.
pages.markdown:
# FormattedNumber A number written the way a language and region write it, as plain digits, a currency, a percentage or a short form. Use it wherever a number is shown to a person: a total, a price, a count in a table. It groups the digits, puts the currency sign where the region puts it, and keeps the digits one width so a column lines up. ```tsx import { FormattedNumber } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return (
Seats
Revenue
Conversion
Requests
); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { FormattedNumber, formatNumber } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` (required) | `number` | | The number. | | `locale` | `string` | `"en-US"` | The language and region whose rules the number is written by, as a BCP 47 tag such as `"de-DE"`. It's `"en-US"` unless you say otherwise, and never the visitor's own: the server and the browser would then write two different texts for one page. | | `format` | `"currency" \| "decimal" \| "percent"` | `"decimal"` | `"percent"` takes a ratio, so 0.25 is written as 25%. `"currency"` needs `currency`. | | `currency` | `string` | | The currency, as an ISO 4217 code such as `"EUR"`. Giving one is enough to get a currency: `format` can be left out. | | `compact` | `boolean` | `false` | Writes a large number short, as in 1.2M. | | `signDisplay` | `"always" \| "auto" \| "exceptZero" \| "never"` | `"auto"` | When the sign is written. `"exceptZero"` writes a plus on a gain, for a number that's a change. | | `minimumFractionDigits` | `number` | | The fewest digits after the decimal point. | | `maximumFractionDigits` | `number` | | The most digits after the decimal point. | | `options` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` | | Anything else `Intl.NumberFormat` takes, such as a unit. What's here wins over the props above. | Everything else is passed to the `` element, including `ref` and `className`. It takes no children: the text is the number. ## Languages and regions `locale` is a BCP 47 tag. The same number and the same props give each region its own digits, separators and place for the currency. ```tsx import { FormattedNumber } from "@nuvui/react"; const places = [ { locale: "en-US", currency: "USD", name: "United States" }, { locale: "de-DE", currency: "EUR", name: "Germany" }, { locale: "fr-CH", currency: "CHF", name: "Switzerland, in French" }, { locale: "en-IN", currency: "INR", name: "India" }, { locale: "ja-JP", currency: "JPY", name: "Japan" }, ]; export default function Example() { return (
{places.map(({ locale, currency, name }) => (
{name}
))}
); } ``` The default is `"en-US"`, and not the visitor's own language. A page is written once on the server and again in the browser, and the two can disagree about the visitor's language. React then reports that the two texts don't match. Pass the locale your app already knows, from its router or its translation library, to every number. ## As text `formatNumber` gives the same text as a string, with the same options. It's for the places a component can't go: an `aria-label`, the axis of a chart, a page's title. ```tsx import { formatNumber, Progress } from "@nuvui/react"; const used = 37.4; const total = 50; export default function Example() { const unit = { options: { style: "unit", unit: "gigabyte" } } as const; return (
{formatNumber(used, unit)} of {formatNumber(total, unit)}
); } ``` A unit, as here, goes through `options`, which takes anything `Intl.NumberFormat` does. ## Accessibility A number has no keyboard behavior. It isn't a control and can't take focus. ### What the component handles - It's a `` element, read in place with the text around it. Its `value` attribute holds the plain number for anything that reads the page by machine. - The digits are one width each, so a number that updates doesn't move the text after it. - The number stays on one line. A currency sign is never left alone at the end of one. ### What you need to handle - A short form is read as it's written: a screen reader says "1.2 M", not "1.2 million". Where that matters, give the long form in an `aria-label`, written with `formatNumber` and `options={{ notation: "compact", compactDisplay: "long" }}`. - Say what the number counts. "48,250" alone means nothing. A label, a table heading or the sentence around it has to say. - A number that changes while the page is open isn't announced. If the change matters, say it in an element with `role="status"`. ## CSS variables | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-formatted-number-numeric` | `tabular-nums` | The `font-variant-numeric` of the digits. Set it to `normal` to give each digit its own width back, in running text set in a font whose even digits look loose. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-formatted-number` | Every formatted number. | ## Server components FormattedNumber has no `"use client"` directive and uses no state, so it renders in a server component as it is. `formatNumber` is a plain function and runs anywhere. ## Do and don't **Do** - Pass the same `locale` to every number on a page. - Use `compact` where room is short, and the full number where someone will act on it. **Don't** - Don't format a number yourself and then pass the text. The component needs the number. - Don't use `format="percent"` on a number that's already a percentage. It takes a ratio: 0.25 for 25%.

| `value` (required) | `number` |  | The number. |
| `locale` | `string` | `"en-US"` | The language and region whose rules the number is written by, as a BCP 47 tag such as `"de-DE"`. It's `"en-US"` unless you say otherwise, and never the visitor's own: the server and the browser would then write two different texts for one page. |
| `format` | `"currency" \| "decimal" \| "percent"` | `"decimal"` | `"percent"` takes a ratio, so 0.25 is written as 25%. `"currency"` needs `currency`. |
| `currency` | `string` |  | The currency, as an ISO 4217 code such as `"EUR"`. Giving one is enough to get a currency: `format` can be left out. |
| `compact` | `boolean` | `false` | Writes a large number short, as in 1.2M. |
| `signDisplay` | `"always" \| "auto" \| "exceptZero" \| "never"` | `"auto"` | When the sign is written. `"exceptZero"` writes a plus on a gain, for a number that's a change. |
| `minimumFractionDigits` | `number` |  | The fewest digits after the decimal point. |
| `maximumFractionDigits` | `number` |  | The most digits after the decimal point. |
| `options` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` |  | Anything else `Intl.NumberFormat` takes, such as a unit. What's here wins over the props above. |

Everything else is passed to the `<data>` element, including `ref` and `className`. It takes no children: the text is the number.

sections.heading: Languages and regions
As text
Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

A number has no keyboard behavior. It isn't a control and can't take focus.

### What the component handles

- It's a `<data>` element, read in place with the text around it. Its `value` attribute holds the plain number for anything that reads the page by machine.
- The digits are one width each, so a number that updates doesn't move the text after it.
- The number stays on one line. A currency sign is never left alone at the end of one.

### What you need to handle

- A short form is read as it's written: a screen reader says "1.2 M", not "1.2 million". Where that matters, give the long form in an `aria-label`, written with `formatNumber` and `options={{ notation: "compact", compactDisplay: "long" }}`.
- Say what the number counts. "48,250" alone means nothing. A label, a table heading or the sentence around it has to say.
- A number that changes while the page is open isn't announced. If the change matters, say it in an element with `role="status"`.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-formatted-number-numeric` | `tabular-nums` | The `font-variant-numeric` of the digits. Set it to `normal` to give each digit its own width back, in running text set in a font whose even digits look loose. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-formatted-number` | Every formatted number. |

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

FormattedNumber has no `"use client"` directive and uses no state, so it renders in a server component as it is. `formatNumber` is a plain function and runs anywhere.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Pass the same `locale` to every number on a page.
- Use `compact` where room is short, and the full number where someone will act on it.

**Don't**

- Don't format a number yourself and then pass the text. The component needs the number.
- Don't use `format="percent"` on a number that's already a percentage. It takes a ratio: 0.25 for 25%.

pages.description: A button that acts only after it's been held down, with the wait drawn along its edge, for things that can't be undone.
pages.markdown:
# HoldToConfirm A button that acts only after it's been held down, with the wait drawn along its edge, for things that can't be undone. Use hold to confirm for something that can't be undone and isn't worth stopping for: removing a row, discarding a draft, ending a session. Holding takes a moment of intent, which a stray click doesn't have. For something with consequences worth reading first, use an [alert dialog](page:components/alert-dialog). ```tsx "use client"; import { HoldToConfirm } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { const [deleted, setDeleted] = useState(0); return (
setDeleted(deleted + 1)}> Hold to delete

Deleted {deleted} {deleted === 1 ? "time" : "times"}

); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { HoldToConfirm } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `onConfirm` (required) | `() => void` | | Called once the button has been held for the whole of `duration`, or pressed twice by someone whose way of pressing can't be held. | | `duration` | `number` | `1500` | How long the button has to be held, in milliseconds. | | `hint` | `string` | `"Hold down to confirm."` | What a screen reader says about the button, and says again when it's let go of too soon. Translate it with the rest of your interface. | | `againLabel` | `string` | `"Press again to confirm."` | What a screen reader says after the first of two presses. Translate it with the rest of your interface. | It's a [`Button`](page:components/button), and takes what one takes: `intent`, which is `"danger"` here unless you say otherwise, `size`, `disabled`, `ref` and `className`. It doesn't take `asChild`: what's held has to be a button. ## How long to hold `duration` is in milliseconds, and 1500 by default. Shorter than about 800 and a slow click gets through. Longer than about 3000 and people give up, or wonder whether it's working. Letting go before the time is up cancels, and the bar along the bottom of the button drains away. So does moving the pointer off the button, and moving focus away. ## Pressing without holding Not everything that presses a button can hold it. A screen reader, a switch and a voice command each send one press, with no down and no up. For those, the first press asks for a second, and the second within five seconds confirms. The button says so: "Press again to confirm." Nobody chooses between the two ways. A press that begins with a pointer or a key going down is a hold, and one that arrives with neither is the first of two. ## Say what holding does The button's text is yours, and it's the only instruction a sighted person gets. Start it with "Hold to": "Hold to delete", "Hold to discard". A button that says only "Delete" and then does nothing on a click looks broken. ## Accessibility | Key | What it does | | --- | --- | | Space or Enter, held down | Starts the wait. Confirms when the time is up. | | Space or Enter, let go | Cancels, if the time isn't up. | | Tab | Moves on, and cancels a hold. | ### What the component handles - The button is described by `hint`, "Hold down to confirm.", which a screen reader reads after its name. - Letting go too soon says the hint again, in a status that's in the page from the start. - A press that can't be held is asked for twice, and the first one says "Press again to confirm." - The bar is a picture and is hidden from screen readers. - The bar is under the button's text and not behind it, so the text is as easy to read while it's held as when it isn't. - The bar moves for everyone, including a visitor who asked for less motion. It's the only thing that shows how much longer to hold, and it's one slow fill, not a decoration. - Where the browser forces its own colors the bar is drawn in the highlight color. - A finger held on the button doesn't scroll the page or open the phone's menu. ### What you need to handle - Translate `hint` and `againLabel`. [Translation](page:translation) lists them. - Say what happened afterwards, in a [toast](page:components/toast) or in the page. The button doesn't. - Move focus somewhere sensible if confirming removes the button. - Where a mistake would be costly, offer an undo as well, or use an [alert dialog](page:components/alert-dialog). Holding is harder for some people than a press, whatever they press with. ## On small screens The button is 44 pixels tall with a finger, as any button is. A held finger covers a small button, and the bar with it, so let the button be as wide as its text and more. ## CSS variables Set any of these on the `HoldToConfirm`, or on anything around it. The [button's own variables](page:components/button#css-variables) work here too. ```css .danger-zone { --nuv-hold-to-confirm-progress-size: 6px; } ``` | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-hold-to-confirm-progress-size` | `4px` | Thickness of the bar. | | `--nuv-hold-to-confirm-progress` | `currentcolor` | Color of the bar. The button's text color by default, so it suits every intent. Keep it at 3:1 against the button. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-hold-to-confirm` | HoldToConfirm. On the button, with the button's own classes. | | `.nuv-hold-to-confirm__label` | What wraps the button's content. | | `.nuv-hold-to-confirm__progress` | The bar. | | `.nuv-hold-to-confirm__status` | What's said to a screen reader, drawn for nobody. It comes after the button. | What the button is doing is in a `data-state` attribute: `idle`, `holding`, or `armed` after the first of two presses. ## Server components HoldToConfirm starts with `"use client"`: it keeps time. `onConfirm` is a function, so the component that renders it has to be a client component too, or pass a server action. ## Do and don't **Do** - Start the button's text with "Hold to". - Use it where the action is clear from where the button is: in a row, on a card. **Don't** - Don't use it for an action that can be undone. A plain button and an undo is quicker for everyone. - Don't use it for the main action of a form. - Don't stack it with a dialog. One way of being sure is enough.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onConfirm` (required) | `() => void` |  | Called once the button has been held for the whole of `duration`, or pressed twice by someone whose way of pressing can't be held. |

| `hint` | `string` | `"Hold down to confirm."` | What a screen reader says about the button, and says again when it's let go of too soon. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |
