sections.markdown:
## How long to hold

`duration` is in milliseconds, and 1500 by default. Shorter than about 800 and a slow click gets through. Longer than about 3000 and people give up, or wonder whether it's working.

Letting go before the time is up cancels, and the bar along the bottom of the button drains away. So does moving the pointer off the button, and moving focus away.

sections.heading: Pressing without holding
sections.markdown:
## Pressing without holding

Not everything that presses a button can hold it. A screen reader, a switch and a voice command each send one press, with no down and no up. For those, the first press asks for a second, and the second within five seconds confirms. The button says so: "Press again to confirm."

Nobody chooses between the two ways. A press that begins with a pointer or a key going down is a hold, and one that arrives with neither is the first of two.

sections.heading: Say what holding does
sections.markdown:
## Say what holding does

The button's text is yours, and it's the only instruction a sighted person gets. Start it with "Hold to": "Hold to delete", "Hold to discard". A button that says only "Delete" and then does nothing on a click looks broken.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Space or Enter, held down | Starts the wait. Confirms when the time is up. |
| Space or Enter, let go | Cancels, if the time isn't up. |
| Tab | Moves on, and cancels a hold. |

### What the component handles

- The button is described by `hint`, "Hold down to confirm.", which a screen reader reads after its name.
- Letting go too soon says the hint again, in a status that's in the page from the start.
- A press that can't be held is asked for twice, and the first one says "Press again to confirm."
- The bar is a picture and is hidden from screen readers.
- The bar is under the button's text and not behind it, so the text is as easy to read while it's held as when it isn't.
- The bar moves for everyone, including a visitor who asked for less motion. It's the only thing that shows how much longer to hold, and it's one slow fill, not a decoration.
- Where the browser forces its own colors the bar is drawn in the highlight color.
- A finger held on the button doesn't scroll the page or open the phone's menu.

### What you need to handle

- Translate `hint` and `againLabel`. [Translation](page:translation) lists them.
- Say what happened afterwards, in a [toast](page:components/toast) or in the page. The button doesn't.
- Move focus somewhere sensible if confirming removes the button.
- Where a mistake would be costly, offer an undo as well, or use an [alert dialog](page:components/alert-dialog). Holding is harder for some people than a press, whatever they press with.

pages.title: HoloCard
pages.description: A 3D tilting card with a pointer-tracked holographic glare and texture overlay, built for membership cards, passes, and collectibles.
pages.markdown:
# HoloCard A 3D tilting card with a pointer-tracked holographic glare and texture overlay, built for membership cards, passes, and collectibles. Use a holo card for the one thing on a screen that's meant to feel like an object: a membership card, an event pass, a badge someone earned. It's decoration. For content in a box, use a [card](page:components/card). ```tsx import { HoloCard } from "@nuvui/react"; import type { CSSProperties } from "react"; // The face's colors are the card's, so the glare and the texture lie on // the face and the words float over them. const face = { "--nuv-holo-card-bg": "var(--color-primary)", "--nuv-holo-card-fg": "var(--color-primary-foreground)", inlineSize: "100%", maxInlineSize: 340, } as CSSProperties; export default function Example() { return (
Northwind Rewards Gold member
Sajan 4821 0093 5567
); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { HoloCard } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `shine` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether a shine is drawn across it under the pointer. | | `texture` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether an embossed texture is drawn on its face: fine lines pressed into the card, which catch the light under the pointer. | | `lift` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether what's on it rises off its face while the pointer is on the card, so that it floats over the face as the card tilts. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | It lies flat and doesn't follow the pointer. | It's a `div`, and takes what a `div` takes, including `ref` and `className`. ## The face and what's on it The card has a face, and what you put in it lies on that face. Give the face its color with `--nuv-holo-card-bg`, which takes anything `background` does, a picture included, and the text its color with `--nuv-holo-card-fg`. ```tsx ``` The glare and the texture are drawn on the face, under the content. So don't give what you put in the card a background of its own: it would cover them. ## Floating content While the pointer is on the card, what's on it rises off the face toward you, and throws a shadow on the face away from the pointer. As the card tilts, the words move against the face behind them, which is what makes them look as if they float. At rest they lie on the face, at the size you gave them. `lift={false}` keeps them on the face. `--nuv-holo-card-lift` says how far they rise. Nothing is cut off at the card's edges, since cutting would press everything flat again. Keep what's in the card inside its padding. ## How it moves A mouse or a pen over the card tilts it, with the side under the pointer going down as if pressed, and draws a shine where the pointer is. When the pointer leaves, the card goes flat again. A finger doesn't move it. A finger on a card is usually on its way to scroll the page, and a card that turned under it would get in the way. The keyboard doesn't move it either. So nothing the card says may depend on the tilt or the shine. ## Your own look How far it tilts, its corners and the shine are CSS variables. The shine's colored band is the theme's primary, success, warning and danger colors unless you give it a gradient of your own. ```tsx import { HoloCard } from "@nuvui/react"; import type { CSSProperties } from "react"; // A steeper tilt, square corners, words that rise further, and a foil // of one color where the default has the theme's four. const look = { "--nuv-holo-card-bg": "var(--color-surface)", "--nuv-holo-card-fg": "var(--color-surface-foreground)", "--nuv-holo-card-lift": "2.5rem", "--nuv-holo-card-tilt": "14deg", "--nuv-holo-card-radius": "var(--radius-sm)", "--nuv-holo-card-foil": "linear-gradient(115deg, transparent 30%, var(--color-warning) 50%, transparent 70%)", inlineSize: "100%", maxInlineSize: 340, } as CSSProperties; export default function Example() { return (
Sales kickoff 2027 Speaker Tom Becker, Finance
); } ``` ## The texture On the card's face is an embossed texture: fine lines pressed into it both ways, each a line of light beside a line of shade. It's faint while the card is at rest, and shows more under the pointer, where it catches the light. `texture={false}` leaves it out. ```tsx ``` The pattern is a CSS variable, `--nuv-holo-card-texture`, which takes any background image: gradients of your own, or a picture of a pattern. ## Accessibility A holo card has no role and no keyboard behavior. It can't take focus. What's in it can, and is read, pressed and selected as it would be anywhere. ### What the component handles - The shine and the texture are hidden from screen readers and let presses through to what's under them. - For a visitor who asked for less motion, the card doesn't tilt, has no shine, and its content stays on the face. The texture stays, and doesn't change. - Where the browser forces its own colors, there's no shine and no texture. - The shine and the texture are on the face, under the content. Neither is ever over the text. ### What you need to handle - The texture and the shine change the face's color behind the text a little, the shine only while the pointer is on the card. Keep text on the card well above 4.5:1 against the face, or lower `--nuv-holo-card-texture-opacity` and `--nuv-holo-card-shine-opacity`. An automatic check can't measure text over a pattern, so look at it yourself. - Don't put anything on a card that needs careful aim, such as a small link. The card moves a little under the pointer. - Use one on a screen, not a grid of them. ## CSS variables Set any of these on the `HoloCard`, or on anything around it. ```css .pass { --nuv-holo-card-tilt: 12deg; } ``` | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-holo-card-radius` | `var(--radius-xl)` | Corner radius of the card and its face. | | `--nuv-holo-card-perspective` | `50rem` | How far away the card is looked at from. A smaller distance makes the tilt look deeper. | | `--nuv-holo-card-bg` | `transparent` | The face: a color, a gradient or a picture. Anything background takes. | | `--nuv-holo-card-fg` | `inherit` | Color of the text on the card. | | `--nuv-holo-card-pointer-y` | `0.5` | Where the pointer is down the card, from 0 to 1. The component writes this. Don't set it. | | `--nuv-holo-card-tilt` | `8deg` | How far it turns when the pointer is at an edge. | | `--nuv-holo-card-pointer-x` | `0.5` | Where the pointer is across the card, from 0 to 1. The component writes this. Don't set it. | | `--nuv-holo-card-duration` | `400ms` | How long it takes to go flat again, and the shine to fade. | | `--nuv-holo-card-lift` | `1.5rem` | How far the content rises off the face under the pointer. | | `--nuv-holo-card-shadow` | `var(--color-black)` | Color of the shadow the risen content throws on the face. | | `--nuv-holo-card-texture` | `repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-white) 70%, transparent) 0 1px, color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-black) 55%, transparent) 1px 2px, transparent 2px 7px), repeating-linear-gradient(-45deg, color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-white) 70%, transparent) 0 1px, color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-black) 55%, transparent) 1px 2px, transparent 2px 7px)` | The texture, as a background image. Lines both ways unless you give it another. | | `--nuv-holo-card-texture-opacity` | `0.2` | How strong the texture is at rest. Under the pointer it's two and a half times this. | | `--nuv-holo-card-glare` | `var(--color-white)` | Color of the soft light under the pointer. | | `--nuv-holo-card-foil` | `linear-gradient(115deg, transparent 25%, var(--color-primary) 38%, var(--color-success) 46%, var(--color-warning) 54%, var(--color-danger) 62%, transparent 75%)` | The colored band, as a gradient. It's drawn two and a half times the card's size and slides with the pointer. | | `--nuv-holo-card-shine-opacity` | `0.7` | How strong the shine is while the pointer is on the card. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-holo-card` | HoloCard. The box the pointer is measured in, which doesn't turn. | | `.nuv-holo-card--lift` | With lift. The content rises off the face under the pointer. | | `.nuv-holo-card__content` | What you put in, over the face. | | `.nuv-holo-card__shine` | The shine, on the face. | | `.nuv-holo-card__surface` | The face. It's what turns. | | `.nuv-holo-card__texture` | The embossed texture, on the face. | While a pointer is on it the card has a `data-active` attribute, and with `disabled` a `data-disabled` one. ## Server components HoloCard starts with `"use client"`: it follows the pointer. It takes no functions, so a server component can render it and put server-rendered content in it. ## Do and don't **Do** - Give it a face with `--nuv-holo-card-bg`: a color, a gradient or a picture. - Keep it to things that stand for an object someone holds. **Don't** - Don't use it for ordinary content, a form or a row in a list. Movement under the pointer makes those harder to use. - Don't make it the only way to see anything.

## Floating content

While the pointer is on the card, what's on it rises off the face toward you, and throws a shadow on the face away from the pointer. As the card tilts, the words move against the face behind them, which is what makes them look as if they float. At rest they lie on the face, at the size you gave them.

`lift={false}` keeps them on the face. `--nuv-holo-card-lift` says how far they rise.

Nothing is cut off at the card's edges, since cutting would press everything flat again. Keep what's in the card inside its padding.

sections.heading: How it moves
sections.markdown:
## How it moves

A mouse or a pen over the card tilts it, with the side under the pointer going down as if pressed, and draws a shine where the pointer is. When the pointer leaves, the card goes flat again.

A finger doesn't move it. A finger on a card is usually on its way to scroll the page, and a card that turned under it would get in the way. The keyboard doesn't move it either. So nothing the card says may depend on the tilt or the shine.

sections.heading: Your own look
The texture
sections.markdown:
## The texture

On the card's face is an embossed texture: fine lines pressed into it both ways, each a line of light beside a line of shade. It's faint while the card is at rest, and shows more under the pointer, where it catches the light. `texture={false}` leaves it out.

```tsx
<HoloCard texture={false}>
  <MemberCard />
</HoloCard>
```

The pattern is a CSS variable, `--nuv-holo-card-texture`, which takes any background image: gradients of your own, or a picture of a pattern.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

A holo card has no role and no keyboard behavior. It can't take focus. What's in it can, and is read, pressed and selected as it would be anywhere.

### What the component handles

- The shine and the texture are hidden from screen readers and let presses through to what's under them.
- For a visitor who asked for less motion, the card doesn't tilt, has no shine, and its content stays on the face. The texture stays, and doesn't change.
- Where the browser forces its own colors, there's no shine and no texture.
- The shine and the texture are on the face, under the content. Neither is ever over the text.

### What you need to handle

- The texture and the shine change the face's color behind the text a little, the shine only while the pointer is on the card. Keep text on the card well above 4.5:1 against the face, or lower `--nuv-holo-card-texture-opacity` and `--nuv-holo-card-shine-opacity`. An automatic check can't measure text over a pattern, so look at it yourself.
- Don't put anything on a card that needs careful aim, such as a small link. The card moves a little under the pointer.
- Use one on a screen, not a grid of them.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on the `HoloCard`, or on anything around it.

```css
.pass {
  --nuv-holo-card-tilt: 12deg;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-holo-card-radius` | `var(--radius-xl)` | Corner radius of the card and its face. |
| `--nuv-holo-card-perspective` | `50rem` | How far away the card is looked at from. A smaller distance makes the tilt look deeper. |
| `--nuv-holo-card-bg` | `transparent` | The face: a color, a gradient or a picture. Anything background takes. |
| `--nuv-holo-card-fg` | `inherit` | Color of the text on the card. |
| `--nuv-holo-card-pointer-y` | `0.5` | Where the pointer is down the card, from 0 to 1. The component writes this. Don't set it. |
| `--nuv-holo-card-tilt` | `8deg` | How far it turns when the pointer is at an edge. |
| `--nuv-holo-card-pointer-x` | `0.5` | Where the pointer is across the card, from 0 to 1. The component writes this. Don't set it. |
| `--nuv-holo-card-duration` | `400ms` | How long it takes to go flat again, and the shine to fade. |
| `--nuv-holo-card-lift` | `1.5rem` | How far the content rises off the face under the pointer. |
| `--nuv-holo-card-shadow` | `var(--color-black)` | Color of the shadow the risen content throws on the face. |
| `--nuv-holo-card-texture` | `repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-white) 70%, transparent) 0 1px, color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-black) 55%, transparent) 1px 2px, transparent 2px 7px), repeating-linear-gradient(-45deg, color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-white) 70%, transparent) 0 1px, color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-black) 55%, transparent) 1px 2px, transparent 2px 7px)` | The texture, as a background image. Lines both ways unless you give it another. |
| `--nuv-holo-card-texture-opacity` | `0.2` | How strong the texture is at rest. Under the pointer it's two and a half times this. |
| `--nuv-holo-card-glare` | `var(--color-white)` | Color of the soft light under the pointer. |
| `--nuv-holo-card-foil` | `linear-gradient(115deg, transparent 25%, var(--color-primary) 38%, var(--color-success) 46%, var(--color-warning) 54%, var(--color-danger) 62%, transparent 75%)` | The colored band, as a gradient. It's drawn two and a half times the card's size and slides with the pointer. |
| `--nuv-holo-card-shine-opacity` | `0.7` | How strong the shine is while the pointer is on the card. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-holo-card` | HoloCard. The box the pointer is measured in, which doesn't turn. |
| `.nuv-holo-card--lift` | With lift. The content rises off the face under the pointer. |
| `.nuv-holo-card__content` | What you put in, over the face. |
| `.nuv-holo-card__shine` | The shine, on the face. |
| `.nuv-holo-card__surface` | The face. It's what turns. |
| `.nuv-holo-card__texture` | The embossed texture, on the face. |

While a pointer is on it the card has a `data-active` attribute, and with `disabled` a `data-disabled` one.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

HoloCard starts with `"use client"`: it follows the pointer. It takes no functions, so a server component can render it and put server-rendered content in it.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Give it a face with `--nuv-holo-card-bg`: a color, a gradient or a picture.
- Keep it to things that stand for an object someone holds.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for ordinary content, a form or a row in a list. Movement under the pointer makes those harder to use.
- Don't make it the only way to see anything.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { HoverCard, HoverCardContent, HoverCardTrigger } from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `HoverCard` | Holds the open state and the timing. Renders nothing itself. |
| `HoverCardTrigger` | The link the card belongs to. It renders an `a`, and takes `href` like one. |
| `HoverCardContent` | The card. |

These are separate exports, not properties of `HoverCard`. `HoverCard.Content` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

### HoverCardContent

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sideOffset` | `number` | `8` | The gap between the trigger and the card, in pixels. |
| `collisionPadding` | `number \| Partial<Record<"bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top", number>>` | `8` | How close the card may get to the edge of the screen, in pixels. It moves or flips to keep this much room. |
| `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the card is rendered into. Set this when the card should pick up a `data-theme` from a section of the page. |

These come from Radix and are the ones you're most likely to set:

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `side` | `"bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top"` |  | The side of the link the card opens on. It's `"bottom"` unless you say otherwise, and it flips to the opposite side when there isn't room. |
| `align` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start"` |  | How the card lines up with the link along that side. It's `"center"` unless you say otherwise. |

### HoverCard

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `openDelay` | `number` |  | How long the pointer has to rest on the link before the card shows, in milliseconds. It's 700 unless you say otherwise. |
| `closeDelay` | `number` |  | How long the card stays after the pointer leaves, in milliseconds. It's 300 unless you say otherwise. |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Whether it's showing, when you control it yourself. Use it with `onOpenChange`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` |  | Whether it starts out showing, when you don't control it. |
| `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean) => void)` |  | Called when it shows or hides. |

`HoverCardTrigger` takes what an `a` takes, and `asChild` to render your router's link in its place. The [Radix Hover Card reference](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/hover-card#api-reference) has the full list.

## Timing The card waits 700 milliseconds before it shows, so that it doesn't flash up under a pointer that's only passing over. It stays for 300 after the pointer leaves, which is what lets the pointer cross the gap from the link to the card. ```tsx import { HoverCard, HoverCardContent, HoverCardTrigger } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return ( Theming guide Theming

Presets, density, and how to change a token for one section of a page.

); } ``` Shorten `openDelay` where the cards are the point of the page. Don't set `closeDelay` to zero: the card would close before the pointer could reach it.

sections.heading: On touch screens
sections.markdown:
## On touch screens

A tap on the link doesn't open the card. The link goes where it goes. That's how Radix handles touch, and this library doesn't change it.

So treat the card as a preview and nothing more. Whatever it shows has to be on the page the link opens.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves focus to the link, which shows the card after the same delay as the pointer. Moving on hides it. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Follows the link. |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Hides the card. Focus stays on the link. |

<kbd>Tab</kbd> doesn't go into the card. Radix takes any link or button inside it out of the tab order, because the card closes as soon as focus leaves its link.

### What the component handles

Most of this is Radix. The library doesn't change it.

- The card shows on keyboard focus as well as on hover.
- It stays while the pointer moves from the link onto the card, and <kbd>Esc</kbd> hides it without moving the pointer. WCAG 1.4.13 asks for both.
- Text in the card can be selected with the mouse, and the card stays open while it is.
- It never runs off the screen. A card with more in it than fits scrolls inside itself.
- It only fades in when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion.

### What you need to handle

- The card isn't tied to its link for screen readers: it has no role, and the link isn't described by it. Someone using a screen reader may never come across it. This is the main reason the card can only repeat what the linked page says.
- Don't put the only way to do something in the card. A "Follow" button there can't be reached by keyboard or on a phone.
- The link needs text that makes sense without the card.
- Style the link yourself. `HoverCardTrigger` adds no class, so it looks like the other links on your page.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Hover cards render at the end of `<body>`, so set these on `:root` or `body`, or straight on `HoverCardContent` with `style` or a class.

```css
:root {
  --nuv-hover-card-width: 22rem;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-hover-card-width` | `18rem` | Width of the card. It's never wider than the room beside the link. |
| `--nuv-hover-card-padding` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 4)` | Padding inside the card. |
| `--nuv-hover-card-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Border color. |
| `--nuv-hover-card-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius. |
| `--nuv-hover-card-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color. |
| `--nuv-hover-card-shadow` | `var(--shadow-lg)` | Shadow under the card. |
| `--nuv-hover-card-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-hover-card` | HoverCardContent. |

Radix sets `data-state="open"` or `data-state="closed"` on the link and the card, and `data-side` on the card for where it ended up. The animation hangs off `data-state`.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

The hover card parts are client components. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files.

You can put a hover card together inside a server component, as the examples on this page do.

sections.heading: Themed sections
sections.markdown:
## Themed sections

A card opened from inside a `data-theme="dark"` section doesn't inherit that theme, because it isn't rendered inside the section. Pass the section's element as `container` and it will be.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Keep the card to a few lines: a name, a role, a sentence.
- Use it on links, where there's a page to fall back on.
- Load what the card shows before it opens, or keep its size steady while it loads.

**Don't**

- Don't put anything in the card that isn't on the linked page.
- Don't put buttons, forms or menus in it. For those, use a [popover](page:components/popover), which opens on a click.
- Don't use one to explain a button. That's a [tooltip](page:components/tooltip).

pages.title: Input
pages.description: A one-line text field. It's the browser's own input with the library's styles, so every type and attribute works.
pages.markdown:
# Input A one-line text field. It's the browser's own input with the library's styles, so every type and attribute works. Use an input for a short piece of text: a name, an email address, a number, a date. For several lines, use a [textarea](page:components/textarea). To give it a label, a hint and an error message that screen readers tie together, put it in a [Field](page:components/field). ```tsx import { Input, Label } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return (
); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Input } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Props Input adds no props of its own. These are the ones you'll reach for most. | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `type` | `HTMLInputTypeAttribute` | | What kind of value it takes. The browser picks the keyboard and the checks to match. | | `value` | `string \| number \| readonly string[]` | | The text, when you control it yourself. Use it with `onChange`. | | `defaultValue` | `string \| number \| readonly string[]` | | The text it starts with, when you don't control it. | | `placeholder` | `string` | | An example of what to type, shown while it's empty. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | | Stops it from being focused or changed, and leaves it out of the form. | | `readOnly` | `boolean` | | Lets the text be selected and copied and not changed. It's still submitted. | | `required` | `boolean` | | Inside a form, the browser won't submit while it's empty. | | `name` | `string` | | The name the value is submitted under in a form. | | `autoComplete` | `HTMLInputAutoCompleteAttribute` | | What the browser may fill in, such as `"email"` or `"name"`. | Everything else is passed to the `` element, including `ref`, `id`, `className` and event handlers. ## Types `type` goes straight to the browser. On a phone it decides which keyboard opens. ```tsx import { Input, Label } from "@nuvui/react"; const field = { display: "grid", gap: 6 }; export default function Example() { return (
); } ``` `type="file"` gets the browser's own button, styled to match. For a drop area and a list of the chosen files, use [FileUpload](page:components/file-upload). For a password with a button that shows it, use [PasswordInput](page:components/password-input). ## States ```tsx import { Input, Label } from "@nuvui/react"; const field = { display: "grid", gap: 6 }; export default function Example() { return (
Enter an email address, like ada@example.com.
); } ``` Set `aria-invalid` and the edge turns to the danger color. Color isn't enough to go on, so say what's wrong in words too, and tie the message to the input with `aria-describedby`. [Field](page:components/field) does both. A read-only input is filled with the muted color, so it's clear that it isn't waiting for input. ## Width An input fills the width of its container. Give the container a width, or set `--nuv-input-width`. ## On small screens An input is 44 pixels tall on a touch screen and 40 with a mouse, where [density](page:theming#density) moves it. Its text is 16 pixels on a touch screen and 14 with a mouse. iOS zooms the page in when a field with text under 16 pixels takes focus, and doesn't zoom back out. ## Accessibility ### Keyboard | Key | What it does | | --- | --- | | Tab | Moves focus to the input. Disabled ones are skipped. | Everything else is the browser's own text editing. ### What the component handles - It renders a native ``, so the role, the keyboard and form submission come from the browser. - The edge uses `--color-border-strong`, which has at least 3:1 contrast with the page in every theme, so an empty input is still visible as a control. - The placeholder uses `--color-muted-foreground` at full opacity, which has at least 4.5:1 against the input. Firefox would otherwise fade it. - Focus shows a 2 pixel ring in `--color-ring`. - The edge only animates when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion. ### What you need to handle - Give it a name. Use a [label](page:components/label) whose `htmlFor` matches the input's `id`, or `aria-label` when there's no visible text. - Set `autoComplete` on fields about the person filling in the form, such as their name, email and address. It lets the browser fill them in, and WCAG asks for it. A field about someone else, such as a teammate to invite, takes `autoComplete="off"`, or the browser offers the reader's own details for it. - When the value is wrong, set `aria-invalid` and describe the problem in text. ## CSS variables Set any of these on the input, or on anything around it. ```css .search { --nuv-input-radius: var(--radius-full); } ``` | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-input-width` | `100%` | Width. It fills its container by default. | | `--nuv-input-padding-inline` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 3)` | Padding left and right. | | `--nuv-input-border` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Border color. | | `--nuv-input-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius. | | `--nuv-input-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color. | | `--nuv-input-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Text color. | | `--nuv-input-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-md)` | Minimum height. sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { Input } from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

Input adds no props of its own. These are the ones you'll reach for most.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `HTMLInputTypeAttribute` |  | What kind of value it takes. The browser picks the keyboard and the checks to match. |
| `value` | `string \| number \| readonly string[]` |  | The text, when you control it yourself. Use it with `onChange`. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| number \| readonly string[]` |  | The text it starts with, when you don't control it. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  | An example of what to type, shown while it's empty. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Stops it from being focused or changed, and leaves it out of the form. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` |  | Lets the text be selected and copied and not changed. It's still submitted. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Inside a form, the browser won't submit while it's empty. |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the value is submitted under in a form. |
| `autoComplete` | `HTMLInputAutoCompleteAttribute` |  | What the browser may fill in, such as `"email"` or `"name"`. |

Everything else is passed to the `<input>` element, including `ref`, `id`, `className` and event handlers.

sections.heading: Types
sections.markdown:
## Types `type` goes straight to the browser. On a phone it decides which keyboard opens. ```tsx import { Input, Label } from "@nuvui/react"; const field = { display: "grid", gap: 6 }; export default function Example() { return (
); } ``` `type="file"` gets the browser's own button, styled to match. For a drop area and a list of the chosen files, use [FileUpload](page:components/file-upload). For a password with a button that shows it, use [PasswordInput](page:components/password-input).

sections.heading: States
sections.markdown:
## States ```tsx import { Input, Label } from "@nuvui/react"; const field = { display: "grid", gap: 6 }; export default function Example() { return (
Enter an email address, like ada@example.com.
); } ``` Set `aria-invalid` and the edge turns to the danger color. Color isn't enough to go on, so say what's wrong in words too, and tie the message to the input with `aria-describedby`. [Field](page:components/field) does both. A read-only input is filled with the muted color, so it's clear that it isn't waiting for input.

sections.heading: Width
sections.markdown:
## Width

An input fills the width of its container. Give the container a width, or set `--nuv-input-width`.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

An input is 44 pixels tall on a touch screen and 40 with a mouse, where [density](page:theming#density) moves it.

Its text is 16 pixels on a touch screen and 14 with a mouse. iOS zooms the page in when a field with text under 16 pixels takes focus, and doesn't zoom back out.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves focus to the input. Disabled ones are skipped. |

Everything else is the browser's own text editing.

### What the component handles

- It renders a native `<input>`, so the role, the keyboard and form submission come from the browser.
- The edge uses `--color-border-strong`, which has at least 3:1 contrast with the page in every theme, so an empty input is still visible as a control.
- The placeholder uses `--color-muted-foreground` at full opacity, which has at least 4.5:1 against the input. Firefox would otherwise fade it.
- Focus shows a 2 pixel ring in `--color-ring`.
- The edge only animates when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion.

### What you need to handle

- Give it a name. Use a [label](page:components/label) whose `htmlFor` matches the input's `id`, or `aria-label` when there's no visible text.
- Set `autoComplete` on fields about the person filling in the form, such as their name, email and address. It lets the browser fill them in, and WCAG asks for it. A field about someone else, such as a teammate to invite, takes `autoComplete="off"`, or the browser offers the reader's own details for it.
- When the value is wrong, set `aria-invalid` and describe the problem in text.

| `--nuv-input-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Text color. |
| `--nuv-input-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-md)` | Minimum height. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. |
| `--nuv-input-font-size` | `var(--text-base)`, `var(--text-sm)` | Font size. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. Keep it at 16px or more on phones. |
| `--nuv-input-placeholder` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the placeholder. |
| `--nuv-input-readonly-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background color while read-only. |

# InputGroup An input with text, an icon or a small button inside the same box, before or after what's typed. Use an input group when something belongs inside the field with the value: a unit, a currency sign, the fixed start of an address, a search icon, a button that clears or copies. To join a full-size button to the side of an input, use a [ButtonGroup](page:components/button-group). ```tsx import { Input, InputGroup, InputGroupAddon, Label } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return (

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `InputGroup` | The box. It draws the edge, and the input inside gives up its own. |
| `Input` | The ordinary [Input](page:components/input). |
| `InputGroupAddon` | Text or an icon that isn't interactive. |
| `InputGroupButton` | A small button inside the box. |

Write the parts in the order they should appear. The first is at the start of the line, which is the right in a right-to-left layout.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

None of the parts add props of their own. `InputGroup` and `InputGroupAddon` take those of a `<div>`, and `InputGroupButton` those of a `<button>`.

One default differs from HTML. The `type` of `InputGroupButton` is `"button"`, not `"submit"`, so it doesn't submit a form around it.

sections.heading: Icons and buttons
Units
sections.markdown:
## Units ```tsx import { Field, FieldControl, FieldError, FieldLabel, Input, InputGroup, InputGroupAddon, } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return (
Monthly budget $ USD Discount % Enter a number from 0 to 100.
); } ``` Inside a [Field](page:components/field), wrap the input in `FieldControl`, not the group. The group takes its invalid edge and its disabled look from the input.

sections.heading: How the box behaves
sections.markdown:
## How the box behaves

- A press anywhere in the box that isn't on a button or the input itself puts the cursor in the input. The text and icons beside it read as part of the field, so they act like it.
- While the input has keyboard focus, the ring goes around the whole box. While a button inside has focus, the ring is around that button.
- When the input has `aria-invalid`, the box's edge turns to the danger color. When the input is disabled, the box fades.

The last two use the CSS `:has()` selector, which arrived in Firefox 121. In an older Firefox the ring shows while anything in the box has focus, and the edge doesn't change for an invalid input. The error message still shows.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

The box is 44 pixels tall on a touch screen and 40 with a mouse, where [density](page:theming#density) moves it. A button inside is drawn 8 pixels shorter than the box. On a touch screen the area that responds to a tap is 44 by 44 pixels, centered on the button.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves to the input, then to each button, in the order they're written. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> | On a button, presses it. |

### What the component handles

- The group adds no role. A screen reader meets the input and the buttons as it would outside one.
- The box's edge uses `--color-border-strong`, which has at least 3:1 contrast with the page in every theme.
- Text in an addon uses `--color-muted-foreground`, which has at least 4.5:1 against the box.

### What you need to handle

- An addon isn't part of the input's name. A screen reader reads "Monthly budget", not "dollars". If the unit matters to understanding the field, put it in the label too: "Monthly budget in US dollars".
- Give every icon-only button an `aria-label`.
- Label the input itself, with a [label](page:components/label) or `aria-label`.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on the group, or on anything around it.

```css
.search {
  --nuv-input-group-radius: var(--radius-full);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-input-group-width` | `100%` | Width. It fills its container by default. |
| `--nuv-input-group-border` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Border color of the box. |
| `--nuv-input-group-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius of the box. |
| `--nuv-input-group-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of the box. |
| `--nuv-input-group-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Text color of the input. |
| `--nuv-input-group-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-md)` | Minimum height of the box. The buttons inside are sized from it. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. |
| `--nuv-input-group-addon-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the text and icons in an addon. |
| `--nuv-input-group-button-radius` | `var(--radius-sm)` | Corner radius of a button. |
| `--nuv-input-group-button-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of a button's text or icon. |
| `--nuv-input-group-button-bg-hover` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of a button while hovered. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-input-group` | InputGroup. |
| `.nuv-input-group__addon` | InputGroupAddon. |
| `.nuv-input-group__button` | InputGroupButton. |

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

The parts are client components, because the group listens for a press to focus its input. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files. You can put a group together inside a server component, as the first example on this page does.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Keep addons short: a sign, a unit, a few fixed characters.
- Put the thing people read first, such as a currency sign, before the input.

**Don't**

- Don't put more than one input in a group.
- Don't put the field's only label in an addon. It isn't read as one.
- Don't crowd the box. One addon and one button on a side is about the limit on a phone.

pages.title: Item
pages.description: A row with a picture, a title, a description and something to do at its end, and a list that groups rows into a panel.
pages.markdown:
# Item A row with a picture, a title, a description and something to do at its end, and a list that groups rows into a panel. Use an item for one thing in a list of things: a setting with its switch, a person with their role, a page to go to. `ItemGroup` turns several into a list. ```tsx import { Button, Item, ItemActions, ItemContent, ItemDescription, ItemMedia, ItemTitle, } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return ( Two-step sign-in Ask for a code from your phone as well as your password. ); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Item, ItemActions, ItemContent, ItemDescription, ItemGroup, ItemMedia, ItemTitle, } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `Item` | The row. | | `ItemMedia` | What's at the start: an icon, an avatar or a picture. | | `ItemContent` | The title and the description. It takes the room the rest leaves. | | `ItemTitle` | The row's name. | | `ItemDescription` | A line or two under it. | | `ItemActions` | What's at the end: a switch, a button, a badge, an arrow. | | `ItemGroup` | A list of items. A `ul`, with each item in an `li`. | Only `Item` is needed, and it can hold anything. The parts are there for the usual layout. ## Props ### Item | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead of a `div`, and give it the item's class and props. This is how a whole row becomes a link or a button: it then has a hover color and a focus ring. | | `variant` | `"muted" \| "outline" \| "plain"` | `"plain"` | `"outline"` draws an edge around the row and `"muted"` fills it. In an outlined `ItemGroup` leave it plain: the group draws the edges. | | `size` | `"md" \| "sm"` | `"md"` | `"sm"` has less padding, for a dense list. | ### ItemMedia | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `variant` | `"icon" \| "plain"` | `"plain"` | `"icon"` draws a small filled square behind an icon. `"plain"` draws nothing, for an avatar or a picture. | ### ItemGroup | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `variant` | `"outline" \| "plain"` | `"plain"` | `"outline"` puts one edge around all the rows and a line between them, as a settings panel has. | The other parts add no props of their own. Each takes what its element takes, including `ref` and `className`. ## Variants and sizes `variant` is how one row is drawn: `"plain"` with nothing around it, `"outline"` with an edge, `"muted"` with a fill. `size="sm"` takes padding off, for a dense list. ```tsx import { Avatar, AvatarFallback, Item, ItemContent, ItemDescription, ItemGroup, ItemMedia, ItemTitle, } from "@nuvui/react"; const people = [ { initials: "AO", name: "Ada Osei", role: "Owner", variant: "plain" }, { initials: "GL", name: "Grace Lindqvist", role: "Admin", variant: "outline", }, { initials: "TM", name: "Tomás Marín", role: "Member", variant: "muted" }, ] as const; export default function Example() { return ( {people.map((person) => ( {person.initials} {person.name} {person.role}, as variant="{person.variant}" ))} ); } ``` ## A settings panel An `ItemGroup` with `variant="outline"` puts one edge around all its rows and a line between them. Leave the items plain inside it: the group draws the edges. ```tsx "use client"; import { Item, ItemActions, ItemContent, ItemDescription, ItemGroup, ItemTitle, NativeSelect, Slider, Switch, } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { const [volume, setVolume] = useState([60]); return (

Notifications

Weekly digest A summary of your team's week, every Monday. Mentions Where to tell you about them. Alert volume {volume[0]}%
); } ``` A control in `ItemActions` has no label of its own. Give the title an `id` and point the control at it with `aria-labelledby`, and the title is the control's name. `aria-describedby` does the same for the description. Any control works at the end of a row: a [switch](page:components/switch), a [native select](page:components/native-select), a [slider](page:components/slider). Give `ItemActions` a width when the control fills what it's given, as a slider does. ## Rows that go somewhere With `asChild`, the row is the element you give it. A row that's a link or a button gets a hover color, a pointer and a focus ring, and is at least 44 pixels tall on a touch screen. ```tsx import { Badge, Item, ItemActions, ItemContent, ItemDescription, ItemGroup, ItemTitle, } from "@nuvui/react"; const pages = [ { href: "#profile", title: "Profile", text: "Your name, your picture and your time zone.", }, { href: "#billing", title: "Billing", text: "Cards, invoices and the plan.", badge: "Past due", }, { href: "#members", title: "Members", text: "Who's on the team, and what each can do.", }, ]; function Arrow() { return ( ); } export default function Example() { return ( {pages.map((page) => ( {page.title} {page.text} {page.badge ? {page.badge} : null} ))} ); } ``` Don't put another control inside such a row. A button inside a link can't be reached by itself, and a screen reader reads the whole row as one name. If a row needs both, leave it a plain row and put a link in its title. ## In a group `ItemGroup` is a list, and a screen reader says how many rows it has. Inside one, each `Item` is wrapped in an `li` for you. That works however deep the item is: a component of your own that renders an `Item` is still a row of the list. Put only items in a group. A heading goes above it, and names it through `aria-labelledby`. ## Accessibility An item has no keyboard behavior of its own. A row that's a link or a button is reached with Tab and works as that element does. ### What the component handles - A group is a `ul` with an `li` around each row. It says it's a list in so many words, because Safari stops treating a list as one once its bullets are styled away. - A row that's a link stays a link: the list item is the box around it, not the row. - The focus ring of a row is drawn inside it, so a group that clips its corners doesn't clip the ring. - A filled row and the square behind an icon each have a border that can't be seen until the browser forces its own colors. It's drawn there in place of the fill. - The description has at least 4.5:1 against the page, a surface and a filled row in every theme. ### What you need to handle - Name a group, with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. - Name each control in `ItemActions` by the row's title, with `aria-labelledby`. - An icon in `ItemMedia` that only decorates needs `aria-hidden="true"`. A picture that says something needs an `alt`. ## On small screens The row doesn't wrap. The text takes what's left after the picture and the action, and wraps inside its own column, so the action stays at the end of the row. Keep what's in `ItemActions` small: one control, or a badge and an arrow. ## CSS variables Set any of these on an `Item`, on an `ItemGroup`, or on anything around them. ```css .member-list { --nuv-item-padding-inline: 0; --nuv-item-group-gap: 0; } ``` | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-item-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 3)`, `calc(var(--spacing) * 2)` | Space between the picture, the text and the action. | | `--nuv-item-padding-block` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 3)`, `calc(var(--spacing) * 2)` | Padding above and below. Less at size="sm". | | `--nuv-item-padding-inline` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 4)`, `calc(var(--spacing) * 3)` | Padding left and right. Less at size="sm". | | `--nuv-item-border` | `transparent`, `var(--color-border)` | Border color. Transparent unless the variant is "outline". | | `--nuv-item-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius of a row. Square inside an outlined group. | | `--nuv-item-bg` | `transparent`, `var(--color-muted)` | Background color. Transparent unless the variant is "muted". | | `--nuv-item-fg` | `inherit` | Text color. The color of what's around it by default. | | `--nuv-item-hover-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background color of a row that's a link or a button, under the pointer. | | `--nuv-item-media-size` | `2.25rem` | Width and height of the square behind an icon. | | `--nuv-item-media-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background color of that square. | | `--nuv-item-media-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of the icon in it. | | `--nuv-item-muted-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the description. Keep it at 4.5:1 against the background. | | `--nuv-item-group-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 1)` | Space between rows in a plain group. | | `--nuv-item-group-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of an outlined group's edge and of the lines between its rows. | | `--nuv-item-group-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of an outlined group. | | `--nuv-item-group-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of an outlined group. | | `--nuv-item-group-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color in an outlined group. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-item` | Every item. | | `.nuv-item--muted` | variant="muted" | | `.nuv-item--outline` | variant="outline" | | `.nuv-item--sm` | size="sm" | | `.nuv-item-group` | ItemGroup | | `.nuv-item-group--outline` | ItemGroup with variant="outline" | | `.nuv-item-group__row` | The `li` around each item in a group. | | `.nuv-item__actions` | ItemActions | | `.nuv-item__content` | ItemContent | | `.nuv-item__description` | ItemDescription | | `.nuv-item__media` | ItemMedia | | `.nuv-item__media--icon` | ItemMedia with variant="icon" | | `.nuv-item__title` | ItemTitle | ## Server components `Item` and `ItemGroup` start with `"use client"`: an item has to find out whether it's in a group. You can still use them from a server component, with server-rendered content inside. The other parts are in the same file, so they're client components too. ## Do and don't **Do** - Keep one kind of thing at the end of every row in a list: all switches, or all arrows. - Use an outlined group for settings, and plain rows for a list of people or files. **Don't** - Don't nest a control in a row that's a link. - Don't use an item where the rows have columns to compare. That's a [table](page:table/index).


sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import {
  Item,
  ItemActions,
  ItemContent,
  ItemDescription,
  ItemGroup,
  ItemMedia,
  ItemTitle,
} from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Item` | The row. |
| `ItemMedia` | What's at the start: an icon, an avatar or a picture. |
| `ItemContent` | The title and the description. It takes the room the rest leaves. |
| `ItemTitle` | The row's name. |
| `ItemDescription` | A line or two under it. |
| `ItemActions` | What's at the end: a switch, a button, a badge, an arrow. |
| `ItemGroup` | A list of items. A `ul`, with each item in an `li`. |

Only `Item` is needed, and it can hold anything. The parts are there for the usual layout.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

### Item

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead of a `div`, and give it the item's class and props. This is how a whole row becomes a link or a button: it then has a hover color and a focus ring. |
| `variant` | `"muted" \| "outline" \| "plain"` | `"plain"` | `"outline"` draws an edge around the row and `"muted"` fills it. In an outlined `ItemGroup` leave it plain: the group draws the edges. |
| `size` | `"md" \| "sm"` | `"md"` | `"sm"` has less padding, for a dense list. |

### ItemMedia

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"icon" \| "plain"` | `"plain"` | `"icon"` draws a small filled square behind an icon. `"plain"` draws nothing, for an avatar or a picture. |

### ItemGroup

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"outline" \| "plain"` | `"plain"` | `"outline"` puts one edge around all the rows and a line between them, as a settings panel has. |

The other parts add no props of their own. Each takes what its element takes, including `ref` and `className`.

sections.heading: Variants and sizes
A settings panel
sections.markdown:
## A settings panel An `ItemGroup` with `variant="outline"` puts one edge around all its rows and a line between them. Leave the items plain inside it: the group draws the edges. ```tsx "use client"; import { Item, ItemActions, ItemContent, ItemDescription, ItemGroup, ItemTitle, NativeSelect, Slider, Switch, } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { const [volume, setVolume] = useState([60]); return (

Notifications

Weekly digest A summary of your team's week, every Monday. Mentions Where to tell you about them. Alert volume {volume[0]}%
); } ``` A control in `ItemActions` has no label of its own. Give the title an `id` and point the control at it with `aria-labelledby`, and the title is the control's name. `aria-describedby` does the same for the description. Any control works at the end of a row: a [switch](page:components/switch), a [native select](page:components/native-select), a [slider](page:components/slider). Give `ItemActions` a width when the control fills what it's given, as a slider does.

sections.heading: Rows that go somewhere
In a group
sections.markdown:
## In a group

`ItemGroup` is a list, and a screen reader says how many rows it has. Inside one, each `Item` is wrapped in an `li` for you. That works however deep the item is: a component of your own that renders an `Item` is still a row of the list.

Put only items in a group. A heading goes above it, and names it through `aria-labelledby`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

An item has no keyboard behavior of its own. A row that's a link or a button is reached with Tab and works as that element does.

### What the component handles

- A group is a `ul` with an `li` around each row. It says it's a list in so many words, because Safari stops treating a list as one once its bullets are styled away.
- A row that's a link stays a link: the list item is the box around it, not the row.
- The focus ring of a row is drawn inside it, so a group that clips its corners doesn't clip the ring.
- A filled row and the square behind an icon each have a border that can't be seen until the browser forces its own colors. It's drawn there in place of the fill.
- The description has at least 4.5:1 against the page, a surface and a filled row in every theme.

### What you need to handle

- Name a group, with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Name each control in `ItemActions` by the row's title, with `aria-labelledby`.
- An icon in `ItemMedia` that only decorates needs `aria-hidden="true"`. A picture that says something needs an `alt`.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

The row doesn't wrap. The text takes what's left after the picture and the action, and wraps inside its own column, so the action stays at the end of the row. Keep what's in `ItemActions` small: one control, or a badge and an arrow.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on an `Item`, on an `ItemGroup`, or on anything around them.

```css
.member-list {
  --nuv-item-padding-inline: 0;
  --nuv-item-group-gap: 0;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-item-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 3)`, `calc(var(--spacing) * 2)` | Space between the picture, the text and the action. |
| `--nuv-item-padding-block` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 3)`, `calc(var(--spacing) * 2)` | Padding above and below. Less at size="sm". |
| `--nuv-item-padding-inline` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 4)`, `calc(var(--spacing) * 3)` | Padding left and right. Less at size="sm". |
| `--nuv-item-border` | `transparent`, `var(--color-border)` | Border color. Transparent unless the variant is "outline". |
| `--nuv-item-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius of a row. Square inside an outlined group. |
| `--nuv-item-bg` | `transparent`, `var(--color-muted)` | Background color. Transparent unless the variant is "muted". |
| `--nuv-item-fg` | `inherit` | Text color. The color of what's around it by default. |
| `--nuv-item-hover-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background color of a row that's a link or a button, under the pointer. |
| `--nuv-item-media-size` | `2.25rem` | Width and height of the square behind an icon. |
| `--nuv-item-media-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background color of that square. |
| `--nuv-item-media-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of the icon in it. |
| `--nuv-item-muted-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the description. Keep it at 4.5:1 against the background. |
| `--nuv-item-group-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 1)` | Space between rows in a plain group. |
| `--nuv-item-group-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of an outlined group's edge and of the lines between its rows. |
| `--nuv-item-group-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of an outlined group. |
| `--nuv-item-group-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of an outlined group. |
| `--nuv-item-group-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color in an outlined group. |

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

`Item` and `ItemGroup` start with `"use client"`: an item has to find out whether it's in a group. You can still use them from a server component, with server-rendered content inside. The other parts are in the same file, so they're client components too.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Keep one kind of thing at the end of every row in a list: all switches, or all arrows.
- Use an outlined group for settings, and plain rows for a list of people or files.

**Don't**

- Don't nest a control in a row that's a link.
- Don't use an item where the rows have columns to compare. That's a [table](page:table/index).

pages.title: Kbd
pages.description: A key on the keyboard, drawn as a key cap, for writing out shortcuts.
pages.markdown:
# Kbd A key on the keyboard, drawn as a key cap, for writing out shortcuts. Use `Kbd` wherever text names a key: in help text, in a tooltip, in a table of shortcuts. It renders the HTML `` element, which is the element for something the reader types. ```tsx import { Kbd } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return (

Press Ctrl + K to search, and Esc to close.

); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Kbd } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Props `Kbd` adds no props of its own. It takes what a `` takes, including `ref` and `className`. ## It follows the text around it A key is sized in `em`, so it's as big as the text it sits in. It never makes its line taller: the cap is taller than its letters, and that extra height sits in the space between lines. With a line height under about 1.3, the caps on two lines one above the other can touch. ```tsx import { Kbd } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return (

Small text: Tab

Body text: Tab

Large text: Tab

); } ``` ## Combinations Write each key as its own `Kbd` and put the plus sign between them as plain text. A screen reader then reads the keys in the order they're written, plus sign included, and each key is one key. Keys differ between systems. Where a shortcut uses Ctrl on Windows and Linux and Command on a Mac, say both, or show the one for the system the visitor is on. A symbol such as the Command sign is read differently by different screen readers, so wrap it in an `` with the key's name as its `title`. ```tsx import { Kbd } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return (

Save with{" "} ⌘ {" "} + S on a Mac, and Ctrl + S elsewhere.

); } ``` ## In a menu A menu item's shortcut has its own part: `DropdownMenuShortcut`, `ContextMenuShortcut` and `MenubarShortcut`. Those are laid out at the end of the row and hidden from screen readers, with the keys given in `aria-keyshortcuts`. Use them there, and `Kbd` in running text. ## Accessibility A key has no keyboard behavior. It's text. ### What the component handles - It's a `` element. Browsers and screen readers treat it as text, and tools that list a page's shortcuts can find it. - Its edge has at least 3:1 against the page in every theme, and its text at least 4.5:1 against its fill. - The edge is a border, so the key keeps its shape where the browser forces its own colors. ### What you need to handle - Write the key's name, not only its symbol: "Shift", "Enter", "Esc". - A page that shows a shortcut has to make the shortcut work. `Kbd` only draws it. - Don't build a shortcut on a single letter without a way to turn it off. Speech input users trigger those by talking. [WCAG 2.1.4](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/character-key-shortcuts) has the details. ## CSS variables Set any of these on the key, or on anything around it. ```css .shortcut-table { --nuv-kbd-font: var(--font-mono); } ``` | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-kbd-size` | `1.6em` | Smallest width and height, in em of the key's own font size. A key with one letter is a square of this size. | | `--nuv-kbd-padding-inline` | `0.4em` | Padding left and right. | | `--nuv-kbd-border` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Border color. | | `--nuv-kbd-radius` | `var(--radius-sm)` | Corner radius. | | `--nuv-kbd-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background color. | | `--nuv-kbd-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Text color. | | `--nuv-kbd-font` | `var(--font-sans)` | Font family. The interface's font by default, not the browser's monospace font for kbd. | | `--nuv-kbd-font-size` | `0.8em` | Font size. A little under the text around it by default. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-kbd` | Every key. | ## Server components Kbd has no `"use client"` directive and uses no state, so it renders in a server component as it is. ## Do and don't **Do** - Use the names printed on the keys. - Keep the same order everywhere: modifiers first, then the key. **Don't** - Don't use it for text people type in, such as a command. That's ``. - Don't put a whole combination in one `Kbd`.

sections.heading: Around a control
Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

A label has no keyboard behavior of its own. Focus goes to the control it names.

### What the component handles

- It renders a native `<label>`, so the browser ties it to the control: a screen reader reads the label's text as the control's name, and a click or a tap on the label focuses or toggles the control.
- A double click on a label selects its text in most browsers, which gets in the way when someone clicks a checkbox's label twice. This one doesn't. That part is Radix.
- A click on a button, an input or a select inside the label is left alone.

### What you need to handle

- Point it at the control. Set `htmlFor` to the control's `id`, or put the control inside the label.
- Keep it visible. A placeholder isn't a label: it disappears as soon as someone types.
- A label can't tell whether its control is disabled. Set the `data-disabled` attribute on it to fade it. Field does this for you.

sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Give every control a label that people can see.
- Keep it short, and put any explanation in a description under the control.

**Don't**

- Don't use a placeholder in place of a label.
- Don't put a link or a button inside a label. A click on it is ambiguous.

pages.title: ListView
pages.description: A list whose rows can be selected and can each hold buttons, moved through with the arrow keys.
pages.markdown:
# ListView A list whose rows can be selected and can each hold buttons, moved through with the arrow keys. Use a list view for rows that are things to work on: people with a button each, requests to approve, files to open. The arrow keys move between rows and Tab goes into the row it's at, so a list of a hundred rows with three buttons each is one stop for Tab and not three hundred. For rows that only show something, use an [item](page:components/item). For rows with columns to sort and filter, use a [data table](page:table/index). ```tsx "use client"; import { Badge, Button, ListView, ListViewItem } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; const people = [ { id: "ada", name: "Ada Lovelace", role: "Owner" }, { id: "bo", name: "Bo Jensen", role: "Admin" }, { id: "cleo", name: "Cleo Park", role: "Member" }, { id: "dan", name: "Dan Abbott", role: "Member" }, ]; export default function Example() { const [said, setSaid] = useState(""); return (
{people.map((person) => ( {person.name} {person.role} ))}

{said}

); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { ListView, ListViewItem } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `ListView` | The list. It keeps which rows are selected. | | `ListViewItem` | A row. Put text in it, and any buttons or links. | What you put in a row is laid side by side and centered. Give the part that should take the room `flex: 1`. ## Selecting one row `selectionMode="single"` lets one row be selected at a time. `value` is a list in every mode, here with one value in it or none. ```tsx "use client"; import { ListView, ListViewItem } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; const plans = [ { id: "starter", name: "Starter", price: "Free" }, { id: "team", name: "Team", price: "$12 a seat" }, { id: "business", name: "Business", price: "$24 a seat" }, ]; export default function Example() { const [value, setValue] = useState(["team"]); const plan = plans.find((other) => other.id === value[0]); return (
{plans.map((item) => ( {item.name} {item.price} ))}

Showing: {plan ? plan.name : "nothing"}

); } ``` ## Selecting several With `selectionMode="multiple"`, a press on a row adds it to the selection, and a press on a selected row takes it out. Nothing has to be held down, so it works the same with a finger. Shift and a press selects every row from the last one pressed to this one. ```tsx "use client"; import { Button, ListView, ListViewItem } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; const invoices = [ { id: "INV-2041", to: "Northwind", locked: false }, { id: "INV-2042", to: "Contoso", locked: false }, { id: "INV-2043", to: "Fabrikam", locked: true }, { id: "INV-2044", to: "Adatum", locked: false }, ]; export default function Example() { const [value, setValue] = useState(["INV-2041"]); return (
{invoices.map((invoice) => ( {invoice.id}, {invoice.to} {invoice.locked ? " (already sent)" : ""} ))}

{value.length} selected

); } ``` ## Doing something with a row `onAction` is called with a row's value when Enter is pressed on it. Where rows can't be selected, a press on the row calls it too. A press on a button inside the row is the button's alone: it doesn't select the row or call `onAction`. ```tsx "use client"; import { Button, ListView, ListViewItem } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; const reports = [ { id: "q3", name: "Q3 revenue" }, { id: "churn", name: "Churn by plan" }, { id: "seats", name: "Seats in use" }, ]; export default function Example() { const [said, setSaid] = useState("Nothing opened yet."); const name = (id: string) => reports.find((report) => report.id === id)?.name ?? id; return (
setSaid(`Opened ${name(id)}.`)} > {reports.map((report) => ( {report.name} ))}

{said}

); } ``` Where rows can be selected, a press selects, so give the row a button or a link for a mouse to open it with. Enter still calls `onAction`. ## A row that doesn't start with its name Typing a letter goes to the next row whose text starts with it. When a row starts with something else, a date or a count, say what its name is with `textValue`. ```tsx 9 October Northwind ``` ## ListView props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `selectionMode` | `"multiple" \| "none" \| "single"` | `"none"` | Whether rows can be selected, and how many. With `"multiple"`, a press adds a row to the selection or takes it out, and Shift selects a run of them. | | `value` | `string[]` | | The selected rows' values, when you control them. | | `defaultValue` | `string[]` | | The rows selected at first, when you don't. | | `onValueChange` | `((value: string[]) => void)` | | Called with every selected row's value when the selection changes. | | `onAction` | `((value: string) => void)` | | Called with a row's value when Enter is pressed on it. Where rows can't be selected, a press on the row calls it too. | It also takes what a `div` takes, including `ref` and `className`. ## ListViewItem props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` (required) | `string` | | What the row is known by in `value`.
