sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { ListView, ListViewItem } from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `ListView` | The list. It keeps which rows are selected. |
| `ListViewItem` | A row. Put text in it, and any buttons or links. |

What you put in a row is laid side by side and centered. Give the part that should take the room `flex: 1`.

sections.heading: Selecting one row
Selecting several
Doing something with a row
A row that doesn't start with its name
sections.markdown:
## A row that doesn't start with its name

Typing a letter goes to the next row whose text starts with it. When a row starts with something else, a date or a count, say what its name is with `textValue`.

```tsx
<ListViewItem value="inv-2041" textValue="Northwind">
  <time dateTime="2026-10-09">9 October</time>
  Northwind
</ListViewItem>
```

sections.heading: ListView props
sections.markdown:
## ListView props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selectionMode` | `"multiple" \| "none" \| "single"` | `"none"` | Whether rows can be selected, and how many. With `"multiple"`, a press adds a row to the selection or takes it out, and Shift selects a run of them. |
| `value` | `string[]` |  | The selected rows' values, when you control them. |
| `defaultValue` | `string[]` |  | The rows selected at first, when you don't. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string[]) => void)` |  | Called with every selected row's value when the selection changes. |
| `onAction` | `((value: string) => void)` |  | Called with a row's value when Enter is pressed on it. Where rows can't be selected, a press on the row calls it too. |

It also takes what a `div` takes, including `ref` and `className`.

sections.heading: ListViewItem props
sections.markdown:
## ListViewItem props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | What the row is known by in `value`. No two the same. |
| `textValue` | `string` |  | The row's name as plain text, which typing a letter looks for. Needed when the row's text doesn't start with it. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | A row that can't be selected or acted on. The arrow keys still stop at it, so a screen reader can read it. Disable the buttons inside it yourself. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | What the row shows: text, and any buttons or links. |

It also takes what a `div` takes, including `ref` and `className`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

It follows the [grid pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/grid/) of the ARIA Authoring Practices, as a grid one column wide. That's the pattern for a list whose rows hold controls: a `listbox` can't have buttons inside its options.

### Keyboard

The list is one stop for Tab. With focus on a row:

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Down, Up | Moves to the next or the previous row. |
| Home, End | Moves to the first or the last row. |
| Tab | Moves to the first button in the row, then the next. After the last, it leaves the list. |
| Shift and Tab | From a button, moves back through the row's buttons to the row. From the row, it leaves the list. |
| Enter | Calls `onAction`. With no `onAction`, selects the row. |
| Space | Selects the row, or with several, adds it or takes it out. With no selection, calls `onAction`. |
| A letter | Moves to the next row that starts with it. Letters typed quickly make a word. |
| Shift and Down or Up | With several: moves, and selects the row it arrives at. |
| Ctrl or Command and A | With several: selects every row. |

With focus on a button or in a field inside a row, every key is that control's. The arrow keys work again once focus is back on the row.

### What the component handles

- The roles: `grid`, `row` and `gridcell`. A screen reader says which row of how many it's on.
- `aria-selected` on every row when rows can be selected, and `aria-multiselectable` on the list when several can.
- Only the buttons of the row Tab is at are in the Tab order. The list takes the others out by setting their `tabindex` to `-1`, and gives each back what it had when its row is the one. A press on a button in any row still works, and makes that the row.
- Tab stops at the row focus was last in. If that row goes, because the data changed, Tab stops at the first row.
- A selected row differs by more than its background: a bar at its start, drawn as a border, which is still there where the browser forces its own colors.
- A disabled row can still be reached with the arrow keys, so a screen reader can read it. It can't be selected or acted on.

### What you need to handle

- Name the list with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Give every row a `value` no other row has.
- A row's name is all its text, button names included. Where every row has a button that says the same, name each for its row: `aria-label="Message Ada Lovelace"`.
- Disable the buttons inside a disabled row. The row doesn't do it for you.
- Render something else when there are no rows, such as an [empty state](page:components/empty). A grid with no rows isn't valid.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

A row is at least 44 pixels tall, and as tall as what's in it. What's in a row stays on one line. For a row with more than fits, put the text in an element with `flex: 1` and `min-inline-size: 0` so it wraps or is cut short, and keep to one or two buttons, or put the rest in a [menu](page:components/dropdown-menu).

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on the `ListView`, or on anything around it.

```css
.requests {
  --nuv-list-view-padding-inline: 1rem;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-list-view-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of the text. |
| `--nuv-list-view-row-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)` | Least height of a row. |
| `--nuv-list-view-padding-block` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 2)` | Space above and below what's in a row. |
| `--nuv-list-view-padding-inline` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 3)` | Space at the start and end of a row. |
| `--nuv-list-view-radius` | `0` | Corner radius of a row. |
| `--nuv-list-view-divider` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of the line between rows. |
| `--nuv-list-view-hover-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of the row under the pointer. |
| `--nuv-list-view-selected-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of a selected row. |
| `--nuv-list-view-selected-line-width` | `2px` | Thickness of the bar at the start of a selected row. |
| `--nuv-list-view-selected-line` | `var(--color-primary)` | Color of that bar. Keep it at 3:1 against the row. |
| `--nuv-list-view-button-bg` | `var(--color-background)` | Background of a secondary button in a row. The page's color by default, so the button can be told from a selected row. |
| `--nuv-list-view-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 3)` | Space between the things in a row. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-list-view` | ListView |
| `.nuv-list-view__cell` | The row's one cell, which holds what you gave it. |
| `.nuv-list-view__item` | ListViewItem: the row, which is what's pressed. |

A selected row has `aria-selected="true"` and a disabled one `aria-disabled="true"`.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

ListView starts with `"use client"`: it keeps which rows are selected. You can render it from a server component with rows written there, as long as you leave `onValueChange` and `onAction` out, since a function can't be passed from the server.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Keep a row to one line of what it is and one or two things to do with it.
- Say what happened after a button in a row is pressed, in a status or a [toast](page:components/toast). The row may be gone.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for rows nobody acts on. That's a plain list, or [items](page:components/item).
- Don't nest a list view in a row.

pages.title: Menubar
pages.description: A row of menus across the top of an application, like the File, Edit and View of a desktop program.
pages.markdown:
# Menubar A row of menus across the top of an application, like the File, Edit and View of a desktop program. Use a menubar in something that works like a desktop application: an editor, a design tool, a spreadsheet. It holds every command the application has, grouped under a few names. For a single list of actions on one thing, use a [dropdown menu](page:components/dropdown-menu). For links between the pages of a site, use a [navigation menu](page:components/navigation-menu). ```tsx import { Menubar, MenubarContent, MenubarItem, MenubarMenu, MenubarSeparator, MenubarShortcut, MenubarTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return ( File New Ctrl+N Open Ctrl+O Open recent Print Ctrl+P Edit Undo Ctrl+Z Redo Ctrl+Y Find Help Keyboard shortcuts Send feedback ); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Menubar, MenubarContent, MenubarItem, MenubarMenu, MenubarSeparator, MenubarShortcut, MenubarTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `Menubar` | The bar. It holds which menu is open. | | `MenubarMenu` | One menu: its entry in the bar and its panel. Renders nothing itself. | | `MenubarTrigger` | The entry in the bar that opens the menu. | | `MenubarContent` | The panel with the items. | | `MenubarItem` | One command. | | `MenubarCheckboxItem` | An item that's on or off. | | `MenubarRadioGroup` | Wraps radio items and holds which one is chosen. | | `MenubarRadioItem` | One choice in a radio group. | | `MenubarLabel` | A heading for the items under it. It can't be focused. | | `MenubarSeparator` | A line between groups of items. | | `MenubarShortcut` | The keys that do the same as an item, shown at the end of its row. | | `MenubarGroup` | Groups items for screen readers. It has no look of its own. | | `MenubarSub` | Holds the open state of a submenu. | | `MenubarSubTrigger` | The item that opens the submenu. | | `MenubarSubContent` | The submenu's panel. | These are separate exports, not properties of `Menubar`. `Menubar.Menu` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component. What goes inside a menu is the same as in a [dropdown menu](page:components/dropdown-menu), part for part. ## Props ### Menubar | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` | `string` | | The `value` of the menu that's open, when you control it yourself. An empty string means none. Use it with `onValueChange`. | | `defaultValue` | `string` | | The menu that starts open, when you don't control it. | | `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void)` | | Called with a menu's `value` when it opens, and with an empty string when the last one closes. | | `loop` | `boolean` | | Whether the arrow keys wrap from the last entry to the first and back. On unless you pass `false`. | | `dir` | `"ltr" \| "rtl"` | | The reading direction. With `"rtl"`, the left and right arrow keys swap, and submenus open to the left. | ### MenubarMenu | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` | `string` | | A name for this menu, to use with the bar's `value`. Only needed when you control which menu is open. | ### MenubarContent | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `align` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start"` | `"start"` | Which edge of the trigger the menu lines up with. | | `sideOffset` | `number` | `6` | The gap between the trigger and the menu, in pixels. | | `collisionPadding` | `number \| Partial>` | `8` | How close the menu may get to the edge of the screen, in pixels. It moves or flips to keep this much room. | | `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the menu is rendered into. Set this when the menu should pick up a `data-theme` from a section of the page. | ### MenubarItem | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `intent` | `"danger" \| "neutral"` | `"neutral"` | Use `"danger"` for an action that destroys something. | | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `onSelect` | `((event: Event) => void)` | | Called when the item is chosen, by click or by keyboard. Call `event.preventDefault()` in it to keep the menu open. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | | Stops the item from being chosen. The arrow keys skip it. | | `textValue` | `string` | | The text that typing a letter matches against. Only needed when the item's content isn't plain text. | ### MenubarSubContent | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `collisionPadding` | `number \| Partial>` | `8` | How close the submenu may get to the edge of the screen, in pixels. | | `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the submenu is rendered into. Pass the same one as the menu's. | `MenubarTrigger` takes `disabled`, and what a `button` takes. The other parts take the same props as the Radix parts they wrap. The [Radix Menubar reference](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/menubar#api-reference) lists them. ## Shortcuts `MenubarShortcut` shows the keys that do the same thing as an item. It only shows them: listening for the keys is your code's job. It's hidden from screen readers, because its text would otherwise run into the item's name. To have the keys announced, put them in `aria-keyshortcuts` on the item, as the first example does. That attribute has its own way of writing keys: `Control+N`, not `Ctrl+N`. ## Checkable items ```tsx "use client"; import { Menubar, MenubarCheckboxItem, MenubarContent, MenubarLabel, MenubarMenu, MenubarRadioGroup, MenubarRadioItem, MenubarSeparator, MenubarTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { const [ruler, setRuler] = useState(true); const [zoom, setZoom] = useState("100"); return (
View Show ruler Zoom 50% 100% 200%

Zoom {zoom}%, ruler {ruler ? "shown" : "hidden"}

); } ``` ## Submenus ```tsx import { Menubar, MenubarContent, MenubarItem, MenubarMenu, MenubarSub, MenubarSubContent, MenubarSubTrigger, MenubarTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return ( Share Copy link Export as PDF Word document Plain text ); } ``` ## Moving between menus A click on an entry opens its menu. From then on, moving the pointer to another entry opens that one and closes the first, with no click, until a menu is closed again. The arrow keys do the same from inside a menu. A menu here closes at once, with no fade. A menu that's fading out is still on the page, and Radix would then take focus arriving in the next menu for a click outside the old one and close them both. ## On small screens A menubar belongs to wide screens and a pointer. On a phone the entries are 44 pixels tall, and a bar with more entries than fit wraps onto a second line, so it still works. But a row of menus is a poor fit for a narrow screen. Consider putting the same commands in a [sheet](page:components/sheet) there. ## Accessibility ### Keyboard | Key | What it does | | --- | --- | | Tab | Moves focus into the bar, to the entry that last had it. Pressed again, it leaves the bar. | | → and ← | On the bar, move to the next or previous entry. Inside a menu, close it and open the one beside it. | | Enter, Space or ↓ | On an entry, opens its menu and moves focus to the first item. | | ↓ and ↑ | Move to the next or previous item. Disabled items are skipped. | | Home and End | Move to the first or last item. | | A letter | Moves to the next item that starts with it. | | Enter or Space | Chooses the focused item. | | → | On a submenu's trigger, opens the submenu. | | ← | Inside a submenu, closes it and goes back to its trigger. | | Esc | Closes the menu and returns focus to its entry. | When → or ← opens the menu beside the one you were in, focus lands on the menu and not on its first item. ↓ goes to the first item from there. That's how Radix does it. ### What the component handles Most of this is Radix. The library doesn't change it. - The bar has `role="menubar"`. Its entries are `menuitem`s with `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`, and each panel is a `menu` named by its entry. - The bar is one stop in the tab order. The arrow keys move inside it and skip a disabled entry. - The menus aren't modal: the rest of the page stays reachable while one is open, and a click anywhere else closes it. - An entry with keyboard focus has a ring. The row that has focus inside a menu is filled with the primary color, which has at least 3:1 contrast with the panel. - Where the browser forces its own colors, as Windows high contrast does, the fill isn't drawn. The focused row has an outline there instead. - Entries are 44 pixels tall on a touch screen and 32 with a mouse, and so are the rows. - A menu only fades in when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion. ### What you need to handle - Name the bar with `aria-label`, such as "Document". A page can then have more than one and a screen reader can tell them apart. - Listen for the shortcuts you show. `MenubarShortcut` is only text. - Keep the entries to a word each, and the same from one screen to the next. People learn where a command lives. - In a right-to-left layout, pass `dir="rtl"`. ## CSS variables The bar and its menus have separate variables, because they're separate things on the page. Set the bar's on `Menubar` or anything around it. ```css .editor { --nuv-menubar-bg: transparent; --nuv-menubar-border: transparent; } ``` The menus render at the end of ``, so set theirs on `:root` or `body`, or straight on `MenubarContent` with `style` or a class. | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-menubar-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Border color of the bar. | | `--nuv-menubar-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of the bar. | | `--nuv-menubar-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of the bar. | | `--nuv-menubar-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color of the entries. | | `--nuv-menubar-menu-width` | `12rem` | The narrowest a menu gets. It grows to fit its longest item. | | `--nuv-menubar-menu-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Border color of a menu's panel, and the color of the separators. | | `--nuv-menubar-menu-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of a menu's panel. | | `--nuv-menubar-menu-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of a menu's panel. | | `--nuv-menubar-menu-shadow` | `var(--shadow-lg)` | Shadow under a menu's panel. | | `--nuv-menubar-menu-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color in a menu. | | `--nuv-menubar-menu-item-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-sm)` | Minimum height of a row. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. | | `--nuv-menubar-menu-highlight-bg` | `var(--color-primary)` | Background of the row that has focus, from the pointer or the arrow keys. Keep it at 3:1 against the panel. | | `--nuv-menubar-menu-highlight-fg` | `var(--color-primary-foreground)` | Text color of that row. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-menubar` | Menubar. | | `.nuv-menubar__check` | The check mark inside it. | | `.nuv-menubar__chevron` | The arrow at the end of MenubarSubTrigger. | | `.nuv-menubar__content` | MenubarContent and MenubarSubContent. | | `.nuv-menubar__dash` | The dash shown while a checkbox item is indeterminate. | | `.nuv-menubar__indicator` | The mark at the end of a checked item. sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import {
  Menubar,
  MenubarContent,
  MenubarItem,
  MenubarMenu,
  MenubarSeparator,
  MenubarShortcut,
  MenubarTrigger,
} from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Menubar` | The bar. It holds which menu is open. |
| `MenubarMenu` | One menu: its entry in the bar and its panel. Renders nothing itself. |
| `MenubarTrigger` | The entry in the bar that opens the menu. |
| `MenubarContent` | The panel with the items. |
| `MenubarItem` | One command. |
| `MenubarCheckboxItem` | An item that's on or off. |
| `MenubarRadioGroup` | Wraps radio items and holds which one is chosen. |
| `MenubarRadioItem` | One choice in a radio group. |
| `MenubarLabel` | A heading for the items under it. It can't be focused. |
| `MenubarSeparator` | A line between groups of items. |
| `MenubarShortcut` | The keys that do the same as an item, shown at the end of its row. |
| `MenubarGroup` | Groups items for screen readers. It has no look of its own. |
| `MenubarSub` | Holds the open state of a submenu. |
| `MenubarSubTrigger` | The item that opens the submenu. |
| `MenubarSubContent` | The submenu's panel. |

These are separate exports, not properties of `Menubar`. `Menubar.Menu` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component.

What goes inside a menu is the same as in a [dropdown menu](page:components/dropdown-menu), part for part.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

### Menubar

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` |  | The `value` of the menu that's open, when you control it yourself. An empty string means none. Use it with `onValueChange`. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | The menu that starts open, when you don't control it. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void)` |  | Called with a menu's `value` when it opens, and with an empty string when the last one closes. |
| `loop` | `boolean` |  | Whether the arrow keys wrap from the last entry to the first and back. On unless you pass `false`. |
| `dir` | `"ltr" \| "rtl"` |  | The reading direction. With `"rtl"`, the left and right arrow keys swap, and submenus open to the left. |

### MenubarMenu

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` |  | A name for this menu, to use with the bar's `value`. Only needed when you control which menu is open. |

### MenubarContent

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `align` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start"` | `"start"` | Which edge of the trigger the menu lines up with. |
| `sideOffset` | `number` | `6` | The gap between the trigger and the menu, in pixels. |
| `collisionPadding` | `number \| Partial<Record<"bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top", number>>` | `8` | How close the menu may get to the edge of the screen, in pixels. It moves or flips to keep this much room. |
| `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the menu is rendered into. Set this when the menu should pick up a `data-theme` from a section of the page. |

### MenubarItem

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `intent` | `"danger" \| "neutral"` | `"neutral"` | Use `"danger"` for an action that destroys something. |

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onSelect` | `((event: Event) => void)` |  | Called when the item is chosen, by click or by keyboard. Call `event.preventDefault()` in it to keep the menu open. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Stops the item from being chosen. The arrow keys skip it. |
| `textValue` | `string` |  | The text that typing a letter matches against. Only needed when the item's content isn't plain text. |

### MenubarSubContent

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `collisionPadding` | `number \| Partial<Record<"bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top", number>>` | `8` | How close the submenu may get to the edge of the screen, in pixels. |
| `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the submenu is rendered into. Pass the same one as the menu's. |

`MenubarTrigger` takes `disabled`, and what a `button` takes. The other parts take the same props as the Radix parts they wrap. The [Radix Menubar reference](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/menubar#api-reference) lists them.

sections.heading: Shortcuts
sections.markdown:
## Shortcuts

`MenubarShortcut` shows the keys that do the same thing as an item. It only shows them: listening for the keys is your code's job.

It's hidden from screen readers, because its text would otherwise run into the item's name. To have the keys announced, put them in `aria-keyshortcuts` on the item, as the first example does. That attribute has its own way of writing keys: `Control+N`, not `Ctrl+N`.

sections.heading: Checkable items
sections.markdown:
## Checkable items ```tsx "use client"; import { Menubar, MenubarCheckboxItem, MenubarContent, MenubarLabel, MenubarMenu, MenubarRadioGroup, MenubarRadioItem, MenubarSeparator, MenubarTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { const [ruler, setRuler] = useState(true); const [zoom, setZoom] = useState("100"); return (
View Show ruler Zoom 50% 100% 200%

Zoom {zoom}%, ruler {ruler ? "shown" : "hidden"}

); } ```

sections.heading: Submenus
sections.markdown:
## Submenus

```tsx
import {
  Menubar,
  MenubarContent,
  MenubarItem,
  MenubarMenu,
  MenubarSub,
  MenubarSubContent,
  MenubarSubTrigger,
  MenubarTrigger,
} from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Menubar aria-label="Document">
      <MenubarMenu>
        <MenubarTrigger>Share</MenubarTrigger>
        <MenubarContent>
          <MenubarItem>Copy link</MenubarItem>
          <MenubarSub>
            <MenubarSubTrigger>Export as</MenubarSubTrigger>
            <MenubarSubContent>
              <MenubarItem>PDF</MenubarItem>
              <MenubarItem>Word document</MenubarItem>
              <MenubarItem>Plain text</MenubarItem>
            </MenubarSubContent>
          </MenubarSub>
        </MenubarContent>
      </MenubarMenu>
    </Menubar>
  );
}
```

sections.heading: Moving between menus
sections.markdown:
## Moving between menus

A click on an entry opens its menu. From then on, moving the pointer to another entry opens that one and closes the first, with no click, until a menu is closed again. The arrow keys do the same from inside a menu.

A menu here closes at once, with no fade. A menu that's fading out is still on the page, and Radix would then take focus arriving in the next menu for a click outside the old one and close them both.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

A menubar belongs to wide screens and a pointer. On a phone the entries are 44 pixels tall, and a bar with more entries than fit wraps onto a second line, so it still works. But a row of menus is a poor fit for a narrow screen. Consider putting the same commands in a [sheet](page:components/sheet) there.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves focus into the bar, to the entry that last had it. Pressed again, it leaves the bar. |
| <kbd>→</kbd> and <kbd>←</kbd> | On the bar, move to the next or previous entry. Inside a menu, close it and open the one beside it. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>, <kbd>Space</kbd> or <kbd>↓</kbd> | On an entry, opens its menu and moves focus to the first item. |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> and <kbd>↑</kbd> | Move to the next or previous item. Disabled items are skipped. |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> | Move to the first or last item. |
| A letter | Moves to the next item that starts with it. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> | Chooses the focused item. |
| <kbd>→</kbd> | On a submenu's trigger, opens the submenu. |
| <kbd>←</kbd> | Inside a submenu, closes it and goes back to its trigger. |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Closes the menu and returns focus to its entry. |

When <kbd>→</kbd> or <kbd>←</kbd> opens the menu beside the one you were in, focus lands on the menu and not on its first item. <kbd>↓</kbd> goes to the first item from there. That's how Radix does it.

### What the component handles

Most of this is Radix. The library doesn't change it.

- The bar has `role="menubar"`. Its entries are `menuitem`s with `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`, and each panel is a `menu` named by its entry.
- The bar is one stop in the tab order. The arrow keys move inside it and skip a disabled entry.
- The menus aren't modal: the rest of the page stays reachable while one is open, and a click anywhere else closes it.
- An entry with keyboard focus has a ring. The row that has focus inside a menu is filled with the primary color, which has at least 3:1 contrast with the panel.
- Where the browser forces its own colors, as Windows high contrast does, the fill isn't drawn. The focused row has an outline there instead.
- Entries are 44 pixels tall on a touch screen and 32 with a mouse, and so are the rows.
- A menu only fades in when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion.

### What you need to handle

- Name the bar with `aria-label`, such as "Document". A page can then have more than one and a screen reader can tell them apart.
- Listen for the shortcuts you show. `MenubarShortcut` is only text.
- Keep the entries to a word each, and the same from one screen to the next. People learn where a command lives.
- In a right-to-left layout, pass `dir="rtl"`.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

The bar and its menus have separate variables, because they're separate things on the page. Set the bar's on `Menubar` or anything around it.

```css
.editor {
  --nuv-menubar-bg: transparent;
  --nuv-menubar-border: transparent;
}
```

The menus render at the end of `<body>`, so set theirs on `:root` or `body`, or straight on `MenubarContent` with `style` or a class.

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-menubar-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Border color of the bar. |
| `--nuv-menubar-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of the bar. |
| `--nuv-menubar-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of the bar. |
| `--nuv-menubar-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color of the entries. |
| `--nuv-menubar-menu-width` | `12rem` | The narrowest a menu gets. It grows to fit its longest item. |
| `--nuv-menubar-menu-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Border color of a menu's panel, and the color of the separators. |
| `--nuv-menubar-menu-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of a menu's panel. |
| `--nuv-menubar-menu-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of a menu's panel. |
| `--nuv-menubar-menu-shadow` | `var(--shadow-lg)` | Shadow under a menu's panel. |
| `--nuv-menubar-menu-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color in a menu. |
| `--nuv-menubar-menu-item-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-sm)` | Minimum height of a row. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. |
| `--nuv-menubar-menu-highlight-bg` | `var(--color-primary)` | Background of the row that has focus, from the pointer or the arrow keys. Keep it at 3:1 against the panel. |
| `--nuv-menubar-menu-highlight-fg` | `var(--color-primary-foreground)` | Text color of that row. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-menubar` | Menubar. |
| `.nuv-menubar__check` | The check mark inside it. |
| `.nuv-menubar__chevron` | The arrow at the end of MenubarSubTrigger. |
| `.nuv-menubar__content` | MenubarContent and MenubarSubContent. |
| `.nuv-menubar__dash` | The dash shown while a checkbox item is indeterminate. |
| `.nuv-menubar__indicator` | The mark at the end of a checked item. Radix only renders it while the item is checked or indeterminate. |
| `.nuv-menubar__item` | Every kind of item, and MenubarSubTrigger. |
| `.nuv-menubar__item--danger` | An item with intent="danger". |
| `.nuv-menubar__label` | MenubarLabel. |
| `.nuv-menubar__separator` | MenubarSeparator. |
| `.nuv-menubar__shortcut` | MenubarShortcut. |
| `.nuv-menubar__trigger` | MenubarTrigger. |

The panels are rendered at the end of `<body>`, not inside the bar. Their classes still start with `nuv-menubar`, because they belong to it.

Radix sets `data-state="open"` on the entry whose menu is open, `data-highlighted` on the entry or row that has focus, and `data-disabled` on a disabled one.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

The menubar parts are client components. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files.

You can put a menubar together inside a server component, as the first example on this page does. An `onSelect` handler is the usual reason to need a client component of your own.

sections.heading: Themed sections
sections.markdown:
## Themed sections

A menu opened from a bar inside a `data-theme="dark"` section doesn't inherit that theme, because it isn't rendered inside the section. Pass the section's element as `container` to `MenubarContent`, and to `MenubarSubContent` if there is one.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Use the names people know from other programs: File, Edit, View, Help.
- Leave an unavailable command in place and disable it, so the menus don't change shape.
- Show a shortcut next to every command that has one.

**Don't**

- Don't use a menubar for links between the pages of a site.
- Don't put a single command straight in the bar. Every entry opens a menu.
- Don't hide a screen's main action in a menu. Give it a button as well.

Use a native select to pick one value from a list when the options are plain text. It opens the picker people already know from their phone or computer, and it works before any JavaScript has loaded. Reach for [Select](page:components/select) when the options need styling of their own, icons, or anything else a native `` elements. `className` goes on the wrapper that carries the arrow. Everything else, `ref` and `id` included, goes to the ``, so the role, the keyboard, the system picker and form submission come from the browser. - The browser's arrow is replaced with one drawn in the theme's colors. It sits at the end of the box, so in a right-to-left layout it's on the left. A click on it goes through to the select. - The edge uses `--color-border-strong`, which has at least 3:1 contrast with the page in every theme. - Text is 16 pixels on a touch screen, so iOS doesn't zoom in when it takes focus. - With `multiple`, or a `size` above 1, the browser shows the options as a list in the page. The arrow is hidden then. ### What you need to handle - Give it a name. Use a [label](page:components/label) whose `htmlFor` matches its `id`, or `aria-label` when there's no visible text. - When the value is wrong, set `aria-invalid` and describe the problem in text. ## CSS variables Set any of these on the select, or on anything around it. It fills its container by default. | | `--nuv-native-select-border` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Border color. | | `--nuv-native-select-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius. | | `--nuv-native-select-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color. | | `--nuv-native-select-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Text color. | | `--nuv-native-select-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-md)` | Minimum height. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. | | `--nuv-native-select-icon` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the arrow. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-native-select` | The wrapper. It's what `className` is added to. | | `.nuv-native-select__control` | The select. | | `.nuv-native-select__icon` | The arrow. | ## Server components NativeSelect has no `"use client"` directive and uses no state, so it renders in a server component as it is. sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { NativeSelect } from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

NativeSelect adds no props of its own. These are the ones you'll reach for most.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string \| number \| readonly string[]` |  | The chosen option, when you control it yourself. Use it with `onChange`. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| number \| readonly string[]` |  | The option chosen at first, when you don't control it. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Stops it from being focused or changed. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Inside a form, the browser won't submit while the chosen option's value is empty. |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the value is submitted under in a form. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` |  | Lets several options be chosen. The options then show in the page as a list. |

The options are plain `<option>` and `<optgroup>` elements.

`className` goes on the wrapper that carries the arrow. Everything else, `ref` and `id` included, goes to the `<select>` itself.

States

Pick a plan to continue.

sections.heading: A placeholder
sections.markdown:
## A placeholder

A select has no placeholder. The usual stand-in is a first option with an empty value, as in the first example on this page. Mark it `disabled` so it can't be chosen again, and add `required` to the select if a real choice is needed: the browser won't submit while the empty one is chosen.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

The keys are the browser's and the operating system's own, so they vary a little. These hold everywhere.

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves focus to the select. Disabled ones are skipped. |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> and <kbd>↑</kbd> | Change the chosen option. |
| A letter | Chooses the next option that starts with it. |

### What the component handles

- It renders a native `<select>`, so the role, the keyboard, the system picker and form submission come from the browser.
- The browser's arrow is replaced with one drawn in the theme's colors. It sits at the end of the box, so in a right-to-left layout it's on the left. A click on it goes through to the select.
- The edge uses `--color-border-strong`, which has at least 3:1 contrast with the page in every theme.
- Text is 16 pixels on a touch screen, so iOS doesn't zoom in when it takes focus.
- With `multiple`, or a `size` above 1, the browser shows the options as a list in the page. The arrow is hidden then.

### What you need to handle

- Give it a name. Use a [label](page:components/label) whose `htmlFor` matches its `id`, or `aria-label` when there's no visible text.
- When the value is wrong, set `aria-invalid` and describe the problem in text.

| `--nuv-native-select-border` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Border color. |
| `--nuv-native-select-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius. |
| `--nuv-native-select-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color. |
| `--nuv-native-select-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Text color. |
| `--nuv-native-select-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-md)` | Minimum height. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. |
| `--nuv-native-select-font-size` | `var(--text-base)`, `var(--text-sm)` | Font size. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. |
| `--nuv-native-select-icon` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the arrow. |

sections.markdown:

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-native-select` | The wrapper. It's what `className` is added to. |

NativeSelect has no `"use client"` directive and uses no state, so it renders in a server component as it is. An `onChange` handler is the usual reason to need a client component around it.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Use it on forms that are mostly filled in on phones.
- Order the options in a way people can predict.

**Don't**

- Don't use a select for two or three options. Show them as [radio buttons](page:components/radio-group).
- Don't use `multiple` for more than a handful of options. Few people know how to pick several from a list box, and [checkboxes](page:components/checkbox) are clearer.

pages.title: Navbar
pages.description: The bar across the top of a site or an app, with its links in the bar on a wide screen and in a panel behind a button on a narrow one.
pages.markdown:
# Navbar The bar across the top of a site or an app, with its links in the bar on a wide screen and in a panel behind a button on a narrow one. Use a navbar for the handful of places a whole site or app has, with its name at one end and a few actions at the other. For an app with many sections, use a [sidebar](page:components/sidebar). For links that open panels of more links, put a [navigation menu](page:components/navigation-menu) in the bar. ```tsx import { Button, Navbar, NavbarActions, NavbarBrand, NavbarLink, NavbarMenu, NavbarNav, } from "@nuvui/react"; const pages = [ { name: "Orders", href: "#orders" }, { name: "Customers", href: "#customers" }, { name: "Reports", href: "#reports" }, ]; // The links are written once and drawn twice: in the bar on a wide // screen, and in the panel on a narrow one. function Links() { return pages.map((page, index) => ( {page.name} )); } export default function Example() { return ( Acme
); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Navbar, NavbarActions, NavbarBrand, NavbarLink, NavbarMenu, NavbarNav, } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. The panel is a [sheet](page:components/sheet), so its styles are needed too. ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `Navbar` | The bar. A `header`. | | `NavbarBrand` | The name or the logo, at the start. Put a link in it. | | `NavbarNav` | The links in the bar. A `nav`. Hidden on a narrow screen. | | `NavbarLink` | One link, in the bar or in the panel. | | `NavbarActions` | What's at the far end at every width. | | `NavbarMenu` | The button that's shown on a narrow screen, and the panel it opens. | ## Try it Make the window narrower than the `collapse` breakpoint to see the button. ## Props ### Navbar | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `sticky` | `boolean` | `false` | Keeps the bar at the top of the window while the page scrolls under it. | | `hideOnScroll` | `boolean` | `false` | Slides the bar out of the way while the page scrolls down, and brings it back as soon as it scrolls up. It stays while focus is inside it. The bar is sticky when this is on. | | `collapse` | `"lg" \| "md" \| "sm"` | `"md"` | The breakpoint below which `NavbarNav` is hidden and the button of `NavbarMenu` is shown: 40, 48 or 64rem. | ### NavbarNav | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead of a `nav`, and give it this part's classes and props. For a child that's a `nav` already, such as a `NavigationMenu`. | ### NavbarLink | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `current` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the link as the page that's open. A screen reader says so, and the link is drawn stronger and underlined. | | `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead of an `a`, and give it the link's classes and props. This is how you use your router's link. | ### NavbarMenu | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `label` | `string` | `"Menu"` | Accessible name of the button, and the title of the panel it opens. Translate it with the rest of your interface. | | `closeLabel` | `string` | `"Close"` | Accessible name of the button that closes the panel. Translate it with the rest of your interface. | | `side` | `"end" \| "start"` | `"end"` | The edge of the screen the panel is attached to. | | `children` | `ReactNode` | | What's in the panel: the links, and anything else. | `NavbarBrand` and `NavbarActions` add no props of their own. Every part but `NavbarMenu` takes what its element takes, including `ref` and `className`. ## The links, twice On a wide screen the links are in `NavbarNav`. On a narrow one they're in the panel of `NavbarMenu`. They're the same links, so write them once, as a component or an array, and put them in both. The bar doesn't move them for you, because the two places rarely hold quite the same things: a panel has room for the sign-in link that the bar shows as a button, and for a second level that the bar keeps in a menu. Below the `collapse` breakpoint `NavbarNav` is taken out of the page with CSS, for screen readers as much as for the eye, and the panel's contents are only in the page while it's open. So nothing is announced twice. ## Staying at the top `sticky` keeps the bar at the top of the window while the page scrolls under it. `hideOnScroll` is for a phone, where the bar takes a good part of the screen. The bar slides away while the page scrolls down and comes back as soon as it scrolls up, as a browser's own address bar does. It's always there at the top of the page, and it never leaves while focus is inside it. ## The page that's open `current` on a `NavbarLink` marks it. Which link that is comes from your router: ```tsx Orders ``` ## With a navigation menu When some entries open a panel of more links, the bar's links are a [NavigationMenu](page:components/navigation-menu). It's a `nav` already, so give `NavbarNav` `asChild`, and it hands the menu its place in the bar without wrapping one `nav` in another. ```tsx … ``` ## Accessibility | Key | What it does | | --- | --- | | Tab | Moves through the name, the links and the actions, in the order they're written. | | Enter | Follows a link, or opens the panel from its button. | | Escape | Closes the panel, and puts focus back on its button. | ### What the component handles - The bar is a `header`. At the top level of a page that's the banner landmark. - `NavbarNav` is a `nav`, which a screen reader can jump to. - The open page's link has `aria-current="page"`, and differs by a line under it as well as by color. - The button has a name, says whether the panel is open, and is 44 pixels square. - The panel is a dialog named by the same word, holds focus while it's open, and closes on Escape. - Following a link in the panel closes it. Keep the actions to one or two: a phone is 320 pixels wide at its narrowest. Links are 44 pixels tall with a finger and 40 with a mouse. In the panel each is a row the width of the panel. ## CSS variables Set any of these on the `Navbar`, or on anything around it. ```css .site { --nuv-navbar-height: 3.5rem; } ``` | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-navbar-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 4)` | Space between the parts of the bar. | | `--nuv-navbar-height` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 16)` | Least height of the bar, with its bottom edge. | | `--nuv-navbar-padding` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 4)` | Space at each end of the bar. | | `--nuv-navbar-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of the line under the bar. | | `--nuv-navbar-bg` | `var(--color-background)` | Background color. Keep it solid on a sticky bar, so the page doesn't show through. | | `--nuv-navbar-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Text color. | | `--nuv-navbar-z` | `20` | Stacking order of a sticky bar. Over the page and under anything that opens over it. | | `--nuv-navbar-link-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius of a link, and of the button. | | `--nuv-navbar-link-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of a link that isn't the open page. Keep it at 4.5:1 against the bar. | | `--nuv-navbar-link-hover-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of a link, and of the button, under the pointer. | | `--nuv-navbar-link-active-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of the open page's link, and of a link under the pointer. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-navbar` | Navbar | | `.nuv-navbar--collapse-lg` | collapse="lg" | | `.nuv-navbar--collapse-md` | collapse="md" | | `.nuv-navbar--collapse-sm` | collapse="sm" | | `.nuv-navbar--sticky` | sticky, or hideOnScroll. | | `.nuv-navbar__actions` | NavbarActions | | `.nuv-navbar__brand` | NavbarBrand | | `.nuv-navbar__link` | NavbarLink | | `.nuv-navbar__menu` | What holds NavbarMenu's children, in the panel. | | `.nuv-navbar__nav` | NavbarNav | | `.nuv-navbar__toggle` | The button of NavbarMenu. | A bar that's out of the way has a `data-hidden` attribute. The panel is a sheet, with the sheet's classes. ## Server components Navbar starts with `"use client"`: it watches the page scroll, and the panel opens and closes. You can render it from a server component, with links that are server-rendered. ## Do and don't **Do** - Keep the bar to five or six links. More than that is a sidebar, or a menu. - Put the one action that matters most at the far end, and leave the rest for the panel. **Don't** - Don't hide the bar on scroll on a wide screen. It costs little room there and people look for it. - Don't put a second row in it. Tabs for a page belong to the page.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import {
  Navbar,
  NavbarActions,
  NavbarBrand,
  NavbarLink,
  NavbarMenu,
  NavbarNav,
} from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. The panel is a [sheet](page:components/sheet), so its styles are needed too.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Navbar` | The bar. A `header`. |
| `NavbarBrand` | The name or the logo, at the start. Put a link in it. |
| `NavbarNav` | The links in the bar. A `nav`. Hidden on a narrow screen. |
| `NavbarLink` | One link, in the bar or in the panel. |
| `NavbarActions` | What's at the far end at every width. |
| `NavbarMenu` | The button that's shown on a narrow screen, and the panel it opens. |

sections.heading: Try it
sections.markdown:
## Try it

Make the window narrower than the `collapse` breakpoint to see the button.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

### Navbar

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sticky` | `boolean` | `false` | Keeps the bar at the top of the window while the page scrolls under it. |
| `hideOnScroll` | `boolean` | `false` | Slides the bar out of the way while the page scrolls down, and brings it back as soon as it scrolls up. It stays while focus is inside it. The bar is sticky when this is on. |
| `collapse` | `"lg" \| "md" \| "sm"` | `"md"` | The breakpoint below which `NavbarNav` is hidden and the button of `NavbarMenu` is shown: 40, 48 or 64rem. |

### NavbarNav

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead of a `nav`, and give it this part's classes and props. For a child that's a `nav` already, such as a `NavigationMenu`. |

### NavbarLink

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `current` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the link as the page that's open. A screen reader says so, and the link is drawn stronger and underlined. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead of an `a`, and give it the link's classes and props. This is how you use your router's link. |

### NavbarMenu

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `"Menu"` | Accessible name of the button, and the title of the panel it opens. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |
| `closeLabel` | `string` | `"Close"` | Accessible name of the button that closes the panel. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |
| `side` | `"end" \| "start"` | `"end"` | The edge of the screen the panel is attached to. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | What's in the panel: the links, and anything else. |

`NavbarBrand` and `NavbarActions` add no props of their own. Every part but `NavbarMenu` takes what its element takes, including `ref` and `className`.

sections.heading: The links, twice
sections.markdown:
## The links, twice

On a wide screen the links are in `NavbarNav`. On a narrow one they're in the panel of `NavbarMenu`. They're the same links, so write them once, as a component or an array, and put them in both.

The bar doesn't move them for you, because the two places rarely hold quite the same things: a panel has room for the sign-in link that the bar shows as a button, and for a second level that the bar keeps in a menu.

Below the `collapse` breakpoint `NavbarNav` is taken out of the page with CSS, for screen readers as much as for the eye, and the panel's contents are only in the page while it's open. So nothing is announced twice.

sections.heading: Staying at the top
sections.markdown:
## Staying at the top

`sticky` keeps the bar at the top of the window while the page scrolls under it.

`hideOnScroll` is for a phone, where the bar takes a good part of the screen. The bar slides away while the page scrolls down and comes back as soon as it scrolls up, as a browser's own address bar does. It's always there at the top of the page, and it never leaves while focus is inside it.

sections.heading: The page that's open
sections.markdown:
## The page that's open

`current` on a `NavbarLink` marks it. Which link that is comes from your router:

```tsx
<NavbarLink asChild current={pathname === "/orders"}>
  <Link href="/orders">Orders</Link>
</NavbarLink>
```

sections.heading: With a navigation menu
sections.markdown:
## With a navigation menu

When some entries open a panel of more links, the bar's links are a [NavigationMenu](page:components/navigation-menu). It's a `nav` already, so give `NavbarNav` `asChild`, and it hands the menu its place in the bar without wrapping one `nav` in another.

```tsx
<NavbarNav asChild>
  <NavigationMenu aria-label="Main">…</NavigationMenu>
</NavbarNav>
```

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves through the name, the links and the actions, in the order they're written. |
| Enter | Follows a link, or opens the panel from its button. |
| Escape | Closes the panel, and puts focus back on its button. |

### What the component handles

- The bar is a `header`. At the top level of a page that's the banner landmark.
- `NavbarNav` is a `nav`, which a screen reader can jump to.
- The open page's link has `aria-current="page"`, and differs by a line under it as well as by color.
- The button has a name, says whether the panel is open, and is 44 pixels square.
- The panel is a dialog named by the same word, holds focus while it's open, and closes on Escape.
- Following a link in the panel closes it. That matters for a link to a part of the page that's already open.
- The panel closes by itself when the window gets wide enough for the links to be in the bar.
- A bar that hides on scroll stays while focus is in it, and doesn't slide for a visitor who asked for less motion.

### What you need to handle

- Name `NavbarNav`, and the `nav` in the panel, with `aria-label`: "Main" is the usual name.
- Translate `label` and `closeLabel` on `NavbarMenu`. [Translation](page:translation) lists them.
- Put a "Skip to content" link before the bar, so a keyboard user doesn't tab through it on every page.
- With `sticky`, give what links jump to a `scroll-margin-top` of the bar's height, or headings land under it.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

Below the breakpoint the bar holds the name, the actions and the button. Keep the actions to one or two: a phone is 320 pixels wide at its narrowest.

Links are 44 pixels tall with a finger and 40 with a mouse. In the panel each is a row the width of the panel.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on the `Navbar`, or on anything around it.

```css
.site {
  --nuv-navbar-height: 3.5rem;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-navbar-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 4)` | Space between the parts of the bar. |
| `--nuv-navbar-height` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 16)` | Least height of the bar, with its bottom edge. |
| `--nuv-navbar-padding` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 4)` | Space at each end of the bar. |
| `--nuv-navbar-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of the line under the bar. |
| `--nuv-navbar-bg` | `var(--color-background)` | Background color. Keep it solid on a sticky bar, so the page doesn't show through. |
| `--nuv-navbar-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Text color. |
| `--nuv-navbar-z` | `20` | Stacking order of a sticky bar. Over the page and under anything that opens over it. |
| `--nuv-navbar-link-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius of a link, and of the button. |
| `--nuv-navbar-link-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of a link that isn't the open page. Keep it at 4.5:1 against the bar. |
| `--nuv-navbar-link-hover-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of a link, and of the button, under the pointer. |
| `--nuv-navbar-link-active-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of the open page's link, and of a link under the pointer. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-navbar` | Navbar |
| `.nuv-navbar--collapse-lg` | collapse="lg" |
| `.nuv-navbar--collapse-md` | collapse="md" |
| `.nuv-navbar--collapse-sm` | collapse="sm" |
| `.nuv-navbar--sticky` | sticky, or hideOnScroll. |
| `.nuv-navbar__actions` | NavbarActions |
| `.nuv-navbar__brand` | NavbarBrand |
| `.nuv-navbar__link` | NavbarLink |
| `.nuv-navbar__menu` | What holds NavbarMenu's children, in the panel. |
| `.nuv-navbar__nav` | NavbarNav |
| `.nuv-navbar__toggle` | The button of NavbarMenu. |

A bar that's out of the way has a `data-hidden` attribute. The panel is a sheet, with the sheet's classes.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

Navbar starts with `"use client"`: it watches the page scroll, and the panel opens and closes. You can render it from a server component, with links that are server-rendered.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Keep the bar to five or six links. More than that is a sidebar, or a menu.
- Put the one action that matters most at the far end, and leave the rest for the panel.

**Don't**

- Don't hide the bar on scroll on a wide screen. It costs little room there and people look for it.
- Don't put a second row in it. Tabs for a page belong to the page.

It draws its own arrow. | | `NavigationMenuContent` | What the panel shows for that button. | | `NavigationMenuLink` | A link, in the row or inside a panel. | These are separate exports, not properties of `NavigationMenu`. `NavigationMenu.List` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component. What goes in `NavigationMenuContent` is up to you. The examples use a `ul` of links. ## Props ### NavigationMenu | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `align` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start"` | `"start"` | Which edge of the menu the open panel lines up with, on screens wide enough for the panel to be narrower than the menu. `"start"` is the left edge in a left-to-right layout. | | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` | `string` | | The `value` of the entry whose panel is open, when you control it yourself. An empty string means none. Use it with `onValueChange`. | | `defaultValue` | `string` | | The entry whose panel starts open, when you don't control it. | | `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void)` | | Called with an entry's `value` when its panel opens, and with an empty string when the panel closes. | | `delayDuration` | `number` | `200` | How long the pointer has to rest on a button before its panel opens, in milliseconds. It's 300 unless you say otherwise. | | `dir` | `"ltr" \| "rtl"` | | The reading direction. With `"rtl"`, the left and right arrow keys swap. | ### NavigationMenuItem | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` | `string` | | A name for this entry, to use with the menu's `value`. Only needed when you control which panel is open. | ### NavigationMenuLink | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `active` | `boolean` | | Marks the link as the page the visitor is on. It gets a fill, heavier text and `aria-current="page"`. | | `onSelect` | `((event: Event) => void)` | | Called when the link is followed. Call `event.preventDefault()` in it to leave the panel open. | | `asChild` | `boolean` | | Renders the element you pass in place of the `a`. This is how you use your router's link. | `NavigationMenuTrigger` takes `disabled`, and what a `button` takes. The other parts take what their elements take. The [Radix Navigation Menu reference](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/navigation-menu#api-reference) has the full list. ## The current page Pass `active` to the link for the page the visitor is on. Work out which one that is from your router. ```tsx import { NavigationMenu, NavigationMenuItem, NavigationMenuLink, NavigationMenuList, } from "@nuvui/react"; const pages = [ { name: "Overview", href: "/docs" }, { name: "Theming", href: "/docs/theming" }, { name: "Navigation menu", href: "/docs/components/navigation-menu" }, ]; export default function Example() { // In an app this comes from the router, such as usePathname() in Next.js. const pathname = "/docs/components/navigation-menu"; return ( {pages.map((page) => ( {page.name} ))} ); } ``` ## With your router's link Pass `asChild` and put the router's link inside. It gets the look and the keyboard behavior, and keeps its own way of changing page. ```tsx import { NavigationMenu, NavigationMenuContent, NavigationMenuItem, NavigationMenuLink, NavigationMenuList, NavigationMenuTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; import Link from "next/link"; export default function Example() { return ( Getting started More guides
  • Tailwind
  • SCSS
); } ``` ## Where the panel sits The panel hangs under the row. On a screen at least 40rem wide it's as wide as what it's showing, between 12rem and 40rem, and `align` says which part of the menu it lines up with: `"start"`, `"center"` or `"end"`. Use `"end"` for a menu at the far side of a header, so the panel doesn't run off the screen. The example above does. The panel is placed against the menu, not against the button that opened it. That's what lets it stay still while its content changes. Unlike a popover, it doesn't move itself to stay on the screen. Radix has no collision handling here. The width limits and `align` are what keep it in view, so check a menu at the widths your header is used at. ## On small screens Below 40rem the panel is as wide as the menu, whatever it holds. Make the menu as wide as the header there, and the panel fills the width of the screen. The entries are 44 pixels tall on a touch screen, and a row with more entries than fit wraps onto a second line. A tap on a button opens its panel, and a second tap closes it. That works, but a full site menu on a phone is more often a button that opens a [sheet](page:components/sheet) with every link in one list. The sheet page has an example. ## Accessibility ### Keyboard | Key | What it does | | --- | --- | | Tab | Moves through the buttons and links in the row. With a panel open, it goes from the button into the panel, through its links, and on to the next entry. | | → and ← | Move to the next or previous entry in the row. | | Home and End | Move to the first or last entry. | | Enter or Space | On a button, opens its panel, or closes it if it's open. Focus stays on the button. | | ↓ | On a button whose panel is open, moves into the panel. Inside it, moves to the next link. | | ↑ | Inside the panel, moves to the previous link. | | Enter | On a link, follows it. | | Esc | Closes the panel and returns focus to its button. | Safari only stops at links with Tab when "Press Tab to highlight each item on a webpage" is turned on in its settings. sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import {
  NavigationMenu,
  NavigationMenuContent,
  NavigationMenuItem,
  NavigationMenuLink,
  NavigationMenuList,
  NavigationMenuTrigger,
} from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `NavigationMenu` | The `nav` landmark around everything. It also renders the panel, under the list. |
| `NavigationMenuList` | The row of entries. A `ul`. |
| `NavigationMenuItem` | One entry. A `li` that holds either a link, or a trigger and its content. |
| `NavigationMenuTrigger` | A button that opens a panel. It draws its own arrow. |
| `NavigationMenuContent` | What the panel shows for that button. |
| `NavigationMenuLink` | A link, in the row or inside a panel. |

These are separate exports, not properties of `NavigationMenu`. `NavigationMenu.List` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component.

What goes in `NavigationMenuContent` is up to you. The examples use a `ul` of links.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

### NavigationMenu

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `align` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start"` | `"start"` | Which edge of the menu the open panel lines up with, on screens wide enough for the panel to be narrower than the menu. `"start"` is the left edge in a left-to-right layout. |

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` |  | The `value` of the entry whose panel is open, when you control it yourself. An empty string means none. Use it with `onValueChange`. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | The entry whose panel starts open, when you don't control it. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void)` |  | Called with an entry's `value` when its panel opens, and with an empty string when the panel closes. |
| `delayDuration` | `number` | `200` | How long the pointer has to rest on a button before its panel opens, in milliseconds. It's 200 unless you say otherwise. |
| `skipDelayDuration` | `number` | `300` | After the panel closes, how long another button can open it without waiting, in milliseconds. It's 300 unless you say otherwise. |
| `dir` | `"ltr" \| "rtl"` |  | The reading direction. With `"rtl"`, the left and right arrow keys swap. |

### NavigationMenuItem

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` |  | A name for this entry, to use with the menu's `value`. Only needed when you control which panel is open. |

### NavigationMenuLink

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `active` | `boolean` |  | Marks the link as the page the visitor is on. It gets a fill, heavier text and `aria-current="page"`. |
| `onSelect` | `((event: Event) => void)` |  | Called when the link is followed. Call `event.preventDefault()` in it to leave the panel open. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` |  | Renders the element you pass in place of the `a`. This is how you use your router's link. |

`NavigationMenuTrigger` takes `disabled`, and what a `button` takes. The other parts take what their elements take. The [Radix Navigation Menu reference](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/navigation-menu#api-reference) has the full list.
