With your router's link
sections.markdown:
## With your router's link Pass `asChild` and put the router's link inside. It gets the look and the keyboard behavior, and keeps its own way of changing page. ```tsx import { NavigationMenu, NavigationMenuContent, NavigationMenuItem, NavigationMenuLink, NavigationMenuList, NavigationMenuTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; import Link from "next/link"; export default function Example() { return ( Getting started More guides
  • Tailwind
  • SCSS
); } ```

sections.heading: Where the panel sits
sections.markdown:
## Where the panel sits

The panel hangs under the row. On a screen at least 40rem wide it's as wide as what it's showing, between 12rem and 40rem, and `align` says which part of the menu it lines up with: `"start"`, `"center"` or `"end"`. Use `"end"` for a menu at the far side of a header, so the panel doesn't run off the screen. The example above does.

The panel is placed against the menu, not against the button that opened it. That's what lets it stay still while its content changes.

Unlike a popover, it doesn't move itself to stay on the screen. Radix has no collision handling here. The width limits and `align` are what keep it in view, so check a menu at the widths your header is used at.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

Below 40rem the panel is as wide as the menu, whatever it holds. Make the menu as wide as the header there, and the panel fills the width of the screen.

The entries are 44 pixels tall on a touch screen, and a row with more entries than fit wraps onto a second line. A tap on a button opens its panel, and a second tap closes it.

That works, but a full site menu on a phone is more often a button that opens a [sheet](page:components/sheet) with every link in one list. The sheet page has an example.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves through the buttons and links in the row. With a panel open, it goes from the button into the panel, through its links, and on to the next entry. |
| <kbd>→</kbd> and <kbd>←</kbd> | Move to the next or previous entry in the row. |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> | Move to the first or last entry. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> | On a button, opens its panel, or closes it if it's open. Focus stays on the button. |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> | On a button whose panel is open, moves into the panel. Inside it, moves to the next link. |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> | Inside the panel, moves to the previous link. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | On a link, follows it. |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Closes the panel and returns focus to its button. |

Safari only stops at links with <kbd>Tab</kbd> when "Press Tab to highlight each item on a webpage" is turned on in its settings. With it off, <kbd>Tab</kbd> stops at the buttons, and the arrow keys still reach every link.

### What the component handles

Most of this is Radix.

- The whole thing is a `nav` landmark, and the row is a list.
- The buttons have `aria-expanded`, and `aria-controls` while their panel is open.
- These are links and buttons, not a `menubar` with `menuitem`s. That's deliberate: site navigation is a list of links, and menu roles would tell a screen reader to expect an application's menu.
- The panel comes right after its button in the tab order, though it's somewhere else in the page.
- Opening by the pointer waits 200 milliseconds, so a pointer passing over the row on its way somewhere else opens nothing. The panel stays while the pointer moves from the button onto it.
- A click on a button whose panel the pointer has just opened leaves the panel open. Radix alone closes it there, so that someone who points at a button and then clicks sees the panel open and shut. This is the one thing the library changes. A second click closes it, and so does a click on a button that a click opened.
- The current page's link has `aria-current="page"`, and is marked by its weight as well as its fill, so it doesn't depend on telling two colors apart.
- Buttons and links have a focus ring, and are 44 pixels tall on a touch screen.
- The panel's size and what it shows only animate when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion.

### What you need to handle

- The landmark is named "Main" unless you say otherwise. That's Radix's default, and it's in English. Pass `aria-label` to translate it, and to tell two menus on one page apart.
- Don't make a trigger a link as well. A button that opens a panel and also goes somewhere can only do one of those from the keyboard.
- In a right-to-left layout, pass `dir="rtl"`.

### A note on automated checks

While a panel is open, Radix puts an invisible element after the open button that takes focus and is hidden from screen readers. The moment <kbd>Tab</kbd> lands on it, it passes focus on into the panel. That's how the panel comes next in the tab order.

axe reports that element under its `aria-hidden-focus` rule, because it's something focusable inside a hidden part. Focus never stays there. The library's own tests leave that rule out for an open panel for this reason.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on `NavigationMenu`, or on anything around it. The panel is inside the menu, so it picks them up too.

```css
.site-header {
  --nuv-navigation-menu-max-width: 32rem;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-navigation-menu-item-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius of the buttons and links. |
| `--nuv-navigation-menu-hover-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of a button or link under the pointer, of the button whose panel is open, and of the current page's link. |
| `--nuv-navigation-menu-offset` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 1.5)` | The gap between the row and the panel. |
| `--nuv-navigation-menu-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Border color of the panel. |
| `--nuv-navigation-menu-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of the panel. |
| `--nuv-navigation-menu-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of the panel. |
| `--nuv-navigation-menu-shadow` | `var(--shadow-lg)` | Shadow under the panel. |
| `--nuv-navigation-menu-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color in the panel. |
| `--nuv-navigation-menu-padding` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 2)` | Padding inside the panel. |
| `--nuv-navigation-menu-min-width` | `12rem` | The narrowest the panel gets on a screen at least 40rem wide. |
| `--nuv-navigation-menu-max-width` | `40rem` | The widest the panel gets there. It's never wider than the screen less 32 pixels. |

The entries in the row take their text color from the page around them.

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-navigation-menu` | NavigationMenu. |
| `.nuv-navigation-menu--center` | The menu with align="center". |
| `.nuv-navigation-menu--end` | The menu with align="end". |
| `.nuv-navigation-menu__chevron` | The arrow in a trigger. |
| `.nuv-navigation-menu__content` | NavigationMenuContent. |
| `.nuv-navigation-menu__frame` | The box under the row that holds the panel and lines it up. |
| `.nuv-navigation-menu__link` | NavigationMenuLink. |
| `.nuv-navigation-menu__list` | NavigationMenuList. |
| `.nuv-navigation-menu__trigger` | NavigationMenuTrigger. |
| `.nuv-navigation-menu__viewport` | The panel. Radix calls it the viewport. |

The menu also gets `nuv-navigation-menu--start` at the default alignment, and each entry gets `nuv-navigation-menu__item`. No styles are attached to either.

Radix sets `data-state="open"` on the button whose panel is open and on the panel, `data-active` on a link with `active`, and `data-motion` on the content as one replaces another. The fills and the animations hang off those.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

The navigation menu parts are client components. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files.

You can put a menu together inside a server component, as the examples on this page do. Only the row is in the HTML the server sends: a panel's links are rendered when it opens. If those links have to be there for search engines, put them in the page's footer or a sitemap as well.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Keep the row to a handful of entries, each a word or two.
- Give a panel's links a line of description when their names alone don't say enough.
- Mark the current page.

**Don't**

- Don't use one for the commands of an application. That's a [menubar](page:components/menubar).
- Don't put a panel inside a panel.
- Don't put a form or anything else that isn't navigation in a panel. For that, use a [popover](page:components/popover).

pages.title: NumberField
pages.description: A field for a number that can be typed or stepped, with limits, a step size, and the number written for a language and region.
pages.markdown:
# NumberField A field for a number that can be typed or stepped, with limits, a step size, and the number written for a language and region. Use a number field for a quantity someone sets: seats, a budget, a discount. It takes typing, a button at each end, and the arrow keys. For a number picked by feel from a range, use a [slider](page:components/slider). ```tsx import { Label, NumberField } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return (
); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { NumberField } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` | `number \| null` | | The number, when you control it yourself. `null` is an empty field. | | `defaultValue` | `number \| null` | | The number at first, when you don't control it. | | `onValueChange` | `((value: number \| null) => void)` | | Called with the new number when it changes: on a press of a button or an arrow key, and when typing is finished, which is on Enter and on leaving the field. Not on every key. `null` means the field was emptied. | | `min` | `number` | | The least the number can be. A smaller one is raised to it. | | `max` | `number` | | The most the number can be. A larger one is lowered to it. | | `step` | `number` | `1` | How much a button or an arrow key changes the number by. | | `largeStep` | `number` | | How much Page Up and Page Down change it by. Ten steps unless you say otherwise. | | `format` | `FormatNumberOptions` | | How the number is written when it isn't being typed: a locale, a currency, a percentage, a number of decimals. What's typed is read by the same rules, so in German `1.234,5` is one number. | | `incrementLabel` | `string` | `"Increase"` | Accessible name of the button that raises the number. Translate it with the rest of your interface. | | `decrementLabel` | `string` | `"Decrease"` | Accessible name of the button that lowers the number. Translate it with the rest of your interface. | | `name` | `string` | | The name the number is submitted under in a form. What's sent is the plain number, such as `1234.5`, however it's written on the screen. | Everything else is passed to the ``, including `ref`, `id`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required` and `placeholder`. `className` goes on the box around it. ## When the number changes `onValueChange` is called when the number changes, and not on every key. A press of a button or an arrow key changes it at once. Typing changes it when the typing is finished: on Enter, and on leaving the field. Until then "12" on its way to "125" isn't reported as twelve. What's typed is tidied when it's taken. A number past `min` or `max` is moved to the limit, a number with more decimals than the format shows is rounded to what it shows, and text that isn't a number is dropped, which puts the last number back. An emptied field is `null`. ## Formats `format` takes what [`FormattedNumber`](page:components/formatted-number) does: a locale, a currency, a percentage, a number of decimals, a unit. The field shows the number that way when it isn't being typed into. ```tsx import { Label, NumberField } from "@nuvui/react"; const row = { display: "grid", gap: 6, inlineSize: "100%", maxInlineSize: 220, }; export default function Example() { return (
); } ``` Typing is read by the same rules. With a German locale `1.234,5` is one thousand two hundred and thirty-four and a half, and a currency sign or a unit that's typed along with the digits is ignored. A percentage is typed as people say it: 15 for 15%, which gives the value 0.15. Give every field the locale your app is in. Left out, it's `"en-US"`, and never the visitor's own, so that the server and the browser write the same text. ## In a form With a `name`, the number is submitted as plain digits, such as `1250`, however it's written on the screen. Inside a [field](page:components/field), the label, the description and the error are connected for you. ```tsx "use client"; import { Button, Field, FieldControl, FieldDescription, FieldLabel, NumberField, } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { const [sent, setSent] = useState(); return (
{ event.preventDefault(); const data = new FormData(event.currentTarget); setSent(String(data.get("amount"))); }} > Amount In euros. What's sent is the plain number. {sent === undefined ? "" : `Sent: ${sent}`}
); } ``` `required` stops the form while the field is empty. `min` and `max` can't fail: a number outside them is moved inside when it's taken. ## Accessibility | Key | What it does | | --- | --- | | Arrow up, Arrow down | One step up or down. | | Page up, Page down | A large step, ten steps unless `largeStep` says otherwise. | | Home, End | To `min` or `max`, when there is one. | | Enter | Takes what's typed. In a form it submits, as in any field. | ### What the component handles - The input has `role="spinbutton"`, with the number, the limits, and the number as it's written on the screen, so a screen reader says "$2,500" and not "2500". - The two buttons are named "Decrease" and "Increase". Tab doesn't stop on them, because the arrow keys do the same from the field. A screen reader and a switch can still reach and press them. - A button is disabled at its limit. - Holding a button repeats the step. - A phone shows its number keypad where a negative number can't be typed, which is when `min` is zero or more. The keypad has a decimal point unless the format has no decimals. - The focus ring goes around the whole box, and the box's edge turns red while the field is invalid. ### What you need to handle - Give it a label, with a [`Label`](page:components/label) and an `id`, or a [`Field`](page:components/field). - Translate the two button names. [Translation](page:translation) lists them. - Say the unit somewhere a screen reader gets it, when the format doesn't write one: in the label, as in "Weight in kilograms". - Say the limits in a description when they aren't obvious. A number that's quietly moved to a limit is confusing without one. ## On small screens Each button is 44 pixels to a finger, though it's drawn smaller. The text is 16 pixels on a touch screen, which keeps iOS from zooming the page in when the field takes focus. ## CSS variables Set any of these on the field, or on anything around it. ```css .quantity { --nuv-number-field-width: 8rem; } ``` | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-number-field-width` | `100%` | Width. It fills its container by default. | | `--nuv-number-field-border` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Border color of the box. | | `--nuv-number-field-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius of the box. | | `--nuv-number-field-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of the box. | | `--nuv-number-field-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Text color. | | `--nuv-number-field-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-md)` | Minimum height of the box. The buttons are sized from it. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. | | `--nuv-number-field-align` | `center` | Where the number sits between the buttons. In the middle by default. Set it to `end` to line numbers up in a column. | | `--nuv-number-field-font-size` | `var(--text-base)`, `var(--text-sm)` | Font size. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. | | `--nuv-number-field-placeholder` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the placeholder. | | `--nuv-number-field-button-radius` | `var(--radius-sm)` | Corner radius of the buttons. | | `--nuv-number-field-button-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the minus and the plus. | | `--nuv-number-field-button-bg-hover` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of a button while hovered. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-number-field` | The box around the input and the buttons. | | `.nuv-number-field__button` | Each of the two buttons. | | `.nuv-number-field__control` | The input. | ## Server components NumberField starts with `"use client"`, because it keeps what's being typed. You can still render it from a server component, with plain props. `onValueChange` needs a client component. ## Do and don't **Do** - Set `min` and `max` wherever the number has them. - Pick a `step` that matches how people change the number: 1 for seats, 50 for a budget. **Don't** - Don't use it for a number that isn't a quantity, such as a phone number, a postcode or a card number. Those are text: use an [input](page:components/input). - Don't rely on the buttons for a large change. Typing has to work, and does.

| `value` | `number \| null` |  | The number, when you control it yourself. `null` is an empty field. |
| `defaultValue` | `number \| null` |  | The number at first, when you don't control it. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: number \| null) => void)` |  | Called with the new number when it changes: on a press of a button or an arrow key, and when typing is finished, which is on Enter and on leaving the field. Not on every key. `null` means the field was emptied. |
| `min` | `number` |  | The least the number can be. A smaller one is raised to it. |
| `max` | `number` |  | The most the number can be. A larger one is lowered to it. |
| `step` | `number` | `1` | How much a button or an arrow key changes the number by. |
| `largeStep` | `number` |  | How much Page Up and Page Down change it by. Ten steps unless you say otherwise. |
| `format` | `FormatNumberOptions` |  | How the number is written when it isn't being typed: a locale, a currency, a percentage, a number of decimals. What's typed is read by the same rules, so in German `1.234,5` is one number. |
| `incrementLabel` | `string` | `"Increase"` | Accessible name of the button that raises the number. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |
| `decrementLabel` | `string` | `"Decrease"` | Accessible name of the button that lowers the number. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the number is submitted under in a form. What's sent is the plain number, such as `1234.5`, however it's written on the screen. |

Everything else is passed to the `<input>`, including `ref`, `id`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required` and `placeholder`. `className` goes on the box around it.

sections.heading: When the number changes
sections.markdown:
## When the number changes

`onValueChange` is called when the number changes, and not on every key. A press of a button or an arrow key changes it at once. Typing changes it when the typing is finished: on Enter, and on leaving the field. Until then "12" on its way to "125" isn't reported as twelve.

What's typed is tidied when it's taken. A number past `min` or `max` is moved to the limit, a number with more decimals than the format shows is rounded to what it shows, and text that isn't a number is dropped, which puts the last number back. An emptied field is `null`.

sections.heading: Formats
In a form
Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Arrow up, Arrow down | One step up or down. |
| Page up, Page down | A large step, ten steps unless `largeStep` says otherwise. |
| Home, End | To `min` or `max`, when there is one. |
| Enter | Takes what's typed. In a form it submits, as in any field. |

### What the component handles

- The input has `role="spinbutton"`, with the number, the limits, and the number as it's written on the screen, so a screen reader says "$2,500" and not "2500".
- The two buttons are named "Decrease" and "Increase". Tab doesn't stop on them, because the arrow keys do the same from the field. A screen reader and a switch can still reach and press them.
- A button is disabled at its limit.
- Holding a button repeats the step.
- A phone shows its number keypad where a negative number can't be typed, which is when `min` is zero or more. The keypad has a decimal point unless the format has no decimals.
- The focus ring goes around the whole box, and the box's edge turns red while the field is invalid.

### What you need to handle

- Give it a label, with a [`Label`](page:components/label) and an `id`, or a [`Field`](page:components/field).
- Translate the two button names. [Translation](page:translation) lists them.
- Say the unit somewhere a screen reader gets it, when the format doesn't write one: in the label, as in "Weight in kilograms".
- Say the limits in a description when they aren't obvious. A number that's quietly moved to a limit is confusing without one.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

Each button is 44 pixels to a finger, though it's drawn smaller. The text is 16 pixels on a touch screen, which keeps iOS from zooming the page in when the field takes focus.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on the field, or on anything around it.

```css
.quantity {
  --nuv-number-field-width: 8rem;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-number-field-width` | `100%` | Width. It fills its container by default. |
| `--nuv-number-field-border` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Border color of the box. |
| `--nuv-number-field-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius of the box. |
| `--nuv-number-field-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of the box. |
| `--nuv-number-field-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Text color. |
| `--nuv-number-field-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-md)` | Minimum height of the box. The buttons are sized from it. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. |
| `--nuv-number-field-align` | `center` | Where the number sits between the buttons. In the middle by default. Set it to `end` to line numbers up in a column. |
| `--nuv-number-field-font-size` | `var(--text-base)`, `var(--text-sm)` | Font size. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. |
| `--nuv-number-field-placeholder` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the placeholder. |
| `--nuv-number-field-button-radius` | `var(--radius-sm)` | Corner radius of the buttons. |
| `--nuv-number-field-button-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the minus and the plus. |
| `--nuv-number-field-button-bg-hover` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of a button while hovered. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-number-field` | The box around the input and the buttons. |
| `.nuv-number-field__button` | Each of the two buttons. |
| `.nuv-number-field__control` | The input. |

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

NumberField starts with `"use client"`, because it keeps what's being typed. You can still render it from a server component, with plain props. `onValueChange` needs a client component.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Set `min` and `max` wherever the number has them.
- Pick a `step` that matches how people change the number: 1 for seats, 50 for a budget.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for a number that isn't a quantity, such as a phone number, a postcode or a card number. Those are text: use an [input](page:components/input).
- Don't rely on the buttons for a large change. Typing has to work, and does.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |

| `length` | `number` | `6` | How many characters the code has. One box is drawn for each. |

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |

sections.heading: Groups
In a form
On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

Each box is 44 pixels square on a touch screen and 40 with a mouse, where [density](page:theming#density) moves it. Six of them with their gaps are 304 pixels wide. In a narrower space the boxes get narrower and keep their height.

With the default `validationType`, a phone opens its number pad.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves into the field, to the first empty box, and out of it again. The boxes are one tab stop together. |
| A character | Fills the box and moves to the next. One that isn't allowed is ignored. |
| <kbd>Backspace</kbd> | Clears the box and moves to the one before. |
| <kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd> | Move between the boxes that are filled, and the first empty one. |
| Paste | Fills the boxes from the start with the pasted code. Spaces in it are dropped. |

### What the component handles

Most of this is Radix. The library doesn't change it.

- The boxes sit in an element with `role="group"`. Give it a name and a screen reader reads it when focus moves in.
- Each box has a name of its own, "Character 2 of 6". `inputLabel` replaces it, for another language.
- `aria-invalid` on the field is put on each box, where it means something, and not on the group.
- A box can't be reached until the ones before it are filled, so a code is always typed in order.
- Each box's edge uses `--color-border-strong`, at least 3:1 against the page in every theme. The box with focus has a 2 pixel ring.

### What you need to handle

- Name the group. Use `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` pointing at visible text. A `<label>` can't do it, because there's no single input for it to point at. In a [Field](page:components/field), use `FieldLabel asChild` around a `<span>`.
- Say where the code was sent, and offer a way to get another one.
- Don't put a short time limit on typing it. If the code expires, say when.


| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-otp-field-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 2)` | Space between boxes. |
| `--nuv-otp-field-size` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-md)` | Width and height of a box. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. |
| `--nuv-otp-field-font-size` | `var(--text-lg)` | Font size of the character in a box. |
| `--nuv-otp-field-border` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Border color of a box. |
| `--nuv-otp-field-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius of a box. |
| `--nuv-otp-field-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of a box. |
| `--nuv-otp-field-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Text color. |
| `--nuv-otp-field-readonly-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background color of a box while read-only. |
| `--nuv-otp-field-separator` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Color of the dash between groups. |

sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-otp-field` | The group around the boxes. |

| `.nuv-otp-field__separator` | The dash between groups. |

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

OtpField is a client component. It carries `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files. You can render it from a server component, as the first example on this page does.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Match `length` to the code you send.
- Leave `autoComplete` at `"one-time-code"` for codes sent by text message.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for a password or anything else people know by heart.
- Don't clear the boxes when the code is wrong. Leave it there, say it didn't match, and let people fix one digit.

pages.title: Pagination
pages.description: Links to the pages of a long list, with Previous and Next and a helper that works out which page numbers to show.
pages.markdown:
# Pagination Links to the pages of a long list, with Previous and Next and a helper that works out which page numbers to show. Use pagination to split a long list into pages people move through: search results, a table of orders, an archive. It comes as parts you put together, because only your app knows where each page lives, and a function, `paginationRange`, that does the arithmetic. ```tsx import { Pagination, PaginationEllipsis, PaginationItem, PaginationLink, PaginationList, PaginationNext, PaginationPrevious, } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return ( 1 2 3 12 ); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Pagination, PaginationEllipsis, PaginationItem, PaginationLink, PaginationList, PaginationNext, PaginationPrevious, paginationRange, } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `Pagination` | The `nav` landmark around the links. | | `PaginationList` | The row. A `ul`. | | `PaginationItem` | One place in the row. A `li`. | | `PaginationLink` | The link to one page. | | `PaginationPrevious` | The link to the page before, with an arrow. | | `PaginationNext` | The link to the page after, with an arrow. | | `PaginationEllipsis` | Three dots that stand for the page numbers left out. | | `paginationRange` | A function, not a component. It says which numbers and gaps to show. | ## Props ### PaginationLink | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `active` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the link as the page being shown. It gets the filled look and `aria-current="page"`. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | For a link that leads nowhere right now, such as "Previous" on the first page. It stays in place, faded, and can't be followed or focused. | | `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead of an `a`, and give it the link's classes and props. This is how you use your router's link, or a `button` when the pages are state and not addresses. | It also takes what an `a` takes, `href` included. `PaginationPrevious` and `PaginationNext` take the same props. ### PaginationEllipsis | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `label` | `string` | `"More pages"` | What a screen reader says for the three dots. Translate it with the rest of your interface. | ### paginationRange | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `page` (required) | `number` | | The page being shown, counted from 1. | | `count` (required) | `number` | | How many pages there are. | | `siblings` | `number` | `1` | How many page numbers to show on each side of the current one. | | `boundaries` | `number` | `1` | How many page numbers to always show at each end. | `Pagination`, `PaginationList` and `PaginationItem` take what their elements take, including `ref` and `className`. ## Working out the numbers `paginationRange` takes the current page and the number of pages, and gives back what to show: page numbers, and `"ellipsis-start"` or `"ellipsis-end"` where numbers were left out. ```ts paginationRange({ page: 10, count: 20 }); // [1, "ellipsis-start", 9, 10, 11, "ellipsis-end", 20] ``` Three things hold for whatever it returns: - The row is the same length whichever page is current, so the links don't move under the pointer as someone clicks through. - A gap always stands for two pages or more. Where only one would be hidden, its number is shown. - No entry appears twice, so each one can be the `key` of its item. `siblings` is how many numbers show on each side of the current page, and `boundaries` how many at each end. Both are 1 unless you say otherwise. ## When the pages are state In a table or a search that keeps its page in state, there's no address to link to. Pass `asChild` and put a `button` inside. It gets the look and `aria-current`, and you give it the `onClick`. ```tsx "use client"; import { Pagination, PaginationEllipsis, PaginationItem, PaginationLink, PaginationList, PaginationNext, PaginationPrevious, paginationRange, } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; const count = 20; export default function Example() { const [page, setPage] = useState(1); return (
{paginationRange({ page, count }).map((entry) => ( {typeof entry === "number" ? ( ) : ( )} ))}

Page {page} of {count}

); } ``` A disabled button needs both: `disabled` on the `PaginationLink`, for the look, and `disabled` on the `button` itself, so the browser stops it being pressed. ## With your router's link `asChild` is also how you use a router's link. `PaginationPrevious` and `PaginationNext` put their arrow inside it, next to its text. ```tsx import { Pagination, PaginationItem, PaginationLink, PaginationList, PaginationNext, PaginationPrevious, } from "@nuvui/react"; import Link from "next/link"; // Stands in for a list of pages your app has. Here they're three of the // guides on this site. const pages = ["/theming", "/tailwind", "/scss"]; const current = 1; export default function Example() { return ( Previous {pages.map((href, index) => ( {index + 1} ))} Next ); } ``` With `asChild` the text comes from your element, so that's where to translate "Previous" and "Next". Without it, pass the translated word as the child: `Weiter`. ## On small screens Each link is 44 pixels square on a touch screen. Seven of them plus Previous and Next don't fit a phone in one row, so the row wraps. Two things keep it to one row there. Below 40rem, Previous and Next show only their arrows. Their text is still there for screen readers. And `siblings: 0` drops the numbers either side of the current page, which leaves the first, the current and the last, with a gap on each side. ```tsx import { Pagination, PaginationEllipsis, PaginationItem, PaginationLink, PaginationList, PaginationNext, PaginationPrevious, paginationRange, } from "@nuvui/react"; const page = 7; const count = 20; export default function Example() { return ( {paginationRange({ page, count, siblings: 0 }).map((entry) => ( {typeof entry === "number" ? ( {entry} ) : ( )} ))} ); } ``` ## Accessibility ### Keyboard | Key | What it does | | --- | --- | | Tab | Moves through the links in order. A disabled one is skipped. | | Enter | Follows the focused link. On a button, Space does too. | Safari only stops at links with Tab when "Press Tab to highlight each item on a webpage" is turned on in its settings. That applies to every link on every site. Buttons, as in the state example, are always stops. ### What the component handles - The row is a `nav` landmark named "Pagination", around a list. - The current page's link has `aria-current="page"`. It's filled with the primary color, which has at least 3:1 contrast with the page, and its number keeps 4.5:1 on that fill. - A disabled link has no `href`, so it can't be followed or focused. It keeps `role="link"` and gets `aria-disabled="true"`, so that it's still exposed as a link that's unavailable and not as loose text. - The arrows are hidden from screen readers, and point the other way in a right-to-left layout. - The dots have a name, "More pages". - Numbers are set in digits of equal width where the font has them, so the row doesn't shift as the numbers change. - Where the browser forces its own colors, as Windows high contrast does, the current page is filled with the system's color for something selected. ### What you need to handle - Give each number link a full name: `aria-label="Page 3"`. "3" alone says little when it's read out of context. - Leave Previous and Next in place on the first and last page, and disable them. A row that changes shape moves the links people are aiming at. - Translate the landmark's name with `aria-label` on `Pagination`, the dots' name with `label`, and the text of Previous and Next. - After the page changes without a full page load, move focus to the top of the new results, or announce the change. sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import {
  Pagination,
  PaginationEllipsis,
  PaginationItem,
  PaginationLink,
  PaginationList,
  PaginationNext,
  PaginationPrevious,
  paginationRange,
} from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Pagination` | The `nav` landmark around the links. |
| `PaginationList` | The row. A `ul`. |
| `PaginationItem` | One place in the row. A `li`. |
| `PaginationLink` | The link to one page. |
| `PaginationPrevious` | The link to the page before, with an arrow. |
| `PaginationNext` | The link to the page after, with an arrow. |
| `PaginationEllipsis` | Three dots that stand for the page numbers left out. |
| `paginationRange` | A function, not a component. It says which numbers and gaps to show. |

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

### PaginationLink

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `active` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the link as the page being shown. It gets the filled look and `aria-current="page"`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | For a link that leads nowhere right now, such as "Previous" on the first page. It stays in place, faded, and can't be followed or focused. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead of an `a`, and give it the link's classes and props. This is how you use your router's link, or a `button` when the pages are state and not addresses. |

It also takes what an `a` takes, `href` included. `PaginationPrevious` and `PaginationNext` take the same props.

### PaginationEllipsis

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `"More pages"` | What a screen reader says for the three dots. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |

### paginationRange

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` (required) | `number` |  | The page being shown, counted from 1. |
| `count` (required) | `number` |  | How many pages there are. |
| `siblings` | `number` | `1` | How many page numbers to show on each side of the current one. |
| `boundaries` | `number` | `1` | How many page numbers to always show at each end. |

`Pagination`, `PaginationList` and `PaginationItem` take what their elements take, including `ref` and `className`.

sections.heading: Working out the numbers
sections.markdown:
## Working out the numbers

`paginationRange` takes the current page and the number of pages, and gives back what to show: page numbers, and `"ellipsis-start"` or `"ellipsis-end"` where numbers were left out.

```ts
paginationRange({ page: 10, count: 20 });
// [1, "ellipsis-start", 9, 10, 11, "ellipsis-end", 20]
```

Three things hold for whatever it returns:

- The row is the same length whichever page is current, so the links don't move under the pointer as someone clicks through.
- A gap always stands for two pages or more. Where only one would be hidden, its number is shown.
- No entry appears twice, so each one can be the `key` of its item.

`siblings` is how many numbers show on each side of the current page, and `boundaries` how many at each end. Both are 1 unless you say otherwise.

sections.heading: When the pages are state
With your router's link
On small screens
Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves through the links in order. A disabled one is skipped. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Follows the focused link. On a button, <kbd>Space</kbd> does too. |

Safari only stops at links with <kbd>Tab</kbd> when "Press Tab to highlight each item on a webpage" is turned on in its settings. That applies to every link on every site. Buttons, as in the state example, are always stops.

### What the component handles

- The row is a `nav` landmark named "Pagination", around a list.
- The current page's link has `aria-current="page"`. It's filled with the primary color, which has at least 3:1 contrast with the page, and its number keeps 4.5:1 on that fill.
- A disabled link has no `href`, so it can't be followed or focused. It keeps `role="link"` and gets `aria-disabled="true"`, so that it's still exposed as a link that's unavailable and not as loose text.
- The arrows are hidden from screen readers, and point the other way in a right-to-left layout.
- The dots have a name, "More pages".
- Numbers are set in digits of equal width where the font has them, so the row doesn't shift as the numbers change.
- Where the browser forces its own colors, as Windows high contrast does, the current page is filled with the system's color for something selected.

### What you need to handle

- Give each number link a full name: `aria-label="Page 3"`. "3" alone says little when it's read out of context.
- Leave Previous and Next in place on the first and last page, and disable them. A row that changes shape moves the links people are aiming at.
- Translate the landmark's name with `aria-label` on `Pagination`, the dots' name with `label`, and the text of Previous and Next.
- After the page changes without a full page load, move focus to the top of the new results, or announce the change. Otherwise nothing tells a screen reader user that the list changed.

| --- | --- | --- |

| `--nuv-pagination-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius of a link. |
| `--nuv-pagination-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Text color of the links. |
| `--nuv-pagination-size` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-md)` | Height of a link, and its smallest width. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. Setting it sets both, so keep it at 44 pixels or more where people use touch. |
| `--nuv-pagination-hover-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of a link under the pointer. |
| `--nuv-pagination-active-bg` | `var(--color-primary)` | Background of the current page's link. Keep it at 3:1 against the page. |
| `--nuv-pagination-active-fg` | `var(--color-primary-foreground)` | Text color of the current page's link. |

**Don't**

# PasswordInput A password field with a button that shows what was typed and hides it again. Use a password input wherever someone types a password or another secret. The button lets people check what they typed before they send it, which matters most on a phone keyboard. ```tsx import { Label, PasswordInput } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return (
); } ``` > **Built on a Radix primitive that isn't at 1.0** > > This wraps Radix's Password Toggle Field, which is at version 0.1 and may still change. The package pins it to an exact version, and this component's own props are what the library promises to keep. ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { PasswordInput } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `visible` | `boolean` | | Whether the password can be read, when you control that yourself. | | `defaultVisible` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the password can be read at first, when you don't control it. | | `onVisibilityChange` | `((visible: boolean) => void)` | | Called with the new state when the button is pressed. | | `showLabel` | `string` | `"Show password"` | Accessible name of the button while the password is hidden. Translate it with the rest of your interface. | | `hideLabel` | `string` | `"Hide password"` | Accessible name of the button while the password can be read. | | `autoComplete` | `"current-password" \| "new-password"` | `"current-password"` | What the browser and password managers fill in. # Popover A small panel that opens next to a button and stays until it's dismissed. Use a popover for a few controls or a bit of detail that belongs to one button: sharing options, a short form, a filter. It doesn't block the page, so it suits things people are free to ignore. For something they have to answer, use a [dialog](page:components/dialog). For a hint on hover, use a [tooltip](page:components/tooltip). ```tsx import { Button, Popover, PopoverClose, PopoverContent, PopoverTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return (

Anyone with the link can view this page.

 ); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Popover, PopoverAnchor, PopoverClose, PopoverContent, PopoverTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `Popover` | Holds the open state. Renders nothing itself. | | `PopoverTrigger` | The button that opens the popover. | | `PopoverContent` | The panel. It places itself next to the trigger, and can draw an arrow that points at it. | | `PopoverClose` | Closes the popover when pressed. Wrap your own button with `asChild`. | | `PopoverAnchor` | Optional. Wrap another element in it to place the panel against that instead of the trigger. | These are separate exports, not properties of `Popover`. `Popover.Content` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component. ## Props ### PopoverContent | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `showArrow` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether to draw an arrow that points at the trigger. | | `sideOffset` | `number` | `8` | The gap between the trigger and the popover, in pixels. With the arrow shown, it's measured from the arrow's tip. | | `collisionPadding` | `number \| Partial>` | `8` | How close the popover may get to the edge of the screen, in pixels. It moves or flips to keep this much room. | | `arrowPadding` | `number` | `12` | How far the arrow keeps from the panel's corners, in pixels. It stops the arrow sitting on the rounded part when the trigger is near a corner. | | `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the popover is rendered into. Set this when the popover should pick up a `data-theme` from a section of the page. | These come from Radix and are the ones you're most likely to set: | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `side` | `"bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top"` | | The side of the trigger the panel opens on. It's `"bottom"` unless you say otherwise, and it flips to the opposite side when there isn't room. | | `align` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start"` | | How the panel lines up with the trigger along that side. It's `"center"` unless you say otherwise. | | `avoidCollisions` | `boolean` | | Pass `false` to keep the panel on the side you chose even when it doesn't fit there. | | `onOpenAutoFocus` | `((event: Event) => void)` | | Called when focus is about to move into the panel. sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import {
  Popover,
  PopoverAnchor,
  PopoverClose,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Popover` | Holds the open state. Renders nothing itself. |
| `PopoverTrigger` | The button that opens the popover. |
| `PopoverContent` | The panel. It places itself next to the trigger, and can draw an arrow that points at it. |
| `PopoverClose` | Closes the popover when pressed. Wrap your own button with `asChild`. |
| `PopoverAnchor` | Optional. Wrap another element in it to place the panel against that instead of the trigger. |

These are separate exports, not properties of `Popover`. `Popover.Content` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

### PopoverContent

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `showArrow` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether to draw an arrow that points at the trigger. |
| `sideOffset` | `number` | `8` | The gap between the trigger and the popover, in pixels. With the arrow shown, it's measured from the arrow's tip. |
| `collisionPadding` | `number \| Partial<Record<"bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top", number>>` | `8` | How close the popover may get to the edge of the screen, in pixels. It moves or flips to keep this much room. |
| `arrowPadding` | `number` | `12` | How far the arrow keeps from the panel's corners, in pixels. It stops the arrow sitting on the rounded part when the trigger is near a corner. |
| `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the popover is rendered into. Set this when the popover should pick up a `data-theme` from a section of the page. |

These come from Radix and are the ones you're most likely to set:

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `side` | `"bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top"` |  | The side of the trigger the panel opens on. It's `"bottom"` unless you say otherwise, and it flips to the opposite side when there isn't room. |
| `align` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start"` |  | How the panel lines up with the trigger along that side. It's `"center"` unless you say otherwise. |
| `avoidCollisions` | `boolean` |  | Pass `false` to keep the panel on the side you chose even when it doesn't fit there. |
| `onOpenAutoFocus` | `((event: Event) => void)` |  | Called when focus is about to move into the panel. Call `event.preventDefault()` to move it somewhere yourself. |

### Popover

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Whether it's open, when you control it yourself. Use it with `onOpenChange`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` |  | Whether it starts open, when you don't control it. |
| `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean) => void)` |  | Called when it opens or closes. |
| `modal` | `boolean` |  | With `true`, the rest of the page can't be clicked, and screen readers can't reach it, while the popover is open. |

The other parts take the same props as the Radix parts they wrap, including `asChild`. The [Radix Popover reference](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/popover#api-reference) lists them.

With an arrow
With a form

## With a form Opening a popover moves focus to the first control inside it, so a field is ready to type in. ```tsx import { Button, Popover, PopoverClose, PopoverContent, PopoverTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; const field = { inlineSize: "100%", minBlockSize: 44, paddingInline: 12, border: "1px solid var(--color-border-strong)", borderRadius: "var(--radius-md)", backgroundColor: "var(--color-surface)", color: "inherit", // 16px keeps iOS from zooming in when the field takes focus. fontSize: 16, }; export default function Example() { return (
); } ```

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

The panel is 18rem wide. It's never wider or taller than the room Radix finds around the trigger, so on a narrow screen it shrinks to fit, and content that's too tall scrolls inside it. The page itself never scrolls sideways because of a popover.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> | On the trigger, opens the popover and moves focus into it. |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves to the next control inside the popover. From the last one it goes back to the first. |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves to the previous control, and from the first to the last. |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Closes the popover and returns focus to the trigger. |

### What the component handles

Most of this is Radix. The library doesn't change it.

- The panel has `role="dialog"`. The trigger gets `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`.
- Opening moves focus to the first control in the panel, or to the panel itself if it has none. Closing returns focus to the trigger.
- A click or tap outside the panel closes it.
- The panel stays inside the screen, with 8 pixels to spare, and flips to the other side of the trigger when it has to.
- The open and close animations only run when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion.
- When the content scrolls and has nothing inside that takes focus, the part that scrolls becomes a tab stop itself, with the popover's name. Without that, someone who doesn't use a mouse would have no way to scroll it.
- The arrow is hidden from screen readers and takes no clicks.

### What you need to handle

- Give `PopoverContent` a name with `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` pointing at a heading inside it. Without one, a screen reader only says "dialog".
- <kbd>Tab</kbd> goes round inside an open popover and doesn't carry on down the page. People leave with <kbd>Esc</kbd> or a click outside. If the panel holds more than a line or two, add a visible way out with `PopoverClose`.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Popovers render at the end of `<body>`, so set these on `:root` or `body`, or straight on `PopoverContent` with `style` or a class. Setting them on the element around the trigger has no effect.

```css
:root {
  --nuv-popover-width: 22rem;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-popover-width` | `18rem` | Width of the panel. It still shrinks to fit a narrow screen. |
| `--nuv-popover-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Border color. The arrow's edge uses it too. |
| `--nuv-popover-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius. |
| `--nuv-popover-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color. The arrow is filled with it too. |
| `--nuv-popover-shadow` | `var(--shadow-lg)` | Shadow under the panel. |
| `--nuv-popover-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color. |
| `--nuv-popover-padding` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 4)` | Padding inside the panel. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-popover` | PopoverContent, which is the panel. |
| `.nuv-popover__arrow` | The arrow. |
| `.nuv-popover__arrow-frame` | An invisible box the arrow is placed against. It's only there with showArrow. |
| `.nuv-popover__body` | The element inside the panel that holds your content. It has the padding, and it's the part that scrolls. |

A `className` or `style` on `PopoverContent` goes to the panel. Your content sits one level down, in the body, so to lay it out as a grid or a row, wrap it in an element of your own.

The trigger is your own element, so it has no class from this component.

Radix sets `data-state="open"` or `data-state="closed"` on the panel, along with `data-side` and `data-align` for where it ended up. The animation hangs off `data-state`.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

The popover parts are client components. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files.

You can put a popover together inside a server component, as the examples on this page do. It only needs a client component of your own when you control `open` or add handlers.

sections.heading: Themed sections
sections.markdown:
## Themed sections

A popover opened from inside a `data-theme="dark"` section doesn't inherit that theme, because it isn't rendered inside the section. Pass the section's element as `container` and it will be.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Keep it small. A popover that needs scrolling on a desktop should probably be a dialog.
- Open it from a button that says what's inside.
- Put the control people came for first, since that's where focus lands.

**Don't**

- Don't open a popover on hover. Touch screens have no hover, and it's easy to trigger by accident with a mouse.
- Don't put the only copy of important information in one. It's gone once it's closed.
- Don't open a popover from inside a popover.

pages.title: Progress
pages.description: A bar that fills as a task gets done.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { Progress } from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number \| null` |  | How far along it is, from 0 to `max`. Pass `null`, or leave it out, while the amount isn't known: the bar then moves from side to side. |
| `max` | `number` | `100` |  |
| `size` | `"lg" \| "md" \| "sm"` | `"md"` |  |
| `getValueLabel` | `((value: number, max: number) => string)` |  | The text a screen reader says for the value. By default it's the percentage, such as "40%". |

Everything else is passed to the `<div>` Radix renders, including `ref`, `className`, `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby`.

A value below 0 or above `max` is held to that range. A value that isn't a number counts as not known.

sections.heading: With a label and a number
When the amount isn't known
Steps and sizes
Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

A progress bar has no keyboard behavior. It reports and can't be changed. For a value people set, use a [slider](page:components/slider).

### What the component handles

- It has `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuetext`. This part is Radix.
- With no value it has no `aria-valuenow`, which is how a screen reader knows the amount isn't known.
- The bar's edge has at least 3:1 against the page in every theme, and the filled part at least 3:1 against the empty part.
- Where the browser forces its own colors, the filled part takes the system's color for something selected.
- It fills from the right in a right-to-left layout.
- The filled part's movement is only animated when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion.

### What you need to handle

- **Name it,** with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Two bars on one page need different names.
- **Don't expect every change to be read out.** A screen reader reads the value when the visitor moves to the bar, and some read changes while focus is on it. For work that takes a while, say the milestones in an element with `role="status"`: "Halfway", "Upload complete".
- **Say when it's done** in words, and say what happens next. A full bar that just sits there looks stuck.
- Mark the region that's being loaded with `aria-busy="true"`, and point its `aria-describedby` at the bar, where the bar is about one part of the page.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on the bar, or on anything around it.

```css
.upload {
  --nuv-progress-indicator: var(--color-success);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-progress-width` | `100%` | Width of the bar. |
| `--nuv-progress-height` | `0.5rem`, `0.375rem`, `0.75rem` | Height of the bar. Differs by size. |
| `--nuv-progress-border` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Color of the edge. Keep it at 3:1 against the page, so the bar's full length can be seen. |
| `--nuv-progress-radius` | `var(--radius-full)` | Corner radius. Fully round by default. |
| `--nuv-progress-track` | `var(--color-muted)` | Color of the part that isn't filled. |
| `--nuv-progress-indicator` | `var(--color-primary)` | Color of the filled part. Keep it at 3:1 against the part that isn't. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-progress` | The bar. |
| `.nuv-progress--lg` | size="lg" |
| `.nuv-progress--sm` | size="sm" |
| `.nuv-progress__indicator` | The filled part. |

A medium bar also has the class `nuv-progress--md`, which has no rules of its own. Radix sets `data-state` to `loading`, `complete` or `indeterminate` on both elements, along with `data-value` and `data-max`.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

Progress is a client component. It carries `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files. You can render it from a server component, as the first example on this page does.

`getValueLabel` is a function, and a server component can't pass a function to a client component. A bar that uses it has to be rendered from a client component, as the steps example is.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Show a real measure. A bar that crawls to 90% and waits there is worse than a spinner.
- Put the number next to the bar when the work is long. A bar's last tenth is hard to judge by eye.

**Don't**

- Don't let it go backwards. If the estimate was wrong, slow down.
- Don't use it for a value that isn't progress, such as disk space used against a warning level. That's a meter, and it wants the `meter` role.

| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables every option. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the group as required. Inside a form, the browser won't submit until an option is picked. |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the value is submitted under in a form. |
| `dir` | `"ltr" \| "rtl"` |  | The reading direction. In `"rtl"` the left and right arrow keys swap. |
| `loop` | `boolean` |  | Whether the arrow keys wrap around from the last option to the first. It's `true` by default. |

### RadioGroupItem

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | What `onValueChange` and the form receive when this option is picked. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Stops this option from being picked. The arrow keys skip it. |

Both parts pass everything else to the element Radix renders. The [Radix Radio Group reference](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/radio-group#api-reference) has the full list.

sections.heading: Side by side
sections.markdown:
## Side by side ```tsx import { RadioGroup, RadioGroupItem } from "@nuvui/react"; const row = { display: "flex", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 }; export default function Example() { return (
); } ```

sections.heading: Controlling it yourself
In a form
sections.markdown:
## In a form

Give `RadioGroup` a `name` and the picked value is submitted with the form. Inside a `<form>`, Radix renders a hidden `<input type="radio">` next to each circle, so `FormData` and `required` both work.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

The circle is 20 pixels, which is too small for a finger. On a touch screen the area that responds to a tap is 44 by 44 pixels, centered on the circle, and the rows of a vertical group are spaced so that two of those areas don't overlap. With a mouse the rows are 12 pixels apart.

That spacing assumes each label is one line. If yours wrap, or you lay the group out yourself, set `--nuv-radio-group-gap`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves focus into the group, to the picked option or the first one, and out again. The group is one tab stop. |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> or <kbd>→</kbd> | Moves to the next option and picks it. Disabled options are skipped. |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> or <kbd>←</kbd> | Moves to the previous option and picks it. |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> | Picks the option that has focus, if it isn't picked. |

In a right-to-left group, <kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd> swap.

### What the component handles

Most of this is Radix. The library doesn't change it.

- The group has `role="radiogroup"` and each option `role="radio"` with `aria-checked`.
- A click on a `<label>` that points at an option picks it.
- The edge of the circle uses `--color-border-strong`, which has at least 3:1 contrast with the page in every theme, so an empty circle is still visible as a control.
- The picked option is filled as well as marked with a dot, and the dot is drawn in the text color, so it's still there where the browser forces its own colors.
- Keyboard focus shows a 2 pixel ring in `--color-ring`.

### What you need to handle

- Name the group, so people know what question the options answer. Use `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, or a [Fieldset](page:components/fieldset) with a legend around it.
- Give each option a `<label>` whose `htmlFor` matches its `id`.
- Start with an option picked when one is a sensible default. A radio group can't be put back to empty once something is picked.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on the group, or on anything around it.

```css
.plans {
  --nuv-radio-group-size: 1.5rem;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-radio-group-gap` | `calc(var(--nuv-touch-size) - var(--nuv-radio-group-size, 1.25rem))`, `calc(var(--spacing) * 3)` | Space between options. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. |
| `--nuv-radio-group-size` | `1.25rem` | Width and height of the circle. |
| `--nuv-radio-group-border` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Border color while not picked. |
| `--nuv-radio-group-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color while not picked. |
| `--nuv-radio-group-fg` | `var(--color-primary-foreground)` | Color of the dot. |
| `--nuv-radio-group-checked-bg` | `var(--color-primary)` | Background and border color while picked. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-radio-group` | RadioGroup. |
| `.nuv-radio-group__dot` | The dot. |
| `.nuv-radio-group__indicator` | The wrapper around the dot. Radix only renders it while the option is picked. |
| `.nuv-radio-group__item` | RadioGroupItem, which is the circle and a button. |

Radix sets `data-state` on an option to `checked` or `unchecked`, `data-disabled` when it's disabled, and `data-orientation` on the group when `orientation` is set.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

The radio group parts are client components. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files.

You can put a group together inside a server component, as the first example on this page does. It needs a client component of your own once you pass `onValueChange` or control `value`.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- List the options in an order people can predict.
- Make the label clickable by linking it with `htmlFor`. It's a much bigger target than the circle.

**Don't**

- Don't use radio buttons for a yes or no. That's one checkbox or a switch.
- Don't use them for something that takes effect at once and changes the page, such as a view. That's a [toggle group](page:components/toggle-group) or tabs.

pages.description: Stars to rate something with, or to show how it was rated, down to part of a star.
pages.markdown:
# Rating Stars to rate something with, or to show how it was rated, down to part of a star. Use a rating to ask how good something was, or to show the answer. To choose from, it's a radio group drawn as stars. To show, it's a picture with a name. ```tsx "use client"; import { Rating } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { const [stars, setStars] = useState(3); return (
How was the delivery? {stars} of 5
); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Rating } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` | `number` | | How many stars are chosen, when you control it. 0 is none. | | `defaultValue` | `number` | `0` | How many stars are chosen at first, when you don't control it. | | `onValueChange` | `((value: number) => void)` | | Called with the number of the star that was chosen. | | `max` | `number` | `5` | How many stars there are. | | `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows a rating that can't be changed, such as an average. It's then a picture with a name, not a set of controls, and the value can have a fraction: 3.5 fills half of the fourth star. | | `size` | `"lg" \| "md" \| "sm"` | `"md"` | | | `itemLabel` | `((value: number, max: number) => string)` | `(value) => (value === 1 ? "1 star" : '${value} stars')` | Accessible name of one star, from its number and the number of stars. Translate it with the rest of your interface. | | `valueLabel` | `((value: number, max: number) => string)` | `(value, max) => '${value} out of ${max}'` | Accessible name of a rating that can't be changed, from its value and the number of stars. Translate it with the rest of your interface. | Everything else is passed to the group, including `ref`, `className`, `name`, `required` and `disabled`. With a `name`, the number of the chosen star is submitted with a form. ## Showing a rating `readOnly` is for a rating nobody changes here: an average, or someone else's review. The value can have a fraction, and the star it falls in is filled that far. ```tsx import { Rating } from "@nuvui/react"; const products = [ { name: "Standing desk", average: 4.5, reviews: 128 }, { name: "Monitor arm", average: 3.7, reviews: 64 }, { name: "Cable tray", average: 2, reviews: 9 }, ]; export default function Example() { return (
    {products.map((product) => (
  • {product.name} {product.average} ({product.reviews})
    • ))}
); } ``` A read-only rating is one picture to a screen reader, named "4.5 out of 5". It isn't a set of disabled controls, which would be read one star at a time and say nothing of the half. Put the number beside it as text when it matters: part of a star is hard to judge by eye. ## Sizes, and more stars `size` changes the stars, and `max` how many there are. ```tsx import { Rating } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return (
); } ``` ## Taking a rating back A radio group has no way to choose nothing once something is chosen. When a rating is optional, put a button beside it that sets the value to 0, which is no stars. ## Accessibility | Key | What it does | | --- | --- | | Tab | Moves to the chosen star, or to the first when none is. | | Arrow right, Arrow down | Chooses the next star. | | Arrow left, Arrow up | Chooses the one before. | | Space | Chooses the star that has focus. | In a right-to-left page the left and right arrows swap, as the stars do. ### What the component handles - To choose from, it's a `radiogroup`, and each star is a radio button named "1 star", "2 stars" and so on. - A star is 44 pixels to a finger on a touch screen. With a mouse the stars close up. - A chosen star is filled and the others are outlines. That's a difference of shape, so it's still there where the browser forces its own colors, and for someone who can't tell the two colors apart. - The outline of an empty star has at least 3:1 against the page in every theme. - Under the pointer, the stars up to it fill, to show what a click would choose. A finger doesn't do this, since it would leave them filled after it lifts. - Read-only, it has `role="img"` and a name made from the value. ### What you need to handle - Name the group with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, such as "How was the delivery?". - Translate the two labels. Both are functions, since the words change with the number. [Translation](page:translation) lists them. - When the page shows the average as stars, show it as a number too. ## CSS variables Set any of these on the rating, or on anything around it. ```css .reviews { --nuv-rating-on: var(--color-warning); } ``` | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-rating-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 0.5)` | Space around each star. Twice this is the space between two. | | `--nuv-rating-size` | `1.5rem`, `1rem`, `2rem` | Width and height of a star. Differs by size. | | `--nuv-rating-off` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Color of an empty star's outline. Keep it at 3:1 against the background. | | `--nuv-rating-on` | `var(--color-primary)` | Color of a filled star. The primary color by default. Keep it at 3:1 against the background. | | `--nuv-rating-part` | `1` | How much of a star is filled, from 0 to 1. The component sets it on each star of a read-only rating. It's not one to set yourself. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-rating` | Every rating. | | `.nuv-rating--lg` | size="lg" | | `.nuv-rating--read-only` | A rating with readOnly. | | `.nuv-rating--sm` | size="sm" | | `.nuv-rating__fill` | The filled star over the empty one in a read-only rating, cut off at the part the value covers. | | `.nuv-rating__item` | One star and the room around it. A radio button, or a span when read-only. | | `.nuv-rating__star` | The star itself, an outline. | | `.nuv-rating__star--on` | A filled star. | ## Server components Rating starts with `"use client"`. A read-only one can still be rendered from a server component: it takes plain props. `itemLabel`, `valueLabel` and `onValueChange` are functions, and need a client component. ## Do and don't **Do** - Use five stars unless you have a reason. It's what people expect. - Say what one star and five stars mean when it isn't obvious, in the text beside it. **Don't** - Don't use stars for a count or a level, such as a password's strength. That's a [progress bar](page:components/progress). - Don't make people rate to get past a form. Leave it optional, or say why it's needed.
