pages.title: Resizable
pages.description: Panels with a handle between them to drag, side by side or one above another.
pages.markdown:
# Resizable Panels with a handle between them to drag, side by side or one above another. Use resizable panels where the reader knows better than you how much room each part needs: a list beside what's chosen from it, an editor above its output, navigation beside a page. Where one size is right, set it and leave this out. ```tsx import { Resizable, ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel } from "@nuvui/react"; const pane = { padding: 16 }; export default function Example() { return (
Folders Messages
); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Resizable, ResizablePanel, ResizableHandle } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `Resizable` | The panels together. It keeps their sizes. | | `ResizablePanel` | One panel. It scrolls what doesn't fit. | | `ResizableHandle` | The line between two panels, which is dragged. | Put a handle between each two panels. The panels and the handles have to be written straight inside `Resizable`, not inside something else that's inside it. `Resizable` fills what it's in, both ways. Give that a height, or the panels have none. It's built on [react-resizable-panels](https://github.com/bvaughn/react-resizable-panels), which does the resizing. ## Sizes A panel's `defaultSize`, `minSize` and `maxSize` are written the same way. A number is pixels. A string is a share of the whole, `"30%"`, or a length, `"20rem"`. ```tsx ``` Give every panel a `minSize`. Without one a panel can be dragged down to nothing, and what's in it is then out of reach. A panel without a `defaultSize` takes a share of what's left. Leave it off at least one panel, so the sizes always add up. ## One above another ```tsx import { Resizable, ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel } from "@nuvui/react"; const pane = { padding: 16 }; export default function Example() { return (
Query Results
); } ``` ## Inside one another A panel can hold another `Resizable` that lies the other way. ```tsx import { Resizable, ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel } from "@nuvui/react"; const pane = { padding: 16 }; export default function Example() { return (
Files Editor Terminal
); } ``` ## A panel that folds away A `collapsible` panel folds to nothing when it's dragged to well under its `minSize`, and opens again when it's dragged back. Enter on the handle after it does the same. To fold it from a button, take a ref with `useResizablePanelRef` and give it to the panel as `panelRef`. It has `collapse`, `expand`, `isCollapsed`, `resize` and `getSize`. ```tsx "use client"; import { Button, Resizable, ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel, useResizablePanelRef, } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; const pane = { padding: 16 }; export default function Example() { const panel = useResizablePanelRef(); const [folded, setFolded] = useState(false); return (
setFolded(size.asPercentage === 0)} style={pane} > Navigation Page
); } ``` A panel folded to nothing still has its content in the page. It's made `inert` while there's no room for it, so Tab and a screen reader pass it by. `collapsedSize` leaves some of the panel showing, for a rail of icons, and then what's in it stays in reach. ## Remembering the sizes `useResizableLayout` keeps the sizes in the browser's `localStorage` under a name, and gives them back on the next visit. It does without, quietly, where storage is missing or refused. Each panel needs an `id`, which is what its size is kept under. Resize these and load the page again. ```tsx "use client"; import { Resizable, ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel, useResizableLayout, } from "@nuvui/react"; const pane = { padding: 16 }; export default function Example() { // Kept in the browser's own storage, under this name. const { defaultLayout, onLayoutChanged } = useResizableLayout({ id: "docs-resizable-saved", }); return (
List Detail
); } ``` It takes a `storage` of your own, anything with `getItem` and `setItem`, for keeping them in a cookie or on your server. To save them yourself, `onLayoutChanged` is called with every panel's size once a drag has ended. `onLayoutChange`, without the d, is called all through the drag. A page drawn on a server doesn't know what the browser kept, so it draws the default sizes and the kept ones are put in place once the browser has the page. With a `storage` of yours that reads a cookie, the server knows them too, and nothing moves. ## Resizable props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Which way the panels are set out: side by side, or one above another. | | `defaultLayout` | `Layout` | | The size of each panel at first, by its `id`, as a share of 100. For putting back sizes you saved. Without it each panel's `defaultSize` is used. | | `onLayoutChange` | `((layout: Layout) => void)` | | Called with every panel's size while they change: for each pixel of a drag, many times a second. | | `onLayoutChanged` | `((layout: Layout, meta: LayoutChangedMeta) => void)` | | Called once the sizes have settled: when a drag ends, or a key is pressed. This is the one to save from. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Panels that can't be resized. The handles stay where they are and can't be moved or reached with Tab. | | `groupRef` | `Ref` | | A ref to read every panel's size from, and to set them. | It also takes what a `div` takes, including `ref` and `className`, and the rest of what react-resizable-panels' `Group` takes. ## useResizableLayout | Option | What it is | | --- | --- | | `id` | A name for these panels. Their sizes are kept under `nuv-resizable:` and the name. | | `storage` | Where to keep them: anything with `getItem` and `setItem`. `localStorage` unless you say. | It returns `defaultLayout` and `onLayoutChanged`, to give to the `Resizable`. `useResizablePanelRef` and `useResizableRef` make the refs for `panelRef` and `groupRef`. ## ResizablePanel props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `id` | `string` | | What the panel is known by in a layout. Give one to every panel whose size you save or set. | | `defaultSize` | `string \| number` | | The panel's size at first. A number is pixels, and a string is a share of the whole (`"30%"`) or a length (`"20rem"`). Without it the panels share the room equally. | | `minSize` | `string \| number` | `"0%"` | The least it can be, written the same way. | | `maxSize` | `string \| number` | `"100%"` | The most it can be. | | `collapsible` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the panel folds away when it's dragged to well under its `minSize`. Enter on the handle after it folds it and opens it again. | | `collapsedSize` | `string \| number` | `"0%"` | How much of a folded panel is left showing. | | `onResize` | `((size: PanelSize, id: string \| number \| undefined, before: PanelSize \| undefined) => void)` | | Called with the panel's size, in pixels and as a share, when it changes. | | `panelRef` | `Ref` | | A ref to fold the panel and open it from, to resize it, and to ask whether it's folded. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | A panel that keeps its size, whatever is dragged. | It also takes what a `div` takes. A panel is two boxes: `ref`, `id` and the rest go on the outer one, which is sized, and `className` and `style` on the inner one, around your content. ## ResizableHandle props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `withGrip` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the handle shows a grip: a mark in the middle of the line that says it can be dragged. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | A handle that can't be moved. The panels either side can still change size when another handle is. | | `aria-label` | `string` | `"Resize"` | What a screen reader calls the handle. Say what it resizes when the page has more than one. | | `children` | `ReactNode` | | Something of yours in place of the grip. | It also takes what a `div` takes, including `ref` and `className`. ## Accessibility It follows the [window splitter pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/windowsplitter/) of the ARIA Authoring Practices. ### Keyboard A handle is a stop for Tab. On it: | Key | What it does | | --- | --- | | Right, Left | Between panels side by side: moves the handle that way, by 5 in 100. | | Down, Up | Between panels one above another: the same. | | Home | Makes the panel before the handle as small as it can be. | | End | Makes it as large as it can be. | | Enter | Folds a `collapsible` panel before the handle, or opens it. | | F6 | Moves to the next handle. With Shift, to the one before. | In a right-to-left page the panels are the other way round. sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { Resizable, ResizablePanel, ResizableHandle } from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Resizable` | The panels together. It keeps their sizes. |
| `ResizablePanel` | One panel. It scrolls what doesn't fit. |
| `ResizableHandle` | The line between two panels, which is dragged. |

Put a handle between each two panels. The panels and the handles have to be written straight inside `Resizable`, not inside something else that's inside it.

`Resizable` fills what it's in, both ways. Give that a height, or the panels have none.

It's built on [react-resizable-panels](https://github.com/bvaughn/react-resizable-panels), which does the resizing.

sections.heading: Sizes
sections.markdown:
## Sizes

A panel's `defaultSize`, `minSize` and `maxSize` are written the same way. A number is pixels. A string is a share of the whole, `"30%"`, or a length, `"20rem"`.

```tsx
<ResizablePanel defaultSize="30%" minSize={200} maxSize="40rem" />
```

Give every panel a `minSize`. Without one a panel can be dragged down to nothing, and what's in it is then out of reach.

A panel without a `defaultSize` takes a share of what's left. Leave it off at least one panel, so the sizes always add up.

sections.heading: One above another
Inside one another
sections.markdown:
## Inside one another A panel can hold another `Resizable` that lies the other way. ```tsx import { Resizable, ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel } from "@nuvui/react"; const pane = { padding: 16 }; export default function Example() { return (
Files Editor Terminal
); } ```

sections.heading: A panel that folds away
Remembering the sizes
Resizable props
sections.markdown:
## Resizable props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Which way the panels are set out: side by side, or one above another. |
| `defaultLayout` | `Layout` |  | The size of each panel at first, by its `id`, as a share of 100. For putting back sizes you saved. Without it each panel's `defaultSize` is used. |
| `onLayoutChange` | `((layout: Layout) => void)` |  | Called with every panel's size while they change: for each pixel of a drag, many times a second. |
| `onLayoutChanged` | `((layout: Layout, meta: LayoutChangedMeta) => void)` |  | Called once the sizes have settled: when a drag ends, or a key is pressed. This is the one to save from. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Panels that can't be resized. The handles stay where they are and can't be moved or reached with Tab. |
| `groupRef` | `Ref<GroupImperativeHandle \| null>` |  | A ref to read every panel's size from, and to set them. |

It also takes what a `div` takes, including `ref` and `className`, and the rest of what react-resizable-panels' `Group` takes.

sections.heading: useResizableLayout
sections.markdown:
## useResizableLayout

| Option | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | A name for these panels. Their sizes are kept under `nuv-resizable:` and the name. |
| `storage` | Where to keep them: anything with `getItem` and `setItem`. `localStorage` unless you say. |

It returns `defaultLayout` and `onLayoutChanged`, to give to the `Resizable`. `useResizablePanelRef` and `useResizableRef` make the refs for `panelRef` and `groupRef`.

sections.heading: ResizablePanel props
sections.markdown:
## ResizablePanel props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` |  | What the panel is known by in a layout. Give one to every panel whose size you save or set. |
| `defaultSize` | `string \| number` |  | The panel's size at first. A number is pixels, and a string is a share of the whole (`"30%"`) or a length (`"20rem"`). Without it the panels share the room equally. |
| `minSize` | `string \| number` | `"0%"` | The least it can be, written the same way. |
| `maxSize` | `string \| number` | `"100%"` | The most it can be. |
| `collapsible` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the panel folds away when it's dragged to well under its `minSize`. Enter on the handle after it folds it and opens it again. |
| `collapsedSize` | `string \| number` | `"0%"` | How much of a folded panel is left showing. |
| `onResize` | `((size: PanelSize, id: string \| number \| undefined, before: PanelSize \| undefined) => void)` |  | Called with the panel's size, in pixels and as a share, when it changes. |
| `panelRef` | `Ref<PanelImperativeHandle \| null>` |  | A ref to fold the panel and open it from, to resize it, and to ask whether it's folded. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | A panel that keeps its size, whatever is dragged. |

It also takes what a `div` takes. A panel is two boxes: `ref`, `id` and the rest go on the outer one, which is sized, and `className` and `style` on the inner one, around your content.

sections.heading: ResizableHandle props
sections.markdown:
## ResizableHandle props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `withGrip` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the handle shows a grip: a mark in the middle of the line that says it can be dragged. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | A handle that can't be moved. The panels either side can still change size when another handle is. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | `"Resize"` | What a screen reader calls the handle. Say what it resizes when the page has more than one. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | Something of yours in place of the grip. |

It also takes what a `div` takes, including `ref` and `className`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

It follows the [window splitter pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/windowsplitter/) of the ARIA Authoring Practices.

### Keyboard

A handle is a stop for Tab. On it:

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Right, Left | Between panels side by side: moves the handle that way, by 5 in 100. |
| Down, Up | Between panels one above another: the same. |
| Home | Makes the panel before the handle as small as it can be. |
| End | Makes it as large as it can be. |
| Enter | Folds a `collapsible` panel before the handle, or opens it. |
| F6 | Moves to the next handle. With Shift, to the one before. |

In a right-to-left page the panels are the other way round. Right and Left still move the handle the way they point, and the handle says the size of the panel on its left, which is then the one after it.

### What the component handles

- A handle is a `separator` that can take focus, with the size of the panel before it as its value, from 0 to 100, and that panel named in `aria-controls`.
- What takes a press is wider than the line that's drawn: 44 pixels with a finger and 10 with a mouse.
- The line is a border, which is still drawn where the browser forces its own colors.
- A disabled handle is out of the Tab order and says it's disabled. So is every handle of a disabled `Resizable`.
- A panel that scrolls and has nothing in it to focus takes focus itself, so it can be scrolled from the keyboard. Then it's a `group`, with the `aria-label` you gave the panel.
- A panel folded to nothing is `inert`: what's in it can't be reached while it can't be seen.
- A double press on a handle puts the panel before it back to its `defaultSize`.

### What you need to handle

- Name each handle with `aria-label` after the panel it resizes, such as "Resize navigation". It's called "Resize" until you do, which says little where there's more than one.
- Give every panel a `minSize` that still fits what's in it.
- Don't make a drag the only way to a size that matters. The arrow keys are one other way. A button that folds a panel, or a few sizes to choose from, is one for people who use a pointer and can't drag.
- The line is as faint as any other border. Where people have to find it, give the handle `withGrip`, or make `--nuv-resizable-line` darker.
- Give a panel that may scroll an `aria-label` that says what's in it.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

Panels side by side on a phone leave neither enough room. Put them one above another there, or show one at a time. `orientation` is a prop, so change it from a media query of your own.

A drag on a handle moves the handle and not the page. Inside a panel the page still scrolls the other way.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on the `Resizable`, or on anything around it.

```css
.workspace {
  --nuv-resizable-line-width: 2px;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-resizable-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of the text in the panels. |
| `--nuv-resizable-line` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of the line between two panels. |
| `--nuv-resizable-line-width` | `1px` | Thickness of that line. |
| `--nuv-resizable-line-active` | `var(--color-primary)` | Color of the line under the pointer, and while it's dragged. |
| `--nuv-resizable-grip-bg` | `var(--color-background)` | Background of the grip. |
| `--nuv-resizable-grip-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the dots in the grip. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-resizable` | Resizable |
| `.nuv-resizable__grip` | The grip in the middle of a handle. |
| `.nuv-resizable__handle` | ResizableHandle |
| `.nuv-resizable__panel` | The box around a ResizablePanel's content. |

A handle has `data-separator`, which is `inactive`, `hover`, `active` while it's dragged, `focus` or `disabled`, and `aria-orientation`, which says which way the line itself lies. A disabled panel has `data-disabled`.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

Resizable starts with `"use client"`: it keeps the panels' sizes. You can render it from a server component with panels written there, as long as you leave out `onLayoutChange`, `onLayoutChanged` and `onResize`, since a function can't be passed from the server.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Start with sizes that suit most people. Most never touch a handle.
- Save the sizes someone chose. Having to set them again on every visit is worse than not being able to.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for a table's columns. [DataTable](page:table/index) resizes its own.
- Don't put more than three or four panels in a row. Each handle moved changes the room the others have.

## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { ScrollArea } from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `"both" \| "horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"vertical"` | Which way the content scrolls. |
| `type` | `"always" \| "auto" \| "hover" \| "scroll"` | `"auto"` | When the scrollbar shows. `"auto"` shows it whenever there's more content than fits, `"always"` even when there isn't, `"scroll"` only while scrolling, and `"hover"` while scrolling or under the pointer. |
| `viewportRef` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  | A ref to the element that scrolls, for reading or setting its scroll position. The component's own `ref` is the box around it. |
| `nonce` | `string` |  | Hiding the browser's own scrollbar takes a `style` element. A page with a content security policy that asks for a nonce passes it here. |

These come from Radix.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scrollHideDelay` | `number` |  | With `type` set to `"scroll"` or `"hover"`, how long the scrollbar stays after scrolling stops or the pointer leaves, in milliseconds. |
| `dir` | `"ltr" \| "rtl"` |  | The reading direction, which decides the side the scrollbar is on. It's taken from `DirectionProvider` when not set. |

Everything else is passed to the outer `<div>`, including `ref`, `className` and `style`. `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby` are the exception: [they go to the element that scrolls](#from-the-keyboard).

sections.heading: Give it a height
Sideways
When the scrollbar shows
sections.markdown:
## When the scrollbar shows

The default, `type="auto"`, shows the scrollbar whenever there's more content than fits. A bar that only appears on hover hides the one sign that there's more to see, and there's no hover on a touch screen.

Use `"hover"` or `"scroll"` where the content makes it plain that it goes on, such as a row of cards with one cut off at the edge.

sections.heading: From the keyboard
sections.markdown:
## From the keyboard

Someone who doesn't use a mouse scrolls a box by moving focus into it and pressing the arrow keys. When the content holds a link or a button, focus gets there by itself. When it's only text, nothing inside can take focus, so the box has to.

The scroll area handles that. While its content scrolls and holds nothing that takes focus, the element that scrolls becomes a stop for the <kbd>Tab</kbd> key, with `role="group"` and the `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` you gave the scroll area. Otherwise it's not a tab stop, and the name isn't used.

So always pass a name. It's what a screen reader says when focus lands on the box. The one case where it can be left out is inside a dialog: with no name of its own, the box takes the dialog's.

Chrome and Firefox make a scrolling box a tab stop on their own. Safari doesn't, which is why this is done here.

sections.heading: A content security policy
sections.markdown:
## A content security policy

Hiding the browser's own scrollbar takes a `<style>` element, which Radix adds next to the scroll area. A policy that doesn't allow inline styles blocks it, and both scrollbars then show. Pass the page's nonce as `nonce` and it's set on that element.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves focus to the first control inside, or to the box itself when there's none and it scrolls. |
| Arrow keys, <kbd>Page Up</kbd>, <kbd>Page Down</kbd>, <kbd>Home</kbd>, <kbd>End</kbd>, <kbd>Space</kbd> | Scroll the box, once focus is in it. This is the browser's own behavior. |

The scrollbar itself can't take focus. It's a pointer's way to scroll, and the keys above are the keyboard's.

### What the component handles

- Scrolling is native, so screen readers, touch, and "find in page" work as usual.
- The tab stop, role and name described above.
- The focus ring is drawn inside the box, where it isn't cut off.
- The thumb has at least 3:1 against the page in every theme, and it's drawn where the browser forces its own colors.
- The scrollbar is on the left in a right-to-left layout.

### What you need to handle

- Pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Don't put a scroll area inside another that scrolls the same way. Whichever is under the pointer scrolls, and people get stuck in the inner one.
- Keep it tall enough to read in. A box that shows two lines of a long text is harder to use than a link to the text.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on the scroll area, or on anything around it.

```css
.side-panel {
  --nuv-scroll-area-max-height: 24rem;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-scroll-area-height` | `auto` | Height of the area. |
| `--nuv-scroll-area-max-height` | `none` | The tallest the area gets before it scrolls. |
| `--nuv-scroll-area-radius` | `0` | Corner radius. The content and the focus ring follow it. |
| `--nuv-scroll-area-scrollbar-padding` | `2px` | Space around the thumb. |
| `--nuv-scroll-area-scrollbar-size` | `0.625rem` | Thickness of the scrollbar, padding included. |
| `--nuv-scroll-area-thumb` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Color of the thumb. Keep it at 3:1 against what's behind it. |
| `--nuv-scroll-area-thumb-hover` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the thumb under the pointer. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-scroll-area` | The outer element, which you size. |
| `.nuv-scroll-area__corner` | The square where two scrollbars meet. |
| `.nuv-scroll-area__scrollbar` | A scrollbar. `data-orientation` says which. |
| `.nuv-scroll-area__thumb` | The part of a scrollbar that's dragged. |
| `.nuv-scroll-area__viewport` | The element that scrolls. |

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

ScrollArea is a client component. It carries `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files. You can render it from a server component, as the first example on this page does.

Before the scripts have run, the content is there and scrolls, with no scrollbar drawn.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Use it where the look of the scrollbar matters: a panel in a designed interface, a dark sidebar.
- Use plain `overflow: auto` where it doesn't. The browser's scrollbar is free and familiar.

**Don't**

- Don't hide the scrollbar to make a design look cleaner.
- Don't use a scroll area to fit a long form into a small box. Let the page scroll.

pages.title: Select
pages.description: A control for picking one option from a list. It works with a label, the keyboard and forms.
pages.markdown:

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import {
  Select,
  SelectContent,
  SelectItem,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
} from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Select` | Holds the value and the open state. Renders nothing itself. |
| `SelectTrigger` | The control on the page. It shows the value and an arrow. |
| `SelectValue` | The text inside the trigger: the chosen option, or the placeholder. |
| `SelectContent` | The list that opens. |
| `SelectItem` | One option. |
| `SelectGroup` | Wraps options that belong together. |
| `SelectLabel` | The heading of a group. |
| `SelectSeparator` | A line between groups. |

These are separate exports, not properties of `Select`. `Select.Item` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

### Select

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` |  | The chosen option, when you control it yourself. Use it with `onValueChange`. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | The option chosen at first, when you don't control it. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void)` |  | Called with an option's `value` when it's chosen. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Stops the select from being opened or focused. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks it as required. Inside a form, the browser won't submit until an option is chosen. |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the value is submitted under in a form. |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Whether the list is open, when you control that yourself. |
| `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean) => void)` |  | Called when the list opens or closes. |
| `dir` | `"ltr" \| "rtl"` |  | The reading direction of the list. |

### SelectTrigger

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"field" \| "inline"` | `"field"` | `"inline"` is a select that sits in a sentence: no box, the size of the text around it, as wide as the option it shows. |

### SelectValue

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placeholder` | `ReactNode` |  | What the trigger shows while nothing is chosen. |

### SelectContent

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | `"item-aligned" \| "popper"` | `"popper"` | `"popper"` opens the list under the trigger, like a menu. `"item-aligned"` lays it over the trigger with the selected option on top of it, the way a native select does on a Mac. |
| `sideOffset` | `number` | `6` | The gap between the trigger and the list, in pixels. Only applies with `position="popper"`. |
| `collisionPadding` | `number \| Partial<Record<"bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top", number>>` | `8` | How close the list may get to the edge of the screen, in pixels. Only applies with `position="popper"`. |
| `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the list is rendered into. Set this when the list should pick up a `data-theme` from a section of the page. |

### SelectItem

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | What `onValueChange` and the form receive when this option is chosen. It can't be an empty string. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Stops the option from being chosen. The arrow keys skip it. |
| `textValue` | `string` |  | The text that typing a letter matches against. Only needed when the option's content isn't plain text. |

The other parts take the same props as the Radix parts they wrap. The [Radix Select reference](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/select#api-reference) lists them.

sections.heading: Controlling it yourself
In a form
sections.markdown:
## In a form

Give `Select` a `name` and the value is submitted with the form. Inside a `<form>`, Radix renders a hidden native `<select>` next to the trigger, so `FormData` and `required` both work.

sections.heading: Width
sections.markdown:
## Width

The trigger is at least 12rem wide and grows with the text in it, up to the width of its container. Set `--nuv-select-width: 100%` to make it fill the container.

A value that's still too long is cut short with an ellipsis. The full text is in the list.

sections.heading: In a sentence
Where the list opens
sections.markdown:
## Where the list opens

By default the list opens under the trigger, like a menu, and is at least as wide as it. With `position="item-aligned"` it lays itself over the trigger with the chosen option on top of it, the way a native select does on a Mac.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

The trigger is 44 pixels tall on a touch screen and 40 with a mouse. Options are 44 and 32.

The list is never taller than the room around the trigger. A long one scrolls inside itself. Radix hides its scrollbar, so an arrow appears at the top or bottom edge whenever there's more in that direction.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>, <kbd>Space</kbd> or <kbd>↓</kbd> | On the trigger, opens the list with focus on the chosen option, or the first one. |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> and <kbd>↑</kbd> | Move to the next or previous option. Disabled options are skipped. |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> | Move to the first or last option. |
| A letter | In the open list, moves to the next option that starts with it. On the closed trigger, chooses that option without opening the list. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> | Chooses the focused option and closes the list. |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Closes the list and keeps the value it had. |

### What the component handles

Most of this is Radix. The library doesn't change it.

- The trigger has `role="combobox"` with `aria-expanded`. The list has `role="listbox"`, the options have `role="option"`, and each group is named by its `SelectLabel`.
- A click on a `<label>` that points at the trigger opens the list.
- Focus moves into the list when it opens and back to the trigger when it closes.
- The trigger's edge uses `--color-border-strong`, which has at least 3:1 contrast with the page in light and dark.
- The option that has focus is filled with the primary color. That fill is the focus indicator: it has at least 3:1 contrast with the list, and the text on it keeps 4.5:1. Radix moves focus to the option under the pointer too, so hovering and arrowing look the same.
- Where the browser forces its own colors, as Windows high contrast does, the fill isn't drawn. The focused option has an outline there instead.
- The check mark on the chosen option isn't copied into the trigger with its text.
- The list only animates when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion.

### What you need to handle

- Give it a name. Use a `<label>` whose `htmlFor` matches the `id` on `SelectTrigger`, or put `aria-label` on the trigger when there's no visible label.
- Don't use the placeholder as the label. It goes away once something is chosen.
- When the value is wrong, set `aria-invalid` and describe the problem in text.

### A note on automated checks

While the list is open, Radix hides the rest of the page from screen readers. If you run axe on a page in that state, it reports the trigger under its `aria-hidden-focus` rule, because the trigger is a focusable element inside the hidden part.

Focus can't actually get there until the list closes. The library's own tests leave that rule out for open lists for this reason.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

The trigger sits in the page, so its variables can be set on it or on anything around it. The list renders at the end of `<body>`, so set the `--nuv-select-content-*` and row variables on `:root` or `body`, or straight on `SelectContent`.

```css
.filters {
  --nuv-select-width: 100%;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-select-width` | `12rem` | The narrowest the trigger gets. Set it to 100% to fill the container. |
| `--nuv-select-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-md)` | Minimum height of the trigger. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. |
| `--nuv-select-border` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Border color of the trigger. |
| `--nuv-select-radius` | `var(--radius-md)`, `var(--radius-sm)` | Corner radius of the trigger. |
| `--nuv-select-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of the trigger. |
| `--nuv-select-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)`, `inherit` | Text color of the trigger once something is chosen. |
| `--nuv-select-inline-font-weight` | `var(--font-weight-medium)` | Weight of an inline trigger's text. Medium by default, so it stands out from the sentence. |
| `--nuv-select-inline-line` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Color of the line under an inline trigger. Keep it at 3:1 against the background. |
| `--nuv-select-content-max-height` | `100vh` | The most height the list takes before it scrolls. It never goes past the room on the screen. |
| `--nuv-select-content-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Border color of the list, and the color of the separators. |
| `--nuv-select-content-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of the list. |
| `--nuv-select-content-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of the list. |
| `--nuv-select-content-shadow` | `var(--shadow-lg)` | Shadow under the list. |
| `--nuv-select-content-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color of the list. |
| `--nuv-select-item-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-sm)` | Minimum height of an option. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. |
| `--nuv-select-highlight-bg` | `var(--color-primary)` | Background of the option that has focus, from the pointer or the arrow keys. Keep it at 3:1 against the list. |
| `--nuv-select-highlight-fg` | `var(--color-primary-foreground)` | Text color of that option. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-select` | SelectTrigger. |
| `.nuv-select--inline` | SelectTrigger with variant="inline". |
| `.nuv-select__content` | SelectContent. |
| `.nuv-select__icon` | The arrow in the trigger. |
| `.nuv-select__indicator` | The check at the end of the chosen option. |
| `.nuv-select__item` | SelectItem. |
| `.nuv-select__label` | SelectLabel. |
| `.nuv-select__scroll-button` | The arrows at the top and bottom edge of a list that's too long to show whole. |
| `.nuv-select__separator` | SelectSeparator. |
| `.nuv-select__value` | The wrapper around SelectValue. It's what cuts a long value short. |
| `.nuv-select__viewport` | The scrolling area inside the list. |

Radix sets `data-placeholder` on the trigger while nothing is chosen, `data-state` on the trigger, the list and the options, `data-highlighted` on the option that has focus, and `data-disabled` on anything disabled.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

The select parts are client components. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files.

You can put a select together inside a server component, as most examples on this page do. It only needs a client component of your own when you control `value` or pass `onValueChange`.

sections.heading: Themed sections
sections.markdown:
## Themed sections

A list opened from inside a `data-theme="dark"` section doesn't inherit that theme, because it isn't rendered inside the section. Pass the section's element as `container` to `SelectContent` and it will be.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Put a visible label above or beside it.
- Order the options in a way people can predict: alphabetical, or most used first.
- Start with a sensible option chosen when there is one.

**Don't**

- Don't use a select for two or three options. Show them.
- Don't use one for actions. That's a [dropdown menu](page:components/dropdown-menu).
- Don't make people scroll a list of hundreds. Let them type to search instead, with a [combobox](page:components/combobox).

# Sheet A panel that slides in from an edge of the screen and takes over the page until it's closed. Use a sheet for something that goes with the page behind it and needs more room than a popover: a set of filters, the details of a row, the site's menu on a phone. It's a [dialog](page:components/dialog) attached to an edge, and behaves like one. ```tsx import { Button, Field, FieldControl, FieldLabel, Input, NativeSelect, Sheet, SheetBody, SheetClose, SheetContent, SheetDescription, SheetFooter, SheetHeader, SheetTitle, SheetTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return ( Filters Narrow down the list of orders.
Customer Status
); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Sheet, SheetBody, SheetClose, SheetContent, SheetDescription, SheetFooter, SheetHandle, SheetHeader, SheetTitle, SheetTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `Sheet` | Holds the open state. Renders nothing itself. | | `SheetTrigger` | The button that opens the sheet. Wrap your own with `asChild`. | | `SheetContent` | The panel. It also renders the overlay behind it and the close button in its corner. | | `SheetTitle` | The heading. Required, because it's the sheet's accessible name. | | `SheetDescription` | A sentence or two under the title. It becomes the sheet's accessible description. | | `SheetHeader` | Holds the title and description, and stays in place while the body scrolls. | | `SheetBody` | The part that scrolls when the content is taller than the screen. | | `SheetFooter` | A row for the action buttons, at the far edge of the panel. | | `SheetClose` | Closes the sheet when pressed. Wrap your own button with `asChild`. | | `SheetHandle` | The bar at the edge of a sheet that can be dragged. Optional. | These are separate exports, not properties of `Sheet`. `Sheet.Content` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component. ## Props `SheetContent` adds these to what Radix provides: | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `side` | `"bottom" \| "end" \| "start" \| "top"` | `"end"` | The edge of the screen the sheet is attached to. `"start"` is the left edge in a left-to-right layout and the right edge in a right-to-left one, and `"end"` is the other. | | `size` | `"lg" \| "md" \| "sm"` | `"md"` | How wide a sheet on the start or end edge is. It's never wider than the screen. A sheet on the top or bottom edge is as wide as the screen and as tall as its content, whatever the size. | | `showCloseButton` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether to render the close button in the corner. If you turn it off, give people another visible way to close the sheet. | | `closeLabel` | `string` | `"Close"` | Accessible name of the close button. Translate it with the rest of your interface. | | `swipe` | `boolean` | `false` | Lets a finger drag the sheet towards its edge, and closes it when it's let go of past halfway or flicked. A drag starts anywhere but on a control or in the part that scrolls, and a `SheetHandle` can be dragged with a mouse as well. On by default when there are `stops`. | | `stops` | `number[]` | | Sizes the sheet stops at, each a share of the screen from 0 to 1: `[0.4, 0.9]` is 40% and 90% of its height for a sheet on the top or bottom edge, and of its width for one on the start or end edge. A drag that's let go of settles on the nearest one, and one that ends well under the smallest closes the sheet. | | `stop` | `number` | | The stop the sheet is at, when you control it. One of `stops`. | | `defaultStop` | `number` | | The stop the sheet opens at, when you don't control it. The smallest unless you say otherwise. | | `onStopChange` | `((stop: number) => void)` | | Called with the stop the sheet has settled on. | | `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the sheet is rendered into. Set this when the sheet should pick up a `data-theme` from a section of the page. | `Sheet`, `SheetTrigger`, `SheetClose`, `SheetTitle` and `SheetDescription` are Radix's dialog parts, and take the same props, including `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal` and `asChild`. The [Radix Dialog reference](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/dialog#api-reference) lists them. `SheetHandle` adds this to what a `button` takes: | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `label` | `string` | `"Change size", or "Dismiss" in a sheet with no stops` | Accessible name of the handle, which says what pressing it does. Translate it with the rest of your interface. | `SheetHeader`, `SheetBody` and `SheetFooter` are plain `div` elements. They take `ref`, `className` and anything else a `div` does. ## Sides ```tsx import { Button, Sheet, SheetContent, SheetDescription, SheetTitle, SheetTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; const sides = ["start", "end", "top", "bottom"] as const; export default function Example() { return ( <> {sides.map((side) => ( On the {side} edge Press Escape, the close button or the page behind to close it. ))} ); } ``` `side` names the edge. `"start"` and `"end"` follow the reading direction: `"end"` is the right edge in a left-to-right layout and the left edge in a right-to-left one. The sheet slides in from the edge it's on. A sheet on the top or bottom edge is as wide as the screen and as tall as what it holds. It stops 48 pixels short of the full height, and its body scrolls from there. ## Sizes `size` sets how wide a sheet on the start or end edge is: 20rem for `sm`, 24rem for `md` and 40rem for `lg`. It doesn't apply to the top and bottom edges. On a narrow screen the sheet stops 48 pixels short of the far side whatever its size. That strip of page is what people tap to close it, so it has to stay. ## Long content Put what scrolls in `SheetBody`. The header and the footer stay where they are, so the title and the buttons are always in view. ```tsx import { Button, Sheet, SheetBody, SheetClose, SheetContent, SheetDescription, SheetFooter, SheetHeader, SheetTitle, SheetTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; const changes = [ "Ada changed the status to Paid.", "Sam added a note for the warehouse.", "The invoice was sent to the customer.", "Ada changed the delivery address.", "The payment was authorized.", "Sam split the order into two parcels.", "The first parcel left the warehouse.", "The customer asked for a later delivery.", "Ada moved the delivery to Friday.", "The second parcel left the warehouse.", "The first parcel was delivered.", "The second parcel was delivered.", ]; export default function Example() { return ( Order 10248 Everything that happened to it.
    {changes.map((change) => (
  1. {change}
    2. ))}
); } ``` The footer sits at the far edge of the panel whether or not there's a body, and however little the sheet holds. ## Swiping it away `swipe` lets a finger drag the sheet towards the edge it came from. Let go of past halfway, or flicked, it closes. Let go of sooner, it comes back. ```tsx import { Button, Sheet, SheetBody, SheetContent, SheetDescription, SheetHandle, SheetHeader, SheetTitle, SheetTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return ( Share this report Drag it down by the bar or the heading, or flick it, to put it away.

Anyone with the link can read the report. Nobody can change it.

); } ``` A drag can start anywhere on the sheet but two places: on a control, where a finger is pressing, and, for a sheet on the top or bottom edge, in the part that scrolls, where a finger is scrolling. So give such a sheet a `SheetHeader` or a `SheetHandle` to drag by, and put what scrolls in a `SheetBody`. A sheet on the start or end edge is dragged sideways, which no scrolling gets in the way of. A mouse doesn't drag the sheet, because a mouse drags across text to select it. It can drag the `SheetHandle`. ## Stops `stops` is a list of sizes the sheet rests at, each a share of the screen: `[0.35, 0.9]` is a sheet that opens a third of the way up and can be pulled nearly to the top. Dragging changes its size under the finger, and letting go settles it on the nearest stop. Dragged well under the smallest, it closes. ```tsx "use client"; import { Button, Sheet, SheetBody, SheetContent, SheetHandle, SheetHeader, SheetTitle, SheetTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; const stops = [0.35, 0.9]; const orders = Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, index) => ({ id: `ORD-${7231 - index}`, total: 40 + ((index * 37) % 260), })); export default function Example() { const [stop, setStop] = useState(stops[0]); return ( Recent orders
    {orders.map((order) => (
  • {order.id} ${order.total}.00
    • ))}
); } ``` The sheet is the height of its stop, not as tall as its content, so what's in it has to scroll: put it in a `SheetBody`. `stop` and `onStopChange` control which one it's at, and `defaultStop` sets where it opens. With stops, `swipe` is on unless you turn it off. ## The handle `SheetHandle` is the short bar that says a sheet can be dragged. Put it first in a sheet on the bottom edge, and last in one on the top. On the start or end edge it stands up along the side that faces the page, wherever you write it. It's a button. Pressing it goes to the next stop, and round to the first, or closes a sheet that has none. That's how the keyboard, a switch and a screen reader do what a drag does, so a sheet with stops should have one. ## As a menu on a phone A sheet on the start edge is the usual place for a site's navigation when the screen is too narrow for a row of links. ```tsx import { Button, Sheet, SheetBody, SheetClose, SheetContent, SheetHeader, SheetTitle, SheetTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; const pages = [ { name: "Getting started", href: "/docs" }, { name: "Theming", href: "/docs/theming" }, { name: "Forms", href: "/docs/forms" }, ]; export default function Example() { return ( Menu
    {pages.map((page) => (
  • {/* Closing on the way out matters when the link leads to a section of the page that's already open. */}
    • ))}
); } ``` Wrap each link in `SheetClose`. A link to another page closes the sheet by leaving, but a link to a section of the same page would leave it open over what the person asked to see. ## Accessibility ### Keyboard | Key | What it does | | --- | --- | | Enter or Space | On the trigger, opens the sheet. | | Tab | Moves to the next control inside the sheet. From the last one it goes back to the first. | | Shift + Tab | Moves to the previous control, and from the first to the last. | | Esc | Closes the sheet. | | ↑ ↓ Page Up Page Down | Scroll the body, when it has focus. | ### What the component handles Most of this is Radix. The library doesn't change it. - The panel has `role="dialog"`, named by `SheetTitle` and described by `SheetDescription`. - Opening moves focus to the first control in the content. Closing returns it to the trigger. - Focus can't leave the sheet while it's open, and the rest of the page is hidden from screen readers. - The trigger gets `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`. - The close button is a real button with an accessible name, and is at least 44 pixels on touch screens. This matters on phones, where there's no Esc key. - A `SheetBody` that scrolls and has nothing inside that takes focus becomes a tab stop itself, named after the sheet. Without that, someone who doesn't use a mouse would have no way to scroll it. A body that fits, or that holds a field or a button, is left alone. - The first and last rows keep clear of a phone's notch and home indicator, on pages that draw under them. - The slide only runs when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion. A sheet that's being dragged follows the finger either way, since the finger is what's moving it. - Nothing a swipe does is out of reach without one: the close button, Escape and a press outside all close the sheet, and `SheetHandle` changes its stop when pressed. - `SheetHandle` is a button with a name, drawn as a border so it's still there where the browser forces its own colors, and it answers to a press 44 pixels tall. ### What you need to handle - Always include a `SheetTitle`. If the design has no visible heading, hide it visually but keep it. - If you leave out `SheetDescription`, pass `aria-describedby={undefined}` to `SheetContent`, or Radix logs a warning. - Translate `closeLabel`, and `label` on `SheetHandle`, along with the rest of your interface. - Give a sheet with `stops` a `SheetHandle`. Without one, only a drag changes its size. - In a right-to-left layout, set `dir="rtl"` on the page's root element. The sheet is rendered at the end of ``, so that's where it takes its direction from. ## CSS variables Sheets render at the end of ``, so set these on `:root` or `body`, not on the element around the trigger. ```css :root { --nuv-sheet-width: 28rem; } ``` | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-sheet-overlay-bg` | `var(--color-overlay)` | Color of the layer that dims the page. | | `--nuv-sheet-width` | `24rem`, `20rem`, `40rem` | Width of a sheet on the start or end edge. Differs by size. It's never wider than the screen less 48 pixels. | | `--nuv-sheet-padding` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 6)` | Padding inside the panel. One length, used on every side. | | `--nuv-sheet-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Border color of the panel. | | `--nuv-sheet-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of the panel. | | `--nuv-sheet-shadow` | `var(--shadow-xl)` | Shadow under the panel. | | `--nuv-sheet-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color. | | `--nuv-sheet-stop` | `1` | The share of the screen a sheet with stops takes. The component sets it on the panel from the stop it's at. It's not one to set yourself. | | `--nuv-sheet-handle-size` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 10)` | Length of the handle. | | `--nuv-sheet-handle-width` | `4px` | Thickness of the handle. | | `--nuv-sheet-handle` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Color of the handle. Keep it at 3:1 against the panel. | ## Classes The overlay and the panel sit next to each other in the page, not one inside the other. That's why the overlay is its own flat class. | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-sheet` | The panel. | | `.nuv-sheet--bottom` | The panel with side="bottom". | | `.nuv-sheet--end` | The panel with side="end". | | `.nuv-sheet--lg` | The panel with size="lg". | | `.nuv-sheet--sm` | The panel with size="sm". | | `.nuv-sheet--start` | The panel with side="start". | | `.nuv-sheet--stops` | The panel when it has stops. | | `.nuv-sheet--swipe` | The panel when it can be dragged. | | `.nuv-sheet--top` | The panel with side="top". | | `.nuv-sheet__body` | SheetBody. | | `.nuv-sheet__close` | The close button in the corner. | | `.nuv-sheet__description` | SheetDescription. | | `.nuv-sheet__footer` | SheetFooter. | | `.nuv-sheet__handle` | SheetHandle. | | `.nuv-sheet__header` | SheetHeader. | | `.nuv-sheet__overlay` | The layer behind the panel. | | `.nuv-sheet__title` | SheetTitle. | The panel also gets `nuv-sheet--md` at the default size. No styles are attached to it, since medium is the base. Radix sets `data-state="open"` or `data-state="closed"` on the overlay and the panel. The animations hang off those. The panel has a `data-dragging` attribute while it's being dragged. ## Server components The sheet parts are client components. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files. You can put a sheet together inside a server component, as every example on this page does. It only needs a client component of your own when you control `open`. ## Themed sections A sheet opened from inside a `data-theme="dark"` section doesn't inherit that theme, because it isn't rendered inside the section. Pass the section's element as `container` and it will be. ## Do and don't **Do** - Use the end edge for details and filters, and the start edge for navigation. - Put the buttons in `SheetFooter`, so they're in the same place every time. - Leave the close button in, unless there's another visible way out. **Don't** - Don't use a sheet for a question that needs an answer. That's an [alert dialog](page:components/alert-dialog). - Don't open a sheet from inside a sheet. - Don't open one without the person doing something to ask for it.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import {
  Sheet,
  SheetBody,
  SheetClose,
  SheetContent,
  SheetDescription,
  SheetFooter,
  SheetHandle,
  SheetHeader,
  SheetTitle,
  SheetTrigger,
} from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Sheet` | Holds the open state. Renders nothing itself. |
| `SheetTrigger` | The button that opens the sheet. Wrap your own with `asChild`. |
| `SheetContent` | The panel. It also renders the overlay behind it and the close button in its corner. |
| `SheetTitle` | The heading. Required, because it's the sheet's accessible name. |
| `SheetDescription` | A sentence or two under the title. It becomes the sheet's accessible description. |
| `SheetHeader` | Holds the title and description, and stays in place while the body scrolls. |
| `SheetBody` | The part that scrolls when the content is taller than the screen. |
| `SheetFooter` | A row for the action buttons, at the far edge of the panel. |
| `SheetClose` | Closes the sheet when pressed. Wrap your own button with `asChild`. |
| `SheetHandle` | The bar at the edge of a sheet that can be dragged. Optional. |

These are separate exports, not properties of `Sheet`. `Sheet.Content` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

`SheetContent` adds these to what Radix provides:

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `side` | `"bottom" \| "end" \| "start" \| "top"` | `"end"` | The edge of the screen the sheet is attached to. `"start"` is the left edge in a left-to-right layout and the right edge in a right-to-left one, and `"end"` is the other. |
| `size` | `"lg" \| "md" \| "sm"` | `"md"` | How wide a sheet on the start or end edge is. It's never wider than the screen. A sheet on the top or bottom edge is as wide as the screen and as tall as its content, whatever the size. |
| `showCloseButton` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether to render the close button in the corner. If you turn it off, give people another visible way to close the sheet. |
| `closeLabel` | `string` | `"Close"` | Accessible name of the close button. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |
| `swipe` | `boolean` | `false` | Lets a finger drag the sheet towards its edge, and closes it when it's let go of past halfway or flicked. A drag starts anywhere but on a control or in the part that scrolls, and a `SheetHandle` can be dragged with a mouse as well. On by default when there are `stops`. |
| `stops` | `number[]` |  | Sizes the sheet stops at, each a share of the screen from 0 to 1: `[0.4, 0.9]` is 40% and 90% of its height for a sheet on the top or bottom edge, and of its width for one on the start or end edge. A drag that's let go of settles on the nearest one, and one that ends well under the smallest closes the sheet. |
| `stop` | `number` |  | The stop the sheet is at, when you control it. One of `stops`. |
| `defaultStop` | `number` |  | The stop the sheet opens at, when you don't control it. The smallest unless you say otherwise. |
| `onStopChange` | `((stop: number) => void)` |  | Called with the stop the sheet has settled on. |
| `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the sheet is rendered into. Set this when the sheet should pick up a `data-theme` from a section of the page. |

`Sheet`, `SheetTrigger`, `SheetClose`, `SheetTitle` and `SheetDescription` are Radix's dialog parts, and take the same props, including `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal` and `asChild`. The [Radix Dialog reference](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/dialog#api-reference) lists them.

`SheetHandle` adds this to what a `button` takes:

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `"Change size", or "Dismiss" in a sheet with no stops` | Accessible name of the handle, which says what pressing it does. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |

`SheetHeader`, `SheetBody` and `SheetFooter` are plain `div` elements. They take `ref`, `className` and anything else a `div` does.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> | On the trigger, opens the sheet. |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves to the next control inside the sheet. From the last one it goes back to the first. |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves to the previous control, and from the first to the last. |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Closes the sheet. |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> <kbd>Page Up</kbd> <kbd>Page Down</kbd> | Scroll the body, when it has focus. |

### What the component handles

Most of this is Radix. The library doesn't change it.

- The panel has `role="dialog"`, named by `SheetTitle` and described by `SheetDescription`.
- Opening moves focus to the first control in the content. Closing returns it to the trigger.
- Focus can't leave the sheet while it's open, and the rest of the page is hidden from screen readers.
- The trigger gets `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`.
- The close button is a real button with an accessible name, and is at least 44 pixels on touch screens. This matters on phones, where there's no <kbd>Esc</kbd> key.
- A `SheetBody` that scrolls and has nothing inside that takes focus becomes a tab stop itself, named after the sheet. Without that, someone who doesn't use a mouse would have no way to scroll it. A body that fits, or that holds a field or a button, is left alone.
- The first and last rows keep clear of a phone's notch and home indicator, on pages that draw under them.
- The slide only runs when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion. A sheet that's being dragged follows the finger either way, since the finger is what's moving it.
- Nothing a swipe does is out of reach without one: the close button, Escape and a press outside all close the sheet, and `SheetHandle` changes its stop when pressed.
- `SheetHandle` is a button with a name, drawn as a border so it's still there where the browser forces its own colors, and it answers to a press 44 pixels tall.

### What you need to handle

- Always include a `SheetTitle`. If the design has no visible heading, hide it visually but keep it.
- If you leave out `SheetDescription`, pass `aria-describedby={undefined}` to `SheetContent`, or Radix logs a warning.
- Translate `closeLabel`, and `label` on `SheetHandle`, along with the rest of your interface.
- Give a sheet with `stops` a `SheetHandle`. Without one, only a drag changes its size.
- In a right-to-left layout, set `dir="rtl"` on the page's root element. The sheet is rendered at the end of `<body>`, so that's where it takes its direction from.
