sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Sheets render at the end of `<body>`, so set these on `:root` or `body`, not on the element around the trigger.

```css
:root {
  --nuv-sheet-width: 28rem;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-sheet-overlay-bg` | `var(--color-overlay)` | Color of the layer that dims the page. |
| `--nuv-sheet-width` | `24rem`, `20rem`, `40rem` | Width of a sheet on the start or end edge. Differs by size. It's never wider than the screen less 48 pixels. |
| `--nuv-sheet-padding` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 6)` | Padding inside the panel. One length, used on every side. |
| `--nuv-sheet-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Border color of the panel. |
| `--nuv-sheet-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of the panel. |
| `--nuv-sheet-shadow` | `var(--shadow-xl)` | Shadow under the panel. |
| `--nuv-sheet-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color. |
| `--nuv-sheet-stop` | `1` | The share of the screen a sheet with stops takes. The component sets it on the panel from the stop it's at. It's not one to set yourself. |
| `--nuv-sheet-handle-size` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 10)` | Length of the handle. |
| `--nuv-sheet-handle-width` | `4px` | Thickness of the handle. |
| `--nuv-sheet-handle` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Color of the handle. Keep it at 3:1 against the panel. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

The overlay and the panel sit next to each other in the page, not one inside the other. That's why the overlay is its own flat class.

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-sheet` | The panel. |
| `.nuv-sheet--bottom` | The panel with side="bottom". |
| `.nuv-sheet--end` | The panel with side="end". |
| `.nuv-sheet--lg` | The panel with size="lg". |
| `.nuv-sheet--sm` | The panel with size="sm". |
| `.nuv-sheet--start` | The panel with side="start". |
| `.nuv-sheet--stops` | The panel when it has stops. |
| `.nuv-sheet--swipe` | The panel when it can be dragged. |
| `.nuv-sheet--top` | The panel with side="top". |
| `.nuv-sheet__body` | SheetBody. |
| `.nuv-sheet__close` | The close button in the corner. |
| `.nuv-sheet__description` | SheetDescription. |
| `.nuv-sheet__footer` | SheetFooter. |
| `.nuv-sheet__handle` | SheetHandle. |
| `.nuv-sheet__header` | SheetHeader. |
| `.nuv-sheet__overlay` | The layer behind the panel. |
| `.nuv-sheet__title` | SheetTitle. |

The panel also gets `nuv-sheet--md` at the default size. No styles are attached to it, since medium is the base.

Radix sets `data-state="open"` or `data-state="closed"` on the overlay and the panel. The animations hang off those. The panel has a `data-dragging` attribute while it's being dragged.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

The sheet parts are client components. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files.

You can put a sheet together inside a server component, as every example on this page does. It only needs a client component of your own when you control `open`.

sections.heading: Themed sections
sections.markdown:
## Themed sections

A sheet opened from inside a `data-theme="dark"` section doesn't inherit that theme, because it isn't rendered inside the section. Pass the section's element as `container` and it will be.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Use the end edge for details and filters, and the start edge for navigation.
- Put the buttons in `SheetFooter`, so they're in the same place every time.
- Leave the close button in, unless there's another visible way out.

**Don't**

- Don't use a sheet for a question that needs an answer. That's an [alert dialog](page:components/alert-dialog).
- Don't open a sheet from inside a sheet.
- Don't open one without the person doing something to ask for it.

pages.title: Sidebar
pages.description: An app's navigation down the side of the screen. It collapses to a strip of icons, becomes a panel on a phone, and remembers how it was left.
pages.markdown:
# Sidebar An app's navigation down the side of the screen. It collapses to a strip of icons, becomes a panel on a phone, and remembers how it was left. Use a sidebar for the main navigation of an app with more destinations than a row across the top can hold. It stays in place while the page scrolls, and people can collapse it when they want the room. ```tsx import { Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarFooter, SidebarGroup, SidebarGroupLabel, SidebarHeader, SidebarMain, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuBadge, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarProvider, SidebarSeparator, SidebarTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; import type { CSSProperties } from "react"; function Icon({ d }: { d: string }) { return ( ); } const icons = { home: "M2.5 7.5 8 3l5.5 4.5V13H10V9.5H6V13H2.5z", inbox: "M2.5 9.5l1.75-6h7.5l1.75 6V13h-11zM2.5 9.5h3.25l.75 1.5h3l.75-1.5h3.25", chart: "M3 13V8M8 13V3M13 13V6", people: "M6 7.5A2.25 2.25 0 1 0 6 3a2.25 2.25 0 0 0 0 4.5zM2 13c0-2.2 1.8-3.5 4-3.5s4 1.3 4 3.5M11 3.2a2.25 2.25 0 0 1 0 4.1M12 9.8c1.2.4 2 1.4 2 3.2", settings: "M3 5h6M12 5h1M3 11h1M7 11h6M10.5 3.5v3M5.5 9.5v3", help: "M8 14A6 6 0 1 0 8 2a6 6 0 0 0 0 12zM6.5 6.25a1.6 1.6 0 1 1 2.4 1.4c-.6.35-.9.7-.9 1.35M8 11.25v.01", }; export default function Example() { return ( Acme Workspace Inbox 12 Reports Customers Account Settings Help {/* A page has one main element, and on this page it's the docs' own. In an app, leave asChild out and SidebarMain is that element. */}

Inbox

Twelve conversations are waiting for a reply.

); } ``` Press the button at the top of the page area, or Ctrl + B. On a phone the same button opens the sidebar as a panel over the page. ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarGroup, SidebarMain, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarProvider, SidebarTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `SidebarProvider` | Holds the state, and lays the sidebar and the page out side by side. | | `Sidebar` | The sidebar. A `nav` element in the page, and a dialog on a phone. | | `SidebarMain` | The page next to the sidebar. A `main` element. | | `SidebarTrigger` | A button that collapses and expands the sidebar. | | `SidebarHeader` | Stays at the top of the sidebar. | | `SidebarContent` | The part in between, which scrolls when it's long. | | `SidebarFooter` | Stays at the bottom. | | `SidebarGroup` | A set of items. | | `SidebarGroupLabel` | The heading over a group. | | `SidebarSeparator` | A line between groups. | | `SidebarMenu` | A list of items. A `ul`. | | `SidebarMenuItem` | One item in it. An `li`. | | `SidebarMenuButton` | The item's button, or its link with `asChild`. | | `SidebarMenuBadge` | A count or a short note at the end of an item's row. | | `SidebarMenuSub` | A list of pages under an item. | | `SidebarMenuSubItem` | One page in it. | | `SidebarMenuSubButton` | That page's link. | These are separate exports, not properties of `Sidebar`. `Sidebar.Menu` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component. ## Props ### SidebarProvider | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `open` | `boolean` | | Whether the sidebar is expanded, when you control it. | | `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the sidebar starts expanded, when you don't control it. On a server, read the cookie and pass what it says, so the page arrives in the state it was left in. | | `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean) => void)` | | Called when the sidebar expands or collapses. | | `cookieName` | `string \| null` | `"nuv-sidebar"` | The cookie the state is remembered in, as `true` or `false`. Pass `null` to store nothing. | | `shortcut` | `string \| null` | `"b"` | A key that expands and collapses the sidebar when pressed with Ctrl, or with Command on a Mac. Pass `null` for no shortcut. | ### Sidebar | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `side` | `"end" \| "start"` | `"start"` | The edge of the screen the sidebar is on. `"start"` is the left edge in a left-to-right layout and the right edge in a right-to-left one. Put the sidebar before or after `SidebarMain` to match. | | `collapsible` | `"icon" \| "none" \| "offcanvas"` | `"icon"` | What collapsing does. `"icon"` leaves a strip of icons, `"offcanvas"` takes the sidebar off the screen, and with `"none"` it can't be collapsed. On a phone it's a panel over the page whichever this is. | | `label` | `string` | `"Sidebar"` | The sidebar's name, for screen readers: of the navigation landmark it is in the page, and of the panel it becomes on a phone. Translate it with the rest of your interface. | | `closeLabel` | `string` | `"Close"` | Accessible name of the button that closes that panel. Translate it with the rest of your interface. | | `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the panel is rendered into on a phone. Set this when it should pick up a `data-theme` from a section of the page. | ### SidebarTrigger | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `label` | `string` | `"Toggle sidebar"` | Accessible name of the button. Translate it with the rest of your interface. | | `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead of the built-in button, and give it the button's props. Use it to make a `Button` the trigger. | ### SidebarMain | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead of a `main`, and give it the class and props. A page has one `main` element, so use this when yours is somewhere else. | ### SidebarMenuButton | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `active` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the item as the page that's open. It's drawn differently, and a screen reader calls it the current page. | | `tooltip` | `ReactNode` | | Shown next to the button while the sidebar is down to its icons, where the button's text is out of sight. Usually the same text. | | `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead of a `button`, and give it the button's classes and props. This is how you make an item a link. | ### SidebarMenuSubButton | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `active` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the item as the page that's open. | | `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead of a link, and give it the link's classes and props. Use it for your router's link. | The other parts are plain elements. They take `ref`, `className` and anything else their element does. ### useSidebar A hook for your own parts, such as a button in the page that opens the sidebar on a phone. It has to be called inside a `SidebarProvider`. | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `state` (required) | `"collapsed" \| "expanded"` | | Whether the sidebar in the page is expanded or collapsed. | | `open` (required) | `boolean` | | Whether the sidebar in the page is expanded. | | `setOpen` (required) | `(open: boolean) => void` | | Expands or collapses the sidebar in the page, and remembers it. | | `openMobile` (required) | `boolean` | | Whether the panel that stands in for the sidebar on a phone is open. | | `setOpenMobile` (required) | `(open: boolean) => void` | | Opens or closes that panel. Nothing is remembered. | | `isMobile` (required) | `boolean` | | Whether the screen is narrow enough for that panel to be in use. | | `toggleSidebar` (required) | `() => void` | | Opens or closes whichever of the two is in use. | ## Layout `SidebarProvider` is a flex row, at least as tall as the screen. The sidebar sticks to the top of it and is as tall as the screen, and `SidebarMain` takes the rest. ```tsx ... {children} ``` Under a header that stays at the top of the screen, tell the sidebar how much room the header takes: ```css .app { --nuv-sidebar-offset: 4rem; --nuv-sidebar-height: calc(100svh - 4rem); } ``` The examples on this page set `--nuv-sidebar-height` too, to fit a box. `SidebarMain` renders the page's `main` element. If your layout already has one elsewhere, pass `asChild` and give it a `div`, as the examples here do, because a page should have one. ## Items Put the icon first in a `SidebarMenuButton`, and the text after it in a `span`. The icon is drawn 1rem square. When the sidebar collapses, the icon is what's left, and it doesn't move. ```tsx Inbox 12 ``` - `asChild` makes the item a link. Use it for anything that goes to a page, with your router's link. - `active` marks the page that's open. It sets `aria-current="page"`, a fill, a heavier weight, and a bar at the start of the row. - `tooltip` names the button while the sidebar is down to its icons. It doesn't show at any other time. - A `SidebarMenuBadge` goes inside the button, last. It's then part of the button's name, so a screen reader says "Inbox 12". Text in a `span` that's too long is cut short with an ellipsis. ## Collapsing `collapsible` says what collapsing does. | Value | What happens | | --- | --- | | `"icon"` | The sidebar narrows to a strip as wide as one icon. Text is cut off, group labels keep their room and go blank, and submenus are hidden. This is the default. | | `"offcanvas"` | The sidebar leaves the screen, and the Tab key no longer stops in it. | | `"none"` | It can't be collapsed. | The state is held by `SidebarProvider`. Leave it alone, or control it with `open` and `onOpenChange`. ```tsx import { Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarGroup, SidebarGroupLabel, SidebarMain, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarProvider, SidebarTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; import type { CSSProperties } from "react"; const sections = ["Summary", "Activity", "Files", "Comments"]; export default function Example() { return (
{/* After the page, to match the side it's on. */} Order 10248 {sections.map((section, index) => ( {section} ))} ); } ``` `side="end"` is for a sidebar on the far side: the right in a left-to-right layout. Put it after `SidebarMain` to match. ## Remembering the state When the sidebar is collapsed or expanded, the provider writes `true` or `false` to a cookie named `nuv-sidebar`. The next time the page loads, it reads the cookie and starts in that state. On a server, read the cookie yourself and pass what it says as `defaultOpen`. The page then arrives in the right state, where otherwise it would arrive expanded and collapse once the script has run. In Next.js: ```tsx import { cookies } from "next/headers"; export default async function Layout({ children }) { const remembered = (await cookies()).get("nuv-sidebar")?.value; return ( ... ); } ``` `cookieName` changes the name, and `cookieName={null}` stores nothing. The cookie lasts a year, is sent to every path, and holds nothing but that one word. Whether it needs a mention in your cookie notice is a question for your own policy. It's a setting the person chose, not tracking. The first example on this page is the only one that writes the cookie. Collapse it and reload the page. ## The shortcut Ctrl + B, or ⌘ + B on a Mac, collapses and expands the sidebar. `shortcut` changes the letter, and `shortcut={null}` turns it off. Something that already uses the keys keeps them: a text editor that handles them and calls `preventDefault`, and any text that's edited in place with `contenteditable`, where the browser makes it bold. ## On a phone Below the `md` breakpoint, 48rem, the sidebar isn't in the page. `SidebarTrigger` opens it as a panel that slides in from its edge, over a dimmed page. It's a dialog: focus moves into it and stays there, Esc closes it, and so does a tap on the strip of page it leaves showing. - The panel is always the whole sidebar, whatever `collapsible` is and whether or not the sidebar is collapsed on a wider screen. - It has a close button in a row of its own at the top. - Opening and closing it isn't remembered, and doesn't change the sidebar a wider screen gets. - A link to another page closes the panel by leaving. In an app that changes pages without loading, close it yourself when the route changes, with `setOpenMobile(false)` from `useSidebar`. Rows are 44 pixels tall on a touch screen and 40 with a mouse. Links in a submenu are 44 and 32. What a server sends is the sidebar for a wide screen, because it can't know the screen. The stylesheet keeps that hidden on a narrow one, so a phone never shows it while the page loads. ## Submenus A `SidebarMenuSub` under an item holds the pages inside it. Put it in a [collapsible](page:components/collapsible) to let people open and close it. ```tsx import { Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger, Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarGroup, SidebarMain, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarMenuSub, SidebarMenuSubButton, SidebarMenuSubItem, SidebarProvider, SidebarTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; import type { CSSProperties } from "react"; function Icon({ d }: { d: string }) { return ( ); } const chart = "M3 13V8M8 13V3M13 13V6"; const file = "M4 2.5h5l3 3v8H4zM9 2.5v3h3"; export default function Example() { return ( Reports Revenue Churn Usage Invoices
); } ``` On the strip of icons a submenu is hidden, so its pages can't be reached from there. Expand the sidebar to get to them, or make the item a link to a page that lists them. ## Colors The sidebar takes the surface colors. Every row's fill is worked out from its text color, so it holds on any background. ```css title="themed.css" /* The primary color as the background. The text and the group label take the color that's made to be read on it. */ .brand-sidebar { --nuv-sidebar-bg: var(--color-primary); --nuv-sidebar-fg: var(--color-primary-foreground); --nuv-sidebar-muted-fg: var(--color-primary-foreground); --nuv-sidebar-border: var(--color-primary); --nuv-focus-ring-color: var(--color-primary-foreground); /* The fills a row gets by default are a little of the text color mixed in, which on a color this strong would bring the two too close to read. These go the other way: away from the text. */ --nuv-sidebar-item-bg-hover: color-mix( in oklab, var(--color-primary) 88%, oklch(from var(--color-primary-foreground) calc(1 - l) 0 0) ); --nuv-sidebar-item-bg-active: color-mix( in oklab, var(--color-primary) 80%, oklch(from var(--color-primary-foreground) calc(1 - l) 0 0) ); } ``` ```tsx import { Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarGroup, SidebarGroupLabel, SidebarMain, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarProvider, SidebarTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; import type { CSSProperties } from "react"; import "./themed.css"; const pages = ["Overview", "Deployments", "Logs", "Billing"]; function Menu() { return ( Project {pages.map((page, index) => ( {page} ))} ); } const box = { "--nuv-sidebar-height": "16rem", "--nuv-sidebar-width": "11rem", border: "1px solid var(--color-border)", borderRadius: "var(--radius-lg)", overflow: "hidden", } as CSSProperties; export default function Example() { return (
{/* Dark, even while the page is light. */}
); } ``` For a dark sidebar in a light app, put `data-theme="dark"` on `Sidebar`. Everything inside takes the dark theme's colors, with the contrast that theme was checked for. For a background of your own, set `--nuv-sidebar-bg` and `--nuv-sidebar-fg`. On a strong color such as the brand color, set the two row fills as well. By default a row under the pointer is filled with a little of the text color, which on a mid-tone background brings the text and the fill too close together to read. The stylesheet above mixes away from the text color. ## Accessibility ### Keyboard | Key | What it does | | --- | --- | | Tab | Moves through the buttons and links in order. | | Enter or Space | Presses the one that has focus. | | Ctrl + B | Collapses or expands the sidebar, or opens and closes the panel on a phone. | | Esc | Closes the panel on a phone. | Safari only stops at links with the Tab key if "Press Tab to highlight each item on a webpage" is turned on in its settings. That's the browser's choice and not something a component can change. ### What the component handles - The sidebar is a `nav` element, so everything in it is inside a navigation landmark, named by `label`. On a phone it's a dialog with the same name. - `SidebarMain` is the page's `main` element. - A group with a `SidebarGroupLabel` has `role="group"` and is named by it. - Menus are lists, so a screen reader says how many items there are. - `active` sets `aria-current="page"`. The fill that marks the row is pale, so it isn't the only sign: the bar at the start of the row has at least 3:1 against the sidebar, and it's drawn as a border, which stays where the browser forces its own colors. - On the strip of icons, a button's text is cut off from view and is still its name. The tooltip is for people who see the icon and don't know what it means. - `SidebarTrigger` has `aria-expanded`, and a name set with `label`. - A button keeps focus when the sidebar collapses around it. - A sidebar that has left the screen is hidden, and not only narrow, so nothing in it takes focus. - When the panel on a phone closes, focus goes back to the button that opened it. - The focus ring is drawn inside each row's edge, where the sidebar can't cut it off. - The width only changes over time when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion. A state that was remembered is applied without a transition. ### What you need to handle - Use links for items that go somewhere, with `asChild`, and buttons for items that do something. - Set `active` on the item for the page that's open, and on no other. - Give every item a `tooltip` if the sidebar can collapse to icons. - Translate `label` and `closeLabel` on `Sidebar`, and `label` on `SidebarTrigger`. - Put the sidebar before `SidebarMain` in the markup when it's on the start side, so the order people tab through matches what they see. ## CSS variables Set these on `SidebarProvider` or anything around it. On a phone the panel renders at the end of ``, so for it, set them on `:root` or `body`, or straight on `Sidebar`. ```css :root { --nuv-sidebar-width: 18rem; } ``` | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-sidebar-height` | `100svh` | Height of the sidebar, and the least the layout is tall. Change it when the sidebar sits under a header. | | `--nuv-sidebar-offset` | `0` | How far from the top of the screen the sidebar sticks. | | `--nuv-sidebar-width` | `16rem` | Width of the sidebar while it's expanded. | | `--nuv-sidebar-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of the edge that faces the page, of separators, and of the line beside a submenu. | | `--nuv-sidebar-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of the sidebar. | | `--nuv-sidebar-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color of the sidebar, and of its rows. | | `--nuv-sidebar-item-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-md)` | Height of a row. It also sets the width of the strip of icons. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. | | `--nuv-sidebar-width-mobile` | `18rem` | The widest the panel gets on a phone. It always leaves a strip of the page showing. | | `--nuv-sidebar-shadow` | `var(--shadow-xl)` | Shadow under the panel on a phone. | | `--nuv-sidebar-overlay-bg` | `var(--color-overlay)` | Color of the layer that dims the page on a phone. | | `--nuv-sidebar-item-bg-hover` | `color-mix(in oklab, currentcolor 8%, transparent)` | Background of a row under the pointer, and of the trigger and the close button. | | `--nuv-sidebar-muted-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Text color of group labels and badges. | | `--nuv-sidebar-item-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius of a row. | | `--nuv-sidebar-item-bg-active` | `color-mix(in oklab, currentcolor 12%, transparent)` | Background of the row for the open page. | | `--nuv-sidebar-active-indicator` | `currentcolor` | Color of the bar at the start of that row. Keep it at 3:1 against the sidebar. | | `--nuv-sidebar-sub-item-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-sm)` | Height of a link in a submenu. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-sidebar` | Sidebar. | | `.nuv-sidebar--end` | A sidebar with `side="end"`. | | `.nuv-sidebar--hidden` | A sidebar that has left the screen. | | `.nuv-sidebar--mobile` | The panel on a phone. | | `.nuv-sidebar--rail` | A sidebar that's down to its strip of icons. | | `.nuv-sidebar-layout` | SidebarProvider. | | `.nuv-sidebar-layout__main` | SidebarMain. | | `.nuv-sidebar__bar` | The row at the top of the panel that holds its close button. | | `.nuv-sidebar__close` | That close button. | | `.nuv-sidebar__content` | SidebarContent. | | `.nuv-sidebar__footer` | SidebarFooter. | | `.nuv-sidebar__group` | SidebarGroup. | | `.nuv-sidebar__group-label` | SidebarGroupLabel. | | `.nuv-sidebar__header` | SidebarHeader. | | `.nuv-sidebar__menu` | SidebarMenu. | | `.nuv-sidebar__menu-badge` | SidebarMenuBadge. | | `.nuv-sidebar__menu-button` | SidebarMenuButton. | | `.nuv-sidebar__menu-item` | SidebarMenuItem. | | `.nuv-sidebar__menu-sub` | SidebarMenuSub. | | `.nuv-sidebar__menu-sub-button` | SidebarMenuSubButton. | | `.nuv-sidebar__menu-sub-item` | SidebarMenuSubItem. | | `.nuv-sidebar__overlay` | The layer that dims the page behind that panel. | | `.nuv-sidebar__separator` | SidebarSeparator. | | `.nuv-sidebar__title` | The panel's name. It isn't drawn. | | `.nuv-sidebar__trigger` | SidebarTrigger. | In the page, the sidebar has `data-state`, which is `expanded` or `collapsed`. A row for the open page has `data-active`. The tooltips are the library's [Tooltip](page:components/tooltip). If you load one stylesheet per component, load `tooltip.css` as well as `sidebar.css`. ## Server components The sidebar parts are client components. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files. A whole sidebar can be put together inside a server component, as every example on this page is. `useSidebar` is a hook, so a part of your own that calls it is a client component. ## Themed sections On a phone the panel renders at the end of ``, outside any `data-theme` section the sidebar is in. `data-theme` on `Sidebar` itself goes to the panel too. For a section's theme, pass the section's element as `container`. ## Not included - A sidebar that floats above the page with a gap around it, or a page area that's inset. The layout is one row with an edge between the two. - A rail to drag or click on the sidebar's edge. `SidebarTrigger` and the shortcut collapse it. - A second button on a row, and a skeleton row. A [dropdown menu](page:components/dropdown-menu) or a [skeleton](page:components/skeleton) can be put in a `SidebarMenuItem` as it is. ## Do and don't **Do** - Keep the names short. One or two words fit at the default width. - Give each item an icon if the sidebar can collapse to icons, and pick icons that differ at a glance. - Order the items by how often they're used, and keep that order the same on every page. **Don't** - Don't nest more than one level of submenu. A third level is a sign the pages need their own navigation. - Don't hide the only way to a page in a submenu that the strip of icons can't show. - Don't put the trigger inside the sidebar only. With `collapsible="offcanvas"` it would leave the screen with it.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import {
  Sidebar,
  SidebarContent,
  SidebarGroup,
  SidebarMain,
  SidebarMenu,
  SidebarMenuButton,
  SidebarMenuItem,
  SidebarProvider,
  SidebarTrigger,
} from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `SidebarProvider` | Holds the state, and lays the sidebar and the page out side by side. |
| `Sidebar` | The sidebar. A `nav` element in the page, and a dialog on a phone. |
| `SidebarMain` | The page next to the sidebar. A `main` element. |
| `SidebarTrigger` | A button that collapses and expands the sidebar. |
| `SidebarHeader` | Stays at the top of the sidebar. |
| `SidebarContent` | The part in between, which scrolls when it's long. |
| `SidebarFooter` | Stays at the bottom. |
| `SidebarGroup` | A set of items. |
| `SidebarGroupLabel` | The heading over a group. |
| `SidebarSeparator` | A line between groups. |
| `SidebarMenu` | A list of items. A `ul`. |
| `SidebarMenuItem` | One item in it. An `li`. |
| `SidebarMenuButton` | The item's button, or its link with `asChild`. |
| `SidebarMenuBadge` | A count or a short note at the end of an item's row. |
| `SidebarMenuSub` | A list of pages under an item. |
| `SidebarMenuSubItem` | One page in it. |
| `SidebarMenuSubButton` | That page's link. |

These are separate exports, not properties of `Sidebar`. `Sidebar.Menu` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

### SidebarProvider

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Whether the sidebar is expanded, when you control it. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the sidebar starts expanded, when you don't control it. On a server, read the cookie and pass what it says, so the page arrives in the state it was left in. |
| `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean) => void)` |  | Called when the sidebar expands or collapses. |
| `cookieName` | `string \| null` | `"nuv-sidebar"` | The cookie the state is remembered in, as `true` or `false`. Pass `null` to store nothing. |
| `shortcut` | `string \| null` | `"b"` | A key that expands and collapses the sidebar when pressed with Ctrl, or with Command on a Mac. Pass `null` for no shortcut. |

### Sidebar

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `side` | `"end" \| "start"` | `"start"` | The edge of the screen the sidebar is on. `"start"` is the left edge in a left-to-right layout and the right edge in a right-to-left one. Put the sidebar before or after `SidebarMain` to match. |
| `collapsible` | `"icon" \| "none" \| "offcanvas"` | `"icon"` | What collapsing does. `"icon"` leaves a strip of icons, `"offcanvas"` takes the sidebar off the screen, and with `"none"` it can't be collapsed. On a phone it's a panel over the page whichever this is. |
| `label` | `string` | `"Sidebar"` | The sidebar's name, for screen readers: of the navigation landmark it is in the page, and of the panel it becomes on a phone. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |
| `closeLabel` | `string` | `"Close"` | Accessible name of the button that closes that panel. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |
| `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the panel is rendered into on a phone. Set this when it should pick up a `data-theme` from a section of the page. |

### SidebarTrigger

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `"Toggle sidebar"` | Accessible name of the button. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead of the built-in button, and give it the button's props. Use it to make a `Button` the trigger. |

### SidebarMain

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead of a `main`, and give it the class and props. A page has one `main` element, so use this when yours is somewhere else. |

### SidebarMenuButton

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `active` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the item as the page that's open. It's drawn differently, and a screen reader calls it the current page. |
| `tooltip` | `ReactNode` |  | Shown next to the button while the sidebar is down to its icons, where the button's text is out of sight. Usually the same text. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead of a `button`, and give it the button's classes and props. This is how you make an item a link. |

### SidebarMenuSubButton

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `active` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the item as the page that's open. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead of a link, and give it the link's classes and props. Use it for your router's link. |

The other parts are plain elements. They take `ref`, `className` and anything else their element does.

### useSidebar

A hook for your own parts, such as a button in the page that opens the sidebar on a phone. It has to be called inside a `SidebarProvider`.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state` (required) | `"collapsed" \| "expanded"` |  | Whether the sidebar in the page is expanded or collapsed. |
| `open` (required) | `boolean` |  | Whether the sidebar in the page is expanded. |
| `setOpen` (required) | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Expands or collapses the sidebar in the page, and remembers it. |
| `openMobile` (required) | `boolean` |  | Whether the panel that stands in for the sidebar on a phone is open. |
| `setOpenMobile` (required) | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Opens or closes that panel. Nothing is remembered. |
| `isMobile` (required) | `boolean` |  | Whether the screen is narrow enough for that panel to be in use. |
| `toggleSidebar` (required) | `() => void` |  | Opens or closes whichever of the two is in use. |

sections.heading: Layout
sections.markdown:
## Layout

`SidebarProvider` is a flex row, at least as tall as the screen. The sidebar sticks to the top of it and is as tall as the screen, and `SidebarMain` takes the rest.

```tsx
<SidebarProvider>
  <Sidebar>...</Sidebar>
  <SidebarMain>{children}</SidebarMain>
</SidebarProvider>
```

Under a header that stays at the top of the screen, tell the sidebar how much room the header takes:

```css
.app {
  --nuv-sidebar-offset: 4rem;
  --nuv-sidebar-height: calc(100svh - 4rem);
}
```

The examples on this page set `--nuv-sidebar-height` too, to fit a box.

`SidebarMain` renders the page's `main` element. If your layout already has one elsewhere, pass `asChild` and give it a `div`, as the examples here do, because a page should have one.

sections.heading: Items
sections.markdown: ## Items Put the icon first in a `SidebarMenuButton`, and the text after it in a `span`. The icon is drawn 1rem square. When the sidebar collapses, the icon is what's left, and it doesn't move. ```tsx Inbox 12 ``` - `asChild` makes the item a link. Use it for anything that goes to a page, with your router's link. - `active` marks the page that's open. It sets `aria-current="page"`, a fill, a heavier weight, and a bar at the start of the row. - `tooltip` names the button while the sidebar is down to its icons. It doesn't show at any other time. - A `SidebarMenuBadge` goes inside the button, last. It's then part of the button's name, so a screen reader says "Inbox 12". Text in a `span` that's too long is cut short with an ellipsis.

sections.heading: Collapsing
sections.markdown:
## Collapsing `collapsible` says what collapsing does. | Value | What happens | | --- | --- | | `"icon"` | The sidebar narrows to a strip as wide as one icon. Text is cut off, group labels keep their room and go blank, and submenus are hidden. This is the default. | | `"offcanvas"` | The sidebar leaves the screen, and the Tab key no longer stops in it. | | `"none"` | It can't be collapsed. | The state is held by `SidebarProvider`. Leave it alone, or control it with `open` and `onOpenChange`. ```tsx import { Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarGroup, SidebarGroupLabel, SidebarMain, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarProvider, SidebarTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; import type { CSSProperties } from "react"; const sections = ["Summary", "Activity", "Files", "Comments"]; export default function Example() { return (
{/* After the page, to match the side it's on. */} Order 10248 {sections.map((section, index) => ( {section} ))} ); } ``` `side="end"` is for a sidebar on the far side: the right in a left-to-right layout. Put it after `SidebarMain` to match.

sections.heading: Remembering the state
The shortcut
sections.markdown:
## The shortcut

<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>B</kbd>, or <kbd>⌘</kbd> + <kbd>B</kbd> on a Mac, collapses and expands the sidebar. `shortcut` changes the letter, and `shortcut={null}` turns it off.

Something that already uses the keys keeps them: a text editor that handles them and calls `preventDefault`, and any text that's edited in place with `contenteditable`, where the browser makes it bold.

sections.heading: On a phone
sections.markdown:
## On a phone

Below the `md` breakpoint, 48rem, the sidebar isn't in the page. `SidebarTrigger` opens it as a panel that slides in from its edge, over a dimmed page. It's a dialog: focus moves into it and stays there, <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes it, and so does a tap on the strip of page it leaves showing.

- The panel is always the whole sidebar, whatever `collapsible` is and whether or not the sidebar is collapsed on a wider screen.
- It has a close button in a row of its own at the top.
- Opening and closing it isn't remembered, and doesn't change the sidebar a wider screen gets.
- A link to another page closes the panel by leaving. In an app that changes pages without loading, close it yourself when the route changes, with `setOpenMobile(false)` from `useSidebar`.

Rows are 44 pixels tall on a touch screen and 40 with a mouse. Links in a submenu are 44 and 32.

What a server sends is the sidebar for a wide screen, because it can't know the screen. The stylesheet keeps that hidden on a narrow one, so a phone never shows it while the page loads.

sections.heading: Submenus
sections.markdown:
## Submenus A `SidebarMenuSub` under an item holds the pages inside it. Put it in a [collapsible](page:components/collapsible) to let people open and close it. ```tsx import { Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger, Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarGroup, SidebarMain, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarMenuSub, SidebarMenuSubButton, SidebarMenuSubItem, SidebarProvider, SidebarTrigger, } from "@nuvui/react"; import type { CSSProperties } from "react"; function Icon({ d }: { d: string }) { return ( ); } const chart = "M3 13V8M8 13V3M13 13V6"; const file = "M4 2.5h5l3 3v8H4zM9 2.5v3h3"; export default function Example() { return ( Reports Revenue Churn Usage Invoices
); } ``` On the strip of icons a submenu is hidden, so its pages can't be reached from there. Expand the sidebar to get to them, or make the item a link to a page that lists them.

sections.heading: Colors
Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves through the buttons and links in order. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> | Presses the one that has focus. |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>B</kbd> | Collapses or expands the sidebar, or opens and closes the panel on a phone. |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Closes the panel on a phone. |

Safari only stops at links with the Tab key if "Press Tab to highlight each item on a webpage" is turned on in its settings. That's the browser's choice and not something a component can change.

### What the component handles

- The sidebar is a `nav` element, so everything in it is inside a navigation landmark, named by `label`. On a phone it's a dialog with the same name.
- `SidebarMain` is the page's `main` element.
- A group with a `SidebarGroupLabel` has `role="group"` and is named by it.
- Menus are lists, so a screen reader says how many items there are.
- `active` sets `aria-current="page"`. The fill that marks the row is pale, so it isn't the only sign: the bar at the start of the row has at least 3:1 against the sidebar, and it's drawn as a border, which stays where the browser forces its own colors.
- On the strip of icons, a button's text is cut off from view and is still its name. The tooltip is for people who see the icon and don't know what it means.
- `SidebarTrigger` has `aria-expanded`, and a name set with `label`.
- A button keeps focus when the sidebar collapses around it.
- A sidebar that has left the screen is hidden, and not only narrow, so nothing in it takes focus.
- When the panel on a phone closes, focus goes back to the button that opened it.
- The focus ring is drawn inside each row's edge, where the sidebar can't cut it off.
- The width only changes over time when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion. A state that was remembered is applied without a transition.

### What you need to handle

- Use links for items that go somewhere, with `asChild`, and buttons for items that do something.
- Set `active` on the item for the page that's open, and on no other.
- Give every item a `tooltip` if the sidebar can collapse to icons.
- Translate `label` and `closeLabel` on `Sidebar`, and `label` on `SidebarTrigger`.
- Put the sidebar before `SidebarMain` in the markup when it's on the start side, so the order people tab through matches what they see.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set these on `SidebarProvider` or anything around it. On a phone the panel renders at the end of `<body>`, so for it, set them on `:root` or `body`, or straight on `Sidebar`.

```css
:root {
  --nuv-sidebar-width: 18rem;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-sidebar-height` | `100svh` | Height of the sidebar, and the least the layout is tall. Change it when the sidebar sits under a header. |
| `--nuv-sidebar-offset` | `0` | How far from the top of the screen the sidebar sticks. |
| `--nuv-sidebar-width` | `16rem` | Width of the sidebar while it's expanded. |
| `--nuv-sidebar-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of the edge that faces the page, of separators, and of the line beside a submenu. |
| `--nuv-sidebar-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of the sidebar. |
| `--nuv-sidebar-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color of the sidebar, and of its rows. |
| `--nuv-sidebar-item-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-md)` | Height of a row. It also sets the width of the strip of icons. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. |
| `--nuv-sidebar-width-mobile` | `18rem` | The widest the panel gets on a phone. It always leaves a strip of the page showing. |
| `--nuv-sidebar-shadow` | `var(--shadow-xl)` | Shadow under the panel on a phone. |
| `--nuv-sidebar-overlay-bg` | `var(--color-overlay)` | Color of the layer that dims the page on a phone. |
| `--nuv-sidebar-item-bg-hover` | `color-mix(in oklab, currentcolor 8%, transparent)` | Background of a row under the pointer, and of the trigger and the close button. |
| `--nuv-sidebar-muted-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Text color of group labels and badges. |
| `--nuv-sidebar-item-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius of a row. |
| `--nuv-sidebar-item-bg-active` | `color-mix(in oklab, currentcolor 12%, transparent)` | Background of the row for the open page. |
| `--nuv-sidebar-active-indicator` | `currentcolor` | Color of the bar at the start of that row. Keep it at 3:1 against the sidebar. |
| `--nuv-sidebar-sub-item-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-sm)` | Height of a link in a submenu. The default differs between touch screens and a mouse. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-sidebar` | Sidebar. |
| `.nuv-sidebar--end` | A sidebar with `side="end"`. |
| `.nuv-sidebar--hidden` | A sidebar that has left the screen. |
| `.nuv-sidebar--mobile` | The panel on a phone. |
| `.nuv-sidebar--rail` | A sidebar that's down to its strip of icons. |
| `.nuv-sidebar-layout` | SidebarProvider. |
| `.nuv-sidebar-layout__main` | SidebarMain. |
| `.nuv-sidebar__bar` | The row at the top of the panel that holds its close button. |
| `.nuv-sidebar__close` | That close button. |
| `.nuv-sidebar__content` | SidebarContent. |
| `.nuv-sidebar__footer` | SidebarFooter. |
| `.nuv-sidebar__group` | SidebarGroup. |
| `.nuv-sidebar__group-label` | SidebarGroupLabel. |
| `.nuv-sidebar__header` | SidebarHeader. |
| `.nuv-sidebar__menu` | SidebarMenu. |
| `.nuv-sidebar__menu-badge` | SidebarMenuBadge. |
| `.nuv-sidebar__menu-button` | SidebarMenuButton. |
| `.nuv-sidebar__menu-item` | SidebarMenuItem. |
| `.nuv-sidebar__menu-sub` | SidebarMenuSub. |
| `.nuv-sidebar__menu-sub-button` | SidebarMenuSubButton. |
| `.nuv-sidebar__menu-sub-item` | SidebarMenuSubItem. |
| `.nuv-sidebar__overlay` | The layer that dims the page behind that panel. |
| `.nuv-sidebar__separator` | SidebarSeparator. |
| `.nuv-sidebar__title` | The panel's name. It isn't drawn. |
| `.nuv-sidebar__trigger` | SidebarTrigger. |

In the page, the sidebar has `data-state`, which is `expanded` or `collapsed`. A row for the open page has `data-active`.

The tooltips are the library's [Tooltip](page:components/tooltip). If you load one stylesheet per component, load `tooltip.css` as well as `sidebar.css`.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

The sidebar parts are client components. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files.

A whole sidebar can be put together inside a server component, as every example on this page is. `useSidebar` is a hook, so a part of your own that calls it is a client component.

sections.heading: Themed sections
sections.markdown:
## Themed sections

On a phone the panel renders at the end of `<body>`, outside any `data-theme` section the sidebar is in. `data-theme` on `Sidebar` itself goes to the panel too. For a section's theme, pass the section's element as `container`.

sections.heading: Not included
sections.markdown:
## Not included

- A sidebar that floats above the page with a gap around it, or a page area that's inset. The layout is one row with an edge between the two.
- A rail to drag or click on the sidebar's edge. `SidebarTrigger` and the shortcut collapse it.
- A second button on a row, and a skeleton row. A [dropdown menu](page:components/dropdown-menu) or a [skeleton](page:components/skeleton) can be put in a `SidebarMenuItem` as it is.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Keep the names short. One or two words fit at the default width.
- Give each item an icon if the sidebar can collapse to icons, and pick icons that differ at a glance.
- Order the items by how often they're used, and keep that order the same on every page.

**Don't**

- Don't nest more than one level of submenu. A third level is a sign the pages need their own navigation.
- Don't hide the only way to a page in a submenu that the strip of icons can't show.
- Don't put the trigger inside the sidebar only. With `collapsible="offcanvas"` it would leave the screen with it.

pages.title: Skeleton
pages.description: A gray box in the shape of content that's still loading.
pages.markdown:
# Skeleton A gray box in the shape of content that's still loading. Use skeletons where content is on its way and you know roughly what shape it will have: a card, a row, a line of text. They hold the layout still, so nothing jumps when the content arrives. Where you don't know the shape, or the wait is for an action and not for content, use a [spinner](page:components/spinner). ```tsx import { Skeleton } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return (
); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Skeleton } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `shape` | `"block" \| "circle" \| "text"` | `"block"` | `"block"` is a rounded box you give a size. `"text"` is as tall as a line of the text around it. `"circle"` is round, for an avatar. | Everything else is passed to the `
`, including `ref`, `className` and `style`. ## Shapes | Shape | What it's for | Its size | | --- | --- | --- | | `block` | A picture, a chart, a button, a whole card. | As wide as its container and 16 pixels tall. Give it the size of what it stands for. | | `text` | A line of text. | One line of the text around it, with a bar as tall as the letters. It follows the font size and the line height. | | `circle` | An [avatar](page:components/avatar). | 40 pixels each way, the same as a medium avatar. | Set a size with `style`, with a class of your own, or with `--nuv-skeleton-width` and `--nuv-skeleton-height`. Two `text` skeletons one after the other are spaced like two lines of a paragraph, because each takes up exactly one line. Make the last one shorter and the block reads as text. ## In place of real content Render the skeletons in the same parts the content will use, and swap one for the other when the data arrives. ```tsx "use client"; import { Button, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle, Skeleton, VisuallyHidden, } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true); return (
{loading ? ( <> ) : ( <> Northwind Traders Customer since March 2021 Fourteen orders this year, the last one on 4 July. Nothing is overdue. )} {/* Says when the content has arrived. The skeletons themselves are hidden from screen readers. */} {loading ? "Loading the customer" : "The customer has loaded"}
); } ``` ## Accessibility A skeleton has no keyboard behavior, and it's hidden from screen readers with `aria-hidden`. A dozen gray boxes would otherwise be a dozen things with nothing to say. ### What the component handles - `aria-hidden="true"` on every skeleton. - The pulse only runs when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion. With reduced motion, the boxes stand still. - Where the browser forces its own colors, a skeleton is an outline. Its fill isn't drawn there. ### What you need to handle - **Say that something is loading.** Put `aria-busy="true"` on the region the skeletons are in, and take it off when the content is there. - **Say when it has loaded,** if the wait was long enough to notice. `aria-busy` isn't announced by itself. A visually hidden element with `role="status"` that changes from "Loading the customer" to "The customer has loaded" is, as in the example above. - Don't leave skeletons up when loading fails. Show an [alert](page:components/alert) that says what went wrong. ## CSS variables Set any of these on the skeleton, or on anything around it. ```css .sidebar { --nuv-skeleton-bg: var(--color-border); } ``` | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-skeleton-width` | `100%`, `2.5rem` | Width. Differs by shape. | | `--nuv-skeleton-height` | `1rem`, `1em`, `2.5rem` | Height. Differs by shape. On the text shape it's the height of the bar, not of the line. | | `--nuv-skeleton-radius` | `var(--radius-md)`, `var(--radius-sm)`, `var(--radius-full)` | Corner radius. Differs by shape. | | `--nuv-skeleton-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Fill color. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-skeleton` | Every skeleton. | | `.nuv-skeleton--circle` | shape="circle" | | `.nuv-skeleton--text` | shape="text" | A block also has the class `nuv-skeleton--block`. It has no rules of its own, because a block is how every skeleton starts. ## Server components Skeleton has no `"use client"` directive and uses no state, so it renders in a server component as it is. That makes it a good fit for the `fallback` of a React `Suspense` boundary, or a `loading.tsx` file in Next.js. ## Do and don't **Do** - Match the shape and size of the real content closely enough that nothing moves when it arrives. - Show them only for a wait people would notice. Content that takes a tenth of a second doesn't need one. **Don't** - Don't draw a skeleton for every small detail. A few boxes that give the layout are enough. - Don't use a skeleton for something that may turn out to be empty. Decide between content and an [empty state](page:components/empty) once you know.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shape` | `"block" \| "circle" \| "text"` | `"block"` | `"block"` is a rounded box you give a size. `"text"` is as tall as a line of the text around it. `"circle"` is round, for an avatar. |

Everything else is passed to the `<div>`, including `ref`, `className` and `style`.

sections.heading: Shapes
sections.markdown:
## Shapes

| Shape | What it's for | Its size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `block` | A picture, a chart, a button, a whole card. | As wide as its container and 16 pixels tall. Give it the size of what it stands for. |
| `text` | A line of text. | One line of the text around it, with a bar as tall as the letters. It follows the font size and the line height. |
| `circle` | An [avatar](page:components/avatar). | 40 pixels each way, the same as a medium avatar. |

Set a size with `style`, with a class of your own, or with `--nuv-skeleton-width` and `--nuv-skeleton-height`.

Two `text` skeletons one after the other are spaced like two lines of a paragraph, because each takes up exactly one line. Make the last one shorter and the block reads as text.

sections.heading: In place of real content
Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

A skeleton has no keyboard behavior, and it's hidden from screen readers with `aria-hidden`. A dozen gray boxes would otherwise be a dozen things with nothing to say.

### What the component handles

- `aria-hidden="true"` on every skeleton.
- The pulse only runs when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion. With reduced motion, the boxes stand still.
- Where the browser forces its own colors, a skeleton is an outline. Its fill isn't drawn there.

### What you need to handle

- **Say that something is loading.** Put `aria-busy="true"` on the region the skeletons are in, and take it off when the content is there.
- **Say when it has loaded,** if the wait was long enough to notice. `aria-busy` isn't announced by itself. A visually hidden element with `role="status"` that changes from "Loading the customer" to "The customer has loaded" is, as in the example above.
- Don't leave skeletons up when loading fails. Show an [alert](page:components/alert) that says what went wrong.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on the skeleton, or on anything around it.

```css
.sidebar {
  --nuv-skeleton-bg: var(--color-border);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-skeleton-width` | `100%`, `2.5rem` | Width. Differs by shape. |
| `--nuv-skeleton-height` | `1rem`, `1em`, `2.5rem` | Height. Differs by shape. On the text shape it's the height of the bar, not of the line. |
| `--nuv-skeleton-radius` | `var(--radius-md)`, `var(--radius-sm)`, `var(--radius-full)` | Corner radius. Differs by shape. |
| `--nuv-skeleton-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Fill color. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-skeleton` | Every skeleton. |
| `.nuv-skeleton--circle` | shape="circle" |
| `.nuv-skeleton--text` | shape="text" |

A block also has the class `nuv-skeleton--block`. It has no rules of its own, because a block is how every skeleton starts.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

Skeleton has no `"use client"` directive and uses no state, so it renders in a server component as it is. That makes it a good fit for the `fallback` of a React `Suspense` boundary, or a `loading.tsx` file in Next.js.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Match the shape and size of the real content closely enough that nothing moves when it arrives.
- Show them only for a wait people would notice. Content that takes a tenth of a second doesn't need one.

**Don't**

- Don't draw a skeleton for every small detail. A few boxes that give the layout are enough.
- Don't use a skeleton for something that may turn out to be empty. Decide between content and an [empty state](page:components/empty) once you know.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { Slider } from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `thumbLabels` | `string[]` |  | Accessible name of each handle, in order. A slider with two handles needs them told apart. Left out, Radix names them "Minimum" and "Maximum", so set this when your interface isn't in English. |
| `getValueLabel` | `((value: number, index: number) => string)` |  | What a screen reader says for a handle's value, in place of the bare number: "40 percent", or the name of a step. It's given the value and the handle's position, counted from 0. |

These come from Radix.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number[]` |  | The values, one for each handle, when you control them yourself. Use it with `onValueChange`. |
| `defaultValue` | `number[]` |  | The values it starts with, when you don't control them. How many there are decides how many handles are drawn. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: number[]) => void)` |  | Called with the values while a handle moves. |
| `onValueCommit` | `((value: number[]) => void)` |  | Called with the values when a handle is let go of, or a key changes it. The place to save. |
| `min` | `number` |  | The lowest value. It's 0 by default. |
| `max` | `number` |  | The highest value. It's 100 by default. |
| `step` | `number` |  | How far the value moves at a time. It's 1 by default. |
| `minStepsBetweenThumbs` | `number` |  | The fewest steps two handles may be apart. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` |  | `"vertical"` stands the slider on end. |
| `inverted` | `boolean` |  | Fills from the far end, and turns the arrow keys around to match. |
| `dir` | `"ltr" \| "rtl"` |  | The reading direction. In `"rtl"` the slider fills from the right. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Stops the handles from being focused or moved. |
| `name` | `string` |  | The name the values are submitted under in a form. |

Everything else is passed to the `<span>` Radix renders around the track, including `ref`, `id` and `className`.

The value is always an array, with one handle too. There's a handle for each number in it.

sections.heading: A range
Vertical
Right to left
sections.markdown:
## Right to left

A slider doesn't read its direction from the page. Pass `dir="rtl"` and it fills from the right, and the left and right arrow keys swap.

sections.heading: In a form
sections.markdown:
## In a form

Give it a `name` and each handle's value is submitted, from a hidden input. With one handle the field is called `name`. With several, each is submitted as `name[]`.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

The handle is 20 pixels, which is too small for a finger. On a touch screen the area that responds to a touch is 44 by 44 pixels, centered on the handle. A touch anywhere on the track moves the nearest handle there, and dragging along the track doesn't scroll the page.

Leave room above and below it. A slider right at the edge of a scrolling list is hard to grab without scrolling.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves focus to a handle. Each handle is a tab stop. |
| <kbd>→</kbd> or <kbd>↑</kbd> | Raises the value by one step. |
| <kbd>←</kbd> or <kbd>↓</kbd> | Lowers the value by one step. |
| <kbd>Page Up</kbd> and <kbd>Page Down</kbd> | Change the value by ten steps. |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> with an arrow | The same, ten steps. |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> | Go to the lowest or highest value. With two handles, it's the handle at that end that moves. |

### What the component handles

- Each handle has `role="slider"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-orientation`. This part is Radix.
- `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` on the slider are moved to where they mean something: the handle when there's one, and a group around the handles when there are several.
- The track uses `--color-border-strong` and the filled part and the handle's edge use `--color-primary`. Each has at least 3:1 contrast with the page in every theme.
- Where the browser forces its own colors, as Windows high contrast does, backgrounds aren't drawn. The track gets an outline there, and the filled part the system's color for something selected.
- Keyboard focus shows a 2 pixel ring around the handle.

### What you need to handle

- Give it a name: `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` pointing at visible text. A `<label>` can't point at a slider. A [Field](page:components/field) does it for you.
- Show the value in text somewhere near it. The handle's position alone is only a rough reading, and a screen reader's "40" means little without a unit.
- If the bare number isn't what people think in, pass `getValueLabel`. A screen reader then says "40 percent" or "Medium" where it would have said "40".

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on the slider, or on anything around it.

```css
.mixer {
  --nuv-slider-range: var(--color-success);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-slider-width` | `100%` | Width of a horizontal slider. It fills its container by default. |
| `--nuv-slider-thumb-size` | `1.25rem` | Width and height of a handle. |
| `--nuv-slider-length` | `10rem` | Height of a vertical slider. |
| `--nuv-slider-track-size` | `0.375rem` | Thickness of the track. |
| `--nuv-slider-track` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Color of the empty part of the track. Keep it at 3:1 against the page. |
| `--nuv-slider-range` | `var(--color-primary)` | Color of the filled part. |
| `--nuv-slider-thumb-border` | `var(--color-primary)` | Color of a handle's edge. |
| `--nuv-slider-thumb-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Fill color of a handle. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-slider` | The slider. |
| `.nuv-slider__range` | The filled part of the track. |
| `.nuv-slider__thumb` | A handle. |
| `.nuv-slider__track` | The track. |

Radix sets `data-orientation` on every part, and `data-disabled` when the slider is disabled.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

Slider is a client component. It carries `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files. You can render it from a server component, as the vertical example on this page does.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Show the current value next to the slider.
- Pick a `step` that matches how exact the setting needs to be. A hundred steps on a phone is hard to land on.

**Don't**

- Don't use a slider for a value people know as a number, such as a quantity or an age.
- Don't use one for a range so wide that a single pixel jumps the value by a lot.

pages.title: Spinner
pages.description: A ring that turns while something is being done and there's no way to say how far along it is.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { Spinner } from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `"lg" \| "md" \| "sm"` | `"md"` |  |
| `label` | `string` | `"Loading"` | What a screen reader says. It's in the page as text nobody sees. Translate it with the rest of your interface. Pass an empty string where text next to the spinner already says it: the spinner is then hidden from screen readers. |

Everything else is passed to the `<span>`, including `ref` and `className`.

sections.heading: In a button
Next to text that says the same
Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

A spinner has no keyboard behavior. It can't take focus.

### What the component handles

- It has `role="status"` and its label is text in the page, hidden from view. A screen reader reads the label when the spinner is added to the page, at the next pause in what it's saying.
- With an empty `label` it has no role and `aria-hidden="true"`.
- It only turns when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion. With reduced motion it stands still: a ring with a quarter of it drawn darker, which still reads as a spinner.
- It's drawn in the text color, which keeps it visible where the browser forces its own colors.

### What you need to handle

- **Say what's loading.** "Loading" is the default because it's always true. "Saving the report" is better.
- **Render the spinner when the wait starts.** A screen reader notices a status that's added to the page. One that's always there and shown with CSS may not be announced.
- **Say when it's over, if nothing visible changes.** Taking a spinner away isn't announced.
- Translate the label with the rest of your interface.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on the spinner, or on anything around it.

```css
.page-loader {
  --nuv-spinner-size: 3rem;
  --nuv-spinner-color: var(--color-primary);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-spinner-size` | `1.25rem`, `1rem`, `2rem` | Width and height. Differs by size. |
| `--nuv-spinner-color` | `currentcolor` | Color of the ring. The color of the text around it by default. |
| `--nuv-spinner-duration` | `0.75s` | How long one turn takes. |
| `--nuv-spinner-track-opacity` | `0.25` | How strongly the part of the ring that isn't the moving arc is drawn, from 0 to 1. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-spinner` | Every spinner. |
| `.nuv-spinner--lg` | size="lg" |
| `.nuv-spinner--sm` | size="sm" |
| `.nuv-spinner__label` | The text for screen readers. |
| `.nuv-spinner__ring` | The drawing, which is what turns. |
| `.nuv-spinner__track` | The pale full circle behind the arc. |

A medium spinner also has the class `nuv-spinner--md`. It has no rules of its own, because medium is how every spinner starts.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

Spinner has no `"use client"` directive and uses no state, so it renders in a server component as it is.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Put it where the result will show up, or in the button that started the work.
- Use one spinner for one piece of work.

**Don't**

- Don't cover the whole page with a spinner for something that affects one part of it.
- Don't show a spinner for longer than a few seconds without saying more. Past that, people want to know what's happening and whether they can leave.

pages.title: Stat
pages.description: One figure for a dashboard, with what it counts, the number, how it changed, and room for a small chart.
pages.markdown:
# Stat

One figure for a dashboard, with what it counts, the number, how it changed, and room for a small chart.

Use a stat for a number someone checks at a glance: revenue this month, tickets open, seats in use. `StatGroup` sets several side by side.

```tsx
import {
  FormattedNumber,
  Stat,
  StatDescription,
  StatGroup,
  StatLabel,
  StatValue,
  Trend,
} from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <StatGroup style={{ inlineSize: "100%" }}>
      <Stat>
        <StatLabel>Revenue</StatLabel>
        <StatValue>
          <FormattedNumber
            value={48250}
            currency="USD"
            maximumFractionDigits={0}
          />
        </StatValue>
        <StatDescription>
          <Trend value={0.125} /> against last month
        </StatDescription>
      </Stat>
      <Stat>
        <StatLabel>New customers</StatLabel>
        <StatValue>
          <FormattedNumber value={1284} />
        </StatValue>
        <StatDescription>
          <Trend value={-0.032} /> against last month
        </StatDescription>
      </Stat>
      <Stat>
        <StatLabel>Failed payments</StatLabel>
        <StatValue>
          <FormattedNumber value={17} />
        </StatValue>
        <StatDescription>
          <Trend value={-0.31} good="down" /> against last month
        </StatDescription>
      </Stat>
    </StatGroup>
  );
}
```

## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Stat,
  StatChart,
  StatDescription,
  StatGroup,
  StatLabel,
  StatValue,
} from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Stat` | One figure. A card unless you say otherwise. |
| `StatLabel` | What the number counts. |
| `StatValue` | The number, large. |
| `StatDescription` | A line under it: how it changed, and against what. |
| `StatChart` | Room for a small chart, 48 pixels high. |
| `StatGroup` | Several stats, as many to a row as fit. |

Only `Stat`, `StatLabel` and `StatValue` are needed. Put the label first: a screen reader reads the parts in the order they're written, and "Revenue, $48,250" makes sense where "$48,250, Revenue" makes someone wait.

## Props

### Stat

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"card" \| "plain"` | `"card"` | `"card"` draws a surface with an edge around the figure. `"plain"` draws nothing, for a figure that's already inside a card or a table. |

The other parts add no props of their own. Each takes what its element takes, including `ref` and `className`.

## The number and its change

The parts take any children. [`FormattedNumber`](page:components/formatted-number) writes the number for a language and region, and [`Trend`](page:components/trend) says which way it moved. Neither is required: a value can be plain text, such as "4m 12s".

## With a chart

`StatChart` is a box with a height, after the rest. What's drawn in it is yours: a sparkline from [`@nuvui/charts`](page:charts/index), or a few lines of SVG as here. The core doesn't depend on a charting library, so it draws nothing itself.

```tsx
import {
  FormattedNumber,
  Stat,
  StatChart,
  StatDescription,
  StatLabel,
  StatValue,
  Trend,
} from "@nuvui/react";

const weeks = [31, 34, 33, 38, 41, 39, 44, 47, 46, 52, 55, 61];

// The line, in a box 110 wide and 40 high, with the first week at the left.
const points = weeks
  .map((value, index) => `${index * 10},${40 - ((value - 30) / 32) * 40}`)
  .join(" ");

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Stat style={{ inlineSize: "16rem" }}>
      <StatLabel>Active teams</StatLabel>
      <StatValue>
        <FormattedNumber value={61} />
      </StatValue>
      <StatDescription>
        <Trend value={0.109} /> in twelve weeks
      </StatDescription>
      {/* The number and the trend already say it, so the picture is hidden
          from screen readers. */}
      <StatChart>
        <svg
          aria-hidden="true"
          viewBox="0 0 110 40"
          preserveAspectRatio="none"
          width="100%"
          height="100%"
          fill="none"
          stroke="var(--color-chart-1)"
          strokeWidth="2"
          strokeLinecap="round"
          strokeLinejoin="round"
        >
          <polyline points={points} vectorEffect="non-scaling-stroke" />
        </svg>
      </StatChart>
    </Stat>
  );
}
```

When the number and the trend already say what the chart shows, hide the chart from screen readers with `aria-hidden="true"`. When the chart says more, give it a name and a table of its numbers, as the [charts](page:charts/index) pages describe.

## Plain, inside something else

`variant="plain"` draws no edge, no fill and no padding, for a stat that sits in a [card](page:components/card) or a table cell that already has them.

```tsx
import {
  Card,
  CardContent,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
  FormattedNumber,
  Stat,
  StatDescription,
  StatGroup,
  StatLabel,
  StatValue,
} from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Card style={{ inlineSize: "100%" }}>
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>This billing period</CardTitle>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>
        <StatGroup>
          <Stat variant="plain">
            <StatLabel>Seats in use</StatLabel>
            <StatValue>
              <FormattedNumber value={42} />
            </StatValue>
            <StatDescription>of 50 on the plan</StatDescription>
          </Stat>
          <Stat variant="plain">
            <StatLabel>Next invoice</StatLabel>
            <StatValue>
              <FormattedNumber value={1260} currency="USD" />
            </StatValue>
            <StatDescription>on 1 November</StatDescription>
          </Stat>
        </StatGroup>
      </CardContent>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

## In a group

`StatGroup` is a grid that fits as many columns as it can at a least width of 13rem, all the same width. On a phone that's one column. It sets no number of columns, so it works in a full-width page and in a narrow panel without a breakpoint. Change the least width with `--nuv-stat-group-min`.

## Accessibility

A stat has no keyboard behavior. It isn't a control and can't take focus.

### What the component handles

- The parts are read in the order they're written, with nothing hidden and nothing added.
- The number's digits are one width each, so a value that updates doesn't shift.
- A card's edge is a border, which is still drawn where the browser forces its own colors.
- The label and the description have at least 4.5:1 against the card in every theme.

### What you need to handle

- Write the label first, then the value.
- Say what a change is measured against, in `StatDescription`.
- A group of stats under a heading is found by that heading. Give the section one.
- A value that changes while the page is open isn't announced. For one that matters, such as an error count passing a limit, say it in a [toast](page:components/toast) or an element with `role="status"`.

## CSS variables

Set any of these on a `Stat`, on a `StatGroup`, or on anything around them.

```css

  --nuv-stat-group-min: 16rem;
  --nuv-stat-shadow: none;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-stat-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 1.5)` | Space between the parts. |
| `--nuv-stat-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)`, `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color. |
| `--nuv-stat-padding` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 4)`, `calc(var(--spacing) * 5)` | Padding of a card. 16 pixels on a phone and 20 from the `sm` breakpoint up. |
| `--nuv-stat-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Border color of a card. |
| `--nuv-stat-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of a card. |
| `--nuv-stat-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of a card. |
| `--nuv-stat-shadow` | `var(--shadow-xs)` | Shadow of a card. |
| `--nuv-stat-muted-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the label and the description. Keep it at 4.5:1 against the background. |
| `--nuv-stat-value-size` | `var(--text-2xl)` | Font size of the number. |
| `--nuv-stat-chart-height` | `3rem` | Height of the chart's box. |
| `--nuv-stat-group-min` | `13rem` | The least width of a column in a group. A narrower group has one column. |
| `--nuv-stat-group-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 4)` | Space between the stats in a group. |

## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-stat` | Every stat. |
| `.nuv-stat--card` | variant="card", the default. |
| `.nuv-stat-group` | StatGroup |
| `.nuv-stat__chart` | StatChart |
| `.nuv-stat__description` | StatDescription |
| `.nuv-stat__label` | StatLabel |
| `.nuv-stat__value` | StatValue |

## Server components

No part has a `"use client"` directive or uses state, so all of them render in a server component as they are. A chart from `@nuvui/charts` is a client component, in a file of its own.

## Do and don't

**Do**

- Keep a group to the few numbers that matter on the page. Four is easy to take in, and twelve isn't.
- Use the same order of parts in every stat of a group.

**Don't**

- Don't make a stat a link without saying where it goes. Wrap it in a link whose name says so, or put a link in the description.
- Don't use a stat for a number that needs a sentence to explain. That's text.

sections.heading: Parts
