sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { Toaster, toast } from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Setup
API
sections.markdown:
## API

### toast(title, options)

Shows a toast and returns its id, a string. `title` is the main line, and can be text or JSX. Everything in `options` is optional:

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` |  | Pass the id of a toast that's already showing to replace it instead of adding another. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | A second line under the title. |
| `intent` | `"danger" \| "info" \| "neutral" \| "success" \| "warning"` | `"neutral"` | Colors the toast's edge. A `"warning"` or `"danger"` toast also interrupts a screen reader to be read out at once, as an alert with that intent does. The others wait until it's quiet. |
| `duration` | `number` |  | How long the toast stays, in milliseconds. `Infinity` keeps it until it's dismissed. Without this, the Toaster's `duration` applies. |
| `action` | `ToastAction` |  | A button in the toast, such as "Undo". |

`action` takes these:

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The text on the button. |
| `altText` (required) | `string` |  | Another way to do the same thing, for screen reader users, who may not reach the button before the toast has gone. For example "Undo with Ctrl+Z". |
| `onClick` (required) | `() => void` |  | Called when the button is pressed. The toast closes afterwards. |

### toast.dismiss(id)

Closes the toast with that id. Called with no id, it closes all of them.

```tsx
const id = toast("Uploading photo.jpg", { duration: Infinity });

// Later
toast.dismiss(id);
```

### Toaster

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | `"bottom-center" \| "bottom-end" \| "bottom-start" \| "top-center" \| "top-end" \| "top-start"` | `"bottom-end"` | Where toasts appear once the screen is at least 40rem wide. On a narrower screen they span its width, and only the top or bottom part of this applies. |
| `duration` | `number` | `5000` | How long a toast stays, in milliseconds, unless it sets its own. |
| `limit` | `number` | `3` | The most toasts shown at once. Any others wait, and each shows when one before it closes. A waiting toast's `duration` starts when it shows. |
| `closeLabel` | `string` | `"Close"` | Accessible name of the close button on each toast. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |
| `toastLabel` | `string` | `"Notification"` | What a screen reader says before the text of each toast. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |
| `swipeDirection` | `"down" \| "left" \| "right" \| "up"` | `"right"` | The direction a toast is swiped in to dismiss it. |

Two more come from Radix:

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` |  | The name of the list of toasts as a landmark. It's `"Notifications ({hotkey})"` unless you say otherwise, and `{hotkey}` is filled in for you. |
| `hotkey` | `string[]` |  | The keys that move focus to the list. It's `["F8"]` unless you say otherwise. |

`Toaster` also takes `ref` and `className`, which go to the list element.

sections.heading: Intents
sections.markdown:
## Intents

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button, toast } from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <>
      <Button intent="secondary" onClick={() => toast("3 files selected")}>
        Neutral
      </Button>
      <Button
        intent="secondary"
        onClick={() => toast("Invitation sent", { intent: "success" })}
      >
        Success
      </Button>
      <Button
        intent="secondary"
        onClick={() =>
          toast("A new version is ready", {
            intent: "info",
            description: "Reload the page to get it.",
          })
        }
      >
        Info
      </Button>
      <Button
        intent="secondary"
        onClick={() =>
          toast("Your trial ends in three days", { intent: "warning" })
        }
      >
        Warning
      </Button>
      <Button
        intent="secondary"
        onClick={() =>
          toast("Couldn't send the invitation", {
            intent: "danger",
            description: "Check the address and try again.",
          })
        }
      >
        Danger
      </Button>
    </>
  );
}
```

The colored edge is decoration. Say what happened in the title, so the message works without it.

sections.heading: With an action
Changing a toast that's showing
How long it stays
sections.markdown:
## How long it stays

A toast stays for 5 seconds unless `duration` says otherwise, on `Toaster` for all of them or in `options` for one. `Infinity` keeps a toast up until it's dismissed.

The clock stops while the pointer is over a toast, and while keyboard focus is anywhere in the list. It starts again when they leave.

sections.heading: Several at once
Where it shows
sections.markdown:
## Where it shows

On a screen narrower than 40rem, toasts span the width of the screen along the bottom, or along the top if `position` starts with `top`. From 40rem up, they're a column 22rem wide in the corner that `position` names.

The newest toast is always the one nearest the edge of the screen.

The list sits where you render `Toaster`, without a portal, so it picks up a `data-theme` from whatever is around it.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>F8</kbd> | Moves focus to the list of toasts, from anywhere on the page. |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves through the toasts and the buttons inside them. |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Closes the toast that has focus. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> | Presses the focused button. |

### What the component handles

Most of this is Radix. The library chooses how each intent is announced.

- Every toast is read out by screen readers when it appears. A `warning` or `danger` toast interrupts whatever is being read, as an [alert](page:components/alert) with that intent does. The others wait until the screen reader is idle.
- No more than three toasts show at once. The rest wait their turn, and each is announced when it shows.
- The list is a landmark named "Notifications (F8)", so it can be found again after the announcement.
- The clock stops on hover and on focus, which gives people time to read a toast and reach its buttons.
- The close button is a real button with an accessible name, and is at least 44 pixels on touch screens.
- A toast can be swiped away to the right, with a finger or a mouse.
- The list takes no clicks itself. Whatever is under an empty part of it still works.
- The animations only run when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion.

### What you need to handle

- Don't put anything essential in a toast. Some people will miss it however long it stays.
- Give a toast with an action, or with a lot of text, a longer `duration`.
- Write an `altText` that says how else to do the action, such as a keyboard shortcut or where to find it on the page.
- Translate `closeLabel`, `toastLabel` and `label` along with the rest of your interface.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-toast-width` | `22rem` | Width of a toast once the screen is at least 40rem wide. |

| `--nuv-toast-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius. |

| `--nuv-toast-shadow` | `var(--shadow-lg)` | Shadow under each toast. |
| `--nuv-toast-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color. |
| `--nuv-toast-accent-width` | `4px` | Thickness of that edge. The padding beside it shrinks to match, so titles stay lined up. |
| `--nuv-toast-accent` | `var(--color-primary)`, `var(--color-success)`, `var(--color-warning)`, `var(--color-danger)` | Color of the thick edge on a toast with an intent. |

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-toast` | One toast. |
| `.nuv-toast--danger` | A toast with intent "danger". |
| `.nuv-toast--info` | A toast with intent "info". |
| `.nuv-toast--success` | A toast with intent "success". |
| `.nuv-toast--warning` | A toast with intent "warning". |
| `.nuv-toast__action` | The action button. |
| `.nuv-toast__close` | The close button. |
| `.nuv-toast__content` | The title and the description together. |
| `.nuv-toast__description` | The description. |
| `.nuv-toast__title` | The title. |
| `.nuv-toaster` | Toaster, which is the list the toasts sit in. |
| `.nuv-toaster--center` | A position that ends with center. |
| `.nuv-toaster--end` | A position that ends with end. |

| `.nuv-toaster--top` | A position that starts with top. |

The list also gets `nuv-toaster--bottom`, and a toast gets `nuv-toast--neutral`, when those apply. No styles are attached to either, since they're the base.

Radix sets `data-state="open"` or `data-state="closed"` on each toast, and `data-swipe` while one is being dragged. The animations hang off those.

sections.markdown:
## Server components

`Toaster` is a client component. It carries `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files. You can render it from a server component, such as a root layout.

`toast()` belongs in the browser. Call it from event handlers and effects in client components. If a client component calls it while it's being rendered on the server, nothing happens: there's nowhere to show it, and a list kept on the server would be shared between requests.

Toasts sent before `Toaster` has mounted aren't lost. They show once it's there.

sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Say what happened in a few words: "Changes saved", "Invitation sent".
- Offer "Undo" in the toast when the thing can be undone.
- Reuse an id for a message that repeats, so it doesn't stack up.

**Don't**

- Don't use a toast for an error in a form. Put the message next to the field.
- Don't send a toast for every item in a batch. Only three show at a time, so the last ones arrive long after the work is done. Send one that covers them all.
- Don't put a toast's only action somewhere people can't get to after it's gone.

pages.title: Toggle
pages.description: A button that stays pressed until it's pressed again, for turning one thing on and off.
pages.markdown: # Toggle A button that stays pressed until it's pressed again, for turning one thing on and off. Use a toggle for an option that's on or off and reads as a button: bold in an editor, a pinned item, a filter. For a setting in a list of settings, a [switch](page:components/switch) is the usual control. For several toggles that belong together, use a [toggle group](page:components/toggle-group). ```tsx import { Toggle } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return Show archived; } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Toggle } from "@nuvui/react"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `variant` | `"ghost" \| "outline"` | `"ghost"` | `"ghost"` has no edge until it's pressed, which suits a row of them in a toolbar. `"outline"` has one, for a toggle that stands alone. | | `size` | `"lg" \| "md" \| "sm"` | `"md"` | | These come from Radix. | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `pressed` | `boolean` | | Whether it's pressed, when you control it yourself. Use it with `onPressedChange`. | | `defaultPressed` | `boolean` | | Whether it starts pressed, when you don't control it. | | `onPressedChange` | `((pressed: boolean) => void)` | | Called with the new state when it's pressed or released. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | | Stops it from being focused or pressed. | Everything else is passed to the `

sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { Toggle } from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"ghost" \| "outline"` | `"ghost"` | `"ghost"` has no edge until it's pressed, which suits a row of them in a toolbar. `"outline"` has one, for a toggle that stands alone. |
| `size` | `"lg" \| "md" \| "sm"` | `"md"` |  |

These come from Radix.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pressed` | `boolean` |  | Whether it's pressed, when you control it yourself. Use it with `onPressedChange`. |
| `defaultPressed` | `boolean` |  | Whether it starts pressed, when you don't control it. |
| `onPressedChange` | `((pressed: boolean) => void)` |  | Called with the new state when it's pressed or released. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Stops it from being focused or pressed. |

Everything else is passed to the `<button>` Radix renders, including `ref`, `className` and `aria-label`.

sections.heading: With icons
sections.markdown:
## With icons A toggle that holds only an icon is square. It needs an `aria-label`, since there's no text to name it. ```tsx import { Toggle } from "@nuvui/react"; import type { ReactNode } from "react"; function Icon({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) { return ( ); } export default function Example() { return (
); } ```

sections.heading: Sizes
Why pressed is a solid fill
sections.markdown:
## Why pressed is a solid fill

A pressed toggle is filled with the primary color. A pale gray fill would be quieter, and `--color-muted` differs from the page by far less than the 3:1 that WCAG asks of something that shows a control's state. The primary color has at least 3:1 against the page in every theme, and its text color at least 4.5:1 against it.

Change it with `--nuv-toggle-on-bg` and `--nuv-toggle-on-fg` if your design calls for something else, and check the contrast when you do.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves focus to the toggle. Disabled ones are skipped. |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> or <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Presses or releases it. |

### What the component handles

- It renders a `<button>` with `aria-pressed`, so a screen reader says whether it's pressed. This part is Radix.
- Its `type` is `"button"`, so it doesn't submit a form around it.
- Where the browser forces its own colors, as Windows high contrast does, a pressed toggle takes the system's colors for something selected.
- Keyboard focus shows a 2 pixel ring in `--color-ring`. A mouse click doesn't.
- The color change is only animated when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion.

### What you need to handle

- Name what it turns on, and keep the name the same in both states. `aria-pressed` already says which state it's in, so a label that changes from "Mute" to "Unmute" says it twice and gets it wrong half the time.
- Give an icon-only toggle an `aria-label`.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on the toggle, or on anything around it.

```css
.editor {
  --nuv-toggle-radius: var(--radius-sm);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-toggle-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 2)` | Space between an icon and the label. |
| `--nuv-toggle-padding-inline` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 2.5)`, `calc(var(--spacing) * 1.5)`, `calc(var(--spacing) * 3.5)` | Padding left and right. Differs by size. |
| `--nuv-toggle-border` | `transparent`, `var(--color-border)` | Border color while not pressed. Only the outline variant shows one by default. |
| `--nuv-toggle-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius. |
| `--nuv-toggle-bg` | `transparent` | Background color while not pressed. |
| `--nuv-toggle-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Text color while not pressed. |
| `--nuv-toggle-font-size` | `var(--text-sm)`, `var(--text-base)` | Font size. Larger on the lg size. |
| `--nuv-toggle-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-sm)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-md)`, `max(var(--nuv-touch-size), var(--nuv-control-height-lg))`, `var(--nuv-control-height-lg)` | Minimum height, and minimum width. Differs by size and by whether the device is touch. |
| `--nuv-toggle-bg-hover` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background color while hovered and not pressed. |
| `--nuv-toggle-on-bg` | `var(--color-primary)` | Background and border color while pressed. Keep it at 3:1 against the page. |
| `--nuv-toggle-on-fg` | `var(--color-primary-foreground)` | Text color while pressed. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-toggle` | Every toggle. |
| `.nuv-toggle--lg` | size="lg" |
| `.nuv-toggle--md` | size="md" |
| `.nuv-toggle--outline` | variant="outline" |
| `.nuv-toggle--sm` | size="sm" |

A ghost toggle also has the class `nuv-toggle--ghost`. It has no rules of its own, because ghost is how every toggle starts. Radix sets `data-state` to `on` or `off`, and `data-disabled` when the toggle is disabled.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

Toggle is a client component. It carries `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files. You can render it from a server component, as the examples on this page do.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Use it for something that takes effect at once.
- Use the outline variant when a toggle stands alone, so it reads as a control before it's pressed.

**Don't**

- Don't use a toggle for an action, such as "Save". That's a [button](page:components/button).
- Don't swap the label when it's pressed.

pages.title: ToggleGroup
pages.description: A strip of toggles that share one value. One can be pressed at a time, or several.
pages.markdown:
# ToggleGroup

A strip of toggles that share one value. One can be pressed at a time, or several.

Use a toggle group to switch between a few views or modes, or to turn several related options on and off, where the choice takes effect at once. In a form that's saved with a button, a [radio group](page:components/radio-group) or [checkboxes](page:components/checkbox) say that better.

```tsx
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <ToggleGroup type="single" aria-label="View" defaultValue="list">
      <ToggleGroupItem value="list">List</ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="board">Board</ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="calendar">Calendar</ToggleGroupItem>
    </ToggleGroup>
  );
}
```

## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

## Import

```tsx
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS. Loaded one by one, a group needs `toggle.css` as well as `toggle-group.css`, because each of its buttons is a [toggle](page:components/toggle).

## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `ToggleGroup` | Holds the value and lays the buttons out. |
| `ToggleGroupItem` | One button. It takes its variant and size from the group. |

## Props

### ToggleGroup

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"ghost" \| "outline"` | `"outline"` | `"outline"` joins the buttons into one strip. `"ghost"` leaves a small gap between them and gives none an edge until it's pressed. |
| `size` | `"lg" \| "md" \| "sm"` | `"md"` | The size of every button in the group. |

These come from Radix.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` (required) | `"multiple" \| "single"` |  | `"single"` lets one button be pressed at a time. `"multiple"` lets any number be. It's required, and it decides what kind of value the group has. |
| `value` | `string \| string[]` |  | The pressed button, or buttons, when you control it yourself: a string for `"single"` and an array of strings for `"multiple"`. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| string[]` |  | The same, for what's pressed at first when you don't control it. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void) \| ((value: string[]) => void)` |  | Called with the new value. With `"single"`, it's an empty string when the pressed button is pressed again. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` |  | `"vertical"` stacks the buttons. It also decides which arrow keys move between them. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables every button. |
| `rovingFocus` | `boolean` |  | Whether the group is one tab stop that the arrow keys move inside. It's `true` by default. |
| `loop` | `boolean` |  | Whether the arrow keys wrap around from the last button to the first. It's `true` by default. |
| `dir` | `"ltr" \| "rtl"` |  | The reading direction. In `"rtl"` the left and right arrow keys swap. |

### ToggleGroupItem

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | What the group's value holds while this button is pressed. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Stops this button from being pressed. The arrow keys skip it. |

## Several at once

```tsx
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <ToggleGroup
      type="multiple"
      variant="ghost"
      aria-label="Text style"
      defaultValue={["bold"]}
    >
      <ToggleGroupItem value="bold">Bold</ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="italic">Italic</ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="underline">Underline</ToggleGroupItem>
    </ToggleGroup>
  );
}
```

`variant="ghost"` leaves a small gap between the buttons and gives none of them an edge. The default, `"outline"`, joins them into one strip.

## Always one pressed

With `type="single"`, pressing the pressed button again lets go of it, and the group has no value. For a view switcher that should always have one, ignore the empty value.

```tsx
"use client";

import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@nuvui/react";
import { useState } from "react";

export default function Example() {
  const [align, setAlign] = useState("left");

  return (
    <ToggleGroup
      type="single"
      aria-label="Alignment"
      value={align}
      // Radix sends an empty string when the pressed button is pressed
      // again. Ignoring it keeps one of them always picked.
      onValueChange={(value) => {
        if (value) setAlign(value);
      }}
    >
      <ToggleGroupItem value="left">Left</ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="center">Center</ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="right">Right</ToggleGroupItem>
    </ToggleGroup>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves focus into the group, to the pressed button or the first one, and out again. The group is one tab stop. |
| <kbd>→</kbd> and <kbd>←</kbd> | Move to the next or previous button, without pressing it. In a vertical group it's <kbd>↓</kbd> and <kbd>↑</kbd>. |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> | Move to the first or last button. |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> or <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Presses or releases the button that has focus. |

In a right-to-left group, <kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd> swap.

### What the component handles

Most of this is Radix. The library doesn't change it.

- With `type="single"`, the group has `role="radiogroup"` and each button `role="radio"` with `aria-checked`. With `type="multiple"`, the group has `role="toolbar"` and each button `aria-pressed`.
- The pressed button is filled with the primary color, which has at least 3:1 contrast with the page in every theme. [Toggle](page:components/toggle#why-pressed-is-a-solid-fill) has the reasoning.
- In a joined strip, the pressed button's edge is drawn over its neighbours', and the button with focus is drawn over both, so its ring isn't cut off.
- The joined corners follow the reading direction and the orientation.

### What you need to handle

- Name the group with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Give each icon-only button an `aria-label`.
- Unlike a radio group, the arrow keys only move focus here. A press is needed to change the value.

## CSS variables

The buttons read the [toggle's variables](page:components/toggle#css-variables). Set them on the group and every button in it follows. The group adds one of its own.

```css
.toolbar {
  --nuv-toggle-on-bg: var(--color-foreground);
  --nuv-toggle-on-fg: var(--color-background);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-toggle-group-gap` | `var(--spacing)` | Space between buttons in the ghost variant. |

## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-toggle-group` | ToggleGroup. |
| `.nuv-toggle-group--ghost` | variant="ghost" |
| `.nuv-toggle-group--horizontal` | orientation="horizontal", which is the default. |
| `.nuv-toggle-group--outline` | variant="outline" |
| `.nuv-toggle-group--vertical` | orientation="vertical" |
| `.nuv-toggle-group__item` | ToggleGroupItem. It has the toggle's classes too: `nuv-toggle` and the two for its variant and size. |

## Server components

The toggle group parts are client components. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files.

You can put a group together inside a server component, as the first example on this page does. It needs a client component of your own once you pass `onValueChange`, which is most real uses.

## Do and don't

**Do**

- Keep it to a handful of buttons with short labels. On a phone a long strip runs off the screen.
- Use it where the change shows straight away.

**Don't**

- Don't mix it up with [tabs](page:components/tabs). Tabs switch between panels of content, each with its own heading. A toggle group changes how one thing is shown.
- Don't use a toggle group for navigation between pages.

pages.title: Toolbar
pages.description: A row of buttons, links and toggles that the Tab key treats as one stop, with the arrow keys moving inside it.
pages.markdown:
# Toolbar

A row of buttons, links and toggles that the Tab key treats as one stop, with the arrow keys moving inside it.

Use a toolbar for a set of controls that act on the same thing: the formatting buttons of an editor, the tools of a drawing app, the actions above a table. What makes it a toolbar is the keyboard: one press of <kbd>Tab</kbd> gets past it, however many controls it holds.

Three controls or fewer don't need one. A plain row of [buttons](page:components/button) is simpler, and each button is then its own tab stop.

```tsx
import {
  Toolbar,
  ToolbarButton,
  ToolbarLink,
  ToolbarSeparator,
  ToolbarToggleGroup,
  ToolbarToggleItem,
} from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Toolbar aria-label="Formatting">
      <ToolbarToggleGroup type="multiple" aria-label="Text style">
        <ToolbarToggleItem value="bold">Bold</ToolbarToggleItem>
        <ToolbarToggleItem value="italic">Italic</ToolbarToggleItem>
      </ToolbarToggleGroup>
      <ToolbarSeparator />
      <ToolbarToggleGroup
        type="single"
        defaultValue="left"
        aria-label="Alignment"
      >
        <ToolbarToggleItem value="left">Left</ToolbarToggleItem>
        <ToolbarToggleItem value="center">Center</ToolbarToggleItem>
        <ToolbarToggleItem value="right">Right</ToolbarToggleItem>
      </ToolbarToggleGroup>
      <ToolbarSeparator />
      <ToolbarLink href="#formatting-help">Help</ToolbarLink>
      <ToolbarButton>Share</ToolbarButton>
    </Toolbar>
  );
}
```

## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Toolbar,
  ToolbarButton,
  ToolbarLink,
  ToolbarSeparator,
  ToolbarToggleGroup,
  ToolbarToggleItem,
} from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Toolbar` | The row. It has `role="toolbar"`. |
| `ToolbarButton` | A button. |
| `ToolbarLink` | A link, which the arrow keys reach like the buttons. |
| `ToolbarToggleGroup` | A group of buttons that stay pressed. |
| `ToolbarToggleItem` | One of those buttons. |
| `ToolbarSeparator` | A line between two groups. |

## Props

All of these come from Radix.

### Toolbar

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` |  | `"horizontal"` or `"vertical"`. It sets the layout and which arrow keys move focus. Horizontal by default. |
| `loop` | `boolean` |  | Whether the arrow keys go round from the last control to the first. On by default. |
| `dir` | `"ltr" \| "rtl"` |  | The reading direction, which decides which of the left and right arrows goes forward. It's taken from `DirectionProvider` when not set. |

### ToolbarToggleGroup

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` (required) | `"multiple" \| "single"` |  | `"single"` lets one button be pressed at a time. `"multiple"` lets any number. |
| `value` | `string \| string[]` |  | The pressed button's value, or an array of them for `"multiple"`, when you control it yourself. Use it with `onValueChange`. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| string[]` |  | What's pressed to begin with, when you don't control it. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void) \| ((value: string[]) => void)` |  | Called with the new value when a button is pressed. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables every button in the group. |

### ToolbarToggleItem

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | What this button stands for in the group's value. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Stops it from being focused or pressed. |

`ToolbarButton`, `ToolbarLink` and `ToolbarSeparator` take what their elements take. `ToolbarButton` also takes `asChild`, which is how [other components join the toolbar](#a-menu-in-a-toolbar).

## Icons

A toolbar of icons needs a name on each control, with `aria-label`. A control holding only an icon comes out square.

```tsx
import {
  Toolbar,
  ToolbarButton,
  ToolbarSeparator,
  ToolbarToggleGroup,
  ToolbarToggleItem,
} from "@nuvui/react";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";

function Icon({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <svg
      aria-hidden="true"
      viewBox="0 0 16 16"
      width="16"
      height="16"
      fill="none"
      stroke="currentColor"
      strokeWidth="1.5"
      strokeLinecap="round"
      strokeLinejoin="round"
    >
      {children}
    </svg>
  );
}

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Toolbar aria-label="Formatting">
      <ToolbarButton aria-label="Undo">
        <Icon>
          <path d="M3 6h7a3.5 3.5 0 010 7H6M3 6l3-3M3 6l3 3" />
        </Icon>
      </ToolbarButton>
      <ToolbarButton aria-label="Redo" disabled>
        <Icon>
          <path d="M13 6H6a3.5 3.5 0 000 7h4M13 6l-3-3M13 6l-3 3" />
        </Icon>
      </ToolbarButton>
      <ToolbarSeparator />
      <ToolbarToggleGroup type="multiple" aria-label="Text style">
        <ToolbarToggleItem value="bold" aria-label="Bold">
          <Icon>
            <path d="M4.5 3h4a2.5 2.5 0 010 5h-4zm0 5h4.5a2.5 2.5 0 010 5H4.5z" />
          </Icon>
        </ToolbarToggleItem>
        <ToolbarToggleItem value="italic" aria-label="Italic">
          <Icon>
            <path d="M6.5 3h5M4.5 13h5M9.5 3l-3 10" />
          </Icon>
        </ToolbarToggleItem>
        <ToolbarToggleItem value="underline" aria-label="Underline">
          <Icon>
            <path d="M4.5 3v4.5a3.5 3.5 0 007 0V3M4 13.5h8" />
          </Icon>
        </ToolbarToggleItem>
      </ToolbarToggleGroup>
    </Toolbar>
  );
}
```

A [tooltip](page:components/tooltip) on each one helps people who see the icon and don't know what it means. `aria-label` doesn't do that: it's for screen readers only.

## A menu in a toolbar

Any button can take part in the toolbar's arrow-key order. Pass `asChild` to `ToolbarButton` and put the other component's trigger inside.

```tsx
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
  Toolbar,
  ToolbarButton,
  ToolbarSeparator,
} from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Toolbar aria-label="Document">
      <ToolbarButton>Save</ToolbarButton>
      <ToolbarButton>Print</ToolbarButton>
      <ToolbarSeparator />
      <DropdownMenu>
        <ToolbarButton asChild>
          <DropdownMenuTrigger>Export</DropdownMenuTrigger>
        </ToolbarButton>
        <DropdownMenuContent>
          <DropdownMenuItem>PDF</DropdownMenuItem>
          <DropdownMenuItem>Word document</DropdownMenuItem>
          <DropdownMenuItem>Plain text</DropdownMenuItem>
        </DropdownMenuContent>
      </DropdownMenu>
    </Toolbar>
  );
}
```

## Vertical

`orientation="vertical"` stacks the controls, turns the separators on their side, and moves focus with the up and down arrows.

```tsx
import { Toolbar, ToolbarButton, ToolbarSeparator } from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Toolbar orientation="vertical" aria-label="Drawing tools">
      <ToolbarButton>Select</ToolbarButton>
      <ToolbarButton>Pen</ToolbarButton>
      <ToolbarButton>Shape</ToolbarButton>
      <ToolbarSeparator />
      <ToolbarButton>Erase</ToolbarButton>
    </Toolbar>
  );
}
```

## On small screens

A toolbar that runs out of room wraps onto another row, so nothing is pushed off the screen. The arrow keys still go through the controls in order.

On a touch screen every control is at least 44 pixels tall and wide. With a mouse or trackpad they're 32 pixels at the default [density](page:theming#density), 28 at compact and 36 at comfortable. A toolbar is a dense row by nature, so it takes the smallest of the three control heights.

## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves focus into the toolbar, to the control that had focus last time, and out again with the next press. |
| <kbd>→</kbd> and <kbd>←</kbd> | Move to the next and the previous control. In a vertical toolbar it's <kbd>↓</kbd> and <kbd>↑</kbd>. In a right-to-left toolbar the left arrow goes forward. |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> | Move to the first and the last control. |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> or <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Press the control that has focus. |

Disabled controls are skipped.

### What the component handles

- `role="toolbar"` and `aria-orientation`, and the keys above. This part is Radix.
- A toggle group of type `single` is a radio group, and each button a radio button with `aria-checked`. One of type `multiple` is a plain group, and each button has `aria-pressed`.
- The separator has `role="separator"`, so a screen reader says where one group ends.
- A pressed toggle is filled with the primary color, which has at least 3:1 against the toolbar in every theme. Where the browser forces its own colors, it takes the system's colors for something selected.
- Keyboard focus shows a 2 pixel ring in `--color-ring`.

### What you need to handle

- **Name the toolbar** with `aria-label`: "Formatting", "Drawing tools". Name each toggle group too.
- **Give an icon-only control an `aria-label`.**
- **Don't put a text field in a toolbar.** The arrow keys move the caret inside a field, so they can't also move to the next control, and people get stuck. A field belongs next to the toolbar. The [ARIA guide](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/) has more on this.
- Keep a toggle's name the same in both states. `aria-pressed` says which state it's in.

## CSS variables

Set any of these on `Toolbar`, or on anything around it.

```css
.editor {
  --nuv-toolbar-border: transparent;
  --nuv-toolbar-padding: 0;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-toolbar-gap` | `var(--spacing)` | Space between the controls. |
| `--nuv-toolbar-padding` | `var(--spacing)` | Padding inside the toolbar. |
| `--nuv-toolbar-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of the toolbar's edge and of the separators. |
| `--nuv-toolbar-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of the toolbar. |
| `--nuv-toolbar-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background color of the toolbar. |
| `--nuv-toolbar-item-padding-inline` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 2.5)` | Padding left and right in a control. |
| `--nuv-toolbar-item-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius of a control. |
| `--nuv-toolbar-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Text color of the controls. |
| `--nuv-toolbar-item-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `var(--nuv-control-height-sm)` | Smallest height, and smallest width, of a control. Differs by whether the device is touch. |
| `--nuv-toolbar-item-hover-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background color of a control under the pointer. |
| `--nuv-toolbar-on-bg` | `var(--color-primary)` | Background color of a pressed toggle. Keep it at 3:1 against the toolbar. |
| `--nuv-toolbar-on-fg` | `var(--color-primary-foreground)` | Text color of a pressed toggle. |

## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-toolbar` | Toolbar. |
| `.nuv-toolbar__button` | ToolbarButton. |
| `.nuv-toolbar__link` | ToolbarLink. |
| `.nuv-toolbar__separator` | ToolbarSeparator. |
| `.nuv-toolbar__toggle-group` | ToolbarToggleGroup. |
| `.nuv-toolbar__toggle-item` | ToolbarToggleItem. |

Radix sets `data-orientation` on the toolbar, the groups and the separators, `data-state` to `on` or `off` on a toggle, and `data-disabled` on a disabled control.

## Server components

The toolbar parts are client components. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files. You can render them from a server component, as the examples on this page do.

## Do and don't

**Do**

- Group controls that belong together, with a separator between groups.
- Put the controls people use most at the start, where focus lands.

**Don't**

- Don't use a toolbar for a site's navigation. That's a [navigation menu](page:components/navigation-menu), or a plain list of links.
- Don't disable a control without saying why somewhere. A grayed-out button with no explanation is a dead end.

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Toolbar` | The row. It has `role="toolbar"`. |
| `ToolbarButton` | A button. |
| `ToolbarLink` | A link, which the arrow keys reach like the buttons. |

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

All of these come from Radix.

### Toolbar

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` |  | `"horizontal"` or `"vertical"`. It sets the layout and which arrow keys move focus. Horizontal by default. |
| `loop` | `boolean` |  | Whether the arrow keys go round from the last control to the first. On by default. |
| `dir` | `"ltr" \| "rtl"` |  | The reading direction, which decides which of the left and right arrows goes forward. It's taken from `DirectionProvider` when not set. |

### ToolbarToggleGroup

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` (required) | `"multiple" \| "single"` |  | `"single"` lets one button be pressed at a time. `"multiple"` lets any number. |
| `value` | `string \| string[]` |  | The pressed button's value, or an array of them for `"multiple"`, when you control it yourself. Use it with `onValueChange`. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| string[]` |  | What's pressed to begin with, when you don't control it. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void) \| ((value: string[]) => void)` |  | Called with the new value when a button is pressed. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables every button in the group. |

### ToolbarToggleItem

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | What this button stands for in the group's value. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Stops it from being focused or pressed. |

`ToolbarButton`, `ToolbarLink` and `ToolbarSeparator` take what their elements take. `ToolbarButton` also takes `asChild`, which is how [other components join the toolbar](#a-menu-in-a-toolbar).

sections.heading: Icons
sections.markdown:
## Icons

A toolbar of icons needs a name on each control, with `aria-label`. A control holding only an icon comes out square.

```tsx
import {
  Toolbar,
  ToolbarButton,
  ToolbarSeparator,
  ToolbarToggleGroup,
  ToolbarToggleItem,
} from "@nuvui/react";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";

function Icon({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <svg
      aria-hidden="true"
      viewBox="0 0 16 16"
      width="16"
      height="16"
      fill="none"
      stroke="currentColor"
      strokeWidth="1.5"
      strokeLinecap="round"
      strokeLinejoin="round"
    >
      {children}
    </svg>
  );
}

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Toolbar aria-label="Formatting">
      <ToolbarButton aria-label="Undo">
        <Icon>
          <path d="M3 6h7a3.5 3.5 0 010 7H6M3 6l3-3M3 6l3 3" />
        </Icon>
      </ToolbarButton>
      <ToolbarButton aria-label="Redo" disabled>
        <Icon>
          <path d="M13 6H6a3.5 3.5 0 000 7h4M13 6l-3-3M13 6l-3 3" />
        </Icon>
      </ToolbarButton>
      <ToolbarSeparator />
      <ToolbarToggleGroup type="multiple" aria-label="Text style">
        <ToolbarToggleItem value="bold" aria-label="Bold">
          <Icon>
            <path d="M4.5 3h4a2.5 2.5 0 010 5h-4zm0 5h4.5a2.5 2.5 0 010 5H4.5z" />
          </Icon>
        </ToolbarToggleItem>
        <ToolbarToggleItem value="italic" aria-label="Italic">
          <Icon>
            <path d="M6.5 3h5M4.5 13h5M9.5 3l-3 10" />
          </Icon>
        </ToolbarToggleItem>
        <ToolbarToggleItem value="underline" aria-label="Underline">
          <Icon>
            <path d="M4.5 3v4.5a3.5 3.5 0 007 0V3M4 13.5h8" />
          </Icon>
        </ToolbarToggleItem>
      </ToolbarToggleGroup>
    </Toolbar>
  );
}
```

A [tooltip](page:components/tooltip) on each one helps people who see the icon and don't know what it means. `aria-label` doesn't do that: it's for screen readers only.

pages.title: Tooltip
pages.description: A short line of text that appears when a control is hovered or focused. It doesn't appear on touch screens.
pages.markdown:
# Tooltip

A short line of text that appears when a control is hovered or focused. It doesn't appear on touch screens.

Use a tooltip to add a few words to a control that already makes sense without them: what a button will do, or its keyboard shortcut.

Tooltips don't show on touch screens, where there's no hover. Never put anything in one that people need.

```tsx
import { Button, Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipTrigger } from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Tooltip>
      <TooltipTrigger asChild>
        <Button intent="secondary">Archive</Button>
      </TooltipTrigger>
      <TooltipContent>
        Takes the project out of your list. You can bring it back later.
      </TooltipContent>
    </Tooltip>
  );
}
```

## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Tooltip,
  TooltipContent,
  TooltipProvider,
  TooltipTrigger,
} from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Tooltip` | Holds the open state for one tooltip. Renders nothing itself. |
| `TooltipTrigger` | The control the tooltip belongs to. Wrap your own button or link with `asChild`. |
| `TooltipContent` | The bubble with the text. |
| `TooltipProvider` | Optional. Put it around a group of tooltips so they share their timing. |

These are separate exports, not properties of `Tooltip`. `Tooltip.Content` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component.

## Props

### TooltipContent

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `showArrow` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether to draw the small arrow that points at the trigger. |
| `sideOffset` | `number` | `4` | The gap between the trigger and the tooltip, in pixels. With the arrow shown, it's measured from the arrow's tip. |
| `collisionPadding` | `number \| Partial<Record<"bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top", number>>` | `8` | How close the tooltip may get to the edge of the screen, in pixels. |
| `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the tooltip is rendered into. Set this when the tooltip should pick up a `data-theme` from a section of the page. |

These come from Radix and are the ones you're most likely to set:

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `side` | `"bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top"` |  | The side of the trigger the tooltip opens on. It's `"top"` unless you say otherwise, and it flips to the opposite side when there isn't room. |
| `align` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start"` |  | How the tooltip lines up with the trigger along that side. It's `"center"` unless you say otherwise. |

### Tooltip

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `delayDuration` | `number` |  | How long the pointer has to rest on the trigger before the tooltip shows, in milliseconds. Keyboard focus doesn't wait. |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Whether it's showing, when you control it yourself. Use it with `onOpenChange`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` |  | Whether it starts out showing, when you don't control it. |
| `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean) => void)` |  | Called when it shows or hides. |
| `disableHoverableContent` | `boolean` |  | With `true`, the tooltip hides as soon as the pointer leaves the trigger, even if it's heading for the tooltip. |

### TooltipProvider

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `delayDuration` | `number` |  | The delay for every tooltip inside, in milliseconds, unless one sets its own. |
| `skipDelayDuration` | `number` |  | After one tooltip hides, how long the next one can show without waiting, in milliseconds. |
| `disableHoverableContent` | `boolean` |  | The same as on `Tooltip`, for every tooltip inside. |

## Several tooltips

On its own, each tooltip waits out its delay. Put a group inside one `TooltipProvider` and only the first one waits. Moving on to the next within a moment shows it at once, which is what you want in a toolbar.

```tsx
import {
  Button,
  Tooltip,
  TooltipContent,
  TooltipProvider,
  TooltipTrigger,
} from "@nuvui/react";

const tools = [
  { name: "Bold", keys: "Ctrl+B", glyph: "B", weight: 700 },
  { name: "Italic", keys: "Ctrl+I", glyph: "I", weight: 400 },
  { name: "Underline", keys: "Ctrl+U", glyph: "U", weight: 400 },
];

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <TooltipProvider>
      {tools.map((tool) => (
        <Tooltip key={tool.name}>
          <TooltipTrigger asChild>
            <Button
              intent="secondary"
              aria-label={tool.name}
              style={{ fontWeight: tool.weight }}
            >
              {tool.glyph}
            </Button>
          </TooltipTrigger>
          <TooltipContent>{tool.keys}</TooltipContent>
        </Tooltip>
      ))}
    </TooltipProvider>
  );
}
```

Outside a provider, a tooltip still works. It brings its own.

## Sides

```tsx
import {
  Button,
  Tooltip,
  TooltipContent,
  TooltipProvider,
  TooltipTrigger,
} from "@nuvui/react";

const sides = ["top", "right", "bottom", "left"] as const;

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <TooltipProvider>
      {sides.map((side) => (
        <Tooltip key={side}>
          <TooltipTrigger asChild>
            <Button intent="secondary">{side}</Button>
          </TooltipTrigger>
          <TooltipContent side={side}>Opens on the {side}</TooltipContent>
        </Tooltip>
      ))}
    </TooltipProvider>
  );
}
```

## On touch screens

A tap on the trigger doesn't open the tooltip. The trigger just does what it does. That's how Radix handles touch, and this library doesn't change it.

So treat a tooltip as extra. The control needs a visible label or an `aria-label` that makes sense alone, and anything people need to know has to be on the page.

## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves focus to the trigger, which shows the tooltip at once. Moving on hides it. |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Hides the tooltip. Focus stays on the trigger. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> | Presses the trigger, and hides the tooltip. |

### What the component handles

- While it's showing, the tooltip's text is tied to the trigger with `aria-describedby`, so a screen reader reads it after the control's name. This part is Radix.
- It shows on keyboard focus as well as on hover.
- It stays while the pointer moves from the trigger onto the tooltip itself, and <kbd>Esc</kbd> hides it without moving the pointer. WCAG 1.4.13 asks for both.
- Its colors are the page's text and background colors swapped, so the contrast is the same as the page's body text in light and dark.
- It never runs off the screen. Long text wraps at 16rem.
- Where the browser forces its own colors, as Windows high contrast does, the bubble loses its background. It has an outline there so it still reads as separate from the page.
- It only fades in when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion.

### What you need to handle

- Put it on something that can take focus, such as a button or a link. With `asChild`, that's the element you pass in. A tooltip on plain text can't be reached by keyboard.
- A disabled `Button` ignores the pointer and can't take focus, so a tooltip on it never shows. If you need to explain why something is unavailable, say so on the page.
- An icon-only button still needs its own name through `aria-label`. The tooltip is a description, read after the name. When both would say the same words, use the tooltip for something extra, as the toolbar example does with shortcuts.
- Keep links and buttons out of the tooltip. People can't get to them.

## CSS variables

Tooltips render at the end of `<body>`, so set these on `:root` or `body`, or straight on `TooltipContent` with `style` or a class.

```css
:root {
  --nuv-tooltip-radius: var(--radius-sm);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-tooltip-width` | `16rem` | The widest the tooltip gets before its text wraps. |
| `--nuv-tooltip-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius. |
| `--nuv-tooltip-bg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Background color of the bubble and the arrow. The page's text color unless you set it. |
| `--nuv-tooltip-fg` | `var(--color-background)` | Text color. The page's background color unless you set it. |

## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-tooltip` | TooltipContent. |
| `.nuv-tooltip__arrow` | The arrow that points at the trigger. |

Radix sets `data-state` on the bubble to `delayed-open` after a hover, `instant-open` after keyboard focus or when the delay was skipped, and `closed` on the way out. Only `delayed-open` is animated. It also sets `data-side` for where the bubble ended up.

## Server components

The tooltip parts are client components. They carry `"use client"`, and the build checks that the directive is still there in the published files.

You can put a tooltip together inside a server component, as the examples on this page do.

## Do and don't

**Do**

- Keep it to a few words. If it needs a second sentence, it belongs on the page.
- Use it for keyboard shortcuts, and for naming what an icon button does.
- Wrap a toolbar's tooltips in one `TooltipProvider`.

**Don't**

- Don't put anything essential in a tooltip. On a phone nobody will see it.
- Don't repeat the button's visible label in it.
- Don't put a tooltip on something that already opens a menu or a popover on click. The two fight for the same spot.

sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Tooltip` | Holds the open state for one tooltip. Renders nothing itself. |
| `TooltipTrigger` | The control the tooltip belongs to. Wrap your own button or link with `asChild`. |
| `TooltipContent` | The bubble with the text. |
| `TooltipProvider` | Optional. Put it around a group of tooltips so they share their timing. |

These are separate exports, not properties of `Tooltip`. `Tooltip.Content` isn't available, because property access on a client component doesn't work from a server component.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

### TooltipContent

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `showArrow` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether to draw the small arrow that points at the trigger. |
| `sideOffset` | `number` | `4` | The gap between the trigger and the tooltip, in pixels. With the arrow shown, it's measured from the arrow's tip. |
| `collisionPadding` | `number \| Partial<Record<"bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top", number>>` | `8` | How close the tooltip may get to the edge of the screen, in pixels. |
| `container` | `DocumentFragment \| Element \| null` | `document.body` | The element the tooltip is rendered into. Set this when the tooltip should pick up a `data-theme` from a section of the page. |

These come from Radix and are the ones you're most likely to set:

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `side` | `"bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "top"` |  | The side of the trigger the tooltip opens on. It's `"top"` unless you say otherwise, and it flips to the opposite side when there isn't room. |
| `align` | `"center" \| "end" \| "start"` |  | How the tooltip lines up with the trigger along that side. It's `"center"` unless you say otherwise. |

### Tooltip

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `delayDuration` | `number` |  | How long the pointer has to rest on the trigger before the tooltip shows, in milliseconds. Keyboard focus doesn't wait. |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Whether it's showing, when you control it yourself. Use it with `onOpenChange`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` |  | Whether it starts out showing, when you don't control it. |
| `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean) => void)` |  | Called when it shows or hides. |
| `disableHoverableContent` | `boolean` |  | With `true`, the tooltip hides as soon as the pointer leaves the trigger, even if it's heading for the tooltip. |

### TooltipProvider

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `delayDuration` | `number` |  | The delay for every tooltip inside, in milliseconds, unless one sets its own. |
| `skipDelayDuration` | `number` |  | After one tooltip hides, how long the next one can show without waiting, in milliseconds. |
| `disableHoverableContent` | `boolean` |  | The same as on `Tooltip`, for every tooltip inside. |

sections.heading: Several tooltips
Sides
On touch screens
sections.markdown:
## On touch screens

A tap on the trigger doesn't open the tooltip. The trigger just does what it does. That's how Radix handles touch, and this library doesn't change it.

So treat a tooltip as extra. The control needs a visible label or an `aria-label` that makes sense alone, and anything people need to know has to be on the page.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Moves focus to the trigger, which shows the tooltip at once. Moving on hides it. |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Hides the tooltip. Focus stays on the trigger. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> | Presses the trigger, and hides the tooltip. |

### What the component handles

- While it's showing, the tooltip's text is tied to the trigger with `aria-describedby`, so a screen reader reads it after the control's name. This part is Radix.
- It shows on keyboard focus as well as on hover.
- It stays while the pointer moves from the trigger onto the tooltip itself, and <kbd>Esc</kbd> hides it without moving the pointer. WCAG 1.4.13 asks for both.
- Its colors are the page's text and background colors swapped, so the contrast is the same as the page's body text in light and dark.
- It never runs off the screen. Long text wraps at 16rem.
- Where the browser forces its own colors, as Windows high contrast does, the bubble loses its background. It has an outline there so it still reads as separate from the page.
- It only fades in when the visitor hasn't asked for reduced motion.

### What you need to handle

- Put it on something that can take focus, such as a button or a link. With `asChild`, that's the element you pass in. A tooltip on plain text can't be reached by keyboard.
- A disabled `Button` ignores the pointer and can't take focus, so a tooltip on it never shows. If you need to explain why something is unavailable, say so on the page.
- An icon-only button still needs its own name through `aria-label`. The tooltip is a description, read after the name. When both would say the same words, use the tooltip for something extra, as the toolbar example does with shortcuts.
- Keep links and buttons out of the tooltip. People can't get to them.

| `--nuv-tooltip-width` | `16rem` | The widest the tooltip gets before its text wraps. |
| `--nuv-tooltip-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius. |
| `--nuv-tooltip-bg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Background color of the bubble and the arrow. The page's text color unless you set it. |
| `--nuv-tooltip-fg` | `var(--color-background)` | Text color. The page's background color unless you set it. |

pages.title: Tree
pages.description: Rows that open to show more rows, moved through with the arrow keys, with one or many of them selected.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { Tree, TreeItem } from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Tree` | The tree. It keeps which rows are open and which are selected. |
| `TreeItem` | A row. Put `TreeItem`s inside it for the rows under it. |

A row with rows inside it can be opened. A row without can't, and has no chevron. Nothing else says which is which.

sections.heading: Selecting one row
Selecting several
Opening rows yourself
Moving rows
A label that isn't plain text
sections.markdown:
## A label that isn't plain text

`label` takes anything: an icon and a name, a name and a count. Typing a letter goes to the next row whose label starts with it. When the label's text doesn't start with the row's name, say what the name is with `textValue`.

```tsx
<TreeItem
  value="inbox"
  textValue="Inbox"
  label={
    <>
      <Badge>12</Badge> Inbox
    </>
  }
/>
```

Keep buttons and links out of a label. A row is one thing to press, and a screen reader in a tree reads rows, not what's inside them.

sections.heading: Tree props
sections.markdown:
## Tree props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selectionMode` | `"multiple" \| "none" \| "single"` | `"none"` | Whether rows can be selected, and how many. With `"multiple"`, a press adds a row to the selection or takes it out, and Shift selects a run of them. |
| `value` | `string[]` |  | The selected rows' values, when you control them. |
| `defaultValue` | `string[]` |  | The rows selected at first, when you don't. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string[]) => void)` |  | Called with every selected row's value when the selection changes. |
| `expanded` | `string[]` |  | The open rows' values, when you control them. |
| `defaultExpanded` | `string[]` |  | The rows open at first, when you don't. |
| `onExpandedChange` | `((expanded: string[]) => void)` |  | Called with every open row's value when a row opens or closes. |
| `onMove` | `((move: TreeMove) => void)` |  | Called when rows are moved, by dragging them or with Alt and an arrow key. Giving it is what lets rows be moved. The tree doesn't move them: change your data to match, and draw the rows again. |
| `canDrop` | `((move: TreeMove) => boolean)` |  | Whether rows can go to a place. Return `false` and it isn't offered: a drag shows no mark there, and the keys pass it by. A row can never go inside itself or inside a disabled row. |
| `getMoveText` | `((move: TreeMove) => string)` | `"Moved Budget into Reports", and the like` | What a screen reader is told when rows have moved. |

It also takes what a `ul` takes, including `ref` and `className`. `TreeMove`, the type of a move, is exported too.

sections.heading: TreeItem props
sections.markdown:
## TreeItem props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | What the row is known by in `value` and `expanded`. No two the same. |
| `label` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | What the row shows: its name, and an icon if you like. |
| `textValue` | `string` |  | The row's name as plain text, which typing a letter looks for. Needed when the label doesn't start with it, as when it starts with a count. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | A row that can't be selected, opened or closed. The arrow keys still stop at it, so a screen reader can read it. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | The rows inside this one: more `TreeItem`s. With any, the row opens. |

It also takes what an `li` takes, including `ref` and `className`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

It follows the [tree view pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/treeview/) of the ARIA Authoring Practices.

### Keyboard

The tree is one stop for Tab. Inside it:

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Down, Up | Moves to the next or the previous row that's shown. |
| Right | Opens a closed row. On an open one, moves to its first row. |
| Left | Closes an open row. On a closed one or one that doesn't open, moves to the row it's inside. |
| Home, End | Moves to the first or the last row that's shown. |
| Enter | Opens or closes the row, and selects it when rows can be selected. |
| Space | Selects the row, or with several, adds it or takes it out. With no selection, opens or closes it. |
| A letter | Moves to the next row that starts with it. Letters typed quickly make a word. |
| `*` | Opens every row beside this one. |
| Shift and Down or Up | With several: moves, and selects the row it arrives at. |
| Ctrl or Command and A | With several: selects every row that's shown. |
| Alt and Down or Up | With `onMove`: moves the row to the next place it can go, down or up. Every place is on the way: into an open row, out of its end, and inside a row that's closed or has nothing in it. |

In a right-to-left page Right and Left change places, as the tree does.

### What the component handles

- The roles: `tree`, `treeitem`, and `group` for the rows inside a row. A screen reader says how deep a row is and how many are beside it from where it is in the lists.
- `aria-expanded` on a row that opens, and `aria-selected` on every row when rows can be selected.
- A row's name is its own label, not that and every row inside it.
- Tab stops at the row focus was last on. If that row goes, because its parent was closed or the data changed, Tab stops at the first row.
- A selected row differs by more than its background: a bar at its start and heavier text. The bar is a border, which is still drawn where the browser forces its own colors.
- A disabled row can still be reached with the arrow keys, so a screen reader can read it. It can't be selected, opened, closed or moved.
- A row that can be moved says so with `aria-keyshortcuts`. After a move, focus stays on the row, and a screen reader is told where it went: "Moved Forms into Reference". The words are in a `status` beside the tree, which is there only with `onMove`.
- Where a drag would put the rows is a line or a ring, not a change of color alone, and both are still drawn where the browser forces its own colors.

### What you need to handle

- Name the tree with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Give every row a `value` no other row has.
- Selecting a row does nothing by itself. Show the file, or the team, from `onValueChange`.
- Offer a way to move a row with a press and no drag, such as a "Move to" menu beside the tree. Someone who uses a pointer and can't drag has neither the drag nor the keys, and WCAG's 2.5.7 asks for it.
- In another language, give the words said after a move with `getMoveText`.
- Say somewhere near the tree that rows can be moved. Nothing about a row shows it.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

A row is 44 pixels tall with a finger and 32 with a mouse. With `onMove`, a finger held on a row for a moment picks it up. A finger that moves first scrolls, as it does anywhere. A long label is cut short, so the tree is as wide as you make it. A deep tree in a narrow space runs out of room for its labels: put it in a [scroll area](page:components/scroll-area), or make `--nuv-tree-indent` smaller.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on the `Tree`, or on anything around it.

```css
.files {
  --nuv-tree-indent: 1.5rem;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-tree-gap` | `1px` | Space between rows. |
| `--nuv-tree-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of the labels. |
| `--nuv-tree-row-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `calc(var(--spacing) * 8)` | Least height of a row. Taller by default with a finger than with a mouse. |
| `--nuv-tree-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius of a row. |
| `--nuv-tree-hover-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of the row under the pointer. |
| `--nuv-tree-selected-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of a selected row. |
| `--nuv-tree-selected-line-width` | `2px` | Thickness of the bar at the start of a selected row. |
| `--nuv-tree-selected-line` | `var(--color-primary)` | Color of that bar. Keep it at 3:1 against the row. |
| `--nuv-tree-dragging-opacity` | `var(--nuv-disabled-opacity)` | How faded a row is while it's being dragged. |
| `--nuv-tree-drop-line-width` | `2px` | Thickness of that line. |
| `--nuv-tree-drop-line` | `var(--color-primary)` | Color of the line, or the ring, where dragged rows would go. Keep it at 3:1 against the page. |
| `--nuv-tree-chevron` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the chevron. |
| `--nuv-tree-indent` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 4)` | How far in the rows inside a row are set. |
| `--nuv-tree-line` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of the line down the side of the rows inside a row. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-tree` | Tree |
| `.nuv-tree__chevron` | The chevron, or its empty place in a row that doesn't open. |
| `.nuv-tree__group` | The list of rows inside a row. |
| `.nuv-tree__item` | TreeItem: the row and the rows inside it. |
| `.nuv-tree__label` | The label. |
| `.nuv-tree__row` | The row itself, which is what's pressed. |
| `.nuv-tree__status` | What a screen reader is told after a move. Beside the tree, and drawn for nobody. |

An open row has `aria-expanded="true"`, a selected one `aria-selected="true"` and a disabled one `aria-disabled="true"`. During a drag the tree and each row being dragged have `data-dragging`, and the row they'd go to has `data-drop`, which is `before`, `after` or `inside`.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

Tree starts with `"use client"`: it keeps which rows are open. You can render it from a server component with rows written there, as long as you leave `onValueChange`, `onExpandedChange` and `onMove` out, since a function can't be passed from the server.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Open the rows the reader most likely wants, with `defaultExpanded`.
- Keep labels short. A path is already said by where the row is.

**Don't**

- Don't use a tree for a list with one level. That's a list.
- Don't put buttons inside a row. Put what can be done to the selection beside the tree, or in an [action bar](page:components/action-bar).
- Don't nest deeper than people can follow. Past four or five levels, think about a search.

pages.title: Trend
pages.description: Which way a number moved and by how much, as an arrow, an amount and a color, with the direction in words for a screen reader.
pages.markdown:
# Trend

Which way a number moved and by how much, as an arrow, an amount and a color, with the direction in words for a screen reader.

Use a trend next to a figure to say how it compares with the one before: revenue against last month, open tickets against last week. It's text, not a control.

```tsx
import { Trend } from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <>
      <Trend value={0.125} />
      <Trend value={-0.04} />
      <Trend value={0} />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/react
```

## Import

```tsx
import { Trend } from "@nuvui/react";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/react/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app. [Getting started](page:index) covers that, and how to load only this component's CSS.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (required) | `number` |  | The change, as a ratio: 0.12 is a rise of 12%. Its sign says which way the arrow points, and zero is no change. |
| `good` | `"down" \| "up"` | `"up"` | Which way is the good news. A rise is, for revenue. A fall is, for costs and for errors: pass `"down"`. It only chooses the color. |
| `variant` | `"outline" \| "plain"` | `"plain"` | `"outline"` puts an edge around it, in the same color, for a trend that stands by itself. |
| `format` | `FormatNumberOptions` |  | How the amount is written, when you don't write it yourself as children. A percentage with at most one decimal unless you say otherwise. |
| `upLabel` | `string` | `"Up"` | What a screen reader says before the amount of a rise. The arrow is a picture, and the color can't be heard. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |
| `downLabel` | `string` | `"Down"` | What a screen reader says before the amount of a fall. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |
| `flatLabel` | `string` | `"No change"` | What a screen reader says when the value is zero, in place of the amount. Translate it with the rest of your interface. |

Everything else is passed to the `<span>`, including `ref` and `className`.

## The value

`value` is a ratio, so `0.125` is written as 12.5%. Its sign chooses the arrow: above zero points up, below zero points down, and zero is a level line.

The amount is written without its sign. The arrow shows the direction, and a screen reader hears it in words, so "Down 4%" isn't followed by a minus that would be read as well.

## When down is good

Green for a rise and red for a fall is right for revenue and wrong for costs. `good="down"` swaps the two colors and leaves the arrows as they are.

```tsx
import { Trend } from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <dl
      style={{
        display: "grid",
        gridTemplateColumns: "auto auto",
        gap: "0.5rem 2rem",
        margin: 0,
      }}
    >
      <dt>Revenue</dt>
      <dd style={{ margin: 0 }}>
        <Trend value={0.082} />
      </dd>
      <dt>Failed payments</dt>
      <dd style={{ margin: 0 }}>
        <Trend value={-0.31} good="down" />
      </dd>
      <dt>Time to first reply</dt>
      <dd style={{ margin: 0 }}>
        <Trend value={0.15} good="down" />
      </dd>
    </dl>
  );
}
```

## Outline

`variant="outline"` puts an edge around the trend, in its own color. Use it for a trend that stands alone, away from the number it belongs to.

```tsx
import { Trend } from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <>
      <Trend variant="outline" value={0.125} />
      <Trend variant="outline" value={-0.04} />
      <Trend variant="outline" value={0} />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Your own text

Children replace the amount. The value still chooses the arrow and the color, so it can be any number with the right sign. To keep the number and write it another way, pass `format`, which takes what [`FormattedNumber`](page:components/formatted-number) does.

```tsx
import { Trend } from "@nuvui/react";

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <>
      <Trend value={12}>12 more seats</Trend>
      <Trend value={-3} good="down">
        3 fewer open tickets
      </Trend>
      <Trend value={1.8} format={{ format: "decimal" }} />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

A trend has no keyboard behavior. It isn't a control and can't take focus.

### What the component handles

- The direction is in the page as words: "Up", "Down" or "No change". Nobody sees them, and a screen reader reads them before the amount. The arrow is hidden from it.
- With no change, the words are read in place of "0%".
- The colors are the theme's success and danger colors, which have at least 4.5:1 as text on the page and on a surface in every theme.
- The arrow is drawn in the text's color, so it's still there where the browser forces its own colors.

### What you need to handle

- Translate the three labels. [Translation](page:translation) lists them with every other piece of text the library writes.
- Say what the change is measured against. "Up 12.5%" needs "against last month" beside it.
- Color isn't the message. The arrow and the words carry it, so a trend still works for someone who can't tell green from red. Don't hide the arrow.

## CSS variables

Set any of these on the trend, or on anything around it.

```css
.quiet-trend {
  --nuv-trend-fg: var(--color-muted-foreground);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-trend-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 0.5)` | Space between the arrow and the amount. |

| Class | What it's on |

**Do**

## The value

`value` is a ratio, so `0.125` is written as 12.5%. Its sign chooses the arrow: above zero points up, below zero points down, and zero is a level line.

The amount is written without its sign. The arrow shows the direction, and a screen reader hears it in words, so "Down 4%" isn't followed by a minus that would be read as well.

Your own text

## Accessibility

A trend has no keyboard behavior. It isn't a control and can't take focus.

### What the component handles

- The direction is in the page as words: "Up", "Down" or "No change". Nobody sees them, and a screen reader reads them before the amount. The arrow is hidden from it.
- With no change, the words are read in place of "0%".
- The colors are the theme's success and danger colors, which have at least 4.5:1 as text on the page and on a surface in every theme.
- The arrow is drawn in the text's color, so it's still there where the browser forces its own colors.

### What you need to handle

- Translate the three labels. [Translation](page:translation) lists them with every other piece of text the library writes.
- Say what the change is measured against. "Up 12.5%" needs "against last month" beside it.
- Color isn't the message. The arrow and the words carry it, so a trend still works for someone who can't tell green from red. Don't hide the arrow.
