sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

A QR code has nothing to press and nothing to focus.

### What the component handles

- It's an `<svg>` with `role="img"`, so a screen reader meets one picture and not a thousand squares.
- It has a name. Without `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, the name is the value.
- The squares stay black on white in a dark theme and where the browser forces colors, because that's what a camera reads.

### What you need to handle

- Name it for what scanning it does: "Open order 1042". A long address read out letter by letter helps nobody.
- Never make a QR code the only way to get what it holds. Someone reading the page on the phone they'd scan with can't scan it, and neither can someone who can't see it. Put a link, or the text, next to it.
- An `<image>` in `overlay` is part of the picture and needs no name of its own.
- If you change the colors, keep the squares dark and the ground light, and scan it.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on the code, or on anything around it.

```css
.ticket {
  --nuv-qrcode-fg: var(--color-gray-950);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-qrcode-bg` | `var(--color-white)` | Color of the ground, under the code and under the overlay. White in every theme by default. Keep it light. |
| `--nuv-qrcode-fg` | `var(--color-black)` | Color of the squares. Black in every theme by default. Keep it much darker than the ground. |
| `--nuv-qrcode-invalid` | `var(--color-danger)` | Color of the edge and the line of a code that can't be drawn. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-qrcode` | QRCode: the svg. |
| `.nuv-qrcode__cross-arms` | QRCodeSwissCross: the white cross. |
| `.nuv-qrcode__cross-ground` | QRCodeSwissCross: its black square. |
| `.nuv-qrcode__ground` | The rectangle behind the squares, and the one behind the overlay. |
| `.nuv-qrcode__mark` | The edge and the line through a code that can't be drawn. |
| `.nuv-qrcode__overlay` | The box in the middle that `overlay` is drawn in. |
| `.nuv-qrcode__squares` | The dark squares, as one path. |

A code has `data-error-correction`, its level, and `data-version`, a number from 1 to 40 that says how many squares it has: 21 along a side at version 1, and four more with each version. One that can't be drawn has `data-invalid` instead.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

QRCode has no `"use client"`. Rendered in a server component, it's SVG in the HTML and sends no script. `saveCode` needs a browser, so the button that calls it is in a client component.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Scan the code you ship, at the size and on the surface it will be seen.
- Keep the value short. Put an address in the code and the rest at the address.
- Say next to the code what scanning it does.

**Don't**

- Don't put a code on a photograph or a pattern. Leave it its white, and space around it.
- Don't put something secret in one. Anyone who can see it can read it.
- Don't use it on a page people open on their phones without a link beside it.

pages.title: Chat
pages.description: The @nuvui/chat package. The parts of a conversation with an assistant, installed next to @nuvui/react. Messages, the scrolling around them, markdown and code, the box a prompt is written in, files, sources, tool calls, reasoning and the list of past conversations.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/chat @nuvui/react
```

`@nuvui/react` is a peer dependency. Some parts are built on the core's: the ones that open on its Collapsible, the thread list on its ListView.

Two things come from outside, each only for the part that needs it:

- **`Markdown`** reads markdown with [react-markdown](https://github.com/remarkjs/react-markdown) and [remark-gfm](https://github.com/remarkjs/remark-gfm), which are installed with the package. It has an entry of its own, `@nuvui/chat/markdown`, and isn't exported from `@nuvui/chat`, so they're loaded only by an app that imports it. They're ESM only: an app that's bundled doesn't notice, and one that loads `@nuvui/chat/markdown` with `require` needs Node 20.19, or 22.12 and later.
- **The ready highlighter** at `@nuvui/chat/shiki` uses [Shiki](https://shiki.style), which is an optional peer dependency: install it if you use that entry. Nothing else needs it.

sections.heading: Load the styles
sections.markdown:
## Load the styles

Import the package's stylesheet once, after the core's:

```tsx title="app/layout.tsx"
import "@nuvui/react/styles.css";
import "@nuvui/chat/styles.css";
```

Both files open with the same line naming the cascade layers, so the order you import them in doesn't decide which rule wins. Each component's styles are also on their own, at `@nuvui/chat/css/conversation.css` and so on, one file for each page here. A part that's built on one of the core's needs that one's file as well:

| Stylesheet | Also needs, from `@nuvui/react/css/` |
| --- | --- |
| `message.css` | `tooltip.css`, for the action buttons |
| `markdown.css` | `code-block.css` from this package |
| `prompt-input.css` | `attachment.css` from this package and `spinner.css`, if it takes files |
| `attachment.css` | `spinner.css` |
| `source.css` | `collapsible.css` |
| `tool-call.css` | `collapsible.css`, `spinner.css`, `button.css` |
| `reasoning.css` | `collapsible.css`, `spinner.css`, `text-shimmer.css` |
| `thread-list.css` | `list-view.css` |

sections.heading: Put them together
Where the messages come from is yours
sections.markdown:
## Where the messages come from is yours

Nothing here talks to a model or to a server. The components take messages as props and tell you when something is sent. That's on purpose: how a reply is fetched, streamed, stored and retried differs from one app to the next, and a UI library that decided it would be in the way of most of them.

So they work with whatever you fetch with. The names line up with what most of those give you: a message has a role, `"user"` or `"assistant"`, which is `Message`'s `from`, and a request has a state, which is `PromptInput`'s `busy` and `Message`'s `streaming`.

sections.heading: What a screen reader is told
sections.markdown:
## What a screen reader is told

- The messages are a log. A message that's added is read out, and the rest isn't read again.
- A reply that's still arriving is marked as busy, and read once it's whole. Without that, every few words would be read as they came, over each other. Set `streaming` on the message for as long as it's being written.
- Each message starts with who it's from, "You" or "Assistant", said and not seen. `label` changes the words, for another language or another name.
- The button that sends is named "Send", and "Stop" while it stops a reply.

All of that is checked by the tests as roles, names and states. What each screen reader then says hasn't been checked by a person.

sections.heading: Languages
sections.markdown:
## Languages

The few words the components say themselves are props with English defaults:

| Component | Prop | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Message` | `label` | `"You"` or `"Assistant"` |
| `MessageActions` | `label` | `"Message actions"` |
| `MessageCopyAction` | `label`, `copiedLabel` | `"Copy"`, `"Copied"` |
| `MessageLoader` | `label` | `"Writing a reply"` |
| `CodeBlock` | `copyLabel`, `copiedLabel`, `label` | `"Copy code"`, `"Copied"`, `"Code"` |
| `Markdown` | `tableLabel`, `doneLabel`, `todoLabel`, and the three of `CodeBlock` as `copyLabel`, `copiedLabel`, `codeLabel` | `"Table"`, `"Done"`, `"To do"` |
| `ConversationScrollButton` | `label` | `"Go to the latest message"` |
| `PromptInputSubmit` | `label`, `stopLabel` | `"Send"`, `"Stop"` |
| `PromptSuggestions` | `label` | `"Suggestions"` |
| `PromptInputAttach` | `label` | `"Attach files"` |
| `PromptInputAttachments` | `label`, `removeLabel`, `announce` | `"Files to send"`, `"Remove …"`, `"2 files attached"` |
| `Attachment` | `removeLabel`, `uploadingLabel` | `"Remove …"`, `"Uploading"` |
| `SourcesTrigger` | children | `"Sources"` |
| `ToolCallTrigger` | `statusLabel` | `"Running"`, `"Needs approval"`, `"Done"`, `"Failed"`, `"Denied"` |
| `ToolCallInput`, `ToolCallOutput`, `ToolCallError` | `label` | `"Request"`, `"Result"`, `"Error"` |
| `ToolCallApproval` | `label`, `approveLabel`, `denyLabel` | `"Approval"`, `"Approve"`, `"Deny"` |
| `ReasoningTrigger` | children | `"Thinking"`, then `"Reasoning"` |

A file's size is written in the reader's own number format. `formatSize` on `Attachment` and `PromptInputAttachments` writes it your way.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

`Conversation`, `Message`, `Markdown`, `CodeBlock`, `PromptInput`, `Sources`, `ToolCall`, `Reasoning` and `ThreadList` are client components: they follow the scrolling, copy to the clipboard, color code, keep what's typed, and open and close. They carry `"use client"`, so a server component can render them. `MessageLoader`, `PromptSuggestions`, `PromptSuggestion`, `Attachments` and `Attachment` have no state and aren't client components.

A conversation that changes is a client component of yours in any case, since it holds the messages.

sections.heading: What it leaves out
sections.markdown:
## What it leaves out

- **Talking to a model.** Covered above: the messages are yours.
- **Uploading.** The prompt box hands you `File` objects.
- **Math and diagrams in markdown.** `Markdown` takes your own elements through `components`, which is where a renderer for either goes.

pages.title: Conversation
pages.description: The messages of a chat in a box that scrolls. It starts at the latest message, stays there while a reply arrives, and stops following when the reader scrolls up.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/chat @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import {
  Conversation,
  ConversationContent,
  ConversationEmpty,
  ConversationScrollButton,
} from "@nuvui/chat";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/chat/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Chat](page:chat/index) covers that.

```tsx
<Conversation style={{ blockSize: 480 }}>
  <ConversationContent aria-label="Billing questions">
    {/* messages */}
  </ConversationContent>
  <ConversationScrollButton />
  {/* the prompt box */}
</Conversation>
```

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Conversation` | The whole: a column, as tall as you make it. |
| `ConversationContent` | The messages. This is the box that scrolls, and it takes the room that's left. |
| `ConversationScrollButton` | A button over the end of the messages that goes to the latest one. It's only there while the latest is out of view. |
| `ConversationEmpty` | What's shown before any message, in the middle of the room. |

Whatever else you put in the `Conversation`, such as a [prompt box](page:chat/prompt-input), sits under the messages at its own height.

sections.heading: Give it a height
Following a reply
sections.markdown:
## Following a reply

It starts at the latest message. While that's in view, anything that makes the messages taller keeps it in view: a reply arriving word by word, a new message, a picture that loads.

When the reader scrolls up, it stops. New messages arrive below without moving what they're reading, and the button appears. It follows again once they scroll back to the end, or press the button.

Sending a message from a `PromptInput` inside the conversation goes to the end as well, wherever the reader was: they've just written something and want to see the answer.

sections.heading: Before the first message
From a part of your own
ConversationScrollButton props
sections.markdown:
## ConversationScrollButton props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `"Go to the latest message"` | The button's name for a screen reader. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | In place of the arrow. |

`Conversation`, `ConversationContent` and `ConversationEmpty` take the attributes of a `div`. All four pass `ref` to their element.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Stops at the messages, so they can be scrolled, then at anything in them that takes focus. |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> <kbd>Page Up</kbd> <kbd>Page Down</kbd> <kbd>Home</kbd> <kbd>End</kbd> | With focus on the messages, scroll them. |

### What the component handles

- `ConversationContent` has `role="log"`, so a screen reader reads a message when it's added and doesn't read the others again.
- It can take focus, which is what lets it be scrolled from the keyboard.
- The button to go to the latest message is named, and removed while there's nowhere to go. Pressing it puts focus on the messages, so focus isn't dropped when the button goes.
- For someone who has asked for less motion, going to the end is a jump and not a glide.

### What you need to handle

- Name the messages with `aria-label` on `ConversationContent`: "Conversation with support", say.
- Mark a reply that's still arriving with `streaming` on its [`Message`](page:chat/message), so that it's read once and whole.
- Keep the newest message last in the markup. A log is read in the order it's written.

### What hasn't been checked

The tests check the role, the names and that focus lands where it should. What each screen reader says as messages arrive hasn't been checked by a person.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

The messages have 16 pixels of space around them and are never wider than 48rem. The button to go to the end is 44 pixels on a touch screen and 36 with a mouse.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on the `Conversation`, or on anything around it.

```css
.chat {
  --nuv-conversation-max-width: 40rem;
  --nuv-conversation-gap: 2rem;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-conversation-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Text color. |
| `--nuv-conversation-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 6)` | Space between two messages. |
| `--nuv-conversation-max-width` | `48rem` | The most width the messages take. They sit in the middle of a wider box. |
| `--nuv-conversation-padding` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 4)` | Space around the messages, inside the box that scrolls. |
| `--nuv-conversation-scroll-button-size` | `var(--nuv-touch-size)`, `calc(var(--spacing) * 9)` | The button's width and height. Larger by default with a finger than with a mouse. |
| `--nuv-conversation-scroll-button-offset` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 3)` | How far above the end of the messages the button sits. |
| `--nuv-conversation-scroll-button-border` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Color of that button's edge. Keep it at 3:1 against the messages' background. |
| `--nuv-conversation-scroll-button-bg` | `var(--color-background)` | Background of the button that goes to the end. |
| `--nuv-conversation-scroll-button-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of its arrow. |
| `--nuv-conversation-scroll-button-hover-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Its background under the pointer. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-conversation` | Conversation |
| `.nuv-conversation__content` | The column of messages inside it. |
| `.nuv-conversation__empty` | ConversationEmpty |
| `.nuv-conversation__scroll-button` | ConversationScrollButton |
| `.nuv-conversation__viewport` | ConversationContent: the box that scrolls. |

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

Conversation starts with `"use client"`: it follows the scrolling. A server component can render it with messages written there. A conversation that changes is a client component of yours anyway, since it holds the messages.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Give it a height, from the page or from what it's in.
- Put the prompt box inside the `Conversation`, after the messages, so sending goes to the end.

**Don't**

- Don't scroll to the end yourself when a message arrives. That takes the page away from someone reading further up, which is what this is for.
- Don't put the newest message first. It follows the end.

pages.title: Message
pages.description: One message in a conversation, from the person or from the assistant, with room for a picture, a line of details and a row of actions.
pages.markdown:
# Message One message in a conversation, from the person or from the assistant, with room for a picture, a line of details and a row of actions. Use a message for each turn of a conversation. The person's own sit at the end of the row in a bubble. The assistant's sit at the start and take the row's width, since they're the ones that run long. ```tsx import { Message, MessageContent } from "@nuvui/chat"; export default function Example() { return (
Can I move an invoice to another month? Yes, while it's still a draft. Open the invoice, choose Edit, and change the date. An invoice that's been sent can't be moved: void it and send a new one.
); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/chat @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Message, MessageAction, MessageActions, MessageContent, MessageCopyAction, MessageMeta, } from "@nuvui/chat"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/chat/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Chat](page:chat/index) covers that. ```tsx Two invoices are overdue. ``` ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `Message` | One message. `from` says whose it is. | | `MessageContent` | What it says. | | `MessageMeta` | A small line over or under it: a name, a time. | | `MessageActions` | A row of buttons under it. | | `MessageAction` | One of those buttons: an icon, named by `label`. | | `MessageCopyAction` | A button that copies the message. | ## What it says `MessageContent` shows text as it was written: line breaks are kept, and a long word or address breaks and doesn't push the row wider. It takes anything else as well. What a model writes is usually markdown. Put a [`Markdown`](page:chat/markdown) in the `MessageContent` and it's drawn as headings, lists, tables and code. ## A picture and a name `avatar` puts a picture beside the message, and a `MessageMeta` puts a line over it. Each message is already announced with who it's from. When the name is on the page, in the line, pass `label={null}` so it isn't said twice. ```tsx import { Message, MessageContent, MessageMeta } from "@nuvui/chat"; import { Avatar, AvatarFallback } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return (
AL } > Ada Lovelace · 09:41 Is the March report ready? N } > Northwind assistant · 09:41 It is. Revenue is up 8% on February, and two invoices are overdue.
); } ``` ## A reply that's still arriving Set `streaming` while a reply is being written and take it off when it's done. Nothing looks different. It tells a screen reader to wait and read the message once it's whole, not each piece as it arrives. Before the first words, show a [`MessageLoader`](page:chat/message-loader) where they'll be. ```tsx "use client"; import { Message, MessageContent, MessageLoader } from "@nuvui/chat"; import { Button } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react"; const words = "Revenue for March was 48,200, up 8% on February. Most of the rise came from three new customers on the Team plan.".split( " ", ); export default function Example() { // How many words have arrived. None yet is the wait before a reply. const [count, setCount] = useState(words.length); const timer = useRef>(undefined); useEffect(() => () => clearInterval(timer.current), []); function again() { clearInterval(timer.current); setCount(0); timer.current = setInterval(() => { setCount((now) => { if (now + 1 >= words.length) clearInterval(timer.current); return Math.min(now + 1, words.length); }); }, 150); } const streaming = count < words.length; return (
{count === 0 ? ( ) : ( {words.slice(0, count).join(" ")} )}
); } ``` ## Actions `MessageActions` is a row of buttons under a message. Each `MessageAction` is an icon with a `label`, which is its name for a screen reader and the text of its tooltip. `MessageCopyAction` copies `text` and shows a tick for two seconds. ```tsx "use client"; import { Message, MessageAction, MessageActions, MessageContent, MessageCopyAction, } from "@nuvui/chat"; import { useState } from "react"; const text = "Two invoices are overdue: INV-1042 for Contoso, 12 days, and INV-1057 for Fabrikam, 3 days."; const icon = { width: 16, height: 16, viewBox: "0 0 16 16", fill: "none", stroke: "currentColor", strokeWidth: 1.5, strokeLinecap: "round", strokeLinejoin: "round", } as const; export default function Example() { const [tries, setTries] = useState(1); return (
{text} setTries((now) => now + 1)} >

Answer {tries}

); } ``` The buttons are always there. Showing them only under the pointer would hide them from a touch screen and from the keyboard. Copying needs a page served over HTTPS, or `localhost`. Where the browser refuses, `onCopyError` is called and nothing is shown as copied. ## Message props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `from` (required) | `"assistant" \| "user"` | | Who wrote it. The person's own messages sit at the end of the row in a bubble, and the assistant's at the start, across the row. | | `label` | `ReactNode` | `"You" for the person's own, "Assistant" for the other` | Said before the message to a screen reader, and seen by nobody: who the message is from. Pass `null` when the name is on the page, in a `MessageMeta`. | | `avatar` | `ReactNode` | | A picture of who wrote it, beside the message. An `Avatar`, most often. | | `streaming` | `boolean` | `false` | The message is still being written. A screen reader waits until it's finished and then reads it whole, and doesn't read each piece as it arrives. | ## MessageAction props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `label` (required) | `string` | | What the button does, in a word or two. It's the button's name for a screen reader and the text of its tooltip. | | `children` (required) | `ReactNode` | | The icon. | ## MessageCopyAction props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `text` (required) | `string` | | The text that's copied. | | `label` | `string` | `"Copy"` | | | `copiedLabel` | `string` | `"Copied"` | The button's name for the two seconds after it has copied. | | `onCopy` | `((text: string) => void)` | | Called once the text is on the clipboard. | | `onCopyError` | `((error: unknown) => void)` | | Called if the browser wouldn't copy: the page isn't served over HTTPS, or permission was refused. | ## MessageActions props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `label` | `string` | `"Message actions"` | The name of the group for a screen reader. | `MessageContent` and `MessageMeta` take the attributes of a `div`. Every part passes `ref` to its element. ## Accessibility ### What the component handles - Each message starts with who it's from, "You" or "Assistant", in text that's read and not seen. The side a message is on and its bubble are for the eye. This is the same thing for the ear. - A message with `streaming` has `aria-busy`, and loses it when it's done. - The picture is hidden from screen readers. Who the message is from has been said. - The actions are a group with a name. Each is a real button with a name, and its tooltip shows on focus as well as under the pointer. - When a message has been copied, the button's name changes and "Copied" is announced. - An action is 44 pixels on a touch screen and 32 with a mouse. ### What you need to handle - Translate `label` with the rest of your app, and the actions' labels. - Give every `MessageAction` a `label` that says what it does: "Try again", not "Action 2". - Don't mark who a message is from by color alone if you restyle. Keep the side, the bubble or a name. ## CSS variables Set any of these on a `Message`, or on anything around it. ```css .chat { --nuv-message-user-bg: var(--color-primary); --nuv-message-user-fg: var(--color-primary-foreground); } ``` | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-message-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 3)` | Space between the picture and the message. | | `--nuv-message-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Text color. | | `--nuv-message-font-size` | `var(--text-base)` | Size of the text. | | `--nuv-message-user-max-width` | `85%` | The most of the row the person's own message takes. | | `--nuv-message-user-radius` | `var(--radius-xl)` | Corner radius of the person's own message. | | `--nuv-message-user-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of the person's own message. | | `--nuv-message-user-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of its text. Keep it at 4.5:1 against the background. | | `--nuv-message-meta-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the small line. Keep it at 4.5:1. | | `--nuv-message-action-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of an action's icon. Keep it at 3:1. | | `--nuv-message-action-hover-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of an action under the pointer. | | `--nuv-message-action-hover-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of its icon under the pointer. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-message` | Message | | `.nuv-message__action` | MessageAction and MessageCopyAction. | | `.nuv-message__actions` | MessageActions | | `.nuv-message__avatar` | The picture, from the avatar prop. | | `.nuv-message__body` | The column beside the picture, with everything else in it. | | `.nuv-message__content` | MessageContent | | `.nuv-message__label` | Who the message is from, and that it was copied. Read out and drawn for nobody. | | `.nuv-message__meta` | MessageMeta | A message has `data-from`, and `data-streaming` while it's being written. The copy button has `data-copied` for the two seconds after it has copied. ## Server components Message starts with `"use client"`, for the copy button and the tooltips. A server component can render one, without the functions: `onClick`, `onCopy`. ## Do and don't **Do** - Set `streaming` for exactly as long as the reply is being written. - Keep the actions to a few. Copy and try again cover most of it. **Don't** - Don't put a whole page in a message. A table or a form the assistant made belongs under the reply or beside the conversation. - Don't hide the actions until the pointer is over the message.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/chat @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import {
  Message,
  MessageAction,
  MessageActions,
  MessageContent,
  MessageCopyAction,
  MessageMeta,
} from "@nuvui/chat";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/chat/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Chat](page:chat/index) covers that.

```tsx
<Message from="assistant">
  <MessageContent>Two invoices are overdue.</MessageContent>
</Message>
```

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Message` | One message. `from` says whose it is. |
| `MessageContent` | What it says. |
| `MessageMeta` | A small line over or under it: a name, a time. |
| `MessageActions` | A row of buttons under it. |
| `MessageAction` | One of those buttons: an icon, named by `label`. |
| `MessageCopyAction` | A button that copies the message. |

sections.heading: What it says
sections.markdown:
## What it says

`MessageContent` shows text as it was written: line breaks are kept, and a long word or address breaks and doesn't push the row wider. It takes anything else as well. What a model writes is usually markdown. Put a [`Markdown`](page:chat/markdown) in the `MessageContent` and it's drawn as headings, lists, tables and code.

sections.heading: A picture and a name
A reply that's still arriving
Actions
Message props
sections.markdown:
## Message props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` (required) | `"assistant" \| "user"` |  | Who wrote it. The person's own messages sit at the end of the row in a bubble, and the assistant's at the start, across the row. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | `"You" for the person's own, "Assistant" for the other` | Said before the message to a screen reader, and seen by nobody: who the message is from. Pass `null` when the name is on the page, in a `MessageMeta`. |
| `avatar` | `ReactNode` |  | A picture of who wrote it, beside the message. An `Avatar`, most often. |
| `streaming` | `boolean` | `false` | The message is still being written. A screen reader waits until it's finished and then reads it whole, and doesn't read each piece as it arrives. |

sections.heading: MessageAction props
sections.markdown:

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | What the button does, in a word or two. It's the button's name for a screen reader and the text of its tooltip. |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The icon. |

sections.markdown:

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |

| `text` (required) | `string` |  | The text that's copied. |
| `label` | `string` | `"Copy"` |  |

| `onCopy` | `((text: string) => void)` |  | Called once the text is on the clipboard. |
| `onCopyError` | `((error: unknown) => void)` |  | Called if the browser wouldn't copy: the page isn't served over HTTPS, or permission was refused. |

sections.markdown:

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `"Message actions"` | The name of the group for a screen reader. |

`MessageContent` and `MessageMeta` take the attributes of a `div`. Every part passes `ref` to its element.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### What the component handles

- Each message starts with who it's from, "You" or "Assistant", in text that's read and not seen. The side a message is on and its bubble are for the eye. This is the same thing for the ear.
- A message with `streaming` has `aria-busy`, and loses it when it's done.
- The picture is hidden from screen readers. Who the message is from has been said.
- The actions are a group with a name. Each is a real button with a name, and its tooltip shows on focus as well as under the pointer.
- When a message has been copied, the button's name changes and "Copied" is announced.
- An action is 44 pixels on a touch screen and 32 with a mouse.

### What you need to handle

- Translate `label` with the rest of your app, and the actions' labels.
- Give every `MessageAction` a `label` that says what it does: "Try again", not "Action 2".
- Don't mark who a message is from by color alone if you restyle. Keep the side, the bubble or a name.

sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on a `Message`, or on anything around it.

```css
.chat {
  --nuv-message-user-bg: var(--color-primary);
  --nuv-message-user-fg: var(--color-primary-foreground);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-message-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 3)` | Space between the picture and the message. |
| `--nuv-message-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Text color. |
| `--nuv-message-font-size` | `var(--text-base)` | Size of the text. |
| `--nuv-message-user-max-width` | `85%` | The most of the row the person's own message takes. |
| `--nuv-message-user-radius` | `var(--radius-xl)` | Corner radius of the person's own message. |
| `--nuv-message-user-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of the person's own message. |
| `--nuv-message-user-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of its text. Keep it at 4.5:1 against the background. |
| `--nuv-message-meta-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the small line. Keep it at 4.5:1. |
| `--nuv-message-action-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of an action's icon. Keep it at 3:1. |
| `--nuv-message-action-hover-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of an action under the pointer. |
| `--nuv-message-action-hover-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of its icon under the pointer. |

## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-message` | Message |
| `.nuv-message__action` | MessageAction and MessageCopyAction. |
| `.nuv-message__actions` | MessageActions |

A message has `data-from`, and `data-streaming` while it's being written. The copy button has `data-copied` for the two seconds after it has copied.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

Message starts with `"use client"`, for the copy button and the tooltips. A server component can render one, without the functions: `onClick`, `onCopy`.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Set `streaming` for exactly as long as the reply is being written.
- Keep the actions to a few. Copy and try again cover most of it.

**Don't**

- Don't put a whole page in a message. A table or a form the assistant made belongs under the reply or beside the conversation.
- Don't hide the actions until the pointer is over the message.

pages.title: Markdown
pages.description: A reply's markdown drawn with the library's own type. Headings, lists, tables, links and code, safe to give text a model wrote, and able to take text that's still arriving.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/chat @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { Markdown } from "@nuvui/chat/markdown";
```

It has an entry of its own and isn't exported from `@nuvui/chat`. It brings a markdown parser, [react-markdown](https://github.com/remarkjs/react-markdown) with [remark-gfm](https://github.com/remarkjs/remark-gfm), which is about 42 kB compressed. An app that imports the other parts and not this one doesn't load it.

The styles come from `@nuvui/chat/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Chat](page:chat/index) covers that.

```tsx
<Message from="assistant" streaming={replying}>
  <MessageContent>
    <Markdown streaming={replying}>{message.text}</Markdown>
  </MessageContent>
</Message>
```

sections.heading: What it draws
sections.markdown:
## What it draws

Everything in CommonMark, and GitHub's additions to it: tables, task lists, struck text and addresses that become links by themselves.

A fenced block of code is a [`CodeBlock`](page:chat/code-block), with its language over it and a button that copies it. A table that's wider than the message scrolls in a box of its own.

sections.heading: Text a model wrote is not trusted
sections.markdown: ## Text a model wrote is not trusted What a model writes can be steered by what it read: a web page, a file, an earlier message. So this treats its text as something to show and nothing more. - **HTML in the text is shown as text.** A `

sections.heading: A reply that's still arriving
Colored code
Headings
sections.markdown:
## Headings

A reply's `#` is an `h1`, and your page has one already. `headingOffset` moves a reply's headings down: with `2`, `#` is an `h3` and `##` an `h4`. They don't go past `h6`.

sections.heading: Your own elements
Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `string` |  | The markdown. |
| `streaming` | `boolean` | `false` | The text is still arriving. What's open at its end is closed for the moment, so a block of code is drawn as one before its last line has come, and bold as bold. |
| `highlighter` | `CodeHighlighter` |  | Colors the blocks of code. Without one they're in one color. A ready one for Shiki is at `@nuvui/chat/shiki`. Make it once, outside the component: a new one on every render colors everything again. |
| `allowImages` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether pictures in the text are loaded. Left off, a picture is a link with its description as the text. A picture's address is fetched as soon as it's drawn, and text a model wrote can put anything in that address, the conversation included. |
| `headingOffset` | `number` | `0` | How many levels the headings are moved down, so that they fit under the page's own. With `2`, `#` is an `h3`. |
| `components` | `Components` |  | Your own elements in place of these, by tag name, as react-markdown takes them. Keep the object the same from one render to the next. |
| `tableLabel` | `string` | `"Table"` | The name of the box a wide table scrolls in. |
| `doneLabel` | `string` | `"Done"` | What a ticked item of a task list is called. |
| `todoLabel` | `string` | `"To do"` | What one that isn't ticked is called. |
| `copyLabel` | `string` | `"Copy code"` | The name of the button that copies a block of code. |
| `copiedLabel` | `string` | `"Copied"` | Its name for the two seconds after it has copied. |
| `codeLabel` | `string` | `"Code"` | The name of the box a block of code scrolls in. |

It also takes the attributes of a `div`, and passes `ref` to it.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### What the component handles

- Headings, lists, tables and quotes are the real elements, so a screen reader can move by them.
- A table's box, and a block of code, can take focus when they scroll, and are named "Table" and "Code".
- A task list's box says "Done" or "To do", since nothing else names it.
- A link is underlined. It's told from the text around it by more than a color.
- A picture that isn't loaded is a link with the picture's description as its text.

### What you need to handle

- Put it in a [`Message`](page:chat/message) that has `streaming` while the reply arrives, so a screen reader reads it once it's whole.
- Set `headingOffset` so a reply's headings fit under your page's.
- Translate `tableLabel`, `doneLabel`, `todoLabel`, `copyLabel`, `copiedLabel` and `codeLabel`.
- A model writes what it writes. Headings that skip a level, or a picture with no description, come through as they are.

sections.markdown:

Set any of these on a `Markdown`, or on anything around it.

```css

  --nuv-markdown-gap: calc(var(--spacing) * 4);
  --nuv-markdown-link-fg: var(--color-primary);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-markdown-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 3)` | Space between paragraphs, lists and the other parts. |
| `--nuv-markdown-fg` | `inherit` | Color of the text. It's the message's unless you set it. |
| `--nuv-markdown-link-fg` | `inherit` | Color of a link. Keep it at 4.5:1. The default theme's primary color is checked as a control's color, at 3:1, and not as text. |
| `--nuv-markdown-quote-border` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Color of the line beside a quote. |
| `--nuv-markdown-quote-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of a quote's text. Keep it at 4.5:1. |
| `--nuv-markdown-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of a table's lines and of a rule. |
| `--nuv-markdown-code-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of code in a line. |
| `--nuv-markdown-code-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of code in a line. Keep it at 4.5:1 against its background. |
| `--nuv-markdown-table-head-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of a table's heading row. |

sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-markdown` | Markdown |

What's inside has no classes: it's styled by its element, `h2`, `ul`, `table`, each in `:where()`, which adds nothing to how strong the rule is. A rule of yours with one class wins.

sections.markdown:
## Server components

Markdown starts with `"use client"`. A server component can render it with text and no function: without `highlighter`, and without `components`.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Set `streaming` for exactly as long as the text arrives.
- Make the highlighter once for the whole app.

**Don't**

- Don't turn `allowImages` on for text you can't vouch for.
- Don't use it for a page of your own writing. That's a build step's job, where the text is read once and not in the browser.

pages.title: CodeBlock
pages.description: Code in a box of its own, with its language over it, a button that copies it, and colors from a highlighter you plug in. One for Shiki is ready-made.
pages.markdown:
# CodeBlock Code in a box of its own, with its language over it, a button that copies it, and colors from a highlighter you plug in. One for Shiki is ready-made. Use it for code in a reply. [`Markdown`](page:chat/markdown) draws every fenced block with it, and it works alone where you have the code yourself. ```tsx "use client"; import { CodeBlock } from "@nuvui/chat"; import { createShikiHighlighter } from "@nuvui/chat/shiki"; // One for the whole app, made outside any component. const highlighter = createShikiHighlighter(); const code = `type Invoice = { number: string; amount: number; daysLate: number }; // The ones a reminder should go out for today. export function overdue(invoices: Invoice[], after = 0) { return invoices .filter((invoice) => invoice.daysLate > after) .sort((a, b) => b.daysLate - a.daysLate); }`; export default function Example() { return (
); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/chat @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { CodeBlock } from "@nuvui/chat"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/chat/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Chat](page:chat/index) covers that. ```tsx ``` ## What it shows `code` is the code. `language` is written over it, and `title` takes its place there, for a file's name. A button copies the code, and shows a tick for two seconds. `copyable={false}` leaves the button out. Lines aren't wrapped, since where a line breaks means something in code. A long line scrolls sideways inside the box. `--nuv-code-block-max-height` gives the box a height to scroll down in as well. ## Colors By itself the code is in one color, and the component depends on nothing. Colors come from a `highlighter`: a function that's given the code and the language and returns the code's lines as tokens, each with a color. One for [Shiki](https://shiki.style) is ready. Install Shiki next to the package: ```sh pnpm add shiki ``` ```tsx import { CodeBlock } from "@nuvui/chat"; import { createShikiHighlighter } from "@nuvui/chat/shiki"; // Once for the whole app, outside any component. const highlighter = createShikiHighlighter(); ; ``` Nothing of Shiki is loaded with the page. It's fetched the first time code is colored, and each language's grammar the first time that language turns up. Until then the code is in one color, and it stays that way for a language Shiki doesn't know. It uses Shiki's engine written in JavaScript, so there's no WebAssembly to serve. While code is still arriving, what has been colored stays colored and what's new is added after it in one color until it's colored too. Nothing flickers, and the code on the screen is never behind. ### The colors are the theme's A token's color is a CSS variable, so the code follows the theme and dark mode with nothing to switch. Without the variables set, each kind takes one of the theme's colors that's checked as text against the box's background, in every preset: | Variable | What it colors | Default | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-code-block-token-keyword` | Keywords and operators | `--color-danger` | | `--nuv-code-block-token-string`, `--nuv-code-block-token-string-expression` | Text in quotes | `--color-success` | | `--nuv-code-block-token-constant` | Numbers, constants and names that are defined | `--color-warning` | | `--nuv-code-block-token-comment` | Comments | `--color-muted-foreground` | | `--nuv-code-block-token-punctuation` | Brackets and commas | `--color-muted-foreground` | | `--nuv-code-block-token-function`, `--nuv-code-block-token-parameter`, `--nuv-code-block-token-link` | Function names, parameters, links | The box's text color | | `--nuv-code-block-token-inserted`, `--nuv-code-block-token-deleted`, `--nuv-code-block-token-changed` | Lines of a diff | `--color-success`, `--color-danger`, `--color-warning` | | `--nuv-code-block-foreground` | Everything else | The box's text color | Set them on the block or on anything around it. Keep each at 4.5:1 against the box's background. ```css .chat { --nuv-code-block-token-function: var(--color-chart-1); } ``` ### One of your own A highlighter is a function, so any library fits behind it: ```tsx import type { CodeHighlighter } from "@nuvui/chat"; const highlighter: CodeHighlighter = (code, language) => { if (language !== "json") return null; return code.split("\n").map((line) => [{ content: line, color: "var(--color-success)" }]); }; ``` It returns the lines, each a list of tokens, or a promise of them. The tokens' text, put back together, has to be the code it was given. `null` says the language isn't one it knows. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `code` (required) | `string` | | The code. | | `language` | `string` | | The language it's in, as it's written after the fence in markdown: `"ts"`, `"python"`. It's shown over the code and handed to the highlighter. | | `title` | `ReactNode` | | In place of the language over the code: a file's name, most often. | | `highlighter` | `CodeHighlighter` | | Colors the code. Without one it's in one color. A ready one for Shiki is at `@nuvui/chat/shiki`. | | `copyable` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether there's a button that copies the code. | | `copyLabel` | `string` | `"Copy code"` | The copy button's name for a screen reader. | | `copiedLabel` | `string` | `"Copied"` | Its name for the two seconds after it has copied. | | `onCopy` | `((code: string) => void)` | | Called once the code is on the clipboard. | | `onCopyError` | `((error: unknown) => void)` | | Called if the browser wouldn't copy: the page isn't served over HTTPS, or permission was refused. | | `label` | `string` | `"Code"` | The name of the box the code scrolls in, for a screen reader. | It also takes the attributes of a `div`, and passes `ref` to it. ### A token | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `content` (required) | `string` | | The text. | | `color` | `string` | | Any CSS color. sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/chat @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { CodeBlock } from "@nuvui/chat";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/chat/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Chat](page:chat/index) covers that.

```tsx
<CodeBlock code={code} language="ts" />
```

sections.heading: What it shows
sections.markdown:
## What it shows

`code` is the code. `language` is written over it, and `title` takes its place there, for a file's name. A button copies the code, and shows a tick for two seconds. `copyable={false}` leaves the button out.

Lines aren't wrapped, since where a line breaks means something in code. A long line scrolls sideways inside the box. `--nuv-code-block-max-height` gives the box a height to scroll down in as well.

sections.heading: Colors
Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `code` (required) | `string` |  | The code. |
| `language` | `string` |  | The language it's in, as it's written after the fence in markdown: `"ts"`, `"python"`. It's shown over the code and handed to the highlighter. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  | In place of the language over the code: a file's name, most often. |
| `highlighter` | `CodeHighlighter` |  | Colors the code. Without one it's in one color. A ready one for Shiki is at `@nuvui/chat/shiki`. |
| `copyable` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether there's a button that copies the code. |
| `copyLabel` | `string` | `"Copy code"` | The copy button's name for a screen reader. |
| `copiedLabel` | `string` | `"Copied"` | Its name for the two seconds after it has copied. |
| `onCopy` | `((code: string) => void)` |  | Called once the code is on the clipboard. |
| `onCopyError` | `((error: unknown) => void)` |  | Called if the browser wouldn't copy: the page isn't served over HTTPS, or permission was refused. |
| `label` | `string` | `"Code"` | The name of the box the code scrolls in, for a screen reader. |

It also takes the attributes of a `div`, and passes `ref` to it.

### A token

| `content` (required) | `string` |  | The text. |
| `color` | `string` |  | Any CSS color. Left out, it's the block's own text color. |
| `fontStyle` | `"italic"` |  |  |
| `fontWeight` | `"bold"` |  |  |
| `textDecoration` | `"line-through" \| "underline"` |  |  |

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Goes to the button that copies, and then to the code. |
| Arrow keys | Scroll the code, when it has focus. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> | On the button, copies the code. |

### What the component handles

- The box the code scrolls in can take focus, and is named "Code", so it can be scrolled with the keys.
- The button is named "Copy code". When it has copied, its name changes and "Copied" is announced.
- The colors are decoration. The code is the same text with them and without.
- The default colors are the theme's, which are checked as text against the box's background.
- The button is 44 pixels on a touch screen and 28 with a mouse.

### What you need to handle

- Translate `copyLabel`, `copiedLabel` and `label`.
- If you set the token colors yourself, keep each at 4.5:1 against the box's background, in light and in dark.

Copying needs a page served over HTTPS, or `localhost`. Where the browser refuses, `onCopyError` is called and nothing is shown as copied.

sections.markdown:

```css
  --nuv-code-block-max-height: 24rem;

}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-code-block-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of the box's edge and of the line under its top row. |
| `--nuv-code-block-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of the box. |
| `--nuv-code-block-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background of the box. The default token colors are checked against the default. |
| `--nuv-code-block-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Color of code that has no color of its own. |
| `--nuv-code-block-title-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the language or the title. Keep it at 4.5:1. |
| `--nuv-code-block-copy-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the copy button's icon. Keep it at 3:1. |
| `--nuv-code-block-copy-hover-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of the button under the pointer. |
| `--nuv-code-block-copy-hover-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of its icon under the pointer. |
| `--nuv-code-block-max-height` | `none` | How tall the code gets before it scrolls down. Left out, it's as tall as its lines. |
| `--nuv-code-block-font-size` | `var(--text-sm)` | Size of the code. |

pages.title: PromptInput
pages.description: The box a prompt is written in. A field that grows with the text, sends on Enter, takes files, and has a row under it for buttons, with a button that sends or stops.
pages.markdown:
# PromptInput The box a prompt is written in. A field that grows with the text, sends on Enter, takes files, and has a row under it for buttons, with a button that sends or stops. Use it where someone writes to an assistant. It's a form with one growing field, so it behaves like the message box people already know: Enter sends, Shift with Enter starts a new line, and the box gets taller as the text does. ```tsx "use client"; import { PromptInput, PromptInputSubmit, PromptInputTextarea, PromptInputToolbar, } from "@nuvui/chat"; import { useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { const [sent, setSent] = useState(""); return (

{sent ? `Sent: ${sent}` : "Nothing sent yet."}

); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/chat @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { PromptInput, PromptInputAttach, PromptInputAttachments, PromptInputSubmit, PromptInputTextarea, PromptInputToolbar, PromptInputTools, } from "@nuvui/chat"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/chat/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Chat](page:chat/index) covers that. ```tsx send(text)}> ``` ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `PromptInput` | The box. It's a `form`, and keeps the text. | | `PromptInputTextarea` | The field. | | `PromptInputToolbar` | The row under the field. | | `PromptInputTools` | Buttons at the start of that row. | | `PromptInputSubmit` | The button that sends, and stops. | | `PromptInputAttach` | A button that opens the device's file picker. | | `PromptInputAttachments` | The files waiting to be sent. | ## Sending `onSubmit` is called with the text, and the box is emptied. Text that's only spaces isn't sent. Its second argument holds what goes with the text: `files`, covered [below](#files), and the form's `event`. With a keyboard, Enter sends and Shift with Enter starts a new line. On a touch screen it's the other way: the keyboard's Enter is the only way to start a line there, so it starts one, and the button sends. `submitOnEnter` on the field sets it one way for everyone. Enter that picks a word from an input method's list, as when writing Japanese or Chinese, doesn't send. ## While a reply is on its way Set `busy` from the moment something is sent until the reply is done. Nothing more can be sent until then. The field stays open, so the next message can be written while the reply arrives. With `onStop`, the button to send becomes a button to stop for as long as the box is busy. ```tsx "use client"; import { PromptInput, PromptInputSubmit, PromptInputTextarea, PromptInputToolbar, } from "@nuvui/chat"; import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false); const [said, setSaid] = useState("Nothing sent yet."); const timer = useRef>(undefined); useEffect(() => () => clearTimeout(timer.current), []); function send(text: string) { setBusy(true); setSaid(`Replying to: ${text}`); // A reply that takes ten seconds, long enough to stop it. timer.current = setTimeout(() => { setBusy(false); setSaid("Replied."); }, 10_000); } function stop() { clearTimeout(timer.current); setBusy(false); setSaid("Stopped."); } return (

{said}

); } ``` ## Buttons in the row `PromptInputTools` holds whatever goes with the prompt: where to look, which model, a mode. They sit at the start of the row and the button to send at the end. Give a button `type="button"`, so that pressing it doesn't send. ```tsx "use client"; import { PromptInput, PromptInputSubmit, PromptInputTextarea, PromptInputToolbar, PromptInputTools, } from "@nuvui/chat"; import { Button, NativeSelect } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { const [scope, setScope] = useState("This workspace"); const [sent, setSent] = useState("Nothing sent yet."); return (
setSent(`Asked ${scope}: ${text}`)}> setScope(event.target.value)} >

{sent}

); } ``` ## Files Put a `PromptInputAttachments` over the field and a `PromptInputAttach` in the row, and the box takes files. They wait in it, each with a button that takes it out again, and are handed to `onSubmit` with the text. ```tsx "use client"; import { PromptInput, PromptInputAttach, PromptInputAttachments, type PromptInputFileRejection, PromptInputSubmit, PromptInputTextarea, PromptInputToolbar, PromptInputTools, } from "@nuvui/chat"; import { useState } from "react"; const megabyte = 1024 * 1024; const reasons = { type: "isn't a picture or a PDF", size: "is over 5 MB", count: "is one more than three", }; export default function Example() { const [sent, setSent] = useState("Nothing sent yet."); const [refused, setRefused] = useState(""); function refuse(rejections: PromptInputFileRejection[]) { setRefused( rejections .map(({ file, reason }) => `${file.name} ${reasons[reason]}.`) .join(" "), ); } return (
setRefused("")} onFilesReject={refuse} onSubmit={(text, { files }) => setSent( `Sent "${text}" with ${files.length === 1 ? "1 file" : `${files.length} files`}.`, ) } >

{refused}

{sent}

); } ``` ```tsx send(text, files)} > ``` There are three ways in, and all three go through the same checks: - **The button** opens the device's file picker. - **Pasting** into the field, such as a screenshot. Text that's pasted stays text: cells copied from a spreadsheet come with a picture of themselves, and the picture is left out. - **Dropping** files on the box. While files are over it, its edge is dashed. Pasting and dropping only take files when one of the two parts is in the box. Without them the box is for text, and a file that's dropped on it is the browser's to deal with. `accept` is written as a file input's: `"image/*,.pdf"`. `maxFiles` is the most that can wait at once and `maxFileSize` the largest one may be, in bytes. A file that's turned away isn't shown. `onFilesReject` is called with each one and the reason, `"type"`, `"size"` or `"count"`, and that's where you tell the person. The same file added twice is kept once. With files waiting, the box can be sent with no text. ### Keeping the files yourself Pass `files` and `onFilesChange` to hold them: to start uploading as soon as one is added, or to keep them with a draft. `defaultFiles` starts the box with some. To show how an upload is going, give `PromptInputAttachments` a function. It's called with each file and with the way to take it out, and returns an [`Attachment`](page:chat/attachment): ```tsx {(file, remove) => ( )} ``` The box doesn't upload anything. It hands you `File` objects, and where they go is yours. ## Keeping the text yourself Pass `value` and `onValueChange` to hold the text: to limit it, to keep a draft, or to put a [suggestion](page:chat/prompt-suggestion) in the box. `onValueChange` is called with an empty text after a send. ```tsx "use client"; import { PromptInput, PromptInputSubmit, PromptInputTextarea, PromptInputToolbar, } from "@nuvui/chat"; import { useState } from "react"; const limit = 280; export default function Example() { const [text, setText] = useState(""); return (
setText(next.slice(0, limit))} onSubmit={() => {}} > {limit - text.length} characters left
); } ``` ## How tall it gets The field starts one line tall and grows to 12rem, about eight lines, and scrolls after that. `--nuv-prompt-input-max-height` changes where it stops. ## PromptInput props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` | `string` | | The text in the box, when you keep it. Use it with `onValueChange`. | | `defaultValue` | `string` | | The text in the box to begin with, when it's kept here. | | `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void)` | | Called with the text as it's typed, and with nothing after a send. | | `onSubmit` | `((text: string, submission: PromptInputSubmission) => void)` | | Called with the text when it's sent, by Enter or by the button, and with the files that were waiting. The box is emptied after. Text that's only spaces isn't sent, unless there are files to go with it. | | `files` | `File[]` | | The files waiting to be sent, when you keep them. Use it with `onFilesChange`. | | `defaultFiles` | `File[]` | | The files waiting to begin with, when they're kept here. | | `onFilesChange` | `((files: File[]) => void)` | | Called with all of them when one is added or taken out. | | `accept` | `string` | | The kinds of file it takes, written as a file input's `accept`: `"image/*,.pdf"`. Left out, it takes any. | | `maxFiles` | `number` | | The most files that can wait at once. | | `maxFileSize` | `number` | | The largest a file may be, in bytes. | | `onFilesReject` | `((rejections: PromptInputFileRejection[]) => void)` | | Called with the files that were turned away and the reason for each. Nothing is shown for them, so this is where you tell the person. | | `busy` | `boolean` | `false` | A reply is on its way. Nothing can be sent until it's `false` again, and what's typed meanwhile is kept. With `onStop`, the button to send becomes a button to stop. | | `onStop` | `(() => void)` | | Called by the button to stop, while `busy`. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Nothing can be typed or sent. | It also takes the attributes of a `form`. ## PromptInputTextarea props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `submitOnEnter` | `boolean` | | Whether Enter sends. Left out, it does where there's a keyboard, and starts a new line on a touch screen, where Enter is the only way to start one and the button is the way to send. | It also takes the attributes of a `textarea`, but for `value` and `defaultValue`, which are the box's. ## PromptInputSubmit props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `label` | `string` | `"Send"` | The button's name for a screen reader. | | `stopLabel` | `string` | `"Stop"` | Its name while a reply is on its way and it stops the reply. | | `children` | `ReactNode` | | In place of the arrow, or of the square while it stops a reply. | ## PromptInputAttachments props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `label` | `string` | `"Files to send"` | The list's name for a screen reader. | | `removeLabel` | `((name: string) => string)` | `(name) => 'Remove ${name}'` | The name of the button that takes a file out, from the file's name. | | `formatSize` | `((bytes: number) => string)` | `The size in the reader's own number format, such as "1.2 MB"` | Writes a file's size, from a number of bytes. | | `announce` | `((count: number) => string)` | `(count) => "2 files attached", and the like` | What a screen reader is told when a file is added or taken out, from how many are waiting now. | | `children` | `((file: File, remove: () => void) => ReactNode)` | | Draws each file yourself: called with the file and with the way to take it out, and returns an `Attachment`. For a file that's being uploaded as it waits, or one that failed. | It also takes the attributes of a `ul`. ## PromptInputAttach props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `label` | `string` | `"Attach files"` | The button's name for a screen reader. | | `children` | `ReactNode` | | In place of the paperclip. | It also takes the attributes of a `button`. `PromptInputToolbar` and `PromptInputTools` take the attributes of a `div`. Every part passes `ref` to its element. ## Accessibility ### Keyboard | Key | What it does | | --- | --- | | Enter | Sends, where there's a keyboard. | | Shift + Enter | Starts a new line. | | Tab | Goes from the field to the buttons in the row, and on to the button that sends. | ### What the component handles - It's a real `form` with a real `textarea`, so it works with a password manager, dictation and a browser's own spell check. - The button that sends is named "Send", and "Stop" while it stops a reply. - With nothing to send, the button is marked as disabled with `aria-disabled` and stays in the tab order. A button that left the tab order would be missed by someone feeling out the form with Tab. - When the field has focus from the keyboard, the ring goes round the whole box. - After a send, focus is back in the field. - The text is 16 pixels on a touch screen, which keeps iOS from zooming the page when the field takes focus. - The button that attaches is named "Attach files". The files that wait are a list named "Files to send", and each has a button named after it: "Remove scan.pdf". - When a file is added or taken out, how many are waiting is said to a screen reader: "2 files attached". - When a file is taken out, focus goes to the field. Its button went with it. - Dropping is a shortcut for a mouse. The button does the same with a keyboard and on a touch screen. ### What you need to handle - Name the field with `aria-label`, or a `

## Sending

`onSubmit` is called with the text, and the box is emptied. Text that's only spaces isn't sent. Its second argument holds what goes with the text: `files`, covered [below](#files), and the form's `event`.

With a keyboard, <kbd>Enter</kbd> sends and <kbd>Shift</kbd> with <kbd>Enter</kbd> starts a new line. On a touch screen it's the other way: the keyboard's Enter is the only way to start a line there, so it starts one, and the button sends. `submitOnEnter` on the field sets it one way for everyone.

Enter that picks a word from an input method's list, as when writing Japanese or Chinese, doesn't send.

| `value` | `string` |  | The text in the box, when you keep it. Use it with `onValueChange`. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | The text in the box to begin with, when it's kept here. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void)` |  | Called with the text as it's typed, and with nothing after a send. |
| `onSubmit` | `((text: string, submission: PromptInputSubmission) => void)` |  | Called with the text when it's sent, by Enter or by the button, and with the files that were waiting. The box is emptied after. Text that's only spaces isn't sent, unless there are files to go with it. |
| `files` | `File[]` |  | The files waiting to be sent, when you keep them. Use it with `onFilesChange`. |
| `defaultFiles` | `File[]` |  | The files waiting to begin with, when they're kept here. |
| `onFilesChange` | `((files: File[]) => void)` |  | Called with all of them when one is added or taken out. |
| `accept` | `string` |  | The kinds of file it takes, written as a file input's `accept`: `"image/*,.pdf"`. Left out, it takes any. |
| `maxFiles` | `number` |  | The most files that can wait at once. |
| `maxFileSize` | `number` |  | The largest a file may be, in bytes. |
| `onFilesReject` | `((rejections: PromptInputFileRejection[]) => void)` |  | Called with the files that were turned away and the reason for each. Nothing is shown for them, so this is where you tell the person. |
| `busy` | `boolean` | `false` | A reply is on its way. Nothing can be sent until it's `false` again, and what's typed meanwhile is kept. With `onStop`, the button to send becomes a button to stop. |
| `onStop` | `(() => void)` |  | Called by the button to stop, while `busy`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Nothing can be typed or sent. |

It also takes the attributes of a `form`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Sends, where there's a keyboard. |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Starts a new line. |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Goes from the field to the buttons in the row, and on to the button that sends. |

### What the component handles

- It's a real `form` with a real `textarea`, so it works with a password manager, dictation and a browser's own spell check.
- The button that sends is named "Send", and "Stop" while it stops a reply.
- With nothing to send, the button is marked as disabled with `aria-disabled` and stays in the tab order. A button that left the tab order would be missed by someone feeling out the form with Tab.
- When the field has focus from the keyboard, the ring goes round the whole box.
- After a send, focus is back in the field.
- The text is 16 pixels on a touch screen, which keeps iOS from zooming the page when the field takes focus.
- The button that attaches is named "Attach files". The files that wait are a list named "Files to send", and each has a button named after it: "Remove scan.pdf".
- When a file is added or taken out, how many are waiting is said to a screen reader: "2 files attached".
- When a file is taken out, focus goes to the field. Its button went with it.
- Dropping is a shortcut for a mouse. The button does the same with a keyboard and on a touch screen.

### What you need to handle

- Name the field with `aria-label`, or a `<label>`. The placeholder isn't a name: it's gone as soon as something is typed.
- Translate `label` and `stopLabel`, and for files `removeLabel` and `announce`.
- Tell the person when a file is turned away, and why, from `onFilesReject`. Use a `role="alert"`, or a [toast](page:components/toast).
- If there's a limit on the text, say what's left where a screen reader finds it, with `aria-describedby`.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

The button that sends is 44 pixels on a touch screen and 36 with a mouse, and so is the button that attaches. Enter starts a new line there, as said above.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

PromptInput starts with `"use client"`: it keeps what's typed. `onSubmit` is a function, so the box is rendered from a client component of yours.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Leave the field open while a reply arrives.
- Give it `onStop` if a reply can be stopped. A long answer to the wrong question is a long wait.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for a search field or a comment box. Those are an [`Input`](page:components/input) and a [`Textarea`](page:components/textarea).
- Don't put more in the row than fits on a phone. A menu holds the rest.

# PromptSuggestion Prompts to start from, as buttons in a row that wraps, for a conversation with nothing in it yet. Use suggestions to show what can be asked, where someone would otherwise face an empty box. A press sends one, or puts it in the box to be changed first. ```tsx "use client"; import { PromptInput, PromptInputSubmit, PromptInputTextarea, PromptInputToolbar, PromptSuggestion, PromptSuggestions, } from "@nuvui/chat"; import { useRef, useState } from "react"; const starters = [ "Summarize last month's invoices", "Who hasn't paid yet?", "Draft a reminder for an overdue invoice", ]; export default function Example() { const [text, setText] = useState(""); const field = useRef(null); return (
{starters.map((starter) => ( { // Into the box, to be changed before it's sent. setText(starter); field.current?.focus(); }} > {starter} ))} {}}>
); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/chat @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { PromptSuggestion, PromptSuggestions } from "@nuvui/chat"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/chat/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Chat](page:chat/index) covers that. ```tsx send("Who hasn't paid yet?")}> Who hasn't paid yet? ``` ## What a press does A suggestion is a button, and what it does is yours. Two things are common: - **Send it.** One press and the conversation has started. Right when the suggestions are whole questions. - **Put it in the box.** Set the [prompt box](page:chat/prompt-input)'s `value` and move focus to the field, as the example above does. Right when a suggestion is a start to finish, such as "Draft a reminder for". ## In an empty conversation Inside a [`ConversationEmpty`](page:chat/conversation#before-the-first-message) they sit in the middle, under a greeting. ```tsx "use client"; import { Conversation, ConversationContent, ConversationEmpty, Message, MessageContent, PromptInput, PromptInputSubmit, PromptInputTextarea, PromptInputToolbar, PromptSuggestion, PromptSuggestions, } from "@nuvui/chat"; import { useState } from "react"; const starters = [ "Summarize last month's invoices", "Who hasn't paid yet?", "Draft a reminder", ]; export default function Example() { const [sent, setSent] = useState([]); return ( {sent.length === 0 ? (

What do you want to know?

{starters.map((text) => ( setSent((now) => [...now, text])} > {text} ))} ) : ( sent.map((text, index) => ( {text} )) )}
setSent((now) => [...now, text])}>
); } ``` ## Props `PromptSuggestions` takes `label` and the attributes of a `div`: | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `label` | `string` | `"Suggestions"` | The name of the group for a screen reader. | `PromptSuggestion` takes the attributes of a `button`. Both pass `ref` to their element. ## Accessibility ### What the component handles - The suggestions are a group named "Suggestions", and each is a real button named by its text. - A suggestion is 44 pixels tall on a touch screen and 36 with a mouse. Its text wraps, so a long one doesn't make the page scroll sideways. ### What you need to handle - Translate `label`. - If a press sends, move focus to where the reply will be, or leave it to the conversation: the button is gone once there are messages. ## CSS variables | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-prompt-suggestion-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 2)` | Space between two suggestions. | | `--nuv-prompt-suggestion-justify` | `center` | Where the suggestions sit in their row: center, start or end. | | `--nuv-prompt-suggestion-border` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Color of its edge. Keep it at 3:1 against what's behind it. | | `--nuv-prompt-suggestion-radius` | `var(--radius-full)` | Corner radius of a suggestion. | | `--nuv-prompt-suggestion-bg` | `var(--color-background)` | Background of a suggestion. | | `--nuv-prompt-suggestion-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of its text. | | `--nuv-prompt-suggestion-hover-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Its background under the pointer. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-prompt-suggestion` | PromptSuggestion | | `.nuv-prompt-suggestions` | PromptSuggestions | ## Server components Neither has `"use client"` or state. `onClick` is a function, so they're rendered from a client component of yours. ## Do and don't **Do** - Keep each to a few words, and to three or four of them. - Write what your assistant is good at, in the words your users would use. **Don't** - Don't keep them on screen once the conversation has started. - Don't suggest what the assistant can't do.
