pages.title: Attachment
pages.description: A file shown in a message or waiting in the prompt box, with its name, its size, a picture where there is one, and a button that takes it out.
pages.markdown:
# Attachment A file shown in a message or waiting in the prompt box, with its name, its size, a picture where there is one, and a button that takes it out. Use an attachment for each file that goes with a message: the ones a person sent, the ones an assistant made, and the ones waiting in the [prompt box](page:chat/prompt-input) to be sent. ```tsx import { Attachment, Attachments, Message, MessageContent } from "@nuvui/chat"; // A picture that needs no server: three bars of a chart. const chart = `data:image/svg+xml,${encodeURIComponent( '', )}`; export default function Example() { return (
Here are the two files. Is the total in the chart right?
); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/chat @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Attachment, Attachments } from "@nuvui/chat"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/chat/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Chat](page:chat/index) covers that. ```tsx ``` ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `Attachments` | The list. The files sit side by side and wrap. | | `Attachment` | One file. | ## What a file shows `name` is the only thing a file needs. `size` is a number of bytes, written in the reader's own number format. `detail` is a word or two before it. A long name is cut short with an ellipsis, and the whole of it is the name's `title`. `src` puts a small picture in place of the icon. For a file that's a picture, that's the picture itself. It's decoration: the name says what the file is, so the picture has no text of its own. With `href` the name is a link that opens the file. `linkProps` takes the rest of a link's attributes, such as `download` or `target`. ## Waiting, uploading and failed `onRemove` gives a file a button that takes it out. `uploading` shows a spinner where the icon was and "Uploading" where the size was. `error` takes what went wrong, in words, and shows it in place of the size. ```tsx "use client"; import { Attachment, Attachments } from "@nuvui/chat"; import { Button } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; const all = [ { name: "contract-draft.docx", size: 48_200 }, { name: "site-photos.zip", size: 18_400_000, uploading: true }, { name: "scan-0042.tiff", size: 61_000_000, error: "Too large. The limit is 25 MB.", }, ]; export default function Example() { const [files, setFiles] = useState(all); return (
{files.map((file) => ( setFiles((now) => now.filter((other) => other !== file)) } /> ))}

{files.length} of 3 files left.

); } ``` The prompt box draws the files that wait in it with this component, and keeps the list for you. [PromptInput](page:chat/prompt-input#files) covers that. ## Attachment props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `name` (required) | `string` | | The file's name. | | `size` | `number` | | Its size in bytes, written after the name. | | `detail` | `ReactNode` | | A word or two about it, before the size: "PDF", "3 pages". | | `src` | `string` | | The address of a small picture of it, shown in place of the icon. For a file that's a picture, the picture itself. | | `href` | `string` | | Where the file opens. With it, the name is a link. | | `linkProps` | `Omit, "href">` | | More for that link: `target`, `download`, `rel`. | | `icon` | `ReactNode` | | In place of the icon, for a file with no picture. | | `uploading` | `boolean` | `false` | The file is on its way to the server. A spinner takes the icon's place and `uploadingLabel` the size's. | | `uploadingLabel` | `string` | `"Uploading"` | | | `error` | `ReactNode` | | What went wrong with it, in words. Shown in place of the size, and the file is drawn as one that failed. | | `onRemove` | `(() => void)` | | With it, the file has a button that calls this. | | `removeLabel` | `((name: string) => string)` | `(name) => 'Remove ${name}'` | The name of that button, from the file's name. | | `formatSize` | `((bytes: number) => string)` | `The size in the reader's own number format, such as "1.2 MB"` | Writes the size, from a number of bytes. | It also takes the attributes of an `li`. `Attachments` takes the attributes of a `ul`. Both pass `ref` to their element. ## Accessibility ### What the component handles - The files are a list, so a screen reader says how many there are. It's still called a list in Safari, which stops saying so once the bullets are styled away. - The button that takes a file out is named after its file: "Remove october-invoices.pdf". - A file that's uploading has `aria-busy`, and says "Uploading" in text. - A file that failed says why in text. The red edge is for the eye and isn't the only sign. - The picture and the icon are hidden from screen readers. - The button is 44 pixels on a touch screen and 28 with a mouse. ### What you need to handle - Name the list with `aria-label`: "Files with this message", "Files to send". - Write `error` so that it says what to do: "Too large. The limit is 25 MB." - A file that fails some time after it was added changes on a page the reader may not be looking at. Say so where it will be heard, with a [toast](page:components/toast) or a `role="alert"` of your own. - When a file is taken out, its button goes with it. Move focus somewhere that's still there. The prompt box does this for the files it keeps. - Translate `removeLabel` and `uploadingLabel`. ## CSS variables Set any of these on an `Attachments`, or on anything around it. ```css .chat { --nuv-attachment-max-width: 20rem; --nuv-attachment-radius: var(--radius-md); } ``` | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-attachment-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 2)` | Space between the files. | | `--nuv-attachment-max-width` | `16rem` | The widest a file gets before its name is cut short. | | `--nuv-attachment-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of its edge. | | `--nuv-attachment-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of a file. | | `--nuv-attachment-bg` | `var(--color-background)` | Background of a file. | | `--nuv-attachment-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of the name. | | `--nuv-attachment-error-border` | `var(--color-danger)` | Color of the edge of a file that failed. | | `--nuv-attachment-picture-size` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 9)` | Width and height of the picture. | | `--nuv-attachment-picture-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background behind the icon. | | `--nuv-attachment-picture-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the icon. Keep it at 3:1. | | `--nuv-attachment-detail-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the line under the name. Keep it at 4.5:1. | | `--nuv-attachment-error-fg` | `var(--color-danger)` | Color of what went wrong. Keep it at 4.5:1. | | `--nuv-attachment-remove-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the cross in the button. Keep it at 3:1. | | `--nuv-attachment-remove-hover-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of the button under the pointer. | | `--nuv-attachment-remove-hover-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of its cross under the pointer. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-attachment` | Attachment | | `.nuv-attachment__detail` | The detail and the size, or that it's uploading. | | `.nuv-attachment__error` | What went wrong. | | `.nuv-attachment__image` | The picture, from src. | | `.nuv-attachment__name` | The name. A link when there's an href. | | `.nuv-attachment__picture` | The box the icon, the picture or the spinner is in. | | `.nuv-attachment__remove` | The button that takes it out. | | `.nuv-attachment__text` | The name and the line under it. | | `.nuv-attachments` | Attachments | A file has `data-uploading` while it uploads and `data-error` when it has failed. ## Server components Neither part is a client component. A server component can render both, without the functions: `onRemove`, `removeLabel`, `formatSize`. ## Do and don't **Do** - Give a file its real name. It's what the reader looks for. - Show a file that failed where it was, with the reason, and leave the button that takes it out. **Don't** - Don't show a preview of a whole document here. This is a file's name tag. What's in it opens from the link. - Don't rely on the picture to say what a file is.

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/chat @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { Attachment, Attachments } from "@nuvui/chat";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/chat/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Chat](page:chat/index) covers that.

```tsx
<Attachments aria-label="Files with this message">
  <Attachment name="october-invoices.pdf" detail="PDF" size={248000} />
</Attachments>
```

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Attachments` | The list. The files sit side by side and wrap. |
| `Attachment` | One file. |

sections.heading: What a file shows
sections.markdown:
## What a file shows

`name` is the only thing a file needs. `size` is a number of bytes, written in the reader's own number format. `detail` is a word or two before it. A long name is cut short with an ellipsis, and the whole of it is the name's `title`.

`src` puts a small picture in place of the icon. For a file that's a picture, that's the picture itself. It's decoration: the name says what the file is, so the picture has no text of its own.

With `href` the name is a link that opens the file. `linkProps` takes the rest of a link's attributes, such as `download` or `target`.

sections.heading: Waiting, uploading and failed
Attachment props
sections.markdown:
## Attachment props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | The file's name. |
| `size` | `number` |  | Its size in bytes, written after the name. |
| `detail` | `ReactNode` |  | A word or two about it, before the size: "PDF", "3 pages". |
| `src` | `string` |  | The address of a small picture of it, shown in place of the icon. For a file that's a picture, the picture itself. |
| `href` | `string` |  | Where the file opens. With it, the name is a link. |
| `linkProps` | `Omit<AnchorHTMLAttributes<HTMLAnchorElement>, "href">` |  | More for that link: `target`, `download`, `rel`. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` |  | In place of the icon, for a file with no picture. |
| `uploading` | `boolean` | `false` | The file is on its way to the server. A spinner takes the icon's place and `uploadingLabel` the size's. |
| `uploadingLabel` | `string` | `"Uploading"` |  |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | What went wrong with it, in words. Shown in place of the size, and the file is drawn as one that failed. |
| `onRemove` | `(() => void)` |  | With it, the file has a button that calls this. |
| `removeLabel` | `((name: string) => string)` | `(name) => 'Remove ${name}'` | The name of that button, from the file's name. |
| `formatSize` | `((bytes: number) => string)` | `The size in the reader's own number format, such as "1.2 MB"` | Writes the size, from a number of bytes. |

It also takes the attributes of an `li`. `Attachments` takes the attributes of a `ul`. Both pass `ref` to their element.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### What the component handles

- The files are a list, so a screen reader says how many there are. It's still called a list in Safari, which stops saying so once the bullets are styled away.
- The button that takes a file out is named after its file: "Remove october-invoices.pdf".
- A file that's uploading has `aria-busy`, and says "Uploading" in text.
- A file that failed says why in text. The red edge is for the eye and isn't the only sign.
- The picture and the icon are hidden from screen readers.
- The button is 44 pixels on a touch screen and 28 with a mouse.

### What you need to handle

- Name the list with `aria-label`: "Files with this message", "Files to send".
- Write `error` so that it says what to do: "Too large. The limit is 25 MB."
- A file that fails some time after it was added changes on a page the reader may not be looking at. Say so where it will be heard, with a [toast](page:components/toast) or a `role="alert"` of your own.
- When a file is taken out, its button goes with it. Move focus somewhere that's still there. The prompt box does this for the files it keeps.
- Translate `removeLabel` and `uploadingLabel`.

sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on an `Attachments`, or on anything around it.

```css
.chat {
  --nuv-attachment-max-width: 20rem;
  --nuv-attachment-radius: var(--radius-md);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-attachment-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 2)` | Space between the files. |
| `--nuv-attachment-max-width` | `16rem` | The widest a file gets before its name is cut short. |
| `--nuv-attachment-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of its edge. |
| `--nuv-attachment-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of a file. |
| `--nuv-attachment-bg` | `var(--color-background)` | Background of a file. |
| `--nuv-attachment-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of the name. |
| `--nuv-attachment-error-border` | `var(--color-danger)` | Color of the edge of a file that failed. |
| `--nuv-attachment-picture-size` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 9)` | Width and height of the picture. |
| `--nuv-attachment-picture-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background behind the icon. |
| `--nuv-attachment-picture-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the icon. Keep it at 3:1. |
| `--nuv-attachment-detail-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the line under the name. Keep it at 4.5:1. |
| `--nuv-attachment-error-fg` | `var(--color-danger)` | Color of what went wrong. Keep it at 4.5:1. |
| `--nuv-attachment-remove-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the cross in the button. Keep it at 3:1. |
| `--nuv-attachment-remove-hover-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of the button under the pointer. |
| `--nuv-attachment-remove-hover-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of its cross under the pointer. |

sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-attachment` | Attachment |
| `.nuv-attachment__detail` | The detail and the size, or that it's uploading. |
| `.nuv-attachment__error` | What went wrong. |
| `.nuv-attachment__image` | The picture, from src. |
| `.nuv-attachment__name` | The name. A link when there's an href. |

A file has `data-uploading` while it uploads and `data-error` when it has failed.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

Neither part is a client component. A server component can render both, without the functions: `onRemove`, `removeLabel`, `formatSize`.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Give a file its real name. It's what the reader looks for.
- Show a file that failed where it was, with the reason, and leave the button that takes it out.

**Don't**

- Don't show a preview of a whole document here. This is a file's name tag. What's in it opens from the link.
- Don't rely on the picture to say what a file is.

pages.title: ToolCall
pages.description: Something an assistant did, or asks to do, with a tool. A card with the tool's name and where the call stands, which opens to what was asked and what came back, and asks for approval when it needs it.
pages.markdown:
# ToolCall Something an assistant did, or asks to do, with a tool. A card with the tool's name and where the call stands, which opens to what was asked and what came back, and asks for approval when it needs it. Use a tool call where an assistant acts and doesn't only answer: it searches, reads a record, sends something. The card says which tool and where the call stands. What was asked and what came back are a press away, for the reader who wants to check. ```tsx import { ToolCall, ToolCallContent, ToolCallError, ToolCallInput, ToolCallOutput, ToolCallTrigger, } from "@nuvui/chat"; export default function Example() { return (
Search invoices Look up the customer Read the bank feed The bank didn't answer within 30 seconds.
); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/chat @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { ToolCall, ToolCallApproval, ToolCallContent, ToolCallError, ToolCallInput, ToolCallOutput, ToolCallTrigger, } from "@nuvui/chat"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/chat/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Chat](page:chat/index) covers that. ```tsx Search invoices ``` ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `ToolCall` | The card. `status` says where the call stands. | | `ToolCallTrigger` | Its top line: the tool's name and the status. It opens and closes the card. | | `ToolCallContent` | What the card shows when it's open. | | `ToolCallInput` | What the tool was asked. | | `ToolCallOutput` | What it answered. | | `ToolCallError` | What went wrong, for a call that failed. | | `ToolCallApproval` | The question and its two buttons, for a call that waits to be allowed. | ## Where a call stands `status` is one of five. Each has an icon and words beside the tool's name, so the icon and its color are never the only sign. | `status` | Words | When | | --- | --- | --- | | `"running"` | Running | The tool has been asked and hasn't answered. | | `"approval"` | Needs approval | It waits for the person to allow it. | | `"done"` | Done | It answered. | | `"error"` | Failed | It failed. | | `"denied"` | Denied | The person didn't allow it. | `statusLabel` on the trigger changes the words, for another language or for something more exact: "Done in 2 seconds". ## What was asked and what came back `ToolCallInput` and `ToolCallOutput` take a `value`. Text is shown as it is. Anything else is shown as indented JSON. A long answer scrolls inside its box, up to 16rem tall. Pass children in place of `value` to draw it your own way: a table for rows, a picture for a chart. Name the tool in words a person would use. "Search invoices" says more than `search_invoices`. ## Asking first Some calls shouldn't run until a person says so: the ones that send, pay, or delete. Set `status="approval"` and put a `ToolCallApproval` in the card with the question. It's drawn only while the call waits, and outside the part that opens, so it's seen with the card closed. ```tsx "use client"; import { ToolCall, ToolCallApproval, ToolCallContent, ToolCallInput, ToolCallOutput, type ToolCallStatus, ToolCallTrigger, } from "@nuvui/chat"; import { Button } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { const [status, setStatus] = useState("approval"); const timer = useRef>(undefined); useEffect(() => () => clearTimeout(timer.current), []); // Stands in for the tool doing its work. function approve() { setStatus("running"); timer.current = setTimeout(() => setStatus("done"), 1500); } return (
Send a reminder {status === "done" ? : null} setStatus("denied")} > Send a reminder for INV-1042 to Contoso?
); } ``` What happens next is yours. `onApprove` and `onDeny` tell you which button was pressed, and you move `status` on: to `"running"` and then `"done"`, or to `"denied"`. When a button is pressed, both go. Focus moves to the card's top line first, so it isn't left on nothing. ## Open or closed A card starts closed. `defaultOpen` starts it open, and `open` with `onOpenChange` lets you keep it. These are the [Collapsible](page:components/collapsible)'s props, which `ToolCall` is built on. ## ToolCall props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `status` (required) | `"approval" \| "denied" \| "done" \| "error" \| "running"` | | Where the call stands. | It also takes the props of a [Collapsible](page:components/collapsible#props). ## ToolCallTrigger props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `children` (required) | `ReactNode` | | What the tool is called, in words a person would use. | | `statusLabel` | `ReactNode` | `"Running", "Needs approval", "Done", "Failed" or "Denied"` | Where the call stands, in words. It's written beside the name, so the icon and its color aren't the only way to tell. | ## ToolCallInput and ToolCallOutput props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `label` | `ReactNode` | | The heading over it. | | `value` | `unknown` | | What to show. Text is shown as it is, and anything else as indented JSON. | | `children` | `ReactNode` | | In place of `value`, drawn your own way: a table, a picture. | `label` is "Request" for the one and "Result" for the other. ## ToolCallApproval props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `children` (required) | `ReactNode` | | What's being asked: what the tool will do if it's allowed. | | `onApprove` | `(() => void)` | | Called by the button that allows it. | | `onDeny` | `(() => void)` | | Called by the button that doesn't. | | `approveLabel` | `ReactNode` | `"Approve"` | | | `denyLabel` | `ReactNode` | `"Deny"` | | | `label` | `string` | `"Approval"` | The name of the group for a screen reader. | ## ToolCallError props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `label` | `ReactNode` | `"Error"` | The heading over it. | `ToolCallContent` takes the attributes of a `div`. Every part passes `ref` to its element. ## Accessibility ### Keyboard | Key | What it does | | --- | --- | | Enter or Space | On the top line, opens or closes the card. | | Tab | Goes from the top line into what's open, and to the two buttons when the call waits. | | Arrow keys | Scroll a long request or result that has focus. | ### What the component handles - The top line is a button with `aria-expanded`. sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/chat @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import {
  ToolCall,
  ToolCallApproval,
  ToolCallContent,
  ToolCallError,
  ToolCallInput,
  ToolCallOutput,
  ToolCallTrigger,
} from "@nuvui/chat";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/chat/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Chat](page:chat/index) covers that.

```tsx
<ToolCall status="done">
  <ToolCallTrigger>Search invoices</ToolCallTrigger>
  <ToolCallContent>
    <ToolCallInput value={{ status: "overdue" }} />
    <ToolCallOutput value={result} />
  </ToolCallContent>
</ToolCall>
```

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `ToolCall` | The card. `status` says where the call stands. |
| `ToolCallTrigger` | Its top line: the tool's name and the status. It opens and closes the card. |
| `ToolCallContent` | What the card shows when it's open. |
| `ToolCallInput` | What the tool was asked. |
| `ToolCallOutput` | What it answered. |
| `ToolCallError` | What went wrong, for a call that failed. |
| `ToolCallApproval` | The question and its two buttons, for a call that waits to be allowed. |

sections.heading: Where a call stands
sections.markdown:
## Where a call stands

`status` is one of five. Each has an icon and words beside the tool's name, so the icon and its color are never the only sign.

| `status` | Words | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"running"` | Running | The tool has been asked and hasn't answered. |
| `"approval"` | Needs approval | It waits for the person to allow it. |
| `"done"` | Done | It answered. |
| `"error"` | Failed | It failed. |
| `"denied"` | Denied | The person didn't allow it. |

`statusLabel` on the trigger changes the words, for another language or for something more exact: "Done in 2 seconds".

sections.heading: What was asked and what came back
sections.markdown:
## What was asked and what came back

`ToolCallInput` and `ToolCallOutput` take a `value`. Text is shown as it is. Anything else is shown as indented JSON. A long answer scrolls inside its box, up to 16rem tall.

Pass children in place of `value` to draw it your own way: a table for rows, a picture for a chart.

Name the tool in words a person would use. "Search invoices" says more than `search_invoices`.

sections.heading: Asking first
Open or closed
sections.markdown:
## Open or closed

A card starts closed. `defaultOpen` starts it open, and `open` with `onOpenChange` lets you keep it. These are the [Collapsible](page:components/collapsible)'s props, which `ToolCall` is built on.

sections.heading: ToolCall props
sections.markdown:
## ToolCall props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `status` (required) | `"approval" \| "denied" \| "done" \| "error" \| "running"` |  | Where the call stands. |

It also takes the props of a [Collapsible](page:components/collapsible#props).

sections.heading: ToolCallTrigger props
sections.markdown:
## ToolCallTrigger props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | What the tool is called, in words a person would use. |
| `statusLabel` | `ReactNode` | `"Running", "Needs approval", "Done", "Failed" or "Denied"` | Where the call stands, in words. It's written beside the name, so the icon and its color aren't the only way to tell. |

sections.heading: ToolCallInput and ToolCallOutput props
sections.markdown:
## ToolCallInput and ToolCallOutput props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | The heading over it. |
| `value` | `unknown` |  | What to show. Text is shown as it is, and anything else as indented JSON. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | In place of `value`, drawn your own way: a table, a picture. |

`label` is "Request" for the one and "Result" for the other.

sections.heading: ToolCallApproval props
sections.markdown:
## ToolCallApproval props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | What's being asked: what the tool will do if it's allowed. |
| `onApprove` | `(() => void)` |  | Called by the button that allows it. |
| `onDeny` | `(() => void)` |  | Called by the button that doesn't. |
| `approveLabel` | `ReactNode` | `"Approve"` |  |
| `denyLabel` | `ReactNode` | `"Deny"` |  |
| `label` | `string` | `"Approval"` | The name of the group for a screen reader. |

sections.heading: ToolCallError props
sections.markdown:
## ToolCallError props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | `"Error"` | The heading over it. |

`ToolCallContent` takes the attributes of a `div`. Every part passes `ref` to its element.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> | On the top line, opens or closes the card. |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Goes from the top line into what's open, and to the two buttons when the call waits. |
| Arrow keys | Scroll a long request or result that has focus. |

### What the component handles

- The top line is a button with `aria-expanded`. Its name is the tool's name and the status, so "Search invoices, Done" is read as one.
- The status is words as well as an icon and a color.
- The question and its buttons are a group with a name, "Approval".
- A request or a result that's long enough to scroll can take focus, and is named by its heading.
- Pressing a button that then goes away doesn't drop focus on the page.
- The top line is 44 pixels tall.

### What you need to handle

- Write the question so it says what will happen: "Send a reminder for INV-1042 to Contoso?", not "Allow this tool?".
- Translate `statusLabel`, the sections' `label`, `approveLabel` and `denyLabel`.
- Don't put anything in a request or a result that the reader shouldn't see. It's on the page, a press away.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on a `ToolCall`, or on anything around it.

```css
.chat {
  --nuv-tool-call-radius: var(--radius-md);
  --nuv-tool-call-code-max-height: 24rem;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-tool-call-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of its edge and of the lines inside it. |
| `--nuv-tool-call-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of the card. |
| `--nuv-tool-call-bg` | `var(--color-background)` | Background of the card. |
| `--nuv-tool-call-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of the text. |
| `--nuv-tool-call-hover-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of the top line under the pointer. |
| `--nuv-tool-call-icon-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the status icon and the arrow. Keep it at 3:1. |
| `--nuv-tool-call-error-fg` | `var(--color-danger)` | Color of what went wrong, and of a failed call's icon. Keep it at 4.5:1. |
| `--nuv-tool-call-status-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the status words. Keep it at 4.5:1. |
| `--nuv-tool-call-label-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of a section's heading. Keep it at 4.5:1. |
| `--nuv-tool-call-code-max-height` | `16rem` | How tall a request or a result gets before it scrolls. |
| `--nuv-tool-call-code-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of a request or a result. |
| `--nuv-tool-call-code-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of its text. Keep it at 4.5:1 against the background. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-tool-call` | ToolCall |
| `.nuv-tool-call__approval` | ToolCallApproval |
| `.nuv-tool-call__body` | ToolCallContent |
| `.nuv-tool-call__chevron` | The arrow, which turns when the card opens. |
| `.nuv-tool-call__choices` | The two buttons. |
| `.nuv-tool-call__code` | The box a request or a result scrolls in. |
| `.nuv-tool-call__error` | What went wrong. |
| `.nuv-tool-call__icon` | The status icon. |
| `.nuv-tool-call__label` | A section's heading. |
| `.nuv-tool-call__name` | The tool's name. |
| `.nuv-tool-call__pre` | The text in it. |
| `.nuv-tool-call__question` | The question. |
| `.nuv-tool-call__section` | ToolCallInput, ToolCallOutput and ToolCallError. |
| `.nuv-tool-call__status` | The status, in words. |
| `.nuv-tool-call__trigger` | ToolCallTrigger |

The card has `data-status`, and `data-state`, `"open"` or `"closed"`. A section has `data-kind`: `"input"`, `"output"` or `"error"`.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

ToolCall starts with `"use client"`, since the card opens and closes. A server component can render a call that's over, without the functions: `onOpenChange`, `onApprove`, `onDeny`.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Ask first for anything that can't be taken back.
- Show a call that failed as failed, with what went wrong.

**Don't**

- Don't open every card by default. The reply is what the reader came for.
- Don't use the color of the status as its only sign if you restyle. Keep the words.

pages.title: Reasoning
pages.description: How an assistant got to its reply. A line over the reply that opens to the steps it took, open while it works and closed once it has answered.
pages.markdown:
# Reasoning How an assistant got to its reply. A line over the reply that opens to the steps it took, open while it works and closed once it has answered. Use reasoning over a reply to show how it was reached: what was looked up, what was checked. It's open while the assistant works, so the wait has something in it, and closes when the reply arrives, since the reply is what the reader came for. ```tsx import { Message, MessageContent, Reasoning, ReasoningContent, ReasoningStep, ReasoningSteps, ReasoningTrigger, } from "@nuvui/chat"; export default function Example() { return (
Thought for 6 seconds Two are past their due date. 30 days, with a reminder on day 31. Two invoices are overdue: INV-1042 by 12 days and INV-1057 by 3.
); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/chat @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Reasoning, ReasoningContent, ReasoningStep, ReasoningSteps, ReasoningTrigger, } from "@nuvui/chat"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/chat/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Chat](page:chat/index) covers that. ```tsx {thoughts} ``` ## Parts | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `Reasoning` | The whole of it. It keeps whether the steps are open. | | `ReasoningTrigger` | The line that opens and closes them. | | `ReasoningContent` | What opens. | | `ReasoningSteps` | A list of steps, in the order they were taken. | | `ReasoningStep` | One step. | ## Text or steps `ReasoningContent` takes either. If the model gives you its thinking as text, put the text in. If your app knows the steps, such as each tool that was called, put a `ReasoningSteps` in with a `ReasoningStep` for each. A step has a `label` and, as children, a line more about it. ## While the assistant works Set `streaming` for as long as it's thinking. The steps open, the line shimmers, and the step with `status="active"` shows a spinner. When `streaming` goes back to `false` they close. ```tsx "use client"; import { Message, MessageContent, MessageLoader, Reasoning, ReasoningContent, ReasoningStep, ReasoningSteps, ReasoningTrigger, } from "@nuvui/chat"; import { Button } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useEffect, useState } from "react"; const steps = [ "Looked up Contoso's open invoices", "Checked the payment terms", "Worked out how late each one is", ]; export default function Example() { // How many steps have been taken. One more than there are, and the // reply is written. const [taken, setTaken] = useState(steps.length + 1); const thinking = taken <= steps.length; // Stands in for the assistant: a step every 900 milliseconds. useEffect(() => { if (!thinking) return; const timer = setInterval(() => setTaken((now) => now + 1), 900); return () => clearInterval(timer); }, [thinking]); return (
{thinking ? "Thinking" : "Thought for 3 seconds"} {steps.slice(0, taken + 1).map((step, index) => ( ))} {thinking ? ( ) : ( Two invoices are overdue: INV-1042 by 12 days and INV-1057 by 3. )}
); } ``` If the reader opens or closes the steps themselves, that's kept: from then on `streaming` doesn't move them. Someone who closed them isn't shown them again, and someone who opened them to read isn't interrupted. ## What the line says Left empty, the trigger says "Thinking" while `streaming` and "Reasoning" after. Say more if you know more, such as how long it took: "Thought for 6 seconds". ## Open or closed Without `streaming` it starts closed. `defaultOpen` starts it open, and `open` with `onOpenChange` lets you keep it, in which case `streaming` asks through `onOpenChange` and you decide. These are the [Collapsible](page:components/collapsible)'s props, which `Reasoning` is built on. ## Reasoning props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `streaming` | `boolean` | `false` | The assistant is still working it out. The steps are open for as long as it is, and close when it's done, unless the reader opened or closed them in the meantime: then they stay as the reader left them. | It also takes the props of a [Collapsible](page:components/collapsible#props). ## ReasoningStep props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `label` (required) | `ReactNode` | | What was done, in a few words. | | `status` | `"active" \| "done"` | `"done"` | `"active"` for the step that's being taken now. It shows a spinner and is marked as the current step. | | `children` | `ReactNode` | | More about it, under the label. | It also takes the attributes of an `li`. `ReasoningTrigger` takes the attributes of a `button`, `ReasoningContent` of a `div` and `ReasoningSteps` of an `ol`. Every part passes `ref` to its element. ## Accessibility ### Keyboard | Key | What it does | | --- | --- | | Enter or Space | On the line, opens or closes the steps. | ### What the component handles - The line is a button with `aria-expanded`, tied to what it opens. - While it's closed, the steps aren't in the page for a screen reader or for Tab. - The steps are an ordered list. The one being taken has `aria-current="step"`. - The shimmer and the spinner stand still for someone who has asked for less motion. - The tick and the spinner are hidden from screen readers. The label says what the step is. - The line is 44 pixels tall on a touch screen. ### What you need to handle - Put it in a [`Message`](page:chat/message) that has `streaming` for as long as the reply is being written. Then a screen reader isn't read each step as it arrives, and reads the message once it's whole. - Write each `label` as what was done: "Checked the payment terms". - Translate what the trigger says. ## CSS variables Set any of these on a `Reasoning`, or on anything around it. ```css .chat { --nuv-reasoning-line: var(--color-primary); } ``` | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-reasoning-trigger-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the line that opens the steps. Keep it at 4.5:1. | | `--nuv-reasoning-trigger-hover-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Its color under the pointer. | | `--nuv-reasoning-line` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of the line down the side. | | `--nuv-reasoning-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the text that opens, and of a step's detail. Keep it at 4.5:1. | | `--nuv-reasoning-label-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of a step's label. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-reasoning` | Reasoning | | `.nuv-reasoning__body` | ReasoningContent: what's inside it, with the line down its side. | | `.nuv-reasoning__chevron` | The arrow in it, which turns when the steps open. | | `.nuv-reasoning__content` | The part that opens, whose height is animated. | | `.nuv-reasoning__detail` | The detail, from the step's children. | | `.nuv-reasoning__label` | The label. | | `.nuv-reasoning__marker` | The tick, or the spinner. | | `.nuv-reasoning__step` | ReasoningStep | | `.nuv-reasoning__steps` | ReasoningSteps | | `.nuv-reasoning__text` | The label and the detail. | | `.nuv-reasoning__trigger` | ReasoningTrigger | `Reasoning` has `data-streaming` while the assistant works, and `data-state`, `"open"` or `"closed"`. A step has `data-status`, `"done"` or `"active"`. ## Server components Reasoning starts with `"use client"`, since the steps open and close. A server component can render a finished one, without `onOpenChange`. ## Do and don't **Do** - Close it once the reply is there, which `streaming` does for you. - Show the steps that were really taken. **Don't** - Don't put the reply itself in it. What the reader needs is under it, in the message. - Don't use it for progress through a form or a checkout. That's a [Stepper](page:components/stepper).

- The steps are an ordered list. The one being taken has `aria-current="step"`.
- The shimmer and the spinner stand still for someone who has asked for less motion.
- The tick and the spinner are hidden from screen readers. The label says what the step is.
- The line is 44 pixels tall on a touch screen.

### What you need to handle

- Put it in a [`Message`](page:chat/message) that has `streaming` for as long as the reply is being written. Then a screen reader isn't read each step as it arrives, and reads the message once it's whole.
- Write each `label` as what was done: "Checked the payment terms".
- Translate what the trigger says.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on a `Reasoning`, or on anything around it.

```css
.chat {
  --nuv-reasoning-line: var(--color-primary);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-reasoning-trigger-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the line that opens the steps. Keep it at 4.5:1. |
| `--nuv-reasoning-trigger-hover-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Its color under the pointer. |
| `--nuv-reasoning-line` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of the line down the side. |
| `--nuv-reasoning-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the text that opens, and of a step's detail. Keep it at 4.5:1. |
| `--nuv-reasoning-label-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of a step's label. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-reasoning` | Reasoning |
| `.nuv-reasoning__body` | ReasoningContent: what's inside it, with the line down its side. |
| `.nuv-reasoning__chevron` | The arrow in it, which turns when the steps open. |
| `.nuv-reasoning__content` | The part that opens, whose height is animated. |
| `.nuv-reasoning__detail` | The detail, from the step's children. |
| `.nuv-reasoning__label` | The label. |
| `.nuv-reasoning__marker` | The tick, or the spinner. |
| `.nuv-reasoning__step` | ReasoningStep |
| `.nuv-reasoning__steps` | ReasoningSteps |
| `.nuv-reasoning__text` | The label and the detail. |
| `.nuv-reasoning__trigger` | ReasoningTrigger |

`Reasoning` has `data-streaming` while the assistant works, and `data-state`, `"open"` or `"closed"`. A step has `data-status`, `"done"` or `"active"`.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

Reasoning starts with `"use client"`, since the steps open and close. A server component can render a finished one, without `onOpenChange`.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Close it once the reply is there, which `streaming` does for you.
- Show the steps that were really taken.

**Don't**

- Don't put the reply itself in it. What the reader needs is under it, in the message.
- Don't use it for progress through a form or a checkout. That's a [Stepper](page:components/stepper).

pages.title: ThreadList
pages.description: The conversations someone has had, for a sidebar. A list where one is open and the others can be opened, grouped under headings, with room for buttons on each row.
pages.markdown:

Use a thread list beside a conversation, to go back to an earlier one. {days.map((day) => ( {threads .filter((thread) => thread.when === day) .map((thread) => ( { setThreads((now) => now.filter((other) => other !== thread), ); if (open === thread.id) setOpen(null); }} > {bin} } > {thread.title} ))} ))}

{open ? `Open: ${threads.find((thread) => thread.id === open)?.title}` : "None is open."}

); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/chat @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { ThreadList, ThreadListGroup, ThreadListItem } from "@nuvui/chat"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/chat/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/chat @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { ThreadList, ThreadListGroup, ThreadListItem } from "@nuvui/chat";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/chat/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Chat](page:chat/index) covers that.

```tsx
<ThreadList aria-label="Conversations" value={open} onValueChange={setOpen}>
  <ThreadListGroup label="Today">
    <ThreadListItem value="a1">Overdue invoices</ThreadListItem>
    <ThreadListItem value="a2">Draft a reminder</ThreadListItem>
  </ThreadListGroup>
</ThreadList>
```

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `ThreadList` | The list. It keeps which conversation is open. |
| `ThreadListGroup` | Conversations under a heading of their own. |
| `ThreadListItem` | One conversation. |

sections.heading: Which one is open
sections.markdown:
## Which one is open

`value` is the `value` of the conversation that's open, and `onValueChange` is called with another's when it's pressed, or when Enter or Space is pressed on it. Pass `null` when none is open, as before a new conversation has its first message. `defaultValue` lets the list keep it.

The open one has a background and a bar at its start, so it's told apart without relying on color.

sections.heading: Groups
sections.markdown:
## Groups

`ThreadListGroup` puts a heading over some conversations. Grouping by time is usual: "Today", "Yesterday", "Last week". A list doesn't need groups, and `ThreadListItem` works straight in the `ThreadList`.

sections.heading: Buttons on a row
sections.markdown:
## Buttons on a row

`actions` puts buttons at the end of a row: rename, delete, or a [menu](page:components/dropdown-menu) with both. `detail` puts a word or two before them, such as when the conversation was last written in.

A press on a button is the button's, and doesn't open the conversation. With the keyboard, the buttons of the row that has focus are the next Tab stops. The buttons of every other row are out of the Tab order, so Tab doesn't walk through all of them on its way past.

When a conversation is deleted, its row goes, and focus with it if it was there. Move focus to the row that took its place, or to the button that starts a new conversation.

sections.heading: A long title
sections.markdown:
## A long title

A title takes one line and is cut short with an ellipsis where the row ends. The arrow keys and a screen reader still get the whole of it.

sections.heading: Finding one by typing
sections.markdown:
## Finding one by typing

With focus in the list, typing a letter goes to the next conversation that starts with it, and typing a few quickly looks for the word.

sections.heading: It's a ListView
sections.markdown:
## It's a ListView

`ThreadList` is the core's [ListView](page:components/list-view) with one row selected, and it takes that component's variables as well as its own. Read that page for how the grid, the keys and the rows work.

sections.heading: ThreadList props
sections.markdown:
## ThreadList props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string \| null` |  | The conversation that's open, when you keep it: its `value`, or `null` for none. Use it with `onValueChange`. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | The one that's open to begin with, when it's kept here. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void)` |  | Called with a conversation's `value` when it's opened. |

It also takes the attributes of a `div`.

sections.heading: ThreadListItem props
sections.markdown:
## ThreadListItem props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | What the conversation is known by in the list's `value`. |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The conversation's title. A long one is cut short. |
| `detail` | `ReactNode` |  | A word or two after the title: when it was last written in. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | Buttons at the end of the row: rename, delete, a menu of both. Tab reaches them from the row. |

It also takes `textValue` and `disabled`, which are the [ListViewItem](page:components/list-view)'s.

sections.heading: ThreadListGroup props
sections.markdown:
## ThreadListGroup props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The heading over them: "Today", "Last week". |

Every part passes `ref` to its element.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Into the list, at the row it was last at. Then into that row's buttons, then out. |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> <kbd>↑</kbd> | The next and the previous conversation. |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> <kbd>End</kbd> | The first and the last. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd> | Opens the conversation. |
| A letter | The next conversation that starts with it. |

### What the component handles

- It's a grid one column wide, which is the pattern for a list whose rows hold buttons. Each conversation is a row, and the open one has `aria-selected`.
- A group is a group of rows, named by its heading.
- Moving with the arrow keys doesn't open anything. A conversation opens when it's asked for.
- A row is 44 pixels tall.

### What you need to handle

- Name the list with `aria-label`: "Conversations".
- Name each button on a row after its conversation: "Delete Overdue invoices", not "Delete".
- If opening a conversation moves the reader to another page, the list should be on that page too, with the same one open.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

On a phone there's no room for the list beside the conversation. Put it in a [Sheet](page:components/sheet) that opens from a button, or make it a screen of its own.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on a `ThreadList`, or on anything around it.

```css
.sidebar {
  --nuv-thread-list-radius: var(--radius-sm);
  --nuv-list-view-selected-bg: var(--color-surface);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-thread-list-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius of a row. |
| `--nuv-thread-list-heading-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of a group's heading. Keep it at 4.5:1. |
| `--nuv-thread-list-detail-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the detail after a title. Keep it at 4.5:1. |

The row itself is the [ListView](page:components/list-view#css-variables)'s: `--nuv-list-view-hover-bg`, `--nuv-list-view-selected-bg`, `--nuv-list-view-selected-line` and the rest.

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-thread-list` | ThreadList, next to nuv-list-view. |
| `.nuv-thread-list__actions` | The buttons at the end of the row. |
| `.nuv-thread-list__detail` | The detail after it. |
| `.nuv-thread-list__group` | ThreadListGroup |
| `.nuv-thread-list__heading` | A group's heading. |
| `.nuv-thread-list__title` | The title. |

A row also has the class `nuv-thread-list__item`, next to `nuv-list-view__item`. No rule of the package's uses it. It's there for yours.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

ThreadList starts with `"use client"`: it follows the keys and keeps which row Tab stops at. A server component can render it with `defaultValue`, without `onValueChange`.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Put the most recent first.
- Give a conversation a title that says what it was about, and let it be renamed.

**Don't**

- Don't open a conversation as the arrow keys pass it. Each one may be a request to your server.
- Don't put more than two buttons on a row. A menu holds the rest.

pages.title: Boards
pages.description: The @nuvui/kanban package. A board of columns with cards that are moved between and within them with a mouse, a finger or the keyboard, installed next to @nuvui/react.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/kanban @nuvui/react
```

`@nuvui/react` is a peer dependency: the board is drawn with the core's tokens.

The dragging is done by [dnd kit](https://dndkit.com), `@dnd-kit/core` and `@dnd-kit/sortable`, which are installed with the package. You don't import them yourself.

sections.heading: Load the styles
sections.markdown:
## Load the styles

Import the package's stylesheet once, after the core's:

```tsx title="app/layout.tsx"
import "@nuvui/react/styles.css";
import "@nuvui/kanban/styles.css";
```

Both files open with the same line naming the cascade layers, so the order you import them in doesn't decide which rule wins. The board's styles are also on their own, at `@nuvui/kanban/css/kanban.css`.

sections.heading: What it keeps and what you keep
sections.markdown:
## What it keeps and what you keep

The board keeps the order: which cards are in which column, from first to last, by their ids. What a card is, its title and who it belongs to, stays with you, looked up by id when a card is drawn.

```ts
const columns = [
  { id: "todo", cards: ["brief", "quote"] },
  { id: "doing", cards: ["invoice"] },
  { id: "done", cards: [] },
];
```

When a card is dropped somewhere new, `onValueChange` is called once with the columns as they are now and the move that was made. That's the moment to save it.

sections.heading: What it leaves out
sections.markdown:
## What it leaves out

- **Saving.** It hands you the new order. Sending it to your server, and putting a card back when that fails, is yours.
- **Moving columns.** Cards move. The columns stay in the order you give them.
- **Adding, editing and deleting cards.** They're your data. A header and a column take buttons of yours for them.
- **Swimlanes,** rows that run across the columns.
- **Long columns drawn a part at a time.** Every card in a column is on the page. A column with many hundreds of cards is better filtered.

pages.title: Kanban
pages.description: A board of columns with cards that are moved between and within them. A mouse drags a card, a finger holds it and then drags, and the keyboard moves it from its handle. Every move is read out.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/kanban @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import {
  Kanban,
  KanbanCard,
  KanbanCards,
  KanbanColumn,
  KanbanColumnHeader,
} from "@nuvui/kanban";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/kanban/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Kanban](page:kanban/index) covers that.

```tsx
<Kanban aria-label="Work" value={columns} onValueChange={setColumns}>
  {(columns) =>
    columns.map((column) => (
      <KanbanColumn key={column.id} value={column.id} label={names[column.id]}>
        <KanbanColumnHeader count={column.cards.length}>
          {names[column.id]}
        </KanbanColumnHeader>
        <KanbanCards empty="Nothing here yet">
          {column.cards.map((id) => (
            <KanbanCard key={id} value={id} label={cards[id].title}>
              {cards[id].title}
            </KanbanCard>
          ))}
        </KanbanCards>
      </KanbanColumn>
    ))
  }
</Kanban>
```

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Kanban` | The board. It keeps the order of the cards and carries one while it's moved. |
| `KanbanColumn` | One column. |
| `KanbanColumnHeader` | The top of a column: its title, a count and buttons. |
| `KanbanCards` | A column's cards, and the part a card is dropped on. |
| `KanbanCard` | One card, with its handle. |

A column takes anything else as well, such as a button under the cards that adds one.

sections.heading: The columns and their cards
sections.markdown:
## The columns and their cards

`value` is the columns in order, each with its `id` and the ids of its `cards` from first to last. It holds no titles and no other data: you look those up by id when you draw a card.

`onValueChange` is called once when a card is dropped somewhere new, with the columns as they are now and the move: the card, and the column and index it went `from` and `to`. It isn't called while a card is carried, and isn't called for a card put back where it was. `defaultValue` lets the board keep the columns itself.

sections.heading: Why the board draws through a function
sections.markdown:
## Why the board draws through a function

The child of `Kanban` is a function that's given the columns to draw. While a card is carried over another column it's already in that column on the page, so that the cards there make room for it, and nothing has been dropped yet. The columns the function gets are those, and `value` is still what it was. Draw from the function's columns and not from your own state.

sections.heading: Refusing a move
What a card holds
A column with no cards
sections.markdown:
## A column with no cards

`KanbanCards` is the part a card is dropped on. It keeps a least height with no cards in it, and `empty` is drawn there. While a card is over it, it has a dashed outline.

sections.heading: Disabled
sections.markdown:
## Disabled

`disabled` on `Kanban` stops every card from being moved, for someone who can look and not change. `disabled` on a `KanbanCard` stops that one. Other cards still move around it, and are dropped before or after it.

sections.heading: Kanban props
sections.markdown:
## Kanban props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `KanbanColumnData[]` |  | The columns and the order of the cards in each, when you keep them. Use it with `onValueChange`. A move you don't take is undone. |
| `defaultValue` | `KanbanColumnData[]` |  | The columns to begin with, when they're kept here. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: KanbanColumnData[], move: KanbanMove) => void)` |  | Called once when a card is dropped somewhere new, with the columns as they are now and the move that was made. Not called while a card is still being carried. |
| `children` (required) | `(columns: KanbanColumnData[]) => ReactNode` |  | Draws the board. It's given the columns to draw, which while a card is carried are not yet the ones in `value`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | No card can be moved. |
| `labels` | `KanbanLabels` |  | What's said and not drawn, for another language. |

It also takes the attributes of a `div`.

sections.heading: KanbanColumn props
sections.markdown:
## KanbanColumn props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | What the column is known by: its `id` in the board's `value`. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | The column's name in words: "To do". It names the column to a screen reader and is said when a card is moved into it. |

sections.heading: KanbanColumnHeader props
sections.markdown:
## KanbanColumnHeader props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The column's title as it's drawn. |
| `count` | `ReactNode` |  | Shown after the title, most often how many cards there are. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | Buttons at the end of the header: add a card, a menu. |

sections.heading: KanbanCards props
sections.markdown:
## KanbanCards props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `empty` | `ReactNode` |  | Shown in place of the cards when the column has none. |

sections.heading: KanbanCard props
sections.markdown:
## KanbanCard props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | What the card is known by in its column's `cards`. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | The card's name in words. It names the handle, "Move" and this, and is said as the card is moved. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | This card can't be moved. |
| `handleRef` | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>` |  | For the handle, when you need it. |

It also takes the attributes of an `li`. Every part passes `ref` to its element.

sections.heading: Translation
sections.markdown:
## Translation

Everything that's said and not drawn is in `labels`, in English until you give another. Each is a whole sentence, built by a function from the card's name and its place, since those go together differently in each language.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `move` | `((card: string) => string)` |  | The name of a card's handle. |
| `roleDescription` | `string` |  | What kind of thing the handle is, read after its name. |
| `instructions` | `string` |  | How to move a card with the keyboard, read with the handle. |
| `picked` | `((card: string, place: KanbanSpokenPlace \| null) => string)` |  | Said when a card is picked up, with where it is. |
| `over` | `((card: string, place: KanbanSpokenPlace) => string)` |  | Said at each place a carried card comes to. |
| `dropped` | `((card: string, place: KanbanSpokenPlace \| null) => string)` |  | Said when it's dropped, with where it now is. |
| `cancelled` | `((card: string) => string)` |  | Said when it's put back with Escape. |

A place is the column's `label`, a `position` counted from 1, and the `total` of cards in that column with this one counted.

```tsx
<Kanban
  labels={{
    move: (card) => `Verplaats ${card}`,
    over: (card, place) =>
      `${card} staat op ${place.position} van ${place.total} in ${place.column}.`,
  }}
>
```

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | To each card's handle in turn, and to what's in the card. |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> or <kbd>Enter</kbd> | On a handle, picks the card up. With a card picked up, drops it. |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> <kbd>↑</kbd> | Moves the card one place down or up its column. |
| <kbd>→</kbd> <kbd>←</kbd> | Moves the card into the next column that way, one column at a time. |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Puts the card back where it was. |

The arrows go by where things are on the screen. Where the page reads right to left the first column is at the right, and <kbd>←</kbd> goes to the one after it.

### With a mouse and on a touch screen

A mouse drags a card from anywhere on it. On a touch screen a finger held on a card for a quarter of a second picks it up, and a finger that moves sooner scrolls the board. Near an edge the board and the column scroll under a card that's carried.

### What the component handles

- The board and each column are groups with a name. A column's cards are a list.
- A card's handle is a button. It's described by how to move a card with the keyboard, and says when it's pressed.
- Picking a card up, each place it passes, dropping it and putting it back are each said, with the column's name and the position in it.
- When a card is dropped, focus is on its handle again, in whichever column it's now in.
- The handle is 44 pixels on a touch screen.
- With reduced motion, cards don't slide to make room and a dropped card is in its place at once.

### What you need to handle

- Name the board with `aria-label`, and give every column and every card a `label` that tells it from the others.
- Dragging is never the only way: the keyboard moves a card. For someone who can't do either comfortably, a menu on the card with "Move to" and the columns is worth having, and changing `value` yourself is all it takes.
- Name each button in a card after its card: "Open T-101", not "Open".

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

The columns stay side by side and the board scrolls sideways. A column is at most 85% of the board's width, so some of the next one shows. The page itself doesn't scroll sideways.

A card dragged to the edge scrolls the board to the next column. For a board with many columns, a menu on the card that moves it is quicker on a phone than carrying it across.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on a `Kanban`, or on anything around it.

```css
.board {
  --nuv-kanban-column-width: 20rem;
  --nuv-kanban-max-height: 70dvh;
}
```

With `--nuv-kanban-max-height` set, a column is no taller than that and its cards scroll inside it.

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-kanban-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 4)` | Space between columns. |
| `--nuv-kanban-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of the text. |
| `--nuv-kanban-column-width` | `18rem` | Width of a column. It's never more than 85% of the board. |
| `--nuv-kanban-max-height` | `none` | The most a column's height can be. Its cards scroll inside it. No limit by default. |
| `--nuv-kanban-column-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of a column's border. |
| `--nuv-kanban-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of a column. |
| `--nuv-kanban-column-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of a column. |
| `--nuv-kanban-count-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the count in a header. Keep it at 4.5:1 against the column. |
| `--nuv-kanban-over-border` | `var(--color-ring)` | Color of the outline of an empty column with a card over it. |
| `--nuv-kanban-card-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 2)` | Space between cards. |
| `--nuv-kanban-empty-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the words in a column with no cards. Keep it at 4.5:1 against the column. |
| `--nuv-kanban-card-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of a card's border. |
| `--nuv-kanban-card-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius of a card. |
| `--nuv-kanban-card-bg` | `var(--color-background)` | Background of a card. |
| `--nuv-kanban-card-shadow` | `var(--shadow-xs)` | Shadow of a card. |
| `--nuv-kanban-placeholder-border` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the dashed edge of the place a carried card would land. Keep it at 3:1 against the column. |
| `--nuv-kanban-placeholder-bg` | `transparent` | Background of that place. |
| `--nuv-kanban-overlay-shadow` | `var(--shadow-lg)` | Shadow of the card under the pointer. |
| `--nuv-kanban-handle-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of a handle. Keep it at 3:1. |
| `--nuv-kanban-handle-hover-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Its color with the pointer over it. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-kanban` | Kanban |
| `.nuv-kanban__actions` | The buttons at the end of a header. |
| `.nuv-kanban__card` | KanbanCard, and the card under the pointer. |
| `.nuv-kanban__card-content` | What the card holds. |
| `.nuv-kanban__cards` | KanbanCards, the part a card is dropped on. |
| `.nuv-kanban__column` | KanbanColumn |
| `.nuv-kanban__count` | The count after it. |
| `.nuv-kanban__empty` | What's drawn with no cards. |
| `.nuv-kanban__handle` | The handle. |
| `.nuv-kanban__header` | KanbanColumnHeader |
| `.nuv-kanban__list` | The list of cards inside it. |
| `.nuv-kanban__title` | The title in a header. |

A part's state is an attribute: `data-dragging` on the board and on the card that's carried, `data-overlay` on the card under the pointer, `data-over` and `data-empty` on a column's cards, and `data-disabled` on the board and on a card that can't be moved.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

Kanban starts with `"use client"`, and its child is a function, which a server component can't pass. Put the board in a client component of your own and hand that the columns.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Keep the columns few enough to see together on a desk screen.
- Show how many cards a column holds.
- Say why when a move isn't taken.

**Don't**

- Don't make dragging the only way to change a card's stage. The card's own page should have a field for it too.
- Don't save on every arrow key. `onValueChange` comes once, when the card is dropped.
- Don't give two cards the same `label`.

pages.title: Editor
pages.description: The @nuvui/editor package. A rich text editor on Tiptap, installed next to @nuvui/react, with a toolbar, a menu on the selection, links, a character count, and HTML as its value.
pages.markdown:
# Editor The @nuvui/editor package. A rich text editor on Tiptap, installed next to @nuvui/react, with a toolbar, a menu on the selection, links, a character count, and HTML as its value. The rich text editor is a package of its own, `@nuvui/editor`, since editing formatted text needs an engine the core doesn't have: | Component | What it is | | --- | --- | | [RichTextEditor](page:editor/rich-text-editor) | A box to write formatted text in: bold and italic, headings, lists, quotes, code and links, with a toolbar over it and a small one that comes up over selected text. | ```tsx "use client"; import { RichTextEditor } from "@nuvui/editor"; export default function Example() { return (
); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/editor @nuvui/react ``` `@nuvui/react` is a peer dependency: the toolbar is the core's [Toolbar](page:components/toolbar), and the box for a link is its Popover, Input and Button. The editing is done by [Tiptap](https://tiptap.dev), which is built on ProseMirror. Its packages are MIT licensed and are installed with this one. You don't import them yourself. ## Load the styles Import the package's stylesheet once, after the core's: ```tsx title="app/layout.tsx" import "@nuvui/react/styles.css"; import "@nuvui/editor/styles.css"; ``` Both files open with the same line naming the cascade layers, so the order you import them in doesn't decide which rule wins. The editor's styles are also on their own, at `@nuvui/editor/css/rich-text-editor.css`. With that one, load `toolbar.css`, `popover.css`, `input.css` and `button.css` from `@nuvui/react/css/` as well. Tiptap would otherwise add a few rules of its own in a `style` element it makes at run time. That's turned off, and the rules are in this stylesheet, so a page with a strict content security policy needs no exception for it. ## It's large, so load it when it's needed The editor is about 120 kB compressed, nearly all of it ProseMirror. Most screens of an app don't have one. Load it with the screen that does: ```tsx import { lazy, Suspense } from "react"; const RichTextEditor = lazy(() => import("@nuvui/editor").then((module) => ({ default: module.RichTextEditor, })), ); }> ; ``` In Next.js, `next/dynamic` does the same. ## The value is HTML `value` is a string of HTML, and `onValueChange` is called with one. It's kept the way any field's value is, shown again on any page without the editor, and sent in an email. Nothing written is the empty string. Beside the HTML, `onValueChange` gives the same text as data, as plain words, and its counts. [RichTextEditor](page:editor/rich-text-editor#the-value) has the details. ## Sanitize before you show it The editor only writes the elements it knows: paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes, code, links, and the marks for bold and the like. A link's address is the web, email, a phone number or a place on your site, and nothing that runs. What's pasted in goes through the same rules. That's what the editor writes. What reaches your server is whatever was sent to it, which someone can write by hand. So before HTML from a database is put in a page, pass it through a sanitizer such as [DOMPurify](https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify) or [sanitize-html](https://github.com/apostrophecms/sanitize-html), on the server, with a list of the elements above. Or show it with the editor itself, [read only](page:editor/rich-text-editor#read-only), which reads HTML through the same rules it writes with. ## What it leaves out - **Tiptap extensions of your own.** The engine isn't part of what the component takes or gives, so that it can be changed without changing your code. A mention, a table or an image that uploads isn't built. - **Images, tables, text color and alignment.** - **Markdown as the value.** Underline, and anything that's added later, has no markdown to be written as. - **Several people writing at once.** - **Uploading.** Nothing is uploaded, so nothing is pasted as a file.
