pages.title: RichTextEditor
pages.description: A box to write formatted text in. Bold and italic, headings, lists, quotes, code and links, from a toolbar, from the keyboard, or from a small menu over selected text. Its value is HTML.
pages.markdown:
# RichTextEditor A box to write formatted text in. Bold and italic, headings, lists, quotes, code and links, from a toolbar, from the keyboard, or from a small menu over selected text. Its value is HTML. Use it where what's written will be read as a document: a note to a customer, a description, an announcement, a reply. For a line or two of plain words, a [Textarea](page:components/textarea) is lighter by about 120 kB and says less can go wrong. ```tsx "use client"; import { RichTextEditor } from "@nuvui/editor"; export default function Example() { return (
); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/editor @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { RichTextEditor } from "@nuvui/editor"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/editor/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Editor](page:editor/index) covers that, and loading the editor only on the screens that have one. ```tsx ``` ## Parts By itself `RichTextEditor` draws a toolbar, the text, and a count when there's a `maxLength`. Give it children to choose the parts yourself. | Part | What it is | | --- | --- | | `RichTextEditor` | The box. It keeps the text. | | `RichTextEditorToolbar` | The row of controls over the text. | | `RichTextEditorFormats` | A group of toggles in a toolbar: bold, a heading, a list. | | `RichTextEditorActions` | Buttons in a toolbar that do one thing once: undo, a divider. | | `RichTextEditorLink` | The button for a link, with the box its address is written in. | | `RichTextEditorContent` | The text. | | `RichTextEditorBubbleMenu` | A small toolbar over selected text. It's drawn when you add it. | | `RichTextEditorCount` | How much is written. | ## The value `value` is HTML, and `onValueChange` is called with the HTML each time the text changes. `defaultValue` lets the editor keep it. Nothing written is `""`, not an empty paragraph. The second argument of `onValueChange` has what else you may want from the same change: `text`, the words with no markup, `characters`, `words`, `empty`, and `json`, the document as data. `json` and `text` are worked out when you read them, so one you don't read costs nothing. ```tsx "use client"; import { RichTextEditor } from "@nuvui/editor"; import { Button } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; const start = "

Payment is due 30 days after the invoice.

"; export default function Example() { const [html, setHtml] = useState(start); const [counts, setCounts] = useState("8 words"); return (
{ setHtml(next); setCounts(`${change.words} words`); }} />
{counts} 
        {html || "(nothing written)"}
); } ``` When you set `value` to something other than what's written, the text is replaced and the caret goes to the start. Setting it to what `onValueChange` just gave you changes nothing, so typing isn't disturbed. ## What can be written | Format | In the toolbar | From the keyboard | By typing | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Bold | Bold | Ctrl B | `**text**` | | Italic | Italic | Ctrl I | `*text*` | | Underline | Underline | Ctrl U | | | Strikethrough | Strikethrough | Ctrl Shift S | `~~text~~` | | Code | Code | Ctrl E | `` `text` `` | | Heading | Heading 2, Heading 3 | Ctrl Alt 2 | `## ` | | Bulleted list | Bulleted list | Ctrl Shift 8 | `- ` | | Numbered list | Numbered list | Ctrl Shift 7 | `1. ` | | Quote | Quote | Ctrl Shift B | `> ` | | Code block | Code block | Ctrl Alt C | ` ``` ` | | Divider | | | `---` | | Link | Link | | Paste or type an address | On a Mac, ⌘ is in place of Ctrl. These are Tiptap's own shortcuts. ## Headings `headingLevels` says which headings the text can have, and those are the ones the toolbar offers. It's `[2, 3]` by default: the page the text ends up on has its own `h1`, and usually an `h2` over the text as well. Give the levels that fit under yours. `[]` leaves headings out. A heading of a level that isn't allowed, in a `value` or in what's pasted, becomes a paragraph. ## Links The Link button opens a box to write the address in. What's selected becomes the link's words. With nothing selected, the address is written as the words. On a link, the box has its address, and a button that takes the link off. An address can be the web, `mailto:`, `tel:`, or a place on your own site that starts with `/` or `#`. One with no scheme, `example.com`, is taken for `https://`. Anything else is refused, and the box says so. A click on a link in the text puts the caret there. It doesn't open it. Links are written with `rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"`. ## A limit `maxLength` is the most characters the text takes. Typing and pasting stop there, and a count under the text says how many are written and how many can be. The count turns to the danger color when it's full, and says so in words as well: "140 of 140 characters". ```tsx "use client"; import { RichTextEditor } from "@nuvui/editor"; export default function Example() { return (
); } ``` It counts characters of text, not of HTML. If a column in your database limits the HTML, check that on the server. ## In a form With a `name`, the HTML is sent with the form the editor is in, in a hidden field, as any other field's value is. A `disabled` editor sends nothing. Name the editor with `aria-labelledby` and the `id` of the words that label it. A `label` element can't point at it with `for`, since it isn't an `input`. `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` on `RichTextEditor` go to the text, where a screen reader looks for them. ```tsx "use client"; import { RichTextEditor } from "@nuvui/editor"; import { Button } from "@nuvui/react"; import { type FormEvent, useId, useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { const id = useId(); const [sent, setSent] = useState("Nothing sent yet."); const [missing, setMissing] = useState(false); function submit(event: FormEvent) { event.preventDefault(); const body = String(new FormData(event.currentTarget).get("body") ?? ""); setMissing(body === ""); if (body !== "") setSent(`Sent: ${body}`); } return (
Reply setMissing(false)} /> {missing ? (

Write a reply before you send it.

) : null}

{sent}

); } ``` `aria-required` says it's required. It doesn't stop the form: check for `""` yourself, as above. ## Your own toolbar `RichTextEditorToolbar` takes groups of your choosing. `RichTextEditorFormats` is a group of toggles, and `RichTextEditorActions` a group of buttons, each given the `items` to draw. Put the core's `ToolbarSeparator` between them, and any `ToolbarButton` of your own beside them. ```tsx "use client"; import { RichTextEditor, RichTextEditorActions, RichTextEditorContent, RichTextEditorCount, RichTextEditorFormats, RichTextEditorLink, RichTextEditorToolbar, } from "@nuvui/editor"; import { ToolbarSeparator } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return (
); } ``` The formats are `bold`, `italic`, `underline`, `strike`, `code`, `heading1` to `heading6`, `bulletList`, `orderedList`, `blockquote` and `codeBlock`. The actions are `undo`, `redo`, `horizontalRule` and `clearFormatting`. Leaving a format out of the toolbar doesn't forbid it: its shortcut still works, and it can be pasted. ## A menu on the selection `RichTextEditorBubbleMenu` is a small toolbar that comes up over text when it's selected, with bold, italic, underline and strikethrough, or the `items` you give it. It's for an editor with no toolbar over the text, as here. ```tsx "use client"; import { RichTextEditor, RichTextEditorBubbleMenu, RichTextEditorContent, } from "@nuvui/editor"; export default function Example() { return (
); } ``` It isn't drawn unless you add it. Under a toolbar it covers the toolbar's controls when the first line is selected, and on a phone it comes up where the phone's own menu for copy and paste does. Formatting that's only in this menu can't be reached with the Tab key, so keep it to formats that have a shortcut: the four it starts with do. ## Read only `readOnly` shows the text and lets it be selected and copied, and not changed. With only `RichTextEditorContent` as its child there's no toolbar, and it's a way to show saved text: the editor reads HTML through the same rules it writes with, so what it shows can't run anything. ```tsx "use client"; import { RichTextEditor, RichTextEditorContent } from "@nuvui/editor"; // What someone wrote, shown again. The editor reads the HTML through its // own rules for what text can hold, so nothing in it can run. const saved = '

Late payments

A reminder goes out on day 31.

  • Late fees start at day 45.

  • Questions go to billing@example.com.

'; export default function Example() { return (
); } ``` `disabled` is for a field that can't be used now. It's dimmed, and isn't sent with a form. ## From outside `editorRef` gives a handle on the editor, for a button elsewhere on the page: ```tsx const editor = useRef(null); ``` | Method | What it does | | --- | --- | | `focus()` | Puts the caret in the text. | | `clear()` | Takes everything out. | | `setHTML(html)` | Replaces everything. | | `insertText(text)` | Puts text where the caret is, over what's selected. | | `getHTML()`, `getText()`, `getJSON()` | The text now, as HTML, as plain words, and as data. | `clear`, `setHTML` and `insertText` call `onValueChange`. ## RichTextEditor props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` | `string` | | The text as HTML, when you keep it. Use it with `onValueChange`. Nothing written is the empty string. | | `defaultValue` | `string` | | The text to begin with, when it's kept here. | | `onValueChange` | `((html: string, change: RichTextEditorChange) => void)` | | Called when the text changes, with the HTML and, beside it, the same as data, as plain words, and its counts. | | `placeholder` | `string` | | Shown while nothing is written. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | It can't be written in, and isn't sent with a form. | | `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | It can be read and selected, and not changed. | | `maxLength` | `number` | | The most characters it takes. Typing and pasting stop there. | | `autoFocus` | `boolean` | `false` | Puts the caret in it when it's first drawn. | | `name` | `string` | | With a name, the HTML is sent with the form it's in. | | `headingLevels` | `RichTextEditorHeadingLevel[]` | `[2, 3]` | The heading levels the text can have, and the toolbar offers. Give the ones under the page's own headings. | | `labels` | `RichTextEditorLabels` | | What's said and not drawn, for another language. | | `editorRef` | `Ref` | | The editor from outside: focus, clear, and the text as data. | | `children` | `ReactNode` | | The parts, when the ones it draws by itself aren't the ones you want: a toolbar, the text, and the count if there's a `maxLength`. A menu on the selection is a part to add here. | It also takes the attributes of a `div`, and passes `ref` to it. ## RichTextEditorFormats props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `items` (required) | `RichTextEditorFormat[]` | | The toggles, in the order they're drawn. | ## sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/editor @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { RichTextEditor } from "@nuvui/editor";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/editor/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Editor](page:editor/index) covers that, and loading the editor only on the screens that have one.

```tsx
<RichTextEditor
  aria-label="Notes"
  placeholder="Write a note"
  value={html}
  onValueChange={setHtml}
/>
```

sections.heading: Parts
sections.markdown:
## Parts

By itself `RichTextEditor` draws a toolbar, the text, and a count when there's a `maxLength`. Give it children to choose the parts yourself.

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `RichTextEditor` | The box. It keeps the text. |
| `RichTextEditorToolbar` | The row of controls over the text. |
| `RichTextEditorFormats` | A group of toggles in a toolbar: bold, a heading, a list. |
| `RichTextEditorActions` | Buttons in a toolbar that do one thing once: undo, a divider. |
| `RichTextEditorLink` | The button for a link, with the box its address is written in. |
| `RichTextEditorContent` | The text. |
| `RichTextEditorBubbleMenu` | A small toolbar over selected text. It's drawn when you add it. |
| `RichTextEditorCount` | How much is written. |

sections.heading: The value
What can be written
sections.markdown:
## What can be written

| Format | In the toolbar | From the keyboard | By typing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bold | Bold | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> <kbd>B</kbd> | `**text**` |
| Italic | Italic | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> <kbd>I</kbd> | `*text*` |
| Underline | Underline | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> <kbd>U</kbd> | |
| Strikethrough | Strikethrough | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> <kbd>Shift</kbd> <kbd>S</kbd> | `~~text~~` |
| Code | Code | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> <kbd>E</kbd> | `` `text` `` |
| Heading | Heading 2, Heading 3 | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> <kbd>Alt</kbd> <kbd>2</kbd> | `## ` |
| Bulleted list | Bulleted list | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> <kbd>Shift</kbd> <kbd>8</kbd> | `- ` |
| Numbered list | Numbered list | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> <kbd>Shift</kbd> <kbd>7</kbd> | `1. ` |
| Quote | Quote | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> <kbd>Shift</kbd> <kbd>B</kbd> | `> ` |
| Code block | Code block | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> <kbd>Alt</kbd> <kbd>C</kbd> | ` ``` ` |
| Divider | | | `---` |
| Link | Link | | Paste or type an address |

On a Mac, <kbd>⌘</kbd> is in place of <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>. These are Tiptap's own shortcuts.

sections.heading: Headings
sections.markdown:
## Headings

`headingLevels` says which headings the text can have, and those are the ones the toolbar offers. It's `[2, 3]` by default: the page the text ends up on has its own `h1`, and usually an `h2` over the text as well. Give the levels that fit under yours. `[]` leaves headings out.

A heading of a level that isn't allowed, in a `value` or in what's pasted, becomes a paragraph.

sections.heading: Links
sections.markdown:
## Links

The Link button opens a box to write the address in. What's selected becomes the link's words. With nothing selected, the address is written as the words. On a link, the box has its address, and a button that takes the link off.

An address can be the web, `mailto:`, `tel:`, or a place on your own site that starts with `/` or `#`. One with no scheme, `example.com`, is taken for `https://`. Anything else is refused, and the box says so.

A click on a link in the text puts the caret there. It doesn't open it. Links are written with `rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"`.

sections.heading: A limit
In a form
Your own toolbar
sections.markdown:
## Your own toolbar `RichTextEditorToolbar` takes groups of your choosing. `RichTextEditorFormats` is a group of toggles, and `RichTextEditorActions` a group of buttons, each given the `items` to draw. Put the core's `ToolbarSeparator` between them, and any `ToolbarButton` of your own beside them. ```tsx "use client"; import { RichTextEditor, RichTextEditorActions, RichTextEditorContent, RichTextEditorCount, RichTextEditorFormats, RichTextEditorLink, RichTextEditorToolbar, } from "@nuvui/editor"; import { ToolbarSeparator } from "@nuvui/react"; export default function Example() { return (
); } ``` The formats are `bold`, `italic`, `underline`, `strike`, `code`, `heading1` to `heading6`, `bulletList`, `orderedList`, `blockquote` and `codeBlock`. The actions are `undo`, `redo`, `horizontalRule` and `clearFormatting`. Leaving a format out of the toolbar doesn't forbid it: its shortcut still works, and it can be pasted.

sections.heading: A menu on the selection
Read only
From outside
sections.markdown:
## From outside

`editorRef` gives a handle on the editor, for a button elsewhere on the page:

```tsx
const editor = useRef<RichTextEditorHandle>(null);

<Button onClick={() => editor.current?.insertText("Kind regards, Ada")}>
  Add my signature
</Button>
<RichTextEditor aria-label="Reply" editorRef={editor} />
```

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `focus()` | Puts the caret in the text. |
| `clear()` | Takes everything out. |
| `setHTML(html)` | Replaces everything. |
| `insertText(text)` | Puts text where the caret is, over what's selected. |
| `getHTML()`, `getText()`, `getJSON()` | The text now, as HTML, as plain words, and as data. |

`clear`, `setHTML` and `insertText` call `onValueChange`.

sections.heading: RichTextEditor props
sections.markdown:
## RichTextEditor props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` |  | The text as HTML, when you keep it. Use it with `onValueChange`. Nothing written is the empty string. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | The text to begin with, when it's kept here. |
| `onValueChange` | `((html: string, change: RichTextEditorChange) => void)` |  | Called when the text changes, with the HTML and, beside it, the same as data, as plain words, and its counts. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  | Shown while nothing is written. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | It can't be written in, and isn't sent with a form. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | It can be read and selected, and not changed. |
| `maxLength` | `number` |  | The most characters it takes. Typing and pasting stop there. |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | `false` | Puts the caret in it when it's first drawn. |
| `name` | `string` |  | With a name, the HTML is sent with the form it's in. |
| `headingLevels` | `RichTextEditorHeadingLevel[]` | `[2, 3]` | The heading levels the text can have, and the toolbar offers. Give the ones under the page's own headings. |
| `labels` | `RichTextEditorLabels` |  | What's said and not drawn, for another language. |
| `editorRef` | `Ref<RichTextEditorHandle>` |  | The editor from outside: focus, clear, and the text as data. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | The parts, when the ones it draws by itself aren't the ones you want: a toolbar, the text, and the count if there's a `maxLength`. A menu on the selection is a part to add here. |

It also takes the attributes of a `div`, and passes `ref` to it.

sections.heading: RichTextEditorFormats props
sections.markdown:
## RichTextEditorFormats props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` (required) | `RichTextEditorFormat[]` |  | The toggles, in the order they're drawn. |

sections.heading: RichTextEditorActions props
sections.markdown:
## RichTextEditorActions props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` (required) | `RichTextEditorAction[]` |  | The buttons, in the order they're drawn. |

sections.heading: RichTextEditorBubbleMenu props
sections.markdown:
## RichTextEditorBubbleMenu props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `RichTextEditorFormat[]` | `["bold", "italic", "underline", "strike"]` | The toggles it offers. |

`RichTextEditorToolbar`, `RichTextEditorContent` and `RichTextEditorCount` take the attributes of their element. `RichTextEditorLink` takes none.

## Translation

Every name a screen reader says, and the words in the box for a link, are in `labels`, in English until you give another.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |

| `textStyle` | `string` |  | The name of the group of bold, italic and the like. |
| `blocks` | `string` |  | The name of the group of headings, lists and the like. |
| `selectionMenu` | `string` |  | The name of the menu over selected text. |
| `bold` | `string` |  |  |
| `italic` | `string` |  |  |
| `underline` | `string` |  |  |
| `strike` | `string` |  |  |
| `code` | `string` |  |  |
| `heading` | `((level: RichTextEditorHeadingLevel) => string)` |  |  |
| `bulletList` | `string` |  |  |
| `orderedList` | `string` |  |  |
| `blockquote` | `string` |  |  |
| `codeBlock` | `string` |  |  |
| `undo` | `string` |  |  |
| `redo` | `string` |  |  |
| `horizontalRule` | `string` |  |  |
| `clearFormatting` | `string` |  |  |
| `link` | `string` |  |  |
| `linkAddress` | `string` |  | The name of the field a link's address is written in. |
| `linkApply` | `string` |  |  |
| `linkRemove` | `string` |  |  |
| `linkInvalid` | `string` |  | Said when what's written isn't an address a link can have. |

```tsx
<RichTextEditor
  labels={{
    bold: "Vet",
    heading: (level) => `Kop ${level}`,
    count: (characters, max) => `${characters} van ${max} tekens`,
  }}
/>
```

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | To the toolbar, at the control it was last at. Then to the text. Then out. |
| <kbd>→</kbd> <kbd>←</kbd> | In the toolbar, the next and the previous control. |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> <kbd>End</kbd> | In the toolbar, the first and the last. |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> or <kbd>Enter</kbd> | In the toolbar, presses the control. Focus goes back to the text. |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> in a list | Moves the item in a level, when there's an item above it. <kbd>Shift</kbd> <kbd>Tab</kbd> moves it out. |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Closes the box for a link. |

<kbd>Tab</kbd> in the text goes on to what's after the editor, except in a list item that can be moved in. From there, <kbd>Shift</kbd> <kbd>Tab</kbd> moves the item out, and then leaves.

### What the component handles

- The text is a textbox of many lines, with the name, the description and the invalid and required states you give `RichTextEditor`.
- The toolbar is a toolbar with a name, and one stop for the Tab key. Each control has a name, and a toggle says whether it's on.
- A control that can't be used now, undo with nothing to undo, is disabled.
- After a control is pressed, focus is in the text again, with the selection as it was.
- The menu on the selection isn't reached with the Tab key. What's in it by default has a shortcut each: Ctrl or Command with B, I and U, and with Shift and S.
- Each control is 44 pixels on a touch screen, and the text is 16 pixels there, so iOS doesn't zoom the page when it's tapped.

### What you need to handle

- Name it, with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Choose `headingLevels` so that headings in the text come under the headings of the page it's shown on.
- Say what's wrong in words when it's invalid, and point `aria-describedby` at them.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

The toolbar wraps to as many rows as it needs, and the page doesn't scroll sideways. A toolbar of fourteen controls is three rows on a phone: for a comment or a reply, give it fewer, as in [your own toolbar](#your-own-toolbar).

The menu on the selection, if you add it, comes up over the selection, where a phone puts its own menu for copy and paste. On a phone a toolbar serves better.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on a `RichTextEditor`, or on anything around it.

```css
.reply {
  --nuv-rich-text-editor-min-height: 6rem;
  --nuv-rich-text-editor-max-height: 50dvh;
}
```

With `--nuv-rich-text-editor-max-height` set, the text scrolls inside the box and the toolbar stays in view.

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-rich-text-editor-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of the box's border, and of the lines inside it. |
| `--nuv-rich-text-editor-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of the box. |
| `--nuv-rich-text-editor-bg` | `var(--color-background)` | Background of the box. |
| `--nuv-rich-text-editor-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of the text. |
| `--nuv-rich-text-editor-invalid-border` | `var(--color-danger)` | Color of the border when it's invalid. |
| `--nuv-rich-text-editor-min-height` | `10rem` | The least the text's height can be. 10rem by default. |
| `--nuv-rich-text-editor-max-height` | `none` | The most it can be. The text scrolls inside it. No limit by default. |
| `--nuv-rich-text-editor-padding` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 3)` | Space around the text. |
| `--nuv-rich-text-editor-font-size` | `var(--text-sm)` | Size of the text with a mouse. On a touch screen it's never under 16px. |
| `--nuv-rich-text-editor-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 3)` | Space between paragraphs. |
| `--nuv-rich-text-editor-link-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of a link. It's underlined, so it doesn't rely on color. |
| `--nuv-rich-text-editor-quote-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of the line beside a quote. |
| `--nuv-rich-text-editor-quote-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of a quote's text. Keep it at 4.5:1. |
| `--nuv-rich-text-editor-code-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of code. |
| `--nuv-rich-text-editor-placeholder-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the placeholder. Keep it at 4.5:1. |
| `--nuv-rich-text-editor-count-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the count. Keep it at 4.5:1. |
| `--nuv-rich-text-editor-full-fg` | `var(--color-danger)` | Color of the count when the limit is reached. Keep it at 4.5:1. |

The toolbar is the core's [Toolbar](page:components/toolbar#css-variables), and takes its variables: `--nuv-toolbar-on-bg`, `--nuv-toolbar-item-hover-bg` and the rest.

| `.nuv-rich-text-editor__placeholder` | The empty first line, while the placeholder is shown. |

A state is an attribute on the box: `data-disabled`, `data-readonly` and `data-invalid`. The count has `data-full` at the limit.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

RichTextEditor starts with `"use client"`. A server component can render it with `defaultValue` and a `name`, without `onValueChange`.

Nothing is drawn where the text goes until the page is in a browser: the toolbar and the box are there, and the text comes when the editor starts. That's on purpose. Drawing the HTML on the server would mean putting it in the page without the editor's rules.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Give a comment or a reply a short toolbar, and a document the whole of it.
- Sanitize the HTML on the server before it's shown anywhere without the editor.
- Load the editor only with the screen that has one.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for a single line. An [Input](page:components/input) is a field people already know.
- Don't put the HTML in a page with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` unsanitized.
- Don't rely on `maxLength` to keep the HTML under a database's limit. It counts the text.

# Emoji The @nuvui/emoji package. An emoji picker with search, groups, skin tones and recently used emoji, in a list that draws only the rows in view, and a reaction button with a count, installed next to @nuvui/react. Picking an emoji is a package of its own, `@nuvui/emoji`, since it comes with a list of nineteen hundred emoji that an app with no picker shouldn't carry: | Component | What it is | | --- | --- | | [EmojiPicker](page:emoji/emoji-picker) | A panel with a search box, the emoji in their groups, a choice of skin tone, and the ones picked before. | | [EmojiReaction](page:emoji/emoji-reaction) | A button with an emoji and how many reacted with it, pressed when the reader is one of them. | ```tsx "use client"; import { EmojiPicker } from "@nuvui/emoji"; import { useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { const [picked, setPicked] = useState(""); return (
setPicked(emoji)} />

{picked ? `You picked ${picked}` : "Nothing picked yet"}

); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/emoji @nuvui/react ``` `@nuvui/react` is a peer dependency: the picker is drawn with the core's tokens, and its search box and its menu of skin tones are the core's. Nothing else is installed with it. ## Load the styles Import the package's stylesheet once, after the core's: ```tsx title="app/layout.tsx" import "@nuvui/react/styles.css"; import "@nuvui/emoji/styles.css"; ``` Both files open with the same line naming the cascade layers, so the order you import them in doesn't decide which rule wins. The picker's styles are also on their own, at `@nuvui/emoji/css/emoji-picker.css`. ## The device's own emoji The picker draws emoji as text, in the device's own emoji font. So they look as they do everywhere else on that device: in the message the emoji is put into, in a notification, in another app. There's no artwork to load and none to license. What that costs: - **They look different from one device to the next.** An emoji picked on a phone is the same character on a laptop, drawn by the laptop. - **A device only draws the emoji it has.** One that's newer than the device is an empty box there. So the picker lists emoji up to a version, 15 unless you say otherwise with `emojiVersion`, which is from 2022 and is on what people use now. - **Windows draws no flags.** It draws a flag's two letters. So flags are left out where the device doesn't draw them. `flags` says otherwise. To draw emoji the same everywhere takes a set of pictures, which this package doesn't have. ## The list, and its size The list of emoji, with their names and the words they're found by, is loaded the first time a picker is drawn, and not before. It's about 33 kB compressed. The picker itself is about 4 kB. A reaction button needs no list, and a page with reactions and no picker loads none. The names are English. For another language, or for fewer emoji, give the picker a list of your own with `data`. [EmojiPicker](page:emoji/emoji-picker#a-list-of-your-own) shows one. The list is written from [emojibase-data](https://github.com/milesj/emojibase), which is MIT and takes the names and the keywords from Unicode's CLDR. It has the emoji of Emoji 17. ## What it leaves out - **Pictures of emoji.** See above. - **A button that opens it.** It's a panel. Put it in a [popover](page:components/popover), a [sheet](page:components/sheet), or on the page. - **Putting the emoji in your text.** It hands you the emoji. Where it goes, at the caret of a field or at the end of a message, is yours. - **Who reacted.** A reaction shows a count. The names behind it, in a tooltip or a list, are yours. - **Shortcodes,** such as `:smile:`.

pages.title: EmojiPicker
pages.description: A panel to pick an emoji from, with a search box, the emoji in their groups, a choice of skin tone and the ones picked before. It draws the device's own emoji, and only the rows in view.
pages.markdown:
# EmojiPicker A panel to pick an emoji from, with a search box, the emoji in their groups, a choice of skin tone and the ones picked before. It draws the device's own emoji, and only the rows in view. Use an emoji picker where someone writes to other people: a message, a comment, a status, a reaction. For a choice from a handful of emoji that never changes, a [toggle group](page:components/toggle-group) of them is lighter. ```tsx "use client"; import { EmojiPicker } from "@nuvui/emoji"; import { useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { const [picked, setPicked] = useState(""); return (
setPicked(emoji)} />

{picked ? `You picked ${picked}` : "Nothing picked yet"}

); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/emoji @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { EmojiPicker } from "@nuvui/emoji"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/emoji/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Emoji](page:emoji/index) covers that, and what it means that the emoji are the device's own. ```tsx setText((text) => text + emoji)} /> ``` ## In a popover The picker is a panel, and has no button of its own. Most often it opens from one, in a [popover](page:components/popover). `autoFocus` puts the caret in the search box when it opens, so a name can be typed at once and Enter picks the first emoji found. ```tsx "use client"; import { EmojiPicker } from "@nuvui/emoji"; import { Button, Popover, PopoverContent, PopoverTrigger } from "@nuvui/react"; import { type CSSProperties, useState } from "react"; // The popover is the panel's edge here, so it gives up its own width and // padding, and the picker gives up its border. const bare = { "--nuv-popover-width": "auto", "--nuv-popover-padding": "0px", "--nuv-emoji-picker-border": "transparent", } as CSSProperties; export default function Example() { const [open, setOpen] = useState(false); const [text, setText] = useState("Shipped"); return (

{text}

{ setText((now) => `${now} ${emoji}`); setOpen(false); }} />
); } ``` The popover gives up its width and its padding here, and the picker its border, so the two are one panel. Where there's less room than the picker's height, the picker is made shorter to fit, and its list stays the one thing that scrolls. ## What's picked `onEmojiSelect` is called with the emoji as text, in the skin tone that's set, and with what the list knows of it: its name, its group, and the emoji with no tone. ```tsx { insert(emoji); // "👋🏽" log(item.label); // "waving hand" }} /> ``` ## Searching What's typed is looked for in each emoji's name and in the other words it's found by, a word at a time: "hello" finds the waving hand, and "face big" the grinning face with big eyes. How many were found is said to a screen reader. Enter in the search box picks the first one found. The down arrow goes from the search box into the list. ## Skin tones The hand beside the search box opens the six tones. The one that's chosen is drawn on every emoji that has tones, and remembered. `defaultSkinTone` is where it starts, and `skinTone` with `onSkinToneChange` is for keeping it yourself. Emoji of two people who each have a tone are listed with none. ## The ones picked before The last sixteen emoji picked are listed first the next time the picker is drawn. They aren't added while it's open, so nothing moves under the pointer as emoji are picked. They're kept in the browser's local storage, with the skin tone, under the name `storageKey` gives, which is `"nuvui-emoji"`. To keep them with someone's account, so they follow from one device to the next, give `recent` and `onRecentChange`, and `storageKey={null}` to keep nothing in the browser. ```tsx "use client"; import { EmojiPicker, type EmojiSkinTone } from "@nuvui/emoji"; import { useState } from "react"; export default function Example() { // Kept here, where an app would keep them with the account, so they // follow someone from one device to the next. const [recent, setRecent] = useState(["👍", "🎉", "🚀"]); const [tone, setTone] = useState(3); return (

Recent: {recent.join(" ")}. Skin tone: {tone}.

); } ``` Kept by you, the list is drawn as you give it. Give it the new list when the picker is next opened, and not while it's open, if emoji shouldn't move. ## Which emoji are listed - `emojiVersion` is the newest version of Emoji to list, 15 by default. A device draws an empty box for an emoji it doesn't have, and raising this lists more of those. - `flags` is `"auto"` by default, which lists flags where the device draws them. `true` and `false` say so yourself. ## A list of your own `data` takes the emoji to list: other names, another language, or only the ones that fit. Each is an emoji, a name, the group it's in, and optionally other words to find it by, its version, and its five skin tones. ```tsx "use client"; import { type EmojiItem, EmojiPicker } from "@nuvui/emoji"; import type { CSSProperties } from "react"; import { useState } from "react"; // The few a comment can be answered with, named in Dutch. const reactions: EmojiItem[] = [ { emoji: "👍", label: "duim omhoog", tags: ["goed", "ja"], group: "people" }, { emoji: "👎", label: "duim omlaag", tags: ["slecht", "nee"], group: "people", }, { emoji: "👏", label: "klappende handen", tags: ["bravo"], group: "people" }, { emoji: "😀", label: "grijnzend gezicht", tags: ["blij"], group: "smileys" }, { emoji: "😢", label: "huilend gezicht", tags: ["verdrietig"], group: "smileys", }, { emoji: "🎉", label: "feestknaller", tags: ["feest", "hoera"], group: "activities", }, { emoji: "❤️", label: "rood hart", tags: ["liefde"], group: "symbols" }, ]; const small = { "--nuv-emoji-picker-height": "16rem" } as CSSProperties; export default function Example() { const [picked, setPicked] = useState(""); return (
setPicked(`${emoji} ${item.label}`)} labels={{ search: "Emoji zoeken", list: "Emoji's", groups: "Groepen", results: "Gevonden", skinTone: "Huidskleur", skinTones: [ "Standaard", "Licht", "Lichtgetint", "Getint", "Donkergetint", "Donker", ], group: { smileys: "Gezichten", people: "Mensen", activities: "Activiteiten", symbols: "Symbolen", }, found: (count) => count === 0 ? "Niets gevonden" : `${count} gevonden`, }} />

{picked}

); } ``` With `data`, the list the package comes with isn't loaded. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `onEmojiSelect` | `((emoji: string, item: EmojiItem) => void)` | | Called when an emoji is picked, with the emoji as text, in the skin tone that's set, and with what the list knows about it. | | `data` | `EmojiItem[]` | | The emoji to list, when the ones it comes with aren't the ones you want: another language's names, or fewer. Without it, the list it comes with is loaded when the picker is first drawn. | | `emojiVersion` | `number` | `15` | The newest version of Emoji to list. Newer ones are left out, since a device that doesn't have them draws an empty box. | | `skinTone` | `0 \| 1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5` | | The skin tone, when you keep it. Use it with `onSkinToneChange`. | | `defaultSkinTone` | `0 \| 1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5` | `0` | The skin tone to begin with, when it's kept here. | | `onSkinToneChange` | `((tone: EmojiSkinTone) => void)` | | Called when another skin tone is chosen. | | `recent` | `string[]` | | The emoji picked before, newest first, when you keep them. Use it with `onRecentChange`. An empty list shows none. | | `onRecentChange` | `((recent: string[]) => void)` | | Called with the new list when an emoji is picked. | | `maxRecent` | `number` | `16` | How many picked emoji are remembered. | | `storageKey` | `string \| null` | `"nuvui-emoji"` | The name the recent emoji and the skin tone are kept under in the browser's local storage. `null` keeps nothing there. | | `flags` | `"auto" \| boolean` | `"auto"` | Whether flags are listed. `"auto"` lists them where the device draws them, which Windows doesn't. | | `autoFocus` | `boolean` | `false` | Puts the caret in the search box when it's first drawn. | | `labels` | `EmojiPickerLabels` | | What's said and not drawn, and the headings, for another language. | It's a `div`, and takes what a `div` takes, including `ref` and `className`. ## Translation `labels` takes the picker's own words. The emoji's names come with `data`. | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `search` | `string` | | The name of the search box, and what's written in it while it's empty. | | `list` | `string` | | The name of the list of emoji. | | `groups` | `string` | | The name of the row of buttons that jump to a group. | | `recent` | `string` | | The heading over the ones picked before. | | `results` | `string` | | The heading over what a search found. | | `group` | `Partial>` | | The name of each group. | | `skinTone` | `string` | | The name of the control for the skin tone. | | `skinTones` | `[string, string, string, string, string, string]` | | The six tones, from none to dark. | | `found` | `((count: number) => string)` | | Said after a search, with how many it found. | | `loading` | `string` | | Shown and said while the list is on its way. | ## Accessibility | Key | What it does | | --- | --- | | Tab | Goes to the search box, the skin tone, the list, and each group's button. The list is one stop. | | ↓ in the search box | Goes into the list. | | Enter in the search box | Picks the first emoji found. | | ← → | In the list, the emoji before and after. | | ↑ ↓ | The emoji in the row above and below. | | Home End | The ends of the row. With Ctrl, the ends of the list. | | Page Up Page Down | A screenful of rows. | | Enter Space | Picks the emoji the keys are on. | ### What the component handles - The list is a grid with a name. It holds the focus and says which emoji the keys are on, so only the rows in view have to be on the page. It says how many rows and columns there are in all. - Each emoji is read by its name, "waving hand", and not as the character. - A group's heading is a header in the grid, and its button is named by the group. The button of the group in view is marked as the current one. - After a search, how many emoji were found is said. When none were, that's shown as well. - The skin tones are a menu of six, one of them checked. The button says which. - An emoji's square is 44 pixels on a touch screen, as are the buttons. - Where text reads from the right, the left arrow goes on and the right one back. - Where the browser forces its own colors, the emoji the keys are on has an edge. ### What you need to handle - Name the popover or the dialog you put it in. - Say what was picked where the emoji lands, if it isn't where the reader is: the picker says which emoji the keys are on, and not what your app did with it. - Close the popover when an emoji is picked, or leave it open to pick several. Either is right for something. ## On small screens The picker is never wider than the room it's given, and the emoji in a row fill it. On a phone a [sheet](page:components/sheet) from the bottom holds it better than a popover does: set `--nuv-emoji-picker-width` to `100%` there. The search box is 16 pixels on a touch screen, so iOS doesn't zoom the page when it's tapped. ## CSS variables Set any of these on an `EmojiPicker`, or on anything around it. ```css .composer { --nuv-emoji-picker-width: 22rem; --nuv-emoji-picker-height: 20rem; } ``` | Variable | Default | What it sets | | --- | --- | --- | | `--nuv-emoji-picker-width` | `20rem` | Width of the panel. It's never wider than the room it's given. | | `--nuv-emoji-picker-height` | `24rem` | Height of the panel. The list scrolls in it. | | `--nuv-emoji-picker-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of the panel's border. | | `--nuv-emoji-picker-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of the panel. | | `--nuv-emoji-picker-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background of the panel. | | `--nuv-emoji-picker-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Color of the text. | | `--nuv-emoji-picker-cell` | `2.75rem`, `2.25rem` | Size of an emoji's square, and of the buttons. 2.25rem with a mouse and 2.75rem on a touch screen. Set it for both if you set it. | | `--nuv-emoji-picker-font` | `"Apple Color Emoji", "Segoe UI Emoji", "Noto Color Emoji", sans-serif` | The fonts the emoji are drawn in. The device's emoji fonts by default. | | `--nuv-emoji-picker-hover-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of an emoji or a button under the pointer, and of the emoji the keys are on. | | `--nuv-emoji-picker-heading-height` | `2rem` | Height of a group's heading. | | `--nuv-emoji-picker-heading-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the headings and of the words shown when nothing is found. Keep it at 4.5:1 against the panel. | | `--nuv-emoji-picker-emoji-size` | `1.375rem` | Size of the emoji in its square. | | `--nuv-emoji-picker-current-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of the button of the group in view. | ## Classes | Class | What it's on | | --- | --- | | `.nuv-emoji-picker` | EmojiPicker | | `.nuv-emoji-picker__body` | What holds the list. | | `.nuv-emoji-picker__emoji` | An emoji. | | `.nuv-emoji-picker__group` | A group's button. | | `.nuv-emoji-picker__groups` | The row of group buttons. | | `.nuv-emoji-picker__hand` | The hand in each choice of tone. | | `.nuv-emoji-picker__head` | The search box and the skin tone. | | `.nuv-emoji-picker__heading` | A group's heading. | | `.nuv-emoji-picker__note` | The words shown while the list is on its way, and when nothing is found. | | `.nuv-emoji-picker__row` | A row that's in view. | | `.nuv-emoji-picker__rows` | As tall as every row together. | | `.nuv-emoji-picker__search` | The search box. | | `.nuv-emoji-picker__sizer` | Never seen. The component reads the sizes from it. | | `.nuv-emoji-picker__status` | What's said after a search. Not drawn. | | `.nuv-emoji-picker__tone` | The button for the skin tone. | | `.nuv-emoji-picker__viewport` | The list, which is what scrolls. | The emoji the keys are on has a `data-active` attribute, and the panel has `data-loading` while the list is on its way. ## Server components EmojiPicker starts with `"use client"`, and `onEmojiSelect` is a function, so the component that renders it has to be a client component too. On a server the panel is drawn with its search box and no emoji: the list, what the browser remembers and the room there is are all known only in a browser. ## Do and don't **Do** - Put it where the emoji goes: beside the field, under the message. - Keep the recent ones with the account when people use more than one device. **Don't** - Don't raise `emojiVersion` past what the people who read the text can see. An emoji the reader's device doesn't have is a box to them, whoever picked it. - Don't use an emoji as the only way to say something that matters. It's read as its name, and the name may not be what you meant.

Props

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onEmojiSelect` | `((emoji: string, item: EmojiItem) => void)` |  | Called when an emoji is picked, with the emoji as text, in the skin tone that's set, and with what the list knows about it. |
| `data` | `EmojiItem[]` |  | The emoji to list, when the ones it comes with aren't the ones you want: another language's names, or fewer. Without it, the list it comes with is loaded when the picker is first drawn. |
| `emojiVersion` | `number` | `15` | The newest version of Emoji to list. Newer ones are left out, since a device that doesn't have them draws an empty box. |
| `skinTone` | `0 \| 1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5` |  | The skin tone, when you keep it. Use it with `onSkinToneChange`. |
| `defaultSkinTone` | `0 \| 1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5` | `0` | The skin tone to begin with, when it's kept here. |
| `onSkinToneChange` | `((tone: EmojiSkinTone) => void)` |  | Called when another skin tone is chosen. |
| `recent` | `string[]` |  | The emoji picked before, newest first, when you keep them. Use it with `onRecentChange`. An empty list shows none. |
| `onRecentChange` | `((recent: string[]) => void)` |  | Called with the new list when an emoji is picked. |
| `maxRecent` | `number` | `16` | How many picked emoji are remembered. |
| `storageKey` | `string \| null` | `"nuvui-emoji"` | The name the recent emoji and the skin tone are kept under in the browser's local storage. `null` keeps nothing there. |
| `flags` | `"auto" \| boolean` | `"auto"` | Whether flags are listed. `"auto"` lists them where the device draws them, which Windows doesn't. |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | `false` | Puts the caret in the search box when it's first drawn. |
| `labels` | `EmojiPickerLabels` |  | What's said and not drawn, and the headings, for another language. |

It's a `div`, and takes what a `div` takes, including `ref` and `className`.

sections.heading: Translation
sections.markdown:
## Translation

`labels` takes the picker's own words. The emoji's names come with `data`.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `search` | `string` |  | The name of the search box, and what's written in it while it's empty. |
| `list` | `string` |  | The name of the list of emoji. |
| `groups` | `string` |  | The name of the row of buttons that jump to a group. |
| `recent` | `string` |  | The heading over the ones picked before. |
| `results` | `string` |  | The heading over what a search found. |
| `group` | `Partial<Record<"activities" \| "animals" \| "flags" \| "food" \| "objects" \| "people" \| "smileys" \| "symbols" \| "travel", string>>` |  | The name of each group. |
| `skinTone` | `string` |  | The name of the control for the skin tone. |
| `skinTones` | `[string, string, string, string, string, string]` |  | The six tones, from none to dark. |
| `found` | `((count: number) => string)` |  | Said after a search, with how many it found. |
| `loading` | `string` |  | Shown and said while the list is on its way. |

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Goes to the search box, the skin tone, the list, and each group's button. The list is one stop. |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> in the search box | Goes into the list. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> in the search box | Picks the first emoji found. |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> | In the list, the emoji before and after. |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | The emoji in the row above and below. |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> <kbd>End</kbd> | The ends of the row. With <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>, the ends of the list. |
| <kbd>Page Up</kbd> <kbd>Page Down</kbd> | A screenful of rows. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> <kbd>Space</kbd> | Picks the emoji the keys are on. |

### What the component handles

- The list is a grid with a name. It holds the focus and says which emoji the keys are on, so only the rows in view have to be on the page. It says how many rows and columns there are in all.
- Each emoji is read by its name, "waving hand", and not as the character.
- A group's heading is a header in the grid, and its button is named by the group. The button of the group in view is marked as the current one.
- After a search, how many emoji were found is said. When none were, that's shown as well.
- The skin tones are a menu of six, one of them checked. The button says which.
- An emoji's square is 44 pixels on a touch screen, as are the buttons.
- Where text reads from the right, the left arrow goes on and the right one back.
- Where the browser forces its own colors, the emoji the keys are on has an edge.

### What you need to handle

- Name the popover or the dialog you put it in.
- Say what was picked where the emoji lands, if it isn't where the reader is: the picker says which emoji the keys are on, and not what your app did with it.
- Close the popover when an emoji is picked, or leave it open to pick several. Either is right for something.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

The picker is never wider than the room it's given, and the emoji in a row fill it. On a phone a [sheet](page:components/sheet) from the bottom holds it better than a popover does: set `--nuv-emoji-picker-width` to `100%` there.

The search box is 16 pixels on a touch screen, so iOS doesn't zoom the page when it's tapped.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on an `EmojiPicker`, or on anything around it.

```css
.composer {
  --nuv-emoji-picker-width: 22rem;
  --nuv-emoji-picker-height: 20rem;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-emoji-picker-width` | `20rem` | Width of the panel. It's never wider than the room it's given. |
| `--nuv-emoji-picker-height` | `24rem` | Height of the panel. The list scrolls in it. |
| `--nuv-emoji-picker-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of the panel's border. |
| `--nuv-emoji-picker-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of the panel. |
| `--nuv-emoji-picker-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background of the panel. |
| `--nuv-emoji-picker-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Color of the text. |
| `--nuv-emoji-picker-cell` | `2.75rem`, `2.25rem` | Size of an emoji's square, and of the buttons. 2.25rem with a mouse and 2.75rem on a touch screen. Set it for both if you set it. |
| `--nuv-emoji-picker-font` | `"Apple Color Emoji", "Segoe UI Emoji", "Noto Color Emoji", sans-serif` | The fonts the emoji are drawn in. The device's emoji fonts by default. |
| `--nuv-emoji-picker-hover-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of an emoji or a button under the pointer, and of the emoji the keys are on. |
| `--nuv-emoji-picker-heading-height` | `2rem` | Height of a group's heading. |
| `--nuv-emoji-picker-heading-fg` | `var(--color-muted-foreground)` | Color of the headings and of the words shown when nothing is found. Keep it at 4.5:1 against the panel. |
| `--nuv-emoji-picker-emoji-size` | `1.375rem` | Size of the emoji in its square. |
| `--nuv-emoji-picker-current-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of the button of the group in view. |

sections.markdown:

| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-emoji-picker` | EmojiPicker |
| `.nuv-emoji-picker__body` | What holds the list. |

| `.nuv-emoji-picker__groups` | The row of group buttons. |

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

EmojiPicker starts with `"use client"`, and `onEmojiSelect` is a function, so the component that renders it has to be a client component too. On a server the panel is drawn with its search box and no emoji: the list, what the browser remembers and the room there is are all known only in a browser.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Put it where the emoji goes: beside the field, under the message.
- Keep the recent ones with the account when people use more than one device.

**Don't**

- Don't raise `emojiVersion` past what the people who read the text can see. An emoji the reader's device doesn't have is a box to them, whoever picked it.
- Don't use an emoji as the only way to say something that matters. It's read as its name, and the name may not be what you meant.

pages.title: EmojiReaction
pages.description: A button with an emoji and how many reacted with it, pressed when the reader is one of them. For the row of reactions under a message or a comment.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/emoji @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { EmojiReaction } from "@nuvui/emoji";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/emoji/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Emoji](page:emoji/index) covers that. From `@nuvui/emoji/emoji-reaction` the button comes without the picker, and its styles are at `@nuvui/emoji/css/emoji-reaction.css`.

```tsx
<EmojiReaction
  emoji="👍"
  label="thumbs up"
  count={others + (mine ? 1 : 0)}
  pressed={mine}
  onPressedChange={setMine}
/>
```

sections.heading: The count is yours
sections.markdown:
## The count is yours

The button keeps nothing. `count` is what it shows and `pressed` is whether the reader is one of them, and a press only calls `onPressedChange` with what `pressed` would become. So the count can come from your server, be changed at once and put back if the request fails, or change when someone else reacts.

Count the reader in: three others and the reader is `count={4}` with `pressed`.

A reaction nobody is left on is yours to take off the row. The button doesn't hide itself at zero.

sections.heading: With a picker
Large counts, and reactions that can't be pressed
Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `emoji` (required) | `string` |  | The emoji, as text. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | The emoji's name, such as "thumbs up". It's what the button is read as, with the count, since a screen reader's own name for an emoji varies from one to the next. |
| `count` (required) | `number` |  | How many reacted with it, the reader included when it's theirs. |
| `pressed` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the reader is one of them. |
| `onPressedChange` | `((pressed: boolean) => void)` |  | Called when it's pressed, with what `pressed` would become. The count is yours to change with it. |

It's a `button`, and takes what a `button` takes, including `ref`, `className`, `disabled` and `onClick`. An `onClick` that calls `preventDefault()` stops the press.

sections.heading: Translation
sections.markdown:
## Translation

The button is named `label` and the count, as in "thumbs up, 4", and whether it's pressed is said by the screen reader in its own language. `label` is the one word of yours in it. For a name put together another way, give `aria-label`.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Goes to each reaction in turn. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> <kbd>Space</kbd> | Joins the reaction, or takes the reader's away. |

### What the component handles

- It's a button that says whether it's pressed.
- It's read by the emoji's name and the count, and not as the character, which a screen reader may name another way or not at all.
- The reader's own has an edge in another color that's also twice as thick, so it isn't told apart by color alone. Where the browser forces its own colors the border is the thick one.
- It's 44 pixels tall on a touch screen, and 32 with a mouse.
- The count asks for figures of one width, so the row doesn't shift as a count changes where the font has them.

### What you need to handle

- Give `label` the emoji's name, in the reader's language.
- Say what a press did, in a [live region](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Guides/Live_regions), if it isn't plain from the button: the new count is in its name, and a screen reader doesn't read a name again because it changed.
- When the reader takes away the last of a reaction and you take its button off the row, put the focus somewhere, such as on the button that adds one. The second example does.
- Name the row if there's more than one on the page, with `role="group"` and an `aria-label` such as "Reactions to Priya's message".

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

Put the reactions in a row that wraps. Each keeps its size, and a count never wraps inside its button.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on an `EmojiReaction`, or on anything around it.

```css
.thread {
  --nuv-emoji-reaction-radius: var(--radius-md);
  --nuv-emoji-reaction-height: 2.25rem;
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-emoji-reaction-gap` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 1.5)` | Space between the emoji and the count. |
| `--nuv-emoji-reaction-height` | `var(--nuv-touch-size, 2.75rem)`, `2rem` | Least height of the button. The touch size on a touch screen and 2rem with a mouse. Set it for both if you set it. |
| `--nuv-emoji-reaction-padding-inline` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 3)`, `calc(var(--spacing) * 2.5)` | Space at each end. |
| `--nuv-emoji-reaction-border` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Color of the border. Keep it at 3:1 against what's behind it. |
| `--nuv-emoji-reaction-radius` | `var(--radius-full)` | Corner radius. A pill by default. |
| `--nuv-emoji-reaction-bg` | `transparent` | Background. |
| `--nuv-emoji-reaction-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of the count. |
| `--nuv-emoji-reaction-hover-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background under the pointer. |
| `--nuv-emoji-reaction-pressed-border` | `var(--color-primary)` | Color of the edge of the reader's own, which is twice as thick. |
| `--nuv-emoji-reaction-pressed-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | Background of the reader's own. |
| `--nuv-emoji-reaction-font` | `"Apple Color Emoji", "Segoe UI Emoji", "Noto Color Emoji", sans-serif` | The fonts the emoji is drawn in. The device's emoji fonts by default. |
| `--nuv-emoji-reaction-emoji-size` | `var(--text-base)` | Size of the emoji. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-emoji-reaction` | EmojiReaction |
| `.nuv-emoji-reaction__count` | The count. |
| `.nuv-emoji-reaction__emoji` | The emoji. |

The reader's own has `aria-pressed="true"` and a `data-pressed` attribute.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

EmojiReaction starts with `"use client"`. One that only shows a count, with `disabled` and no `onPressedChange`, can be rendered from a server component. With `onPressedChange`, which is a function, the component that renders it has to be a client component too.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Change the count at once when it's pressed, and put it back if saving fails.
- Keep the order of the row as it is when a count changes, so nothing moves under the pointer.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for a vote that decides something. A reaction is light, and is read as one.
- Don't leave `label` as the emoji itself. It's the name that's read.

pages.title: Map
pages.description: The @nuvui/map package. A map on MapLibre, installed next to @nuvui/react, with markers and popups that are React elements and controls that are the library's own buttons. It needs map tiles from a provider you choose.
pages.markdown:
# Map The @nuvui/map package. A map on MapLibre, installed next to @nuvui/react, with markers and popups that are React elements and controls that are the library's own buttons. It needs map tiles from a provider you choose. The map is a package of its own, `@nuvui/map`, since drawing one needs an engine the core doesn't have: | Component | What it is | | --- | --- | | [MapView](page:map/map-view) | A map, with `MapMarker` for a place on it, `MapPopup` for a box that points at one, and `MapControls` for the buttons over it. | | [MapRoute](page:map/map-route) | A line through a list of places, for a way that was driven or one that's planned. | | [MapClusters](page:map/map-clusters) | Many places, gathered into one button with a number on it where they're near each other. | ```tsx "use client"; import { MapControls, MapMarker, MapView } from "@nuvui/map"; // A style is where the tiles come from and how they're drawn. This one is // OpenFreeMap's, which asks for no key. Use your own provider's. const style = "https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty"; export default function Example() { return ( Berlin office
Friedrichstraße 68, open nine to five } /> ); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/map maplibre-gl @nuvui/react ``` `@nuvui/react` is a peer dependency: the controls are the core's [Button](page:components/button), and the map's box, its markers and its popups are drawn with the core's tokens. The map is drawn by [MapLibre GL JS](https://maplibre.org), which is BSD-3-Clause licensed. It's a peer dependency too, version 6.4.1 or newer, so it's yours to install and to keep up to date, and its worker is a file your app can reach. ## Load the styles Import the package's stylesheet once, after the core's: ```tsx title="app/layout.tsx" import "@nuvui/react/styles.css"; import "@nuvui/map/styles.css"; ``` Both files open with the same line naming the cascade layers, so the order you import them in doesn't decide which rule wins. The map's styles are also on their own, at `@nuvui/map/css/map.css`. With that one, load `button.css` from `@nuvui/react/css/` as well. MapLibre has a stylesheet of its own, and you don't load it. The rules of it that a map can't do without are in this package's stylesheet, in the library's colors. ## Tell the map where its worker is MapLibre does its work off the page's own thread, in a worker, and the worker is a file of its own: `maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl-worker.mjs`. MapLibre looks for it beside itself. A bundler folds MapLibre into a file of the bundler's naming and leaves nothing beside it, so an app that's built with one says where the worker is, once, before a map is drawn. `setMapWorkerUrl` takes the address, and your bundler is asked for it. With Next.js, or webpack: ```tsx title="components/map-worker.ts" "use client"; import { setMapWorkerUrl } from "@nuvui/map"; setMapWorkerUrl( new URL("maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl-worker.mjs", import.meta.url), ); ``` With Vite: ```tsx title="src/main.tsx" import { setMapWorkerUrl } from "@nuvui/map"; import workerUrl from "maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl-worker.mjs?url"; setMapWorkerUrl(workerUrl); ``` Either way the bundler copies the file into what it builds and hands back where it put it. Run this from a file that's loaded before any map is, such as the one your app starts in, or one that your own map component imports. Without it, a map in a bundled app stays on "Loading map". Whatever serves your site has to send that file as JavaScript. A browser won't run a worker that's sent as anything else, and some servers don't know the ending `.mjs`. If the map never loads once the site is up, look at what the worker's address is sent as. ## You bring the map A map is drawn from tiles, small squares of it that are fetched as the map moves, and tiles are served by someone. This package has no tiles and no provider. `mapStyle` takes the address of a [MapLibre style](https://maplibre.org/maplibre-style-spec/), which says where the tiles come from and how they're drawn, or the style itself. ```tsx ``` Who serves the style is your provider, and that's a choice: - **It has a cost.** A provider charges by how much map is looked at, or gives some away, or you run a tile server of your own. Read their terms before a map is on a page that many people open. - **Their names are shown.** Most terms ask that the provider, and the people whose data it is, are named on the map. The names come from the style and are drawn in the map's corner at every width. Don't hide them. - **They see the reader.** A reader's browser asks the provider for the tiles, so the provider learns the reader's address and what part of the world they looked at. Say so where you say such things, such as in a privacy notice. The examples on these pages use [OpenFreeMap](https://openfreemap.org)'s style, which asks for no key. So opening one of these pages asks OpenFreeMap for tiles. ## It's large, so it's loaded when it's needed MapLibre is about 235 kB compressed, and its worker another 120 kB. The package asks for MapLibre when a map is first drawn, and not before, so a page with no map on screen loads neither and a server never does. The rest of the package is about 6 kB. Until MapLibre and the style have come, the box says the map is loading. ## What a browser needs - **WebGL.** A map is drawn with it. Where a browser has none, or it's turned off, the box says the map couldn't be drawn, and `onError` is called. Give the address in words as well where the place matters. - **A content security policy,** if you have one, has to let the map work. The worker is a file on your own site, so `worker-src 'self'` covers it. Served from another origin, such as a CDN, MapLibre runs it from a `blob:` address, and it needs `worker-src blob:`. `connect-src` and `img-src` have to name your provider. ## What it leaves out - **Tiles, and a default style.** See above. - **Finding a place from words,** and directions between two. Those are services, from your provider or another. [MapRoute](page:map/map-route) draws the way such a service gives. - **Drawing on the map,** such as an area to search in. - **A picture of a map** for where there's no WebGL, or for print.

`@nuvui/react` is a peer dependency: the controls are the core's [Button](page:components/button), and the map's box, its markers and its popups are drawn with the core's tokens.

The map is drawn by [MapLibre GL JS](https://maplibre.org), which is BSD-3-Clause licensed. It's a peer dependency too, version 6.4.1 or newer, so it's yours to install and to keep up to date, and its worker is a file your app can reach.

Until MapLibre and the style have come, the box says the map is loading.

- **WebGL.** A map is drawn with it. Where a browser has none, or it's turned off, the box says the map couldn't be drawn, and `onError` is called. Give the address in words as well where the place matters.

Served from another origin, such as a CDN, MapLibre runs it from a `blob:` address, and it needs `worker-src blob:`. `connect-src` and `img-src` have to name your provider.

- **Finding a place from words,** and directions between two. Those are services, from your provider or another. [MapRoute](page:map/map-route) draws the way such a service gives.
- **Drawing on the map,** such as an area to search in.
