pages.title: MapView
pages.description: A map on MapLibre, with markers that are read by name, popups, and controls that are the library's own buttons. It takes the arrow keys, says when it's loading, and says when it can't be drawn.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/map maplibre-gl @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { MapControls, MapMarker, MapPopup, MapView } from "@nuvui/map";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/map/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Map](page:map/index) covers that, and two things a map needs before it's drawn: [where MapLibre's worker is](page:map/index#tell-the-map-where-its-worker-is), and where its tiles come from, which is yours to choose.

```tsx
<MapView
  aria-label="Where the office is"
  mapStyle="https://tiles.example.com/styles/streets.json"
  defaultCenter={[13.3888, 52.5105]}
  defaultZoom={13}
>
  <MapMarker position={[13.3888, 52.5105]} label="Berlin office" />
  <MapControls />
</MapView>
```

A place is written as longitude and then latitude, which is the order GeoJSON and MapLibre have, and the other way round from how coordinates are often said.

sections.heading: Where the map is
Moving it from your code
Markers
A popup of its own
Controls
sections.markdown:
## Controls

`MapControls` is a column of buttons in a corner of the map. They're the core's buttons, so they're in your theme.

- `zoom`, on by default: zoom in and zoom out, each disabled when there's no further to go.
- `compass`: turns north back up, and shows which way north is.
- `locate`: goes to where the reader is, which the browser asks them to allow, and marks it. When the browser won't say, that's said to a screen reader. `onLocate` is called with the place.
- `fullscreen`: fills the screen with the map. It's left out where the browser can't, which is on an iPhone.

`position` is the corner, and children are buttons of your own, after the others.

sections.heading: In a page that scrolls
sections.markdown:
## In a page that scrolls

A map takes the mouse wheel to zoom and a finger to move, which is how someone scrolling down a page gets stuck in one. `cooperativeGestures` leaves both to the page: the map zooms with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> or <kbd>⌘</kbd> held and moves under two fingers, and says so over itself when the wheel or one finger is tried. The examples on this page have it.

Leave it off where the map is the page, as in a screen that's a map from edge to edge.

sections.heading: Loading, and when there's no map
sections.markdown:
## Loading, and when there's no map

Until MapLibre and the style have come, the box says "Loading map". When the map can't be drawn, because the browser has no WebGL or the style can't be had, the box says so and `onError` is called with the error. `onError` is also called for a tile that can't be had, which leaves the map standing.

Where the place matters, don't let the map be the only way to learn it. Write the address beside it.

sections.heading: The map itself
Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

### MapView

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mapStyle` (required) | `MapStyle` |  | The map's style, which says where its tiles come from and how they're drawn: the address of a style, or the style itself. Whoever serves it is the map's provider, and that's yours to choose. |
| `center` | `MapLngLat` |  | The middle of the map, when you keep it. The map moves there when it changes. |
| `defaultCenter` | `MapLngLat` | `[0, 20]` | The middle of the map to begin with. |
| `zoom` | `number` |  | How far in the map is, when you keep it. 0 is the whole world. |
| `defaultZoom` | `number` | `1` | How far in the map is to begin with. |
| `bounds` | `MapBounds` |  | An area to show all of. The map fits it when first drawn, in place of the center and the zoom, and again when it changes. |
| `boundsPadding` | `number` | `48` | The room left around `bounds`, in pixels. |
| `minZoom` | `number` |  |  |
| `maxZoom` | `number` |  |  |
| `interactive` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the map can be moved, by pointer, touch and keys. Read when the map is first drawn. |
| `cooperativeGestures` | `boolean` | `false` | Leaves the wheel and one finger to the page: the map zooms with Ctrl or ⌘ held, and moves under two fingers. For a map in a page that scrolls. Read when the map is first drawn. |
| `onMove` | `((view: MapViewState) => void)` |  | Called as the map moves, with where it is. |
| `onMoveEnd` | `((view: MapViewState) => void)` |  | Called when the map has come to rest. |
| `onLoad` | `((map: MapInstance) => void)` |  | Called once, when the style and the first tiles have come. |
| `onError` | `((error: Error) => void)` |  | Called when the map can't be drawn, or a tile or the style can't be had. |
| `labels` | `MapLabels` |  | The map's own words, for another language. Read when the map is first drawn. |

It's a `div`, and takes what a `div` takes, including `ref`, `className` and `style`. `aria-label` is the map's name.

### MapMarker

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `position` (required) | `MapLngLat` |  | Where it is. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | What it marks, such as "Berlin office". It's the marker's name, read in place of the drawing. |
| `anchor` | `"bottom" \| "center"` | `"bottom"` | The part of the marker that's on the place: the middle of its foot, for a pin, or its own middle, for a dot. |
| `draggable` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether it can be moved, by dragging it or with the arrow keys. |
| `onPositionChange` | `((position: MapLngLat) => void)` |  | Called when it's been moved, with where it was put. |
| `popup` | `ReactNode` |  | What opens over the marker when it's pressed. |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Whether the popup is open, when you keep it. Use it with `onOpenChange`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the popup is open to begin with. |
| `onOpenChange` | `((open: boolean) => void)` |  | Called when the popup opens or closes. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | The marker's drawing, in place of the pin. |

It takes what a `button` takes, including `ref`, `className` and `onClick`. An `onClick` that calls `preventDefault()` leaves the popup closed.

### MapPopup

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `position` (required) | `MapLngLat` |  | The place it points at. |
| `onClose` | `(() => void)` |  | Called when it's closed: by its button, by Escape, or by a press on the map. |
| `offset` | `Offset` | `0` | How far it stands off the place, in pixels. |
| `closeOnMapClick` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether a press on the map closes it. |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the focus goes into it when it opens. Turn it off for one that opens without being asked for, such as with the page. |

It's a `div`, and takes what a `div` takes. Give it an `aria-label`.

### MapControls

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | `"bottom-end" \| "bottom-start" \| "top-end" \| "top-start"` | `"top-end"` | The corner they're in. The start is the left where text reads from the left. |
| `zoom` | `boolean` | `true` | Buttons to zoom in and out. |
| `compass` | `boolean` | `false` | A button that turns north back up. It shows which way north is. |
| `locate` | `boolean` | `false` | A button that goes to where the reader is, which the browser asks them to allow. |
| `fullscreen` | `boolean` | `false` | A button that fills the screen with the map, where the browser can. |
| `onLocate` | `((position: MapLngLat) => void)` |  | Called when the browser has said where the reader is. |

It's a `div`, and takes what a `div` takes.

sections.heading: Translation
sections.markdown:
## Translation

`labels` on `MapView` takes the map's own words: the buttons' names, what's said while it loads and when it can't be drawn, and what `cooperativeGestures` says over the map. They're read when the map is first drawn. A marker's `label` and a popup's `aria-label` are yours.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `map` | `string` |  | The name of the map, when it's given no `aria-label`. |
| `loading` | `string` |  | Shown and said until the map's style has come. |
| `error` | `string` |  | Shown and said when the map can't be drawn. |
| `zoomIn` | `string` |  |  |
| `zoomOut` | `string` |  |  |
| `resetNorth` | `string` |  | The name of the button that turns north back up. |
| `locate` | `string` |  | The name of the button that goes to where the reader is. |
| `locateError` | `string` |  | Said when the browser won't say where the reader is. |
| `location` | `string` |  | The name of the marker at where the reader is. |
| `fullscreen` | `string` |  |  |
| `exitFullscreen` | `string` |  |  |
| `closePopup` | `string` |  |  |
| `gestureMac` | `string` |  | With `cooperativeGestures`, shown over the map on a Mac when the wheel is turned over it. |
| `gestureOther` | `string` |  | The same, on other computers. |
| `gestureTouch` | `string` |  | The same, on a touch screen, when one finger is dragged over it. |

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Goes to the map, then to each marker that's a button, in the order they're written, then to the links that name whose map it is, then to the controls. |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | On the map, moves it. On a marker that can be moved, moves the marker. |
| <kbd>+</kbd> <kbd>−</kbd> | On the map, zooms in and out. |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> with <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> | On the map, turns it. |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> <kbd>Space</kbd> | On a marker, opens its popup or closes it. |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Closes the popup and puts the focus back on its marker. |

### What the component handles

- The map is a region with a name and takes the focus, with a ring when the keys are on it.
- A marker is read by its `label`. One that does something is a button, and says whether its popup is open.
- A popup is a dialog named for its marker. The focus goes into it when the marker is pressed, and back to the marker when it's closed from inside.
- The controls are buttons with names. A zoom button that can go no further is disabled.
- While the map loads, and when it can't be drawn, that's said and not only shown.
- Moves that are asked for are made at once, without a glide, where the reader has asked for less motion.
- A marker and each button take a tap over 44 pixels on a touch screen.
- Where the browser forces its own colors, the pin is drawn in them.

### What you need to handle

- Give the map an `aria-label` that says what it's of: "Our offices", and not "Map".
- A map says little to someone who can't see it. Give what it shows another way as well: a list of the places beside it, or the address in words. The [Find a branch block](https://nuvui.nuvraxis.com/blocks/data) is a list and a map of the same places.
- Keep the markers that are buttons few enough to tab through. Hundreds of stops is no way across a page. [MapClusters](page:map/map-clusters) gathers the ones that are near each other.
- The colors of the map are the style's. Check that what matters on it can be told apart, and that your markers stand off it.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

The map is as wide as the room it's given, and `--nuv-map-height` is how tall. On a phone, with `cooperativeGestures`, one finger scrolls the page and two move the map.

A popup is never wider than `--nuv-map-popup-width`, and opens on whichever side of its place has room.

sections.heading: CSS variables
sections.markdown:
## CSS variables

Set any of these on a `MapView`, or on anything around it.

```css
.locator {
  --nuv-map-height: 32rem;
  --nuv-map-marker-bg: var(--color-danger);
}
```

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--nuv-map-height` | `24rem` | Height of the map's box. |
| `--nuv-map-border` | `var(--color-border)` | Color of the box's border. |
| `--nuv-map-radius` | `var(--radius-lg)` | Corner radius of the box. |
| `--nuv-map-bg` | `var(--color-muted)` | What's behind the map before its tiles come, and behind the words shown in its place. |
| `--nuv-map-note-fg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | Color of the words shown while the map loads and when it can't be drawn. |
| `--nuv-map-marker-bg` | `var(--color-primary)` | Color of the pin, and of the dot where the reader is. |
| `--nuv-map-marker-fg` | `var(--color-primary-foreground)` | Color of the pin's edge and of the dot in it. It's what keeps the pin seen on a map of any color. |
| `--nuv-map-cluster-size` | `2.25rem` | Width and height of a gathering of under ten places. It's half a rem more from ten, and a rem more from a hundred. |
| `--nuv-map-cluster-fg` | `var(--color-primary-foreground)` | Color of a gathering's number and of its edge. Keep it at 4.5:1 against its background. |
| `--nuv-map-cluster-bg` | `var(--color-primary)` | Background of a gathering. |
| `--nuv-map-route-edge` | `var(--color-primary-foreground)` | Color of the edge along a route's line. It's what keeps the line seen on a map of any color. |
| `--nuv-map-route-color` | `var(--color-primary)` | Color of a route's line. |
| `--nuv-map-popup-width` | `18rem` | The most a popup is wide. |
| `--nuv-map-popup-padding` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 3)` | Space inside a popup. |
| `--nuv-map-popup-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Color of a popup's text. |
| `--nuv-map-controls-offset` | `calc(var(--spacing) * 2)` | Space between the controls and the box's edge. |
| `--nuv-map-attribution-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background behind the names of whose map it is. |
| `--nuv-map-attribution-fg` | `var(--color-surface-foreground)` | Color of those names. Keep it at 4.5:1 against its background. |
| `--nuv-map-popup-border` | `var(--color-border-strong)` | Color of the line and the shadow around a popup. |
| `--nuv-map-popup-radius` | `var(--radius-md)` | Corner radius of a popup. |
| `--nuv-map-popup-bg` | `var(--color-surface)` | Background of a popup and its tip. |
| `--nuv-map-gesture-bg` | `var(--color-foreground)` | With cooperativeGestures, what covers the map while it says how to move it. |
| `--nuv-map-gesture-fg` | `var(--color-background)` | Color of those words. |

sections.heading: Classes
sections.markdown:
## Classes

| Class | What it's on |
| --- | --- |
| `.nuv-map` | MapView |
| `.nuv-map__canvas` | What MapLibre draws the map in. |
| `.nuv-map__cluster` | A gathering in MapClusters. It's a marker as well, and has that class too. |
| `.nuv-map__control` | One of the buttons. |
| `.nuv-map__controls` | MapControls |
| `.nuv-map__controls--bottom-end` | In the bottom corner at the end. |
| `.nuv-map__controls--bottom-start` | In the bottom corner at the start. |
| `.nuv-map__controls--top-end` | In the top corner at the end. |
| `.nuv-map__controls--top-start` | In the top corner at the start. |
| `.nuv-map__location` | The dot where the reader is. |
| `.nuv-map__marker` | MapMarker |
| `.nuv-map__marker-holder` | What MapLibre places on the map, with a marker in it. |
| `.nuv-map__note` | The words shown while the map loads, and when it can't be drawn. |
| `.nuv-map__pin` | The pin drawn when a marker has no children. |
| `.nuv-map__pin-body` | The pin's shape. |
| `.nuv-map__pin-dot` | The dot in the pin. |
| `.nuv-map__popup` | MapPopup |
| `.nuv-map__popup-body` | What's in the popup. |
| `.nuv-map__popup-close` | The popup's close button. |
| `.nuv-map__route` | MapRoute's own element. It isn't drawn: the line's colors are read from it. |
| `.nuv-map__status` | What's said when the reader can't be found. Not drawn. |

The box has `data-state`, which is `loading`, `ready` or `error`. A marker that can be moved has `data-draggable`, and a gathering has `data-size`. MapLibre's own elements keep its class names, which begin with `maplibregl-`.

sections.heading: Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

`MapView` and its parts start with `"use client"`. A `MapView` with plain props can be rendered from a server component, and the server draws the box with the words "Loading map". The map itself is drawn in a browser. Markers, popups and controls are drawn once there's a map, so they aren't in what the server sends.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Say what the map is of, and give the same places in words beside it.
- Use `bounds` to show every marker, and not a center and a zoom worked out by hand.
- Turn on `cooperativeGestures` for a map in a page that scrolls.

**Don't**

- Don't hide the names in the map's corner. They're a term of using the map.
- Don't put a map on a page where the address would do. It's 350 kB and a request to someone else's server.
- Don't use a marker's color alone to say something, such as open or closed. Say it in the `label` and the popup.

pages.title: MapRoute
pages.description: A line on a map through a list of places, for a way that was driven or one that's planned. It's drawn in the theme's colors, with an edge that keeps it seen on a map of any color.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/map maplibre-gl @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { MapRoute, MapView, mapBoundsOf } from "@nuvui/map";
```

A route goes inside a [MapView](page:map/map-view), which is where the styles, the worker and the provider are covered.

```tsx
<MapView aria-label="The way to the office" mapStyle={style}>
  <MapRoute
    coordinates={[
      [13.3777, 52.5163],
      [13.3888, 52.5105],
      [13.4050, 52.5200],
    ]}
  />
</MapView>
```

`coordinates` is the places the line goes through, in order, each as longitude and then latitude. A straight line is drawn from each to the next, so a way along roads needs a place at every bend, which is what a routing service gives.

sections.heading: Showing all of it
sections.markdown:
## Showing all of it

`mapBoundsOf` takes a list of places and gives back the area that holds them, for the map's `bounds`. With it the map opens on the whole route, whatever size the map is.

```tsx
<MapView
  aria-label="Van 12 on its round"
  mapStyle={style}
  bounds={mapBoundsOf(way)}
  boundsPadding={64}
>
  <MapRoute coordinates={way} />
</MapView>
```

It works on any list of places, so it's also the one for "show every marker".

sections.heading: Driven and planned
sections.markdown:
## Driven and planned

`dashed` draws the line in dashes. Two routes, one after the other, show a way that's part done: the first for what's behind, the second with `dashed` for what's ahead. The example at the top does that.

`width` is how thick the line is, in pixels.

sections.heading: Colors
Under the place names
sections.markdown:
## Under the place names

A route is drawn over everything in the map's style, names of streets included. `before` takes the name of a layer in the style and draws the route under it, which keeps the names readable over a thick line.

```tsx
<MapRoute coordinates={way} before="road_label" />
```

The names of the layers are the style's own, so they differ from one provider to the next. Your provider's style lists them. A name the style doesn't have leaves the route on top.

sections.heading: Stops along it
sections.markdown:
## Stops along it

A route has no markers. Put a [MapMarker](page:map/map-view#markers) at each place that matters: the start, the end, the stops.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `coordinates` (required) | `MapLngLat[]` |  | The places the line goes through, in order. |
| `width` | `number` | `4` | How thick the line is, in pixels. |
| `dashed` | `boolean` | `false` | Draws it in dashes, for a way that's planned and not yet gone. |
| `before` | `string` |  | The name of a layer in the map's style to draw it under, such as the style's first layer of place names. Left out, it's drawn over the map. |

It renders a `span` that isn't drawn, which is where the colors are read from, and takes what a `span` takes, including `ref`, `className` and `style`. The line itself is drawn by MapLibre on the map's canvas.

### mapBoundsOf

```ts
function mapBoundsOf(places: MapLngLat[]): MapBounds | undefined;
```

The south-west and north-east corners of the area that holds every place. An empty list gives `undefined`, which leaves the map where it is.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.markdown:
## Accessibility

A line on a canvas is a picture, and isn't read. Nothing on it takes the focus.

### What the component handles

- The line has an edge in a second color, so it stands off a map of any color.

### What you need to handle

- Say in words what the route shows: where it starts and ends, the stops in order, how far along it is. A list beside the map does it. The [delivery route block](https://nuvui.nuvraxis.com/blocks/data) is a list and a map of the same stops.
- Give the map an `aria-label` that says whose way it is.
- Don't tell routes apart by color alone.

sections.heading: On small screens
sections.markdown:
## On small screens

The line is as thick on a phone as on a desk. With `bounds` from `mapBoundsOf`, the whole route is in view at any width.

sections.heading: CSS variables
Server components
sections.markdown:
## Server components

`MapRoute` starts with `"use client"`. It's drawn once there's a map, which is in a browser, so it isn't in what a server sends.

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Pass the places a routing service gives, with one at every bend.
- Use `dashed` for what's planned, beside a solid line for what's done.
- Put the stops in words beside the map.

**Don't**

- Don't draw a straight line between two towns and call it a way to drive.
- Don't use more colors than someone can keep apart. Past three or four routes, let the reader choose which to show.

pages.title: MapClusters
pages.description: Many places on a map, gathered into one button with a number on it where they're near each other, and drawn apart as the map zooms in. Each gathering and each place is a button with a name.
pages.markdown:
# MapClusters Many places on a map, gathered into one button with a number on it where they're near each other, and drawn apart as the map zooms in. Each gathering and each place is a button with a name. Use clusters when there are more places than a map can show one by one: every branch in a country, every charging point in a city. Zoomed out, places that would sit on top of each other are one round button that says how many. A press on it zooms the map in, and they come apart. ```tsx "use client"; import { type MapClusterPoint, MapClusters, MapControls, type MapLngLat, MapMarker, MapView, mapBoundsOf, } from "@nuvui/map"; const style = "https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty"; interface Charger extends MapClusterPoint { name: string; free: number; } // Made up, and stands in for the places your server has: a few charging // points around each of four cities. const cities: { name: string; at: MapLngLat; count: number }[] = [ { name: "Amsterdam", at: [4.8952, 52.3702], count: 8 }, { name: "Groningen", at: [6.5665, 53.2194], count: 6 }, { name: "Enschede", at: [6.8937, 52.2215], count: 5 }, { name: "Eindhoven", at: [5.4697, 51.4416], count: 4 }, ]; const around: MapLngLat[] = [ [0, 0], [0.012, 0.006], [-0.01, 0.009], [0.018, -0.008], [-0.016, -0.005], [0.006, 0.015], [-0.004, -0.014], [0.022, 0.012], ]; const chargers: Charger[] = cities.flatMap((city) => around.slice(0, city.count).map((offset, index) => ({ id: `${city.name}-${index + 1}`, name: `${city.name} ${index + 1}`, position: [city.at[0] + offset[0], city.at[1] + offset[1]], free: (index * 3 + city.count) % 4, })), ); const all = mapBoundsOf(chargers.map((charger) => charger.position)); export default function Example() { return ( `${count} charging points`} > {(charger) => ( {charger.name}
{charger.free === 0 ? "All in use" : `${charger.free} of 4 free`} } /> )} ); } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/map maplibre-gl @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { MapClusters, MapMarker, MapView } from "@nuvui/map"; ``` Clusters go inside a [MapView](page:map/map-view), which is where the styles, the worker and the provider are covered. ```tsx {(branch) => } ``` ## The places `points` is every place, in view or not. Each has an `id` that tells it from the others and a `position`, as longitude and then latitude. Whatever else is on it is yours, and comes back to you. ```tsx interface Branch extends MapClusterPoint { name: string; open: boolean; } ``` The child is a function. It's called for each place in view that stands on its own, with that place, and returns its [MapMarker](page:map/map-view#markers): a pin, a popup, a drawing of your own, as for any marker. It isn't called for the places in a gathering, or for those out of view, so a thousand places don't make a thousand elements. ## How near is near `radius` is how close two places are on the screen, in pixels, to be gathered. The default is 50. Smaller, and more places stand alone, closer together. `maxZoom` is the zoom past which nothing is gathered, however near. The default is 14, which is a few streets. Two places at one address stay one button until then, and past it are two markers on the same spot, so raise it where that happens. Changing either gathers the places again from the start. ## What a gathering says A gathering shows its number, shortened past a thousand in the reader's own language. Its name, which is what's read, comes from `clusterLabel`. The default is "12 places". Say what they are: ```tsx `${count} charging points`} > ``` A press on a gathering zooms the map in to where it comes apart, which may be into smaller gatherings. Pressed from the keys, the focus goes to the map, since the button that had it is gone. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `points` (required) | `Point[]` | | Every place, whether it's in view or not. | | `children` (required) | `(point: Point) => ReactNode` | | Draws a place that stands on its own, as a `MapMarker`. It's called for the places in view that aren't gathered, and not for the rest. | | `radius` | `number` | `50` | How near two places are, in pixels, to be gathered into one. | | `maxZoom` | `number` | `14` | The zoom past which nothing is gathered, however near. | | `clusterLabel` | `((count: number) => string)` | `(count) => '${count} places'` | The name of a gathering, from how many places are in it. It's what's read in place of the number. | It renders markers and nothing around them, so it takes no `ref`, `className` or `style`. Style a gathering through the variables below, or by its class. ### MapClusterPoint | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `id` (required) | `string \| number` | | What tells it from the others. | | `position` (required) | `MapLngLat` | | Where it is. | ## Translation `clusterLabel` is the gathering's name, from its number, so it can follow the rules your language has for one, two and many. The number on the button is written by the browser in the reader's language. ## Accessibility | Key | What it does | | --- | --- | | Tab | Goes to each gathering, then to each marker that's a button. | | Enter Space | On a gathering, zooms the map in to where it comes apart. | ### What the component handles - A gathering is a button, read by its name and not by the bare number. - Only what's in view is on the page, so the Tab key doesn't go through places nobody can see. - A gathering takes a tap over 44 pixels on a touch screen. - Pressed from the keys, the focus goes to the map, where the arrow keys and plus and minus go on working. - Where the browser forces its own colors, a gathering has an edge in them. ### What you need to handle - Say in `clusterLabel` what the places are. - Give each marker a `label` that names its place. - A map of many places is hard going without sight. Give the same places as a list that can be searched, as the [charging points block](https://nuvui.nuvraxis.com/blocks/data) does. ## On small screens A narrower map shows less, so more is gathered at the same zoom. Nothing else changes: a gathering is the same size, and is pressed the same way. ## CSS variables A gathering's variables are in the [MapView](page:map/map-view#css-variables) page's list with the rest of the map's: `--nuv-map-cluster-bg`, `--nuv-map-cluster-fg` and `--nuv-map-cluster-size`. ```css .chargers { --nuv-map-cluster-bg: var(--color-danger); --nuv-map-cluster-fg: var(--color-danger-foreground); } ``` A gathering has the class `nuv-map__cluster` and `data-size`, which is `sm` under ten places, `md` under a hundred and `lg` from there. ## Server components `MapClusters` starts with `"use client"`, and its child is a function, so it's written in a client component. It's drawn once there's a map, which is in a browser. ## Do and don't **Do** - Use it from a few dozen places up, or wherever markers would cover each other. - Pass every place and let the map decide what's in view. - Keep `id` the same for a place from one render to the next. **Don't** - Don't gather three or four places that fit on the map as they are. - Don't use the number on a gathering as the only way to learn how many places there are. Say it beside the map.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/map maplibre-gl @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { MapClusters, MapMarker, MapView } from "@nuvui/map";
```

Clusters go inside a [MapView](page:map/map-view), which is where the styles, the worker and the provider are covered.

```tsx
<MapView aria-label="Our branches" mapStyle={style} bounds={all}>
  <MapClusters points={branches}>
    {(branch) => <MapMarker position={branch.position} label={branch.name} />}
  </MapClusters>
</MapView>
```

sections.heading: The places
How near is near
sections.markdown:
## How near is near

`radius` is how close two places are on the screen, in pixels, to be gathered. The default is 50. Smaller, and more places stand alone, closer together.

`maxZoom` is the zoom past which nothing is gathered, however near. The default is 14, which is a few streets. Two places at one address stay one button until then, and past it are two markers on the same spot, so raise it where that happens.

Changing either gathers the places again from the start.

sections.heading: What a gathering says
sections.markdown:
## What a gathering says

A gathering shows its number, shortened past a thousand in the reader's own language. Its name, which is what's read, comes from `clusterLabel`. The default is "12 places". Say what they are:

```tsx
<MapClusters
  points={chargers}
  clusterLabel={(count) => `${count} charging points`}
>
```

A press on a gathering zooms the map in to where it comes apart, which may be into smaller gatherings. Pressed from the keys, the focus goes to the map, since the button that had it is gone.

| `maxZoom` | `number` | `14` | The zoom past which nothing is gathered, however near. |
| `clusterLabel` | `((count: number) => string)` | `(count) => '${count} places'` | The name of a gathering, from how many places are in it. It's what's read in place of the number. |

It renders markers and nothing around them, so it takes no `ref`, `className` or `style`. Style a gathering through the variables below, or by its class.

pages.title: Flow diagrams
pages.description: The @nuvui/flow package. Boxes, circles and other shapes joined by arrows, drawn as SVG, in a view that pans and zooms, and edited with a pointer or the keyboard.

sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/flow @nuvui/react
```

`@nuvui/react` is a peer dependency: the diagram is drawn with the core's tokens. Nothing else is installed with it. The panning, the zooming, the dragging and the lines are written in the package.

sections.heading: Load the styles
sections.markdown:
## Load the styles

Import the package's stylesheet once, after the core's:

```tsx title="app/layout.tsx"
import "@nuvui/react/styles.css";
import "@nuvui/flow/styles.css";
```

Both files open with the same line naming the cascade layers, so the order you import them in doesn't decide which rule wins. The diagram's styles are also on their own, at `@nuvui/flow/css/flow.css`.

sections.heading: What it keeps and what you keep
Large diagrams
What it leaves out
sections.markdown:
## What it leaves out

- **Laying a diagram out by itself.** Every node has a position from you. A library such as dagre or ELK can work positions out, and you hand them in.
- **Anything inside a node but its words.** A node is a shape with a label, drawn in SVG. A button or a field in a node isn't possible.
- **Groups,** a box around some nodes that moves them together.
- **A minimap,** the whole diagram small in a corner.
- **Undo.** The lists are yours, and so is keeping their history.

pages.title: Flow
pages.description: A diagram of shapes joined by arrows, drawn as SVG, in a frame that pans and zooms. Nodes are dragged, joined and removed with a pointer or the keyboard, and only what's in view is drawn.
pages.markdown:
# Flow A diagram of shapes joined by arrows, drawn as SVG, in a frame that pans and zooms. Nodes are dragged, joined and removed with a pointer or the keyboard, and only what's in view is drawn. Use a flow diagram for something that goes from step to step: how an order moves, who approves a request, what a service calls. A diagram shows the shape of the whole. If the steps only go one way, a [stepper](page:components/stepper) or a list says the same more plainly. ```tsx import { Flow, type FlowEdge, type FlowNode } from "@nuvui/flow"; const nodes: FlowNode[] = [ { id: "placed", label: "Order placed", shape: "pill", position: { x: 0, y: 0 }, intent: "primary", }, { id: "stock", label: "In stock?", shape: "diamond", position: { x: 8, y: 110 }, }, { id: "ship", label: "Pack and ship", position: { x: 260, y: 126 }, }, { id: "reorder", label: "Reorder from the supplier", shape: "box", position: { x: 0, y: 270 }, intent: "warning", }, { id: "delivered", label: "Delivered", shape: "pill", position: { x: 260, y: 270 }, intent: "success", }, ]; const edges: FlowEdge[] = [ { id: "placed-stock", from: "placed", to: "stock" }, { id: "stock-ship", from: "stock", to: "ship", label: "yes" }, { id: "stock-reorder", from: "stock", to: "reorder", label: "no" }, { id: "reorder-ship", from: "reorder", to: "ship", dashed: true }, { id: "ship-delivered", from: "ship", to: "delivered" }, ]; // Flow is a client component, and this one only hands it data, so it can // be a server component. export default function Example() { return ; } ``` ## Install ```sh pnpm add @nuvui/flow @nuvui/react ``` ## Import ```tsx import { Flow } from "@nuvui/flow"; ``` The styles come from `@nuvui/flow/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Flow diagrams](page:flow/index) covers that. ```tsx ``` ## Nodes A node has an `id`, a `label` and a `position`: its top left corner, in the diagram's own units. The diagram is fitted into its frame, so the units are whatever you like. `shape` is one of five, each with a meaning a screen reader hears after the label: | Shape | Read as | Default size | | --- | --- | --- | | `box` | step | 160 by 56 | | `rounded`, the default | step | 160 by 56 | | `circle` | event | 88 by 88 | | `diamond` | decision | 144 by 88 | | `pill` | start or end | 160 by 48 | `size` changes one node's size. `intent` draws its outline in a color: `neutral`, `primary`, `success`, `warning` or `danger`. `description` is read after its name and shown in the list. ```tsx import { Flow, type FlowNode } from "@nuvui/flow"; const nodes: FlowNode[] = [ { id: "box", label: "box", shape: "box", position: { x: 0, y: 0 } }, { id: "rounded", label: "rounded", shape: "rounded", position: { x: 200, y: 0 }, intent: "primary", }, { id: "circle", label: "circle", shape: "circle", position: { x: 400, y: -16 }, intent: "success", }, { id: "diamond", label: "diamond", shape: "diamond", position: { x: 528, y: -16 }, intent: "warning", }, { id: "pill", label: "pill", shape: "pill", position: { x: 712, y: 4 }, intent: "danger", }, ]; export default function Example() { return ( ); } ``` The label wraps inside the shape, and after as many lines as the shape has room for it ends with an ellipsis. The whole label is still its name. A circle's and a diamond's words sit in the box that fits inside them, so they're narrower than the shape. ## Edges An edge goes `from` one node `to` another, or to the same node, which draws a loop. `path` says how the line goes: - `curved`, the default, and `step`, at right angles, join the sides of the two nodes that face each other. - `straight` runs from one outline to the other, toward the middles. `edgePath` on the diagram changes the default for every edge that doesn't say. `arrow` puts an arrowhead at the `end`, the default, the `start`, `both` or `none`. `label` writes words on the line, such as "yes" after a decision. `dashed` draws it dashed, and `animated` draws it dashed and moving toward its end, which stops when less motion is asked for. `intent` colors it as a node's. ```tsx import { Flow, type FlowEdge, type FlowNode } from "@nuvui/flow"; const box = (id: string, x: number, y: number): FlowNode => ({ id, label: id, shape: "box", position: { x, y }, size: { width: 120, height: 48 }, }); const nodes: FlowNode[] = [ box("Request", 0, 0), box("Straight", 300, 0), box("Curved", 300, 110), box("Step", 300, 220), box("Both ways", 0, 220), ]; const edges: FlowEdge[] = [ { id: "straight", from: "Request", to: "Straight", path: "straight" }, { id: "curved", from: "Request", to: "Curved", path: "curved", label: "dashed", dashed: true, }, { id: "step", from: "Request", to: "Step", path: "step", label: "running", animated: true, intent: "primary", }, { id: "both", from: "Step", to: "Both ways", arrow: "both", intent: "danger", }, ]; export default function Example() { return ; } ``` ## Editing With `editable`, the diagram can be changed: - **Moving.** Drag a node, or several selected ones. With the keyboard, hold Shift and press an arrow key. `snap` puts moved nodes on a grid of that step, and the arrow keys move by it, or by 10 without one. - **Joining.** Drag from one of the handles on a node's sides to another node. Handles show on the node under the pointer and on a node that's selected alone. With the keyboard, press L on one node, move to another and press L again. - **Removing.** Select nodes or edges and press Delete. A node takes its edges with it. A node with `locked` can be selected but not moved, joined or removed. ```tsx "use client"; import { Flow, type FlowEdge, type FlowNode } from "@nuvui/flow"; import { Button } from "@nuvui/react"; import { useState } from "react"; const start: FlowNode[] = [ { id: "lead", label: "New lead", shape: "pill", position: { x: 0, y: 40 }, intent: "primary", }, { id: "qualify", label: "Qualify", position: { x: 220, y: 36 } }, { id: "won", label: "Won", shape: "pill", position: { x: 440, y: 40 }, intent: "success", }, ]; const links: FlowEdge[] = [ { id: "lead-qualify", from: "lead", to: "qualify" }, { id: "qualify-won", from: "qualify", to: "won" }, ]; export default function Example() { const [nodes, setNodes] = useState(start); const [edges, setEdges] = useState(links); const [last, setLast] = useState("Nothing yet."); const add = () => { const count = nodes.length + 1; setNodes([ ...nodes, { id: `step-${count}`, label: `Step ${count}`, position: { x: 220, y: 140 + (count - 3) * 80 }, }, ]); }; return (
{ setNodes(next); setLast(`Nodes: ${change.type} ${change.ids.join(", ")}`); }} onEdgesChange={(next, change) => { setEdges(next); setLast(`Edges: ${change.type} ${change.ids.join(", ")}`); }} />

{last}

); } ``` ### Who keeps the diagram Pass `nodes` and `edges`, and the diagram draws them and tells you of changes. Pass `defaultNodes` and `defaultEdges` instead, and it keeps them itself and still tells you. `onNodesChange` is called with the nodes as they are after a change, and the change: `{ type: "move", ids }` or `{ type: "remove", ids }`. A drag is reported once, when it ends, and keys once they rest, so a diagram with thousands of nodes isn't copied on every frame. `onNodeDrag` is called on every frame of a drag for an app that wants that. The nodes that didn't change are the same objects as before. `onEdgesChange` is the same for edges, with `{ type: "add", ids }` or `{ type: "remove", ids }`. When you keep `nodes`, a move you don't take is undone: the node goes back to where your nodes say. That's how a step is kept in a lane, or saving that fails is put right. ### Which links may be made By default any two different nodes may be joined, once each way. `canConnect` decides instead: it's called with the two ids, and a link it refuses isn't made. `createEdge` makes the new edge, which by default is `{ id: "from->to", from, to }`. ## Selecting A click selects a node or an edge. Shift and a click adds one or takes it away. Shift and a drag on empty space selects what the box touches, and a click on empty space clears the selection. With the keyboard, Space selects, Ctrl+A selects every node, and Escape clears. `selection`, with `onSelectionChange`, keeps the selection yourself. It's `{ nodes, edges }`, by id, in the order of your lists. `onNodeOpen` is called on a double click on a node, or on Enter, for something such as opening a panel with its details. ## The view The diagram is fitted into its frame when it first shows, and never zoomed in past its own size for that. `defaultViewport` starts it somewhere else instead, and `onViewportChange` is called when the view stops moving. Drag empty space to pan. Pinch on a touch screen. The wheel zooms while the diagram has focus, or with Ctrl held, which is what a pinch on a trackpad sends. Otherwise it scrolls the page past the diagram, as it would past a picture. The buttons in the corner zoom out, zoom in and fit, and so do minus, plus and 0. `minZoom` and `maxZoom` are the limits, 0.05 and 2.5 by default. `controls={false}` leaves the buttons out. `handleRef` gives you the same from your own code: ```tsx const flow = useRef(null); ; flow.current?.center("billing"); ``` | Method | What it does | | --- | --- | | `fit()` | Shows the whole diagram. | | `zoomIn()`, `zoomOut()` | Zooms around the middle of the frame. | | `center(id)` | Moves the view so a node is in the middle. | | `getViewport()` | Where the view is now: `{ x, y, zoom }`. | ## Large diagrams The diagram stays quick with thousands of nodes because the work is kept to what can be seen: - Only the nodes and edges in view, and a margin around it, are on the page. They're found through an index of where everything is, not by looking at every node. - From far out, where words can't be read, nodes are shapes with no words and edges have no arrowheads. Further out, or with too many nodes in view to draw one by one, the diagram is a few paths, one for each color. - Panning and zooming change one attribute, once a frame, and don't render React. A node that moves renders itself and its edges and nothing else. - Nothing is measured: every node's size comes from its shape or from you. The text version, the list, is built when it's opened, two hundred steps at a time. ## Server rendering and a strict policy Every position is an SVG attribute, and nothing is set with a `style` attribute. A server sends the diagram fitted by the SVG's `viewBox`, which needs no size, and a [Content Security Policy](page:content-security-policy) without `style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'` changes nothing. Up to `serverLimit` nodes, 300 by default, the server sends the whole diagram. A larger one is drawn by the browser once it knows the frame's size: the server sends the frame, the controls and the list's button. Flow starts with `"use client"`. A server component can render it and hand it the lists. ## Flow props | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `aria-label` (required) | `string` | | The diagram's name, for a screen reader. Required. | | `nodes` | `FlowNode[]` | | The nodes, when the app keeps them. | | `defaultNodes` | `FlowNode[]` | | The nodes to start with, when the diagram keeps them itself. | | `onNodesChange` | `((nodes: FlowNode[], change: FlowNodesChange) => void)` | | Called with the nodes after a change made in the diagram, and what the change was. A drag is reported once, when it ends. | | `edges` | `FlowEdge[]` | | | | `defaultEdges` | `FlowEdge[]` | | | | `onEdgesChange` | `((edges: FlowEdge[], change: FlowEdgesChange) => void)` | | | | `selection` | `FlowSelection` | | | | `defaultSelection` | `FlowSelection` | | | | `onSelectionChange` | `((selection: FlowSelection) => void)` | | | | `editable` | `boolean` | `false` | Nodes can be dragged, joined and removed, with a pointer or the keyboard. | | `edgePath` | `"curved" \| "step" \| "straight"` | `"curved"` | How an edge's line goes when the edge doesn't say. | | `background` | `"dots" \| "lines" \| "none"` | `"dots"` | | | `snap` | `number` | `0` | The step of a grid that moved nodes land on, in the diagram's units. 0 for none. The arrow keys move a node by this much, or by 10. | | `minZoom` | `number` | `0.05` | | | `maxZoom` | `number` | `2.5` | | | `defaultViewport` | `FlowViewport` | | Where the view starts. The whole diagram, fitted, when not given. | | `onViewportChange` | `((viewport: FlowViewport) => void)` | | Called when the view stops moving. | | `onNodeOpen` | `((id: string) => void)` | | Called on a double click of a node, or Enter on one. | | `onNodeDrag` | `((positions: { id: string; position: Point; }[]) => void)` | | Called on every frame of a drag, with where the dragged nodes are. | | `canConnect` | `((from: string, to: string) => boolean)` | | Whether a link may be made from one node to another. By default any two different nodes that aren't joined that way yet. | | `createEdge` | `((from: string, to: string) => FlowEdge)` | | The edge a new link makes. | | `controls` | `boolean` | `true` | Zoom and fit buttons, and the list's button. | | `serverLimit` | `number` | `300` | How many nodes a server draws. A larger diagram is drawn by the browser, once it knows the frame's size. | | `labels` | `FlowLabels` | | The diagram's own words, for translating. | | `handleRef` | `Ref` | | The diagram's methods: fit, zoom and center. | It also takes the attributes of a `div`, and passes `ref` to it. ## FlowNode | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `id` (required) | `string` | | What edges and changes know it by. Unique in the diagram. | | `label` (required) | `string` | | The words in the shape, and its name for a screen reader. | | `position` (required) | `Point` | | Its top left corner, in the diagram's own units. | | `shape` | `"box" \| "circle" \| "diamond" \| "pill" \| "rounded"` | `"rounded"` | | | `size` | `Size` | | Its size, in the diagram's units. Each shape has its own default. | | `intent` | `"danger" \| "neutral" \| "primary" \| "success" \| "warning"` | `"neutral"` | | | `description` | `string` | | More about it, read after its name and shown in the list. | | `locked` | `boolean` | | In an editable diagram, it can't be moved, joined to another or removed. It can still be selected. | ## FlowEdge | Prop | Type | Default | What it's for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `id` (required) | `string` | | What changes know it by. Unique among the edges. | | `from` (required) | `string` | | The id of the node it starts at. | | `to` (required) | `string` | | The id of the node it goes to. | | `label` | `string` | | Words on the line, such as "yes" after a decision. | | `path` | `"curved" \| "step" \| "straight"` | | How the line goes. It stands still when less motion is asked for. | ## Translation Everything the diagram says and doesn't draw is in `labels`, in English until you give another. sections.heading: Install
sections.markdown:
## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/flow @nuvui/react
```

sections.heading: Import
sections.markdown:
## Import

```tsx
import { Flow } from "@nuvui/flow";
```

The styles come from `@nuvui/flow/styles.css`, which you load once for the whole app, after `@nuvui/react/styles.css`. [Flow diagrams](page:flow/index) covers that.

```tsx
<Flow aria-label="How an order goes" nodes={nodes} edges={edges} />
```

sections.heading: Nodes
Edges
Editing
Selecting
sections.markdown:
## Selecting

A click selects a node or an edge. Shift and a click adds one or takes it away. Shift and a drag on empty space selects what the box touches, and a click on empty space clears the selection. With the keyboard, Space selects, Ctrl+A selects every node, and Escape clears.

`selection`, with `onSelectionChange`, keeps the selection yourself. It's `{ nodes, edges }`, by id, in the order of your lists.

`onNodeOpen` is called on a double click on a node, or on Enter, for something such as opening a panel with its details.

sections.heading: The view
sections.markdown:
## The view

The diagram is fitted into its frame when it first shows, and never zoomed in past its own size for that. `defaultViewport` starts it somewhere else instead, and `onViewportChange` is called when the view stops moving.

Drag empty space to pan. Pinch on a touch screen. The wheel zooms while the diagram has focus, or with Ctrl held, which is what a pinch on a trackpad sends. Otherwise it scrolls the page past the diagram, as it would past a picture. The buttons in the corner zoom out, zoom in and fit, and so do minus, plus and 0. `minZoom` and `maxZoom` are the limits, 0.05 and 2.5 by default. `controls={false}` leaves the buttons out.

`handleRef` gives you the same from your own code:

```tsx
const flow = useRef<FlowHandle>(null);

<Flow aria-label="Services" nodes={nodes} edges={edges} handleRef={flow} />;

flow.current?.center("billing");
```

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `fit()` | Shows the whole diagram. |
| `zoomIn()`, `zoomOut()` | Zooms around the middle of the frame. |
| `center(id)` | Moves the view so a node is in the middle. |
| `getViewport()` | Where the view is now: `{ x, y, zoom }`. |

sections.heading: Large diagrams
sections.markdown:
## Large diagrams

The diagram stays quick with thousands of nodes because the work is kept to what can be seen:

- Only the nodes and edges in view, and a margin around it, are on the page. They're found through an index of where everything is, not by looking at every node.
- From far out, where words can't be read, nodes are shapes with no words and edges have no arrowheads. Further out, or with too many nodes in view to draw one by one, the diagram is a few paths, one for each color.
- Panning and zooming change one attribute, once a frame, and don't render React. A node that moves renders itself and its edges and nothing else.
- Nothing is measured: every node's size comes from its shape or from you.

The text version, the list, is built when it's opened, two hundred steps at a time.

sections.heading: Server rendering and a strict policy
sections.markdown:
## Server rendering and a strict policy

Every position is an SVG attribute, and nothing is set with a `style` attribute. A server sends the diagram fitted by the SVG's `viewBox`, which needs no size, and a [Content Security Policy](page:content-security-policy) without `style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'` changes nothing.

Up to `serverLimit` nodes, 300 by default, the server sends the whole diagram. A larger one is drawn by the browser once it knows the frame's size: the server sends the frame, the controls and the list's button.

Flow starts with `"use client"`. A server component can render it and hand it the lists.

sections.heading: Flow props
sections.markdown:
## Flow props

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aria-label` (required) | `string` |  | The diagram's name, for a screen reader. Required. |
| `nodes` | `FlowNode[]` |  | The nodes, when the app keeps them. |
| `defaultNodes` | `FlowNode[]` |  | The nodes to start with, when the diagram keeps them itself. |
| `onNodesChange` | `((nodes: FlowNode[], change: FlowNodesChange) => void)` |  | Called with the nodes after a change made in the diagram, and what the change was. A drag is reported once, when it ends. |
| `edges` | `FlowEdge[]` |  |  |
| `defaultEdges` | `FlowEdge[]` |  |  |
| `onEdgesChange` | `((edges: FlowEdge[], change: FlowEdgesChange) => void)` |  |  |
| `selection` | `FlowSelection` |  |  |
| `defaultSelection` | `FlowSelection` |  |  |
| `onSelectionChange` | `((selection: FlowSelection) => void)` |  |  |
| `editable` | `boolean` | `false` | Nodes can be dragged, joined and removed, with a pointer or the keyboard. |
| `edgePath` | `"curved" \| "step" \| "straight"` | `"curved"` | How an edge's line goes when the edge doesn't say. |
| `background` | `"dots" \| "lines" \| "none"` | `"dots"` |  |
| `snap` | `number` | `0` | The step of a grid that moved nodes land on, in the diagram's units. 0 for none. The arrow keys move a node by this much, or by 10. |
| `minZoom` | `number` | `0.05` |  |
| `maxZoom` | `number` | `2.5` |  |
| `defaultViewport` | `FlowViewport` |  | Where the view starts. The whole diagram, fitted, when not given. |
| `onViewportChange` | `((viewport: FlowViewport) => void)` |  | Called when the view stops moving. |
| `onNodeOpen` | `((id: string) => void)` |  | Called on a double click of a node, or Enter on one. |
| `onNodeDrag` | `((positions: { id: string; position: Point; }[]) => void)` |  | Called on every frame of a drag, with where the dragged nodes are. |
| `canConnect` | `((from: string, to: string) => boolean)` |  | Whether a link may be made from one node to another. By default any two different nodes that aren't joined that way yet. |
| `createEdge` | `((from: string, to: string) => FlowEdge)` |  | The edge a new link makes. |
| `controls` | `boolean` | `true` | Zoom and fit buttons, and the list's button. |
| `serverLimit` | `number` | `300` | How many nodes a server draws. A larger diagram is drawn by the browser, once it knows the frame's size. |
| `labels` | `FlowLabels` |  | The diagram's own words, for translating. |
| `handleRef` | `Ref<FlowHandle>` |  | The diagram's methods: fit, zoom and center. |

It also takes the attributes of a `div`, and passes `ref` to it.

sections.markdown:
## FlowNode

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` (required) | `string` |  | What edges and changes know it by. Unique in the diagram. |

## Translation

Everything the diagram says and doesn't draw is in `labels`, in English until you give another. The ones that put names into a sentence are functions.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `roleDescription` | `string` |  | What kind of thing the diagram is, read after its name. |
| `shapes` | `Partial<Record<FlowShape, string>>` |  | What each shape means, read after a node's name. |
| `leadsTo` | `((targets: FlowLinkTarget[]) => string)` |  | Where a node leads, read after its name and shown in the list. |
| `instructions` | `string` |  | How to get around the diagram with the keyboard. |
| `editInstructions` | `string` |  | How to change it with the keyboard, read after `instructions`. |
| `controls` | `string` |  | The name of the group of buttons. |
| `zoomIn` | `string` |  |  |
| `zoomOut` | `string` |  |  |
| `fit` | `string` |  |  |
| `showList` | `string` |  | The button that shows the diagram as a list. |
| `hideList` | `string` |  |  |
| `list` | `string` |  | The name of the list. |
| `showMore` | `((count: number) => string)` |  | The button at the end of a long list. |
| `find` | `((label: string) => string)` |  | A step's button in the list, which finds it in the diagram. |
| `removeLink` | `((from: string, to: string) => string)` |  | A link's button in the list of an editable diagram. |
| `linking` | `((from: string) => string)` |  | Said when a link is started with the keyboard. |
| `linked` | `((from: string, to: string) => string)` |  | Said when a link is made. |
| `linkCancelled` | `string` |  | Said when a link that was started is let go. |
| `moved` | `((labels: string[]) => string)` |  | Said when nodes are moved. |
| `removed` | `((nodes: number, links: number) => string)` |  | Said when nodes and links are removed. |

```tsx
<Flow
  aria-label="Bestelling"
  labels={{
    roleDescription: "stroomdiagram",
    shapes: { diamond: "keuze", pill: "begin of einde" },
    leadsTo: (targets) =>
      `gaat naar ${targets.map((target) => target.label).join(" en ")}`,
  }}
/>
```

sections.heading: Do and don't
sections.markdown:
## Do and don't

**Do**

- Keep the diagram to what one reader can follow, and split one that grows past that.
- Give every node a label that reads well on its own, since that's its name.
- Save changes when `onNodesChange` and `onEdgesChange` are called, once each.

**Don't**

- Don't use a diagram for steps that only ever go one way. A list says it more plainly.
- Don't make color the only difference between nodes. Say it in the label or the description too.
- Don't save on every frame of a drag with `onNodeDrag`.

pages.title: Icons
pages.description: The @nuvui/icons package. 317 line icons drawn for nuvui, in three styles, each a React component in the color of the text around it and an SVG file.
pages.markdown:
# Icons

The @nuvui/icons package. 317 line icons drawn for nuvui, in three styles, each a React component in the color of the text around it and an SVG file.

`@nuvui/icons` is a set of 317 line icons drawn for this library, on a 24 pixel grid, in three styles. Each one is a React component and an SVG file. They're MIT licensed like the rest of nuvui: they were drawn for it, and none was traced or adapted from another set.

The components in `@nuvui/react` don't use this package. They draw their few icons themselves, so the core doesn't depend on it, and you install it only if you want the icons.

## Install

```sh
pnpm add @nuvui/icons
```

It needs React and nothing else. There's no stylesheet to import, and it works without `@nuvui/react`.

## Use an icon

```tsx
import { Button } from "@nuvui/react";
import { ArrowRightIcon } from "@nuvui/icons";

export function Next() {
  return (
    <Button>
      Next <ArrowRightIcon size={16} />
    </Button>
  );
}
```

Every icon's name is its name in the set, written as a component, with `Icon` at the end: `arrow-right` is `ArrowRightIcon`, and `map` is `MapIcon`. That's its only name. A bare `Map` or `Image` would hide JavaScript's own in the file that imports it.

## Three styles

| Style | Import from | How it's drawn |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard | `@nuvui/icons` | Round ends, sharp corners. |
| Rounded | `@nuvui/icons/rounded` | Round ends, and corners rounded by 1.5 pixels, or 0.5 on icons that come to a point. |
| Sharp | `@nuvui/icons/sharp` | Square ends and mitered corners. |

The three have the same icons by the same names, so a style is changed by changing where the imports come from. Pick one for an app: icons in two styles side by side look like a mistake.

Rounded and Standard only differ at a corner where two lines meet. An icon without one, such as an arrow whose head meets its shaft at the point, is the same drawing in both.

## Size and color

An icon is 24 pixels square unless `size` says otherwise. A number is pixels, and a string is any CSS length, so `size="1em"` follows the text's size.

The line is the color of the text around it (`currentColor`), so an icon in a button or a link takes that color, in every theme, on hover and when disabled. No color is written into an icon.

The line is 1.5 units thick on the 24 unit grid, and it grows and shrinks with the icon. At 16 pixels it's a pixel wide. `strokeWidth` changes it, in the same units.

Where the browser forces its own colors, as Windows' contrast themes do, the text's color is forced and the icon follows it.

## For screen readers

An icon is hidden from screen readers unless it's given a name, which is right for one beside words that say the same thing. Give it a `title` when nothing else says what it means:

```tsx
<ArrowRightIcon title="Next page" />
```

With a `title` or an `aria-label`, the icon is announced as a picture by that name. A `title` becomes the icon's `aria-label` as well as its tooltip, since Safari doesn't take a picture's name from its `<title>`. An icon alone in a button is better left hidden and the button named instead, with `aria-label` on the button, since it's the button that's pressed.

## In a right-to-left layout

An icon is drawn the same way in either direction. One that points the way of reading, such as an arrow for "next", has to be turned around on a right-to-left page. A clock or a check mark doesn't. Whether an arrow points the way of reading depends on what it means where it's used, so that's left to you, with a selector on the `dir` attribute:

```css
[dir="rtl"] .next-icon {
  transform: scaleX(-1);
}
```

[Right-to-left](page:right-to-left) has the rest, and the SCSS mixin that writes that selector.

## In a server component

Icons have no state and no `"use client"`. A server component renders them as markup, and no script is sent for them.

## What gets bundled

Each icon is a module of its own, and the package says it has no side effects, so a bundler leaves out every icon a page doesn't import. One icon is under half a kilobyte, compressed.

Without that pruning, in a development server, importing from the package loads all 317. Next.js prunes during development too for packages listed in `experimental.optimizePackageImports`:

```js title="next.config.mjs"
export default {
  experimental: {
    optimizePackageImports: ["@nuvui/icons"],
  },
};
```

## An icon of your own

`createIcon` makes a component that's drawn and behaves the way the set's own are, from shapes on the same 24 unit grid:

```tsx
import { createIcon } from "@nuvui/icons";

export const FrameIcon = createIcon("FrameIcon", "standard", [
  ["rect", { x: "4", y: "4", width: "16", height: "16", rx: "2" }],
]);
```

The first argument names it in React's developer tools. The second is the style whose ends and corners it takes.

## SVG files and the list of icons

Every icon also ships as an SVG file, for an email, a slide or a page that isn't React: `@nuvui/icons/svg/standard/arrow-right.svg`, with `rounded` and `sharp` beside `standard`. The files draw in `currentColor` too, which is black where nothing sets a color.

`@nuvui/icons/manifest.json` lists every icon's name, its component's name and its category. The grid below is built from it.

## Props

Each icon takes these, and anything an `<svg>` element takes. Its `ref` is the `<svg>`.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `string \| number` | `24` | Width and height. A number is in pixels. |
| `strokeWidth` | `string \| number` | `1.5` | How thick the lines are, in the units of the 24 by 24 grid the icon is drawn on, so it grows and shrinks with `size`. |
| `title` | `string` |  | What the icon means, for a screen reader, when nothing next to it says so. Without it, or an `aria-label`, the icon is hidden from screen readers, which is right for one beside text that says the same. |

## The Figma file

The icons are drawn in Figma, and the file is yours to download: [NuvUI_Icons_Figma_File.fig](https://nuvui.nuvraxis.com/docs/NuvUI_Icons_Figma_File.fig). Import it from Figma's file browser, or drag it in. Each icon is a component with a variant for each style, so a design made with them uses the same icons, by the same names, as the code. It's MIT licensed like the package.

The download is a copy, saved when the icons last changed. It has the icons and nothing else of the file's: no comments and no version history.

## Where they come from

The icons are drawn in a Figma file, one component for each with a variant for each style. A script in the repository exports them as SVG, makes every file the same, and fails if one breaks the set's rules: a size other than 24 by 24, a color other than the set's ink, or a name that isn't lower case words joined by hyphens. The SVG files are committed, and the components are generated from them when the package is built.

sections.heading: Props
sections.markdown:
## Props

Each icon takes these, and anything an `<svg>` element takes. Its `ref` is the `<svg>`.

| Prop | Type | Default | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `string \| number` | `24` | Width and height. A number is in pixels. |
| `strokeWidth` | `string \| number` | `1.5` | How thick the lines are, in the units of the 24 by 24 grid the icon is drawn on, so it grows and shrinks with `size`. |
| `title` | `string` |  | What the icon means, for a screen reader, when nothing next to it says so. Without it, or an `aria-label`, the icon is hidden from screen readers, which is right for one beside text that says the same. |

sections.heading: The Figma file
sections.markdown:
## The Figma file

The icons are drawn in Figma, and the file is yours to download: [NuvUI_Icons_Figma_File.fig](https://nuvui.nuvraxis.com/docs/NuvUI_Icons_Figma_File.fig). Import it from Figma's file browser, or drag it in. Each icon is a component with a variant for each style, so a design made with them uses the same icons, by the same names, as the code. It's MIT licensed like the package.

The download is a copy, saved when the icons last changed. It has the icons and nothing else of the file's: no comments and no version history.

sections.heading: Where they come from
sections.markdown:
## Where they come from

The icons are drawn in a Figma file, one component for each with a variant for each style. A script in the repository exports them as SVG, makes every file the same, and fails if one breaks the set's rules: a size other than 24 by 24, a color other than the set's ink, or a name that isn't lower case words joined by hyphens. The SVG files are committed, and the components are generated from them when the package is built.

pages.title: Recipes
pages.description: The screens people ask for most, such as a sign-in screen, a form, a table, a dashboard or a chat, and what to build each from.
pages.markdown:
# Recipes

The screens people ask for most, and what to build each from. Where a block already does it, start from the block: it's the components put together the way they're meant to be, with the states and the small screens worked out. [blocks.md](tool:list_blocks) has every block and the command that adds one.

A block is a starting point, to be changed. Its data is made up and stands in for the app's.

## A sign-in screen

Start from the block `sign-in`, or `sign-in-sso` for a company account, `sign-up`, `forgot-password`, `verify-code`.

What it's made of: `Field` around each `Input` and `PasswordInput`, a `Button` with `type="submit"`, an `Alert` for an error that belongs to no field.

Read: [rules/forms.md](rule:forms), [reference/forms.md](page:forms), [reference/components/field.md](page:components/field).

## A form with fields and errors

No block is only this. Build it from [reference/forms.md](page:forms), which has a whole form each way: with the browser's validation, and with React Hook Form.

1. A plain `<form>`, with `noValidate` if a library does the checking.
2. Each control in a `Field`, with a `FieldLabel`, and the control inside `FieldControl`.
3. Each control has a `name`.
4. A message per field in `FieldError`. It renders nothing while it's empty.
5. One `Button` with `type="submit"`.
6. On a submit with errors, move the focus to the first control that has one.

For a settings page, the blocks `profile-form`, `notifications`, `appearance` and `danger-zone` are each a form of a different kind.

## A table of data

Start from the block `table-toolbar`: search, a filter, a column chooser, a menu on each row, and actions for the rows that are ticked.

For less than that, [reference/table/index.md](page:table/index) has a data table in two steps. Add what's needed from the pages beside it: sorting, filtering, pagination, row-selection, column-visibility. For rows that a server sorts and pages: [reference/table/server.md](page:table/server). For many thousands of rows: [reference/table/virtualization.md](page:table/virtualization).

For rows with nothing to do but be read, `Table` alone is enough: [reference/table/table.md](page:table/table).

Don't forget the other states. The block `page-states` is one page with its rows, waiting for them, with none, and after a request that failed.

## A page with a sidebar

Start from the block `app-shell` for the whole of an app's screen: a sidebar that folds to its icons, a bar on top, the page, and a panel on the far side that closes and is a sheet on a phone. `sidebar-nested` is navigation in two levels, and `dashboard` a whole screen with a sidebar in it.

What it's made of: `SidebarProvider` around the layout, `Sidebar` with its parts, and the page's content beside it. [reference/components/sidebar.md](page:components/sidebar) has the parts, and how the sidebar becomes a sheet on a phone.

Mark the page that's open, give the `nav` a name, and keep the page's own content in a `main`.

## A dashboard

Start from the block `dashboard`: a sidebar, four figures with how each has changed, a chart, and a table of recent orders. It needs `@nuvui/charts` and `@nuvui/table`.

The figures are `Stat` with `Trend`. The chart is Recharts in a `ChartContainer`: [reference/charts/index.md](page:charts/index). The block `figures` is the row of figures alone.

## A themed app

Nothing to build: theming is CSS.

1. Pick a preset if one is close, and load its stylesheet after the core's: `import "@nuvui/react/themes/ink.css"`.
2. Set the brand's colors on `:root`, in a rule that's in no layer: `--color-primary`, `--color-primary-foreground`, `--color-ring`. Give dark its own values beside them. [reference/theming.md](page:theming) shows how.
3. `data-theme="system"` on `<html>` to follow the reader's system, or `light` or `dark`.
4. A switch for dark mode sets that attribute, and remembers it. There's no provider.

Check the contrast of any color you set: 4.5 to 1 for text, 3 to 1 for the edge of a control. [tokens.md](tool:get_tokens) has every token.

## A chat with an assistant

Start from the block `assistant-chat` for a whole screen, `assistant-sidebar` for one with past conversations, `ask-panel` for a panel beside a record, `support-chat` for a help desk that opens from a corner.

The components draw the conversation. Fetching and streaming the reply is the app's: [reference/chat/index.md](page:chat/index) says how the props line up with what a fetch gives.

## A board of tasks

Start from the block `task-board`, or `deal-pipeline` for one that adds up each column. [reference/kanban/index.md](page:kanban/index) says what the board keeps and what the app keeps.

## A map of places

Start from the block `branch-finder` for a list beside a map, `delivery-route` for a way with stops, `charging-map` for many places gathered into clusters.

Before any of them works: the worker's address, and a tile provider the app's owner has chosen. [rules/packages.md](rule:packages) has both.

## A marketing page

The blocks `nav-bar`, `hero`, `feature-grid`, `pricing`, `faq`, `reviews`, `case-studies` and `footer` are the parts of one.

## When there's no block

1. Find the components in the table in [SKILL.md](tool:get_rules), and read each one's reference file.
2. Write the structure with the library's components, and the layout around them the way the app styles things.
3. Add the states: nothing to show, waiting, something went wrong.
4. Check it at 320 pixels wide, with the keyboard, and in dark mode.
